When the state of the realm is nominally one of order and peace, unforeseen anxieties often lie hidden within it; therefore, an enlightened ruler is cautious toward it. At the assembly in the Eastern Capital, the hearts of the people were united and blessings and emoluments…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聚矣乃君子則以理亂循環之幾不可忘戰家
邦久遠之計誰能去兵師徒方渙不作則不奮
也臨瀍洛以嚴簡閲之敎觀聽方新不親則不
肅也釋衮冕而躬靺鞈之章六師之氣習安而
靡矣則勗其止齊以示之勇伍兩軍師莫不起
而共武服者作其氣也六師之志狃平而偷矣
則申其誓戒以訓之忠文武將吏莫不起而勤
王愾者作其志也我周本以戎衣開國而維有
夷之御則大烈以揚列侯環視不益震於天威
===
而堅其翊戴之思哉先王嘗以整旅戡亂而今
六師之作則顯謨以承六合風聞不將慴於王
靈而消其釁孽之萌哉蓋當是時天下之治日
趨於尚文不可不耀之以武國家之勢已見其
積弱不可不糾之以强玆役也保治之圖也周
道復興宜矣自周而後天子宿重兵於京師亦
古者六軍遺意彼五柞長楊豈不稱習戎哉而
久之漸替故其季也禁衞雖設而非習服遇小
警即不能受甲焉噫六師之作詎至此乎是故
punctuated: 聚矣。乃君子則以理亂循環之幾不可忘戰，家邦久遠之計誰能去兵？師徒方渙，不作則不奮也，臨瀍、洛以嚴簡閲之敎；觀聽方新，不親則不肅也，釋衮冕而躬靺鞈之章。六師之氣，習安而靡矣，則勗其止齊以示之勇，伍兩軍師莫不起而共武服者，作其氣也；六師之志，狃平而偷矣，則申其誓戒以訓之忠，文武將吏莫不起而勤王愾者，作其志也。我周本以戎衣開國，而維有夷之御，則大烈以揚，列侯環視，不益震於天威而堅其翊戴之思哉？先王嘗以整旅戡亂，而今六師之作，則顯謨以承，六合風聞，不將慴於王靈而消其釁孽之萌哉？蓋當是時，天下之治日趨於尚文，不可不耀之以武；國家之勢已見其積弱，不可不糾之以强。玆役也，保治之圖也，周道復興，宜矣。自周而後，天子宿重兵於京師，亦古者六軍遺意。彼五柞、長楊，豈不稱習戎哉？而久之漸替，故其季也，禁衞雖設而非習服，遇小警即不能受甲焉。噫！六師之作，詎至此乎？是故
translation_en: …had gathered. Yet the noble men believed that in the cyclical pivot of order and disorder one must not forget warfare, and in long-term plans for family and state, who can dispense with arms? When the troops are growing lax, if they are not roused they will not be spirited; thus he approached the Chan and Luo rivers to enforce the instruction of military inspection. When the sights and sounds are newly presented, if he does not attend in person there will be no solemnity; thus he laid aside his ceremonial robes and crown and personally donned the red-dyed knee-covers of war. The spirit of the Six Armies, accustomed to peace, had grown listless; so he exhorted them in halting and dressing ranks to show them valor, and none among the squads, platoons, divisions, and armies failed to rise up and attend to military service—such was his rousing of their spirit. The resolve of the Six Armies, habituated to tranquility, had grown remiss; so he reiterated his oaths and admonitions to instruct them in loyalty, and none among the civil and military officers and functionaries failed to rise up and exert themselves in the king's righteous indignation—such was his rousing of their resolve. Our Zhou dynasty originally founded the state in battle dress, and now in wearing the attire of "Youyi" [?], great merit was thereby proclaimed; as the feudal lords looked on from all sides, would they not be all the more awed by heavenly majesty and strengthen their thoughts of supportive allegiance? The former kings once quelled rebellion by marshaling their hosts, and now with the rousing of the Six Armies, their illustrious plans were thereby continued; as the six directions heard the wind of it, would they not tremble before the royal prestige and extinguish the buds of sedition and evil? Indeed, at that time, the governance of the empire was daily inclining toward the prizing of civil culture, so it could not but be dazzled with martial prowess; the momentum of the state had already shown accumulated weakness, so it could not but be rectified with strength. This campaign was a plan for preserving good order; that the Way of Zhou revived was fitting indeed! From the Zhou onward, the Son of Heaven stationed heavy forces in the capital, which was also the legacy of the ancient Six Armies. Did not those hunts at Wuzuo and Changyang claim to be military exercises? Yet over time they gradually declined, so that in the dynasty's final years, although the imperial guards were established, they were not trained and accustomed to service, and upon encountering a minor alarm they were unable even to put on armor. Alas! Could the rousing of the Six Armies ever come to such a pass? Therefore…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
周雅以頌漢賦以風
乃及王季維德之行大任有身生此文王
段藎國
同考試官訓導趙批上二句作者多以王季大任並
講殊失輕重下二句作者非枯淡則浮泛此作獨得之
同考試官教諭尹批典贍有體
考試官教諭湯批體格純正
考試官教諭王批詞意俱到
周有一德之配而聖人生矣蓋父作之母相之
===
天之所以開聖人也此文王所由生與詩人推
本以戒成王曰我周受命始於文王固矣而其
生豈偶然哉蓋國之將興天必生聖人以長發
其祥聖之將生天必厚聖人之所自生以竝鍾
其德故婦於京而思媚大任之婦道脩矣乃及
王季殆與其明類者有合德也嬪於周而思齊
大任之母道全矣乃及王季殆與其順比者無
違行也夫以德配德則帝祉集而大任身焉因
以凝醇和之氣以德育德則貞元會而文王生
punctuated:
周《雅》以頌，漢賦以風。

「乃及王季，維德之行。大任有身，生此文王。」
段藎國
同考試官訓導趙批：上二句作者多以王季、大任並講，殊失輕重；下二句作者非枯淡則浮泛，此作獨得之。
同考試官教諭尹批：典贍有體。
考試官教諭湯批：體格純正。
考試官教諭王批：詞意俱到。

周有一德之配，而聖人生矣。蓋父作之，母相之，天之所以開聖人也，此文王所由生與？詩人推本以戒成王，曰：我周受命始於文王，固矣，而其生豈偶然哉？蓋國之將興，天必生聖人以長發其祥；聖之將生，天必厚聖人之所自生以竝鍾其德。故婦於京而思媚，大任之婦道脩矣；乃及王季，殆與其明類者有合德也。嬪於周而思齊，大任之母道全矣；乃及王季，殆與其順比者無違行也。夫以德配德，則帝祉集而大任身焉，因以凝醇和之氣；以德育德，則貞元會而文王生…
translation_en:
… the Odes (Ya) of the Zhou offer praise, while the rhapsodies (fu) of the Han offer admonition.

"Then down to King Ji, his conduct was nothing but virtuous. Tai Ren became pregnant, and gave birth to this King Wen."
Duan Jinguo
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao comments: "On the first two lines, most writers discuss King Ji and Tai Ren equally, completely losing the sense of relative weight; on the last two lines, writers are either dry and insipid or superficial and vague, whereas this piece alone has grasped it."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: "Allusive, rich, and formally proper."
Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: "The style and structure are pure and upright."
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: "Both the diction and the meaning hit the mark."

The Zhou had a consort of shared virtue, and thus a sage was born. Indeed, the father initiated it and the mother assisted it—this is how Heaven ushers in a sage; is this not how King Wen came to be born? The poet traced back to the origins in order to admonish King Cheng, saying: That our Zhou received the Mandate began with King Wen—this is certain; yet how could his birth have been a matter of chance? For when a state is about to flourish, Heaven inevitably gives birth to a sage to unfold its auspicious signs at length; and when a sage is about to be born, Heaven inevitably enriches those from whom the sage is born, endowing them both with virtue. Thus, coming as a bride to the capital andCherishing a desire to please, Tai Ren's way as a wife was cultivated; and extending to King Ji, she well-nigh shared a united virtue with his discerning andcategorizing mind. Becoming a consort in Zhou and cherishing a reverent demeanor, Tai Ren's way as a mother was complete; and extending to King Ji, she well-nigh had no conduct that diverged from his compliant and harmonious ways. Now, matching virtue with virtue, the blessings of the Supreme Lord gathered and Tai Ren conceived, thereby condensing thevital energy of pure harmony; nurturing virtue with virtue, the primordial cycles converged and King Wen was born…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
焉遂以協聖作之期胎敎於未生之初言敎於
已生之後人曰任之成厥子也而自其有身之
始則乾坤清淑之英已萃之矣近以拓三分之
基遠以貽八百之緖人曰文之肇厥家也而自
其有生之時則蒼姬靈長之籙已卜之矣故有
王季必不可無文王微文則孰爲之後生文王
必不可無大任微任則孰爲之先吁於此見聖
德之自而後王可繹思矣嘗謂聖人之生天也
而其所以聖則非天也人也不有肅雍臨保則
===
天生文王亦虛矣即季任何稱焉故曰昭事上
帝聿懷多福此戒成王本指也不然述祖而第
夸其誕育之異則亦史臣之侈詞已耳何以爲
周公之詩
春秋
齊師宋師曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕春王正月
城楚丘〔僖公二年〕春諸侯城緣陵〔僖公十有四年〕
劉承芳
punctuated:
焉，遂以協聖作之期。胎敎於未生之初，言敎於已生之後，人曰任之成厥子也，而自其有身之始，則乾坤清淑之英已萃之矣；近以拓三分之基，遠以貽八百之緖，人曰文之肇厥家也，而自其有生之時，則蒼姬靈長之籙已卜之矣。故有王季必不可無文王，微文則孰爲之後？生文王必不可無大任，微任則孰爲之先？吁！於此見聖德之自，而後王可繹思矣。嘗謂聖人之生，天也；而其所以聖，則非天也，人也。不有肅雍臨保，則天生文王亦虛矣，即季、任何稱焉？故曰「昭事上帝，聿懷多福」，此戒成王本指也。不然，述祖而第夸其誕育之異，則亦史臣之侈詞已耳，何以爲周公之詩？

《春秋》
「齊師、宋師、曹師城邢」〔僖公元年〕；「春，王正月，城楚丘」〔僖公二年〕；「春，諸侯城緣陵」〔僖公十有四年〕。
劉承芳
translation_en:
… and thereby matched the appointed time for a sage to arise. With prenatal instruction before his birth and verbal instruction after he was born, people said it was Tai Ren who brought her son to completion; yet from the very moment she conceived, the pure and virtuous essence of Heaven and Earth had already gathered in him. In the near term expanding the foundation of possessing two-thirds of the realm, and in the long term bequeathing an inheritance of eight hundred years, people said it was King Wen who founded his house; yet from the very moment of his birth, the enduring mandate of the姬 (Ji) clan had already been foretold in him. Therefore, having Wang Ji, there could not but be King Wen—without Wen, who would have carried on after him? And to give birth to King Wen, there could not but be Tai Ren—without Ren, who would have preceded him? Ah! In this we see the source of sagely virtue, upon which later kings may well reflect. It has been said that the birth of a sage is due to Heaven, yet that by which he becomes a sage is due not to Heaven, but to man. Had there not been his reverent harmony in approaching and protecting the people, then Heaven's giving birth to King Wen would have been in vain, and what praise would Wang Ji and Tai Ren have had? Thus it is said: "Brightly he served the Lord on High, and so secured abundant blessings"—this is the fundamental intent in admonishing King Cheng. Otherwise, to recount one's ancestors merely by boasting of the marvels of their birth and upbringing would be nothing more than the extravagant words of court historians; how could that constitute an ode by the Duke of Zhou?

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"The army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Cao walled Xing" [First year of Duke Xi]; "In spring, in the king's first month, they walled Chuqiu" [Second year of Duke Xi]; "In spring, the feudal lords walled Yuanling" [Fourteenth year of Duke Xi].
By Liu Chengfang 劉承芳.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導王批叙三城書法得旨經義之佳者
宜錄以式
考試官敎諭湯批格嚴詞鍊
考試官敎諭王批整潔雅健
霸主專以存小春秋因事而示法焉夫善恤患
而惡專命春秋法也此三城之書詞所以異歟
齊桓之霸也存三亡國焉城邢而邢安城楚丘
而衞定城緣陵而杞無恙其事同矣春秋待之
異者何自城邢言之狄難殷而夷儀遷邢亡在
===
旦夕矣桓也即以救邢之師而城以遷之是役
也謂之有命固不可獨不曰爲天子恤庶邦乎
邢之存桓之力也故詳列三師以著其善云自
楚丘言之狄師入而漕邑處衞亡已踰年矣桓
也爰度楚丘之地而城以戍之是役也謂之無
功固不可獨不曰無有封而不告乎衞之有周
之無也故沒諸侯不書以略其功云乃緣陵則
異是矣夷勢不若狄勢之張杞禍未若衞禍之
烈若之何自遷而自城之豈其知有杞不知有
punctuated:
同考試官訓導王批：叙三城書法得旨，經義之佳者，宜錄以式。
考試官敎諭湯批：格嚴詞鍊。
考試官敎諭王批：整潔雅健。
霸主專以存小，《春秋》因事而示法焉。夫善恤患而惡專命，《春秋》法也，此三城之書詞所以異歟！齊桓之霸也，存三亡國焉：城邢而邢安，城楚丘而衞定，城緣陵而杞無恙，其事同矣。《春秋》待之異者何？自城邢言之，狄難殷而夷儀遷，邢亡在旦夕矣。桓也即以救邢之師，而城以遷之。是役也，謂之有命固不可，獨不曰爲天子恤庶邦乎？邢之存，桓之力也，故詳列三師以著其善云。自楚丘言之，狄師入而漕邑處，衞亡已踰年矣。桓也爰度楚丘之地，而城以戍之。是役也，謂之無功固不可，獨不曰「無有封而不告」乎？衞之有，周之無也，故沒諸侯不書以略其功云。乃緣陵則異是矣。夷勢不若狄勢之張，杞禍未若衞禍之烈，若之何自遷而自城之？豈其知有杞不知有
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang: In recounting the historiographical principles behind the three city-wallings, he grasps the essential meaning. An excellent exposition of the Classics, worthy of being recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang: The structure is rigorous and the diction refined.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: Neat, elegant, and vigorous.
When the hegemon acted on his own authority to preserve small states, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) used the events to demonstrate its standard of judgment. Now, to commend the relief of distress while condemning the usurpation of the royal mandate is the standard of the Spring and Autumn Annals; is this not why the wording recorded for these three city-wallings differs? In exercising his hegemony, Duke Huan of Qi preserved three perishing states: he walled Xing and Xing was made secure; he walled Chuqiu and Wei was stabilized; he walled Yuanling and Qi was kept unharmed. The deeds were the same. Why, then, did the Spring and Autumn Annals treat them differently? Speaking with regard to the walling of Xing: the disaster wrought by the Di tribes was severe, and with the relocation to Yiyi, the fall of Xing was imminent at any moment. Huan thereupon used the very armies sent to rescue Xing to wall the city and relocate them there. Of this campaign, one certainly cannot say that it had royal authorization, yet can one not say that he was relieving the myriad states on behalf of the Son of Heaven? The preservation of Xing was due to Huan's strength; therefore, the text lists the three armies in detail in order to make manifest his goodness. Speaking with regard to Chuqiu: the Di armies had invaded and the people were dwelling at the town of Cao; Wei had already been ruined for over a year. Huan then surveyed the territory of Chuqiu, walling and garrisoning it for them. Of this campaign, one certainly cannot say that it lacked merit, yet is it not said, "There shall be no enfeoffment without reporting it [to the King]"? That Wei came to exist meant that Zhou ceased to matter; therefore, the text suppresses the feudal lords and does not record them, so as to pass over his merit. As for Yuanling, however, it differed from these. The power of the Yi tribes was not as rampant as that of the Di, and the calamity of Qi was not yet as fierce as that of Wei—how could he relocate them on his own and wall a city for them on his own? Could it be that he knew only of the existence of Qi and did not know of the existence of…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
周乎此其義不同於恤患而罪差薄於專封故
凡舉諸侯而不序與城邢楚丘異者聖人固權
之審矣吁此尊王賤伯意也雖然當周之季天
下之不胥為夷狄者賴有桓公在耳讀定中木
瓜之詩則衛之德齊甚矣奈何有意督過之蓋
春秋以道義而桓以功利無論緣陵楚丘即城
邢亦不能無譏焉故聶北之次春秋譏之惡其
養亂為功也夫子大管仲之功而無道桓文之
事嗚呼其旨深矣
===
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕吳子使札來聘〔襄公二十有九年〕
梅森
同考試官訓導王批〔責穆公季札詞嚴義正深得聖人之旨〕
考試官教諭湯批〔語峻潔意委曲錄之〕
考試官教諭王批〔詞旨明確〕
春秋責備之義於賢君賢臣見之也此秦穆貳
過季札苦節皆賢者之累也春秋所以備責之
punctuated:
周乎？此其義不同於恤患，而罪差薄於專封，故凡舉諸侯而不序，與城邢、楚丘異者，聖人固權之審矣。吁！此尊王賤伯意也。雖然，當周之季，天下之不胥為夷狄者，賴有桓公在耳。讀《定中》、《木瓜》之詩，則衛之德齊甚矣，奈何有意督過之？蓋《春秋》以道義，而桓以功利，無論緣陵、楚丘，即城邢亦不能無譏焉。故聶北之次，《春秋》譏之，惡其養亂為功也。夫子大管仲之功，而無道桓、文之事，嗚呼！其旨深矣。

秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕吳子使札來聘〔襄公二十有九年〕
梅森
同考試官訓導王批〔責穆公、季札，詞嚴義正，深得聖人之旨。〕
考試官教諭湯批〔語峻潔，意委曲，錄之。〕
考試官教諭王批〔詞旨明確。〕

《春秋》責備之義，於賢君、賢臣見之也。此秦穆貳過、季札苦節，皆賢者之累也，《春秋》所以備責之
translation_en:
… Zhou? Here the principle is different from relieving distress, yet the offense is slightly lighter than usurping the authority to enfeoff; therefore, in referring to the feudal lords collectively without listing them in sequence—unlike the walling of Xing and Chuqiu—the Sage indeed weighed the matter carefully. Alas! This is the intent of honoring the King and disparaging the hegemons. Even so, during the decline of Zhou, that the realm did not sink altogether into barbarism depended solely on the presence of Duke Huan. When one reads the odes "Ding zhong" [Ding zhi fang zhong] and "Mugua," it is clear that Wei felt deeply indebted to Qi's virtue; why, then, deliberately find fault with him? It is because the Spring and Autumn Annals judges by moral principle, whereas Duke Huan acted out of utilitarian calculation; not to mention Yuanling and Chuqiu, even the walling of Xing could not escape criticism. Thus, the Spring and Autumn Annals criticized the halting of troops at Niebei, detesting that he allowed disorder to fester so as to claim credit for himself. The Master praised the achievements of Guan Zhong, yet his disciples did not speak of the affairs of Dukes Huan and Wen—alas, how profound is this meaning!

"The men of Qin attacked Jin" [Third year of Duke Wen]; "The Viscount of Wu sent Zha to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang].
By Mei Sen 梅森.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang's comment: [In faulting Duke Mu and Jizha, the diction is stern and the principle upright; it deeply grasps the intent of the Sage.]
Examiner and Instructor Tang's comment: [The language is incisive and pure, and the reasoning is nuanced; selected for inclusion.]
Examiner and Instructor Wang's comment: [The diction and purport are clear and precise.]

The principle of demanding perfection in the Spring and Autumn Annals is seen in its treatment of worthy rulers and worthy ministers. Here, Duke Mu of Qin repeating his transgression and Jizha practicing extreme abstinence are both blemishes in worthy men; is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals demands perfection of them…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
與且聖人望天下之心無窮故常人待之略而
賢人責之備吾於秦穆季札見之彼三敗未酬
穆所爲伐晉也夫秦之怨晉實深之宜得報者
經何人之耶蓋殽函敗而誓言作穆也一旦有
聲中國矣賢者不貳以蓋愆可也乃郊迎之悔
方新而武關之甲復動官郊取焉河舟焚焉人
之稱是師也謂何卒至新城圍而言始踐亦已
晩矣噫賢如穆方望其脩德以達於王事者而
顧貳過若是穆何以謝天下哉春秋特人之者
===
責之備也夷昧新立札所爲聘魯也夫札之讓
天下高之宜得予者經何名之耶蓋聞魯樂而
知功德札也一旦聲施上國矣賢者行權以達
變可也乃王季之受不從而子臧之節自附父
命去焉兄讓去焉人之稱是辭也謂何卒至刃
難發而禍亡已誰則階之噫賢如札方望其達
節以庶幾中庸者而顧苦節若此札何以謝先
公哉春秋特名之者責之備也噫書取秦誓記
取合禮春秋何過之深與蓋摭一事而節取之
punctuated: 與？且聖人望天下之心無窮，故常人待之略，而賢人責之備，吾於秦穆、季札見之。彼三敗未酬，穆所爲伐晉也。夫秦之怨，晉實深之，宜得報者，經何人之耶？蓋殽、函敗而誓言作，穆也一旦有聲中國矣。賢者不貳以蓋愆可也，乃郊迎之悔方新，而武關之甲復動；官郊取焉，河舟焚焉，人之稱是師也謂何？卒至新城圍而言始踐，亦已晩矣！噫！賢如穆，方望其脩德以達於王事者，而顧貳過若是，穆何以謝天下哉？《春秋》特人之者，責之備也。夷昧新立，札所爲聘魯也。夫札之讓，天下高之，宜得予者，經何名之耶？蓋聞魯樂而知功德，札也一旦聲施上國矣。賢者行權以達變可也，乃王季之受不從，而子臧之節自附；父命去焉，兄讓去焉，人之稱是辭也謂何？卒至刃難發而禍亡已，誰則階之？噫！賢如札，方望其達節以庶幾中庸者，而顧苦節若此，札何以謝先公哉？《春秋》特名之者，責之備也。噫！《書》取《秦誓》，《記》取合禮，《春秋》何過之深與？蓋摭一事而節取之，
translation_en:
…? Moreover, the Sage's expectations for the world are boundless; therefore he treats ordinary men with leniency, yet demands perfection from worthies. I see this in Duke Mu of Qin (Qin Mu) and Jizha.

That his three defeats had not yet been avenged was why Duke Mu attacked Jin. Now, Qin's grievance was indeed deepened by Jin, and he ought to have obtained retribution; why then does the Classic refer to him merely as "the men [of Qin]"? When he suffered defeat at Xiao and Hangu and composed his oath, Duke Mu suddenly gained renown in the Central States. For a worthy man, not repeating an error so as to cover past faults would have been proper. Yet while the remorse expressed when greeting his returning generals in the suburbs was still fresh, the armor at Wuguan was mobilized once again; Wangguan and Jiao were seized, and the boats after crossing the Yellow River were burned—what would people call this campaign? In the end, it was not until the siege of Xincheng that his sworn words were finally fulfilled, which was already too late! Alas! Of a worthy such as Duke Mu, one was just hoping that he would cultivate his virtue so as to attain to the affairs of a true king; yet instead he repeated his error like this—how could Duke Mu apologize to the world? That the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) specifically refers to him as "the men [of Qin]" is to demand perfection of him.

That Yimei had newly been enthroned was why Zha paid a court visit to Lu. Now, Zha's yielding of the throne was esteemed by the whole world, and he ought to have received praise; why then does the Classic refer to him simply by his personal name? When he heard the music of Lu andcomprehended the merits and virtues of its founders, Zha suddenly had his reputation spread throughout the upper states. For a worthy man, exercising moral discretion to adapt to changing circumstances would have been proper. Yet he did not follow the example of King Ji's acceptance of the succession, and instead attached himself to the integrity of Zizang; his father's command was cast aside, and his elder brothers' yielding was cast aside—what would people call this refusal? In the end, blades and turmoil broke out and the disasters never ceased—who then laid the steps for it? Alas! Of a worthy such as Zha, one was just hoping that he would reach balanced principle so as to approximate the Mean; yet instead he clung to bitter integrity like this—how could Zha apologize to the former dukes? That the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records him by his personal name is to demand perfection of him.

Alas! The Book of Documents (Shu) selected the "Oath of Qin" (Qin shi), and the Record of Rites (Ji) approved [Jizha] as conforming to ritual; why then does the Spring and Autumn Annals fault them so deeply? It is because when picking out a single deed and selectively approving it,…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其詞恕統全節而品隲之其法密故曰春秋聖
人之刑書也然觀黃鳥之詩穆眞少恩哉而季
札之讓猶有首陽之風焉此又不可以並論云
禮記
凡聽五刑之訟必原父子之親立君臣之
義以權之意論輕重之序慎測淺深之
量以別之悉其聰明致其忠愛以盡之
疑獄汎與衆共之衆疑赦之必察小大
之比以成之
===
樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批聽訟之權發揮明盡末歸於議
緩尤得欽恤之意
考試官教諭王批婉曲詳明可為司平龜鑑
王制言司理者必詳其聽而後成焉夫聽訟將
以成獄也聽之詳斯成之當矣焉往非公哉記
王制者有曰聖人貴無訟也訟而聽焉非其心
矣矧可弗公乎是故五刑之訟親與義其大矣
而輕重而淺深而法比非訟者所能自明也五
punctuated:
其詞恕；統全節而品隲之，其法密。故曰：《春秋》，聖人之刑書也。然觀《黃鳥》之詩，穆眞少恩哉！而季札之讓，猶有首陽之風焉，此又不可以並論云。

《禮記》
「凡聽五刑之訟，必原父子之親，立君臣之義，以權之；意論輕重之序，慎測淺深之量，以別之；悉其聰明，致其忠愛，以盡之；疑獄，汎與衆共之，衆疑，赦之；必察小大之比，以成之。」

樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批：聽訟之權，發揮明盡，末歸於議緩，尤得欽恤之意。
考試官教諭王批：婉曲詳明，可為司平龜鑑。

《王制》言司理者，必詳其聽而後成焉。夫聽訟將以成獄也，聽之詳，斯成之當矣，焉往非公哉？記《王制》者有曰：聖人貴無訟也。訟而聽焉，非其心矣，矧可弗公乎？是故五刑之訟，親與義其大矣；而輕重、而淺深、而法比，非訟者所能自明也。五
translation_en:
…its words are forgiving; when it encompasses a person's entire conduct to evaluate and rank them, its standards are strict. Therefore it is said: the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) is the penal code of the Sage. Yet when we look at the ode "Yellow Birds" (Huangniao), Duke Mu was truly lacking in grace! Whereas Ji Zha's yielding still carried the air of Mount Shouyang; in this respect, the two cannot be discussed in the same breath.

Record of Rites (Liji):
"In hearing any litigation involving the five punishments, one must trace the affection between father and son and establish the duty between ruler and minister in order to weigh it; thoughtfully consider the sequence of light and heavy offenses and carefully gauge the measure of shallow and deep intent in order to distinguish it; exhaust one's intelligence and perception and extend one's utmost loyalty and loving-kindness in order to get to the bottom of it; in doubtful cases, deliberate broadly with the multitude, and if the multitude is in doubt, pardon the offender; and one must examine the analogies of small and great cases in order to bring the judgment to completion."

Fan Yuheng 樊玉衡
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang: The weighing of judicial hearings is expounded with thorough clarity, and the conclusion turns toward deliberating leniency, which especially captures the spirit of reverent compassion in punishment.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: Nuanced, thorough, and clear; it can serve as a mirror and touchstone for those who administer justice.

The "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi) states that those who administer justice must be thorough in their hearing of a case before bringing the judgment to completion. Now, the purpose of hearing litigation is to conclude a case; only when the hearing is thorough will the conclusion be fitting—and how then could it ever fail to be impartial? The author who recorded the "Royal Regulations" had this to say: What the Sage values is the absence of litigation. Once litigation arises and must be heard, it is already contrary to his wishes—how much less, then, could he fail to be impartial? Therefore, in litigation involving the five punishments, affection and duty are of the greatest moment; yet the degrees of light and heavy, the measures of shallow and deep, and the legal analogies are not things that the litigants can clarify for themselves. In the five…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
刑之聽赦與成其要矣而權之而別之而盡之
皆聽者所當致詳也故其始也原親於父子明
有恩也立義於君臣明有分也法常持於一定
用自妙於無方權其容巳乎然輕重無序淺深
無量未可也則論之以意而測之以慎務區別
而不爽者別此權也然論有遺究測有遁情未
可也又聰明是悉而忠愛是致求畢盡而無遺
者盡此權也於此而猶有疑赦可議矣敢任獨
見乎必汜稽於眾而輿論之皆同斯從而赦焉
===
刑無故縱也巳至是而無可疑獄斯成矣敢行
巳意乎必附比於法而小大之咸當斯從而成
焉刑無故入也巳自權以至於察而上無頗刑
由聽以至於成而下鮮濫獄古之公於蔽訟類
若此甞觀易言治獄者五而獨有取於巽與兌
也兌主其議巽主其緩議之以資吾斷緩之以
行吾仁中孚所爲取象蓋居然法銓也司刑者
毋好深文毋幸速成而服膺兌巽之訓幾矣哉
故樂也者動於內者也禮也者動於外者
punctuated:
刑之聽，赦與成其要矣。而權之、而別之、而盡之，皆聽者所當致詳也。故其始也，原親於父子，明有恩也；立義於君臣，明有分也。法常持於一定，用自妙於無方，權其容巳乎？然輕重無序，淺深無量，未可也。則論之以意而測之以慎，務區別而不爽者，別此權也。然論有遺究，測有遁情，未可也。又聰明是悉而忠愛是致，求畢盡而無遺者，盡此權也。於此而猶有疑，赦可議矣。敢任獨見乎？必汜稽於眾，而輿論之皆同，斯從而赦焉，刑無故縱也巳。至是而無可疑，獄斯成矣。敢行巳意乎？必附比於法，而小大之咸當，斯從而成焉，刑無故入也巳。自權以至於察，而上無頗刑；由聽以至於成，而下鮮濫獄。古之公於蔽訟，類若此。甞觀《易》言治獄者五，而獨有取於《巽》與《兌》也。《兌》主其議，《巽》主其緩；議之以資吾斷，緩之以行吾仁。《中孚》所爲取象，蓋居然法銓也。司刑者毋好深文，毋幸速成，而服膺《兌》《巽》之訓，幾矣哉！

「故樂也者，動於內者也；禮也者，動於外者…
translation_en:
…As for hearing cases of the Five Punishments, pardoning and finalizing the verdict are the essentials. Yet weighing them, distinguishing them, and exhausting them are all matters to which the one hearing the case ought to devote detailed care. Therefore, at the outset, one traces kinship in the relation of father and son, making clear that grace exists; one establishes righteousness in the relation of ruler and minister, making clear that allotted duty exists. While the law is constantly upheld as something fixed, its application is naturally subtle and unconstrained by a single method—how could weighing the circumstances be dispensed with? Yet if light and heavy have no order, and shallow and deep have no measure, that will not do. Thus, evaluating them through intent and fathoming them with caution, striving to differentiate them without error—this is distinguishing what has been weighed. Yet if evaluation leaves investigations incomplete, or fathoming allows the true circumstances to escape, that will not do. Furthermore, fully employing one's acute perception and extending one's loyalty and compassion, seeking to exhaust everything without omission—this is exhausting what has been weighed. If at this point there is still doubt, a pardon may be deliberated. Would one dare rely on a solitary view? One must broadly consult the multitude, and only when public opinion is in complete agreement does one accordingly pardon the offender; thus punishments are never remitted capriciously. When it reaches the point where there is no longer any doubt, the case is then finalized. Would one dare act on one's personal whim? One must attach precedents to the law, and only when matters great and small are all suitably matched does one accordingly finalize the verdict; thus punishments are never inflicted capriciously. From weighing circumstances to investigating details, those above impose no biased punishments; from hearing cases to finalizing verdicts, those below suffer few excessive incarcerations. The impartiality of the ancients in deciding lawsuits was generally like this. I have observed that the Book of Changes (Yi) speaks of adjudicating legal cases in five hexagrams, yet takes its model uniquely from Xun (Gentle Penetration) and Dui (Joyousness). Dui governs deliberation, while Xun governs leniency and delay; one deliberates over cases to aid one's judgment, and delays them to practice one's benevolence. The images adopted by the hexagram Zhongfu (Inner Trust) indeed serve as an evident touchstone of the law. If those in charge of punishments do not delight in harsh and鍛煉 [?] legalities, do not seek hasty conclusions, and instead take to heart the teachings of Dui and Xun, they will be near the mark indeed!

"Therefore, music is that which stirs within; ritual is that which stirs without…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也樂極和禮極順
王一鳴
考試官教諭湯批禮樂身心本爲一道是作探原
發奥殆造詣之深者
考試官教諭王批渾融精切絕無枝蔓
記者原禮樂所由動而各舉其妙焉夫禮樂以
和順爲本也隨所動而會其極治身心者惡能
去之且禮樂身心一道也夫人恒岐而二之此
功之或間而極未臻耳豈知樂之能治心非心
本無樂而以樂治也蓋樂由中出而鐘鼓干戚
特緣物以寄吾心耳故樂非動於聲容者乃未
有聲容之先而此心之和動即樂也動於內者
也禮之能治躬非身本無禮而以禮治也蓋禮
由身體而周旋裼襲特假物以彰吾軌耳故禮
非動於器數者乃未有器數之先而此身之順
動即禮也動於外者也夫樂動於內故宜治心
心苟斯須間焉猶難語和況和之極哉致樂而
至於安久天神是舉其動於內者而渾化之一
punctuated:
也。樂極和，禮極順。」

王一鳴

考試官教諭湯批：禮樂身心，本爲一道。是作探原發奥，殆造詣之深者。

考試官教諭王批：渾融精切，絕無枝蔓。

記者原禮樂所由動，而各舉其妙焉。夫禮樂以和順爲本也，隨所動而會其極，治身心者惡能去之？且禮樂身心，一道也；夫人恒岐而二之，此功之或間，而極未臻耳。豈知樂之能治心，非心本無樂而以樂治也。蓋樂由中出，而鐘鼓干戚，特緣物以寄吾心耳。故樂非動於聲容者，乃未有聲容之先，而此心之和動即樂也，動於內者也。禮之能治躬，非身本無禮而以禮治也。蓋禮由身體，而周旋裼襲，特假物以彰吾軌耳。故禮非動於器數者，乃未有器數之先，而此身之順動即禮也，動於外者也。夫樂動於內，故宜治心。心苟斯須間焉，猶難語和，況和之極哉？致樂而至於安久天神，是舉其動於內者而渾化之，一
translation_en:
… [Music is that which moves within; ritual is that which moves without.] Music reaches the ultimate of harmony, and ritual reaches the ultimate of compliance."

Wang Yiming 王一鳴

Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: Ritual and music, body and mind, are fundamentally a single Way. This composition probes the origin and uncovers the profundities; it is surely the work of someone of deep attainment.

Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Seamlessly integrated, precise, and incisive, with no superfluous branches or tendrils whatsoever.

The chronicler traces the origins from which ritual and music move, and sets forth the subtle perfection of each. Now, ritual and music take harmony and compliance as their root. Following wherever they move and bringing them to their ultimate convergence—how could one who governs body and mind ever dispense with them? Moreover, ritual and music, body and mind, are a single Way. Yet people constantly bifurcate them into two; this is merely why their effort is at times interrupted and the ultimate is not reached. How could they fail to know that music's ability to govern the mind is not because the mind originally lacks music and is governed by means of music? For music issues from within, whereas bells, drums, shields, and battle-axes merely rely on external things to lodge our mind. Therefore, music is not something moved by sounds and appearances; rather, prior to the existence of sounds and appearances, the harmonious movement of this mind is itself music—it is that which moves within. Ritual's ability to govern the person is not because the body originally lacks ritual and is governed by means of ritual. For ritual is embodied by the person, whereas turning and circling, baring the upper garment or covering it, merely borrow external things to manifest our standard. Therefore, ritual is not something moved by ritual vessels and numbers; rather, prior to the existence of vessels and numbers, the compliant movement of this body is itself ritual—it is that which moves without. Now, because music moves within, it is fitting for governing the mind. If the mind has even a moment's interruption, it is still difficult to speak of harmony, how much more so the ultimate of harmony? To carry music to the point of repose, endurance, the Heavenly, and the spiritual is to take all that moves within and fuse it into a seamless transformation; within a single…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
心之中無動非樂卽無動非和也非極和耶禮
動於外故宜治身身苟斯須間焉猶難語順況
順之極哉致禮而至於莊敬威嚴是舉其動於
外者而嘉會之一身之中無動非禮卽無動非
順也非極順耶吁此感人動物之基也抑樂在
心而求之秬黍禮在身而求之綿蕞迹耳舍迹
而求其眞則身心一動和順自充由是官天地
育萬物皆此之推耳故君子反觀於寂然不動
之天而禮樂固森然具也所謂斯須不可去者
===
存吾眞也
第貳場
論
天子以好生爲德
瞿甲
同考試官訓導趙批
好生二字乃人君聯屬人心培植國脉之本是篇以剴切之意命雋偉之詞是雅抱忠悃者
同考試官教諭尹批 學識淵深文藻典雅
考試官教諭湯批 發好生意明盡
punctuated:
心之中，無動非樂，卽無動非和也，非極和耶？禮動於外，故宜治身。身苟斯須間焉，猶難語順，況順之極哉？致禮而至於莊敬威嚴，是舉其動於外者，而嘉會之一身之中，無動非禮，卽無動非順也，非極順耶？吁！此感人動物之基也。抑樂在心而求之秬黍，禮在身而求之綿蕞，迹耳。舍迹而求其眞，則身心一動，和順自充，由是官天地、育萬物，皆此之推耳。故君子反觀於寂然不動之天，而禮樂固森然具也。所謂斯須不可去者，存吾眞也。

第貳場

論

天子以好生爲德

瞿甲
同考試官訓導趙批：好生二字，乃人君聯屬人心、培植國脉之本。是篇以剴切之意，命雋偉之詞，是雅抱忠悃者。
同考試官教諭尹批：學識淵深，文藻典雅。
考試官教諭湯批：發好生意明盡。
translation_en:
… within a single mind, where no movement is not music, and thus no movement is not harmony—is this not the utmost harmony? Ritual moves externally, and therefore is suited to governing the body. If the body is interrupted for even an instant, it is difficult even to speak of compliance, much less the utmost compliance! To carry ritual to its limit until one reaches solemnity, reverence, majesty, and dignity is to take all that moves externally and bring it into auspicious convergence within a single body, where no movement is not ritual, and thus no movement is not compliance—is this not the utmost compliance? Ah! This is the foundation for moving people and stirring creatures. Yet if music lies in the mind and one seeks it in black-millet pitch-measures, or if ritual lies in the body and one seeks it in roped-off thatch markers, these are merely outward traces. If one sets aside the traces and seeks their reality, then as soon as mind and body stir, harmony and compliance naturally fill them; from this, presiding over Heaven and Earth and nurturing the myriad things are all simply extensions of this. Therefore, the gentleman turns his contemplation inward upon the tranquil, unmoving realm of Heaven, and ritual and music are indeed already arrayed there in full. What is meant by "not leaving them for an instant" is preserving our true nature.

Second Session

Discourse

"The Virtue of the Son of Heaven Is the Love of Life"

Qu Jia (瞿甲)
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao: The words "love of life" are the foundation by which a ruler binds together human hearts and nurtures the lifeblood of the state. This essay conveys earnest ideas in striking, grand phrasing; its author is one who has long cherished loyal sincerity.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yin: Deep in learning and insight, classic and refined in literary style.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang: Brings out the meaning of "love of life" with complete clarity.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭王批深得先王制刑本意
人主宰世以代天也必求全其天之所生而後
可夫民之生也天生之天能生民而不能使之
全其生乃舉而屬之人主以治之故四海八埏
奉曰天子天子一心仁庇億兆爲生生之本則
曰天君然而師心焉治終難以諧無厭之欲一
喜爭之志於是倚智而甞姦緣巧而搆釁者叢
纍釁起殆非所以齊衆濟治也不得已而設之
曰天刑而後世藉之以播其酷烈屠其生齒則
===
恣睢之法勝而矜全之意微矣聖人伏而思之
天下何尊何親也檢於刑故人相尊麗於仁故
人相親而奈何以區區督責之術收威於衆乎
是故解苛密之網流愷悌之聲弘欽恤之指副
樹牧之任而天下始鮮有伐生者嗚呼以好生
爲德斯可以爲天子矣甞遡觀皇王之時其動
也習其服也士刻畫衣冠而天下化君子有禮
樂之容野人脩曾史之行結繩亦治象刑亦治
衆庶尊生靡有刑憲刑者所以鋤梗馭宄明飭
punctuated:
考試官敎諭王批：深得先王制刑本意。

人主宰世以代天也，必求全其天之所生而後可。夫民之生也，天生之；天能生民，而不能使之全其生，乃舉而屬之人主以治之。故四海八埏，奉曰「天子」；天子一心，仁庇億兆，爲生生之本，則曰「天君」。然而師心焉治，終難以諧無厭之欲、一喜爭之志。於是倚智而甞姦、緣巧而搆釁者，叢纍釁起，殆非所以齊衆濟治也。不得已而設之，曰「天刑」。而後世藉之以播其酷烈，屠其生齒，則恣睢之法勝，而矜全之意微矣。聖人伏而思之，天下何尊何親也？檢於刑，故人相尊；麗於仁，故人相親。而奈何以區區督責之術，收威於衆乎？是故解苛密之網，流愷悌之聲，弘欽恤之指，副樹牧之任，而天下始鮮有伐生者。嗚呼！以好生爲德，斯可以爲天子矣。

甞遡觀皇王之時，其動也習，其服也士，刻畫衣冠而天下化。君子有禮樂之容，野人脩曾、史之行，結繩亦治，象刑亦治，衆庶尊生，靡有刑憲。刑者，所以鋤梗馭宄，明飭
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: Deeply grasps the fundamental intent behind the Former Kings' establishment of punishments.

A ruler governs the world on behalf of Heaven; only when he seeks to preserve in full what Heaven has given life to is his rule acceptable. Now, as for the life of the people, Heaven gives birth to them. Yet while Heaven can give birth to the people, it cannot cause them to preserve their lives intact, and so it takes them all and entrusts them to the ruler of men to govern. Therefore, throughout the Four Seas and Eight Frontiers, he is revered as the "Son of Heaven"; and when the Son of Heaven, with a single mind, benevolently shelters the myriad millions and serves as the foundation of ceaseless generation, he is called the "Heavenly Sovereign." Even so, if he relies solely on his own heart to govern, it remains ultimately difficult to harmonize insatiable desires or unify contentious wills. Consequently, those who rely on cunning to test out villainy and seize upon artifice to stir up strife arise in tangled multitudes—which is scarcely the way to bring order to the masses and achieve good governance. Only out of necessity were punishments established, and they were called "Heavenly Punishments." Yet later ages used them as a pretext to spread harshness and cruelty and to slaughter the living populace; thus arbitrary and ruthless laws prevailed, while the intent to pity and preserve grew faint. The sages bowed their heads and reflected upon this: Why do the people of the world show respect, and why do they feel affection? Restrained by punishments, people respect one another; attached to benevolence, people feel affection for one another. Why, then, resort to petty techniques of supervision and reproach in order to exact awe from the multitude? Therefore, when one loosens the harsh and closely woven net of the law, spreads abroad a reputation for genial kindness, expands the principle of reverent compassion in sentencing, and fulfills the duty of establishing pastors for the people, only then will there rarely be those in the world who cut short their own lives. Alas! Only when he takes the love of life as his virtue can he truly be the Son of Heaven.

If we look back to the times of the August Ones and the Sovereigns, in their movements people were compliant, and in their submission they were gentlemanly [?]; merely by delineating symbolic caps and robes, the whole world was transformed. Gentlemen possessed the demeanor of ritual and music, while rustic folk cultivated the conduct of Zeng Shen and Shi Qiu; governance was achieved with knotted cords, and governance was likewise achieved with symbolic punishments. The multitude honored life, and there were no penal codes. Punishments are the means to weed out the obstinate, curb traitors, and clearly enforce…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國章也非以讎匹夫濟虓怒也中孚之象澤上
有風君子以議獄緩死夫水體虛故風能入之
心體虛故物能感之感於中而仁生焉是議獄
緩死之心非卽好生之心哉心存而德不踰矣
世主不曉競於煩苛之令搖於鍥薄之風囹圄
如市桎梏若林而有司奉上意指復深文巧詆
以塗民耳目而不知繁策急轡終不可語造父
之御也嚴刑促令終不可語三王之道也德何
以稱哉夫民之爭非其好也其所由來漸矣激
===
之則淫敦之則一激之也者動其爭機敦之也
者篤其古初則王者齊民豈堇堇在法制哉視
其所以激之敦之者耳故夏之肉辟殷之虔劉
鄭之刑書晉之執秩趙之國律楚之僕區法銓
愈備姦偽滋萌庸非任刑之過與任刑而至於
過皆人主欣嗜誅夷而無復以生為好故其下
麇附而景從也天生民而屬之人主欲生之耶
欲刑之耶人主不得已而用刑欲生之耶欲死
之耶夫介鯁之士以彊直加木羸窶之徒以單
punctuated: 國章也，非以讎匹夫、濟虓怒也。《中孚》之《象》：「澤上有風，君子以議獄緩死。」夫水體虛，故風能入之；心體虛，故物能感之。感於中而仁生焉，是議獄緩死之心，非卽好生之心哉？心存而德不踰矣。世主不曉，競於煩苛之令，搖於鍥薄之風，囹圄如市，桎梏若林。而有司奉上意指，復深文巧詆，以塗民耳目。而不知繁策急轡，終不可語造父之御也；嚴刑促令，終不可語三王之道也。德何以稱哉？夫民之爭，非其好也，其所由來漸矣。激之則淫，敦之則一。激之也者，動其爭機；敦之也者，篤其古初。則王者齊民，豈堇堇在法制哉？視其所以激之、敦之者耳。故夏之肉辟、殷之虔劉、鄭之刑書、晉之執秩、趙之國律、楚之僕區，法銓愈備，姦偽滋萌，庸非任刑之過與？任刑而至於過，皆人主欣嗜誅夷，而無復以生為好，故其下麇附而景從也。天生民而屬之人主，欲生之耶？欲刑之耶？人主不得已而用刑，欲生之耶？欲死之耶？夫介鯁之士以彊直加木，羸窶之徒以單
translation_en:
… statutes of the state; they are not for taking vengeance upon commoners or indulging a roaring rage. The Image commentary on the hexagram Zhongfu (Inner Trust) states: "Above the lake there is wind: thus the noble man deliberates over legal cases and delays executions." Now, the substance of water is receptive, and therefore the wind can enter it; the substance of the mind is receptive, and therefore things can move it. When moved within, benevolence is born therein. Is not this mind that deliberates over legal cases and delays executions precisely the mind that loves life? When this mind is preserved, virtue is never transgressed.

Rulers of the age do not understand this. They vie in issuing烦瑣 and harsh ordinances and are swayed by a climate of callous meanness, until prisons are as crowded as marketplaces and fetters stand thick as forests. Meanwhile, the authorities, carrying out the intentions of their superiors, further apply harsh interpretations of the law and craftily slander the accused so as to stop up the ears and eyes of the people. Yet they do not realize that with incessant whipping and a tight rein, one can never speak of the charioteering of Zaofu; with severe punishments and urgent decrees, one can never speak of the Way of the Three Kings. How then can virtue be praised?

Now, when the people contend with one another, it is not because they are fond of doing so; its origins develop gradually. If you provoke them, they become licentious; if you cultivate thickness of character in them, they become unified. To provoke them is to stir up their impulse for contention; to cultivate thickness of character in them is to reinforce their ancient, primal nature. In regulating the people, how could a true king rely merely on legal institutions? It depends solely on that by which he provokes or cultivates them. Therefore, with the corporal punishments of the Xia, the ruthless slaughter of the Yin, the Books of Punishments (Xingshu) of Zheng, the Laws on Offices (Zhizhi) of Jin, the State Statutes (Guolü) of Zhao, and the Law on Concealment (Puqu) of Chu—the more exhaustive the legal scales became, the more treachery and deceit sprouted forth. Was this not the fault of relying on punishments? When reliance on punishments reaches the point of excess, it is always because the ruler delights in execution and extermination and no longer holds a love for life; hence his subordinates flock to him like deer and follow him like shadows.

When Heaven gives birth to the people and entrusts them to a ruler, does It wish to keep them alive, or does It wish to punish them? When a ruler has no choice but to use punishments, does he wish to keep them alive, or does he wish to put them to death? Upright and unyielding scholars are placed in the cangue and stocks for their unbending rectitude; weak and impoverished folk, with their solitary…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
力寡控侗愿之衆以訥辨橫誣少年之子以孱
弱伏辜畜憤之夫以激昂賈罪膏粱之俊以遊
冶蒙辱豈其皆敢於弄法習於爲姦者而一切
寘之不原之典委命下吏情斷意訖目矚廷尉
愕若鬼魑身受黥掠痛甚湯火血流兩觀之下
聲徹九閽之闕嗟嗟是亦重可哀矣哀之則必
有以生之矣先王之令烏無覆巢蟲無殺孩骼
則掩之胔則埋之乃至刑刈百姓竟若草菅則
視胞與賤於羽毛而戴髮含齒之倫不如一道
===
路朽枯之白骨德何衰也故仲尼譏鑄鼎端木
惡猛法要以明人主之所好在此不在彼耳夫
生者萬民系命之原也書稱其德好生易稱觀
我生觀民謂天子而可不好生哉是以古昔聽
民具以兩造詳以三刺孚以五辭俟以歷旬如
此乎矜其生也原以三宥寛以八議參以衆疑
設以二石贖以千鍰如此乎求其生也獄旣成
爲之覆奏爲之籲天爲之垂泣爲之不舉樂不
視朝者凡三日如此乎重其生也故世有鉗灼
punctuated: 力寡控，侗愿之衆以訥辨橫誣，少年之子以孱弱伏辜，畜憤之夫以激昂賈罪，膏粱之俊以遊冶蒙辱。豈其皆敢於弄法、習於爲姦者，而一切寘之不原之典，委命下吏？情斷意訖，目矚廷尉，愕若鬼魑；身受黥掠，痛甚湯火。血流兩觀之下，聲徹九閽之闕。嗟嗟！是亦重可哀矣！哀之則必有以生之矣。先王之令，烏無覆巢，蟲無殺孩，骼則掩之，胔則埋之。乃至刑刈百姓，竟若草菅，則視胞與賤於羽毛，而戴髮含齒之倫，不如一道路朽枯之白骨，德何衰也！故仲尼譏鑄鼎，端木惡猛法，要以明人主之所好在此不在彼耳。夫生者，萬民系命之原也。《書》稱其德好生，《易》稱「觀我生，觀民」，謂天子而可不好生哉？是以古昔聽民，具以兩造，詳以三刺，孚以五辭，俟以歷旬，如此乎矜其生也；原以三宥，寛以八議，參以衆疑，設以二石，贖以千鍰，如此乎求其生也；獄旣成，爲之覆奏，爲之籲天，爲之垂泣，爲之不舉樂、不視朝者凡三日，如此乎重其生也。故世有鉗灼
translation_en: … strength lack means of appeal; the simple and honest multitude are falsely accused because they are slow of speech; youthful sons confess to crimes out of frailty and weakness; men harboring indignation incur guilt through impassioned outbursts; and the scions of wealthy families suffer disgrace from dissolute roaming. How could all of these be people who dare to toy with the law or are habituated to committing wickedness? Yet all alike are subjected to unforgiving statutes, their lives entrusted to petty functionaries! With hope cut off and spirit exhausted, they gaze upon the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement (Tingwei) in terror as though facing ghosts and demons; their bodies suffer tattooing and flogging, a pain worse than boiling water or fire. Their blood flows beneath the Twin Watchtowers, and their cries pierce the nine gates of the palace. Alas! This is truly most pitiable! And if one pities them, one must surely find a way to preserve their lives. According to the ordinances of the former kings, birds' nests were not to be overturned, larval insects were not to be killed, dry bones were to be covered, and decaying flesh was to be buried. When it comes instead to punishing and mowing down the common people as though they were mere grass and reeds, then one regards one's fellow human beings as cheaper than feathers and fur, and the race of those who wear hair and have teeth is treated worse than withered white bones by the roadside—how greatly has virtue declined! Therefore Zhongni [Confucius] criticized the casting of the tripods, and Duanmu [Zigong] despised harsh laws; the essential point was to make clear that what the ruler cherishes lies here and not there. Now life is the fundamental source upon which the myriad people depend for their existence. The Book of Documents (Shu) praises the virtue that loves life, and the Book of Changes (Yi) says, "Contemplating my own life, I contemplate the people." Could one be the Son of Heaven and yet not love life? For this reason, in antiquity when hearing cases among the people, they required both parties to appear, examined them carefully through the three inquiries, verified the truth through the five modes of observing testimony, and waited ten days before deciding—such was their compassion for human life! They pardoned them through the three grounds of leniency, showed clemency through the eight deliberations, consulted the multitude when in doubt, set up the two stones [lapis and lungstone] for redress, and allowed redemption with a thousand huan of bronze—such was their effort to seek a way for them to live! Once a capital sentence was determined, on their behalf memorials were submitted repeatedly, Heaven was called upon, tears were shed, and for three days music was not performed and court was not held—such was the weight they attached to human life! Thus, though the world may have a fondness for shackling and branding …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之好而天子則曰寧䖘法以毋殘其生世有窮
竟之好而天子則曰寧解嬈以毋傾其生世有
傅致之好而天子則曰寧文無害以毋傷其生
世有攈摭深故之好而天子則曰寧開改惡之
路以毋錮其生夫聖人所爲鰓鰓愍惻而不忍
言刑者好生故也攷之天官曰天西方句圜十
五星曰貫索曰天獄獄口星曰闢以示開也獄
事煩多則衆星畢見明王恥之此可以觀天心
矣夫天道先燠而後寒先舒而後慘其所好不
===
旣彰彰著耶人君心天之心則亦好天之好故
草纓艾韠稱爲上業不得已而罹於議則猶誨
之以忠聳之以行敎之以務使之以和又不得
已而干於法則又求明察之官忠信之長慈惠
之師以明聽之豈其好爲姑息以博敦大之名
哉天心好生人君爲天之子亦好其天之所生
者巳耳嗚呼纍臣繫而夏隕霜令史殲而血逆
流天人感應之理若此況於逞燔灼之毒震𩆝
貫之威張虎狼之噬峻鷹鸇之擊驅可矜之人
punctuated: 之好，而天子則曰：「寧䖘法以毋殘其生。」世有窮竟之好，而天子則曰：「寧解嬈以毋傾其生。」世有傅致之好，而天子則曰：「寧文無害以毋傷其生。」世有攈摭深故之好，而天子則曰：「寧開改惡之路以毋錮其生。」夫聖人所爲鰓鰓愍惻而不忍言刑者，好生故也。攷之《天官》，曰：「天西方句圜十五星，曰貫索，曰天獄。獄口星曰闢，以示開也。獄事煩多，則衆星畢見，明王恥之。」此可以觀天心矣。夫天道先燠而後寒，先舒而後慘，其所好不旣彰彰著耶？人君心天之心，則亦好天之好。故草纓艾韠，稱爲上業；不得已而罹於議，則猶誨之以忠，聳之以行，敎之以務，使之以和；又不得已而干於法，則又求明察之官、忠信之長、慈惠之師以明聽之。豈其好爲姑息，以博敦大之名哉？天心好生，人君爲天之子，亦好其天之所生者巳耳。嗚呼！纍臣繫而夏隕霜，令史殲而血逆流，天人感應之理若此。況於逞燔灼之毒，震𩆝貫之威，張虎狼之噬，峻鷹鸇之擊，驅可矜之人、
translation_en:
… [When the world has a fondness for collar-irons and branding,] the Son of Heaven says: "Better to bend the law [?] than to mutilate their lives." When the world has a fondness for pursuing cases to the bitter end, the Son of Heaven says: "Better to untangle vexations than to overturn their lives." When the world has a fondness for forcing confessions and fabricating charges, the Son of Heaven says: "Better that legal statutes cause no harm than to injure their lives." When the world has a fondness for nitpicking and harsh intentionality, the Son of Heaven says: "Better to open a path for reforming evil than to fetter their lives." Indeed, the reason the sages were so anxiously compassionate and could not bear to speak of punishments is because they loved life.

Examining the Treatise on Celestial Offices (Tianguan), it says: "In the western sky there is a hooked circle of fifteen stars called the Coiled Thong (Guansuo), also called the Celestial Prison (Tianyu). The star at the mouth of the prison is called Opening, to show that it should stand open. When prison affairs are numerous and burdensome, all the stars become fully visible, and an enlightened king considers this a disgrace." From this one may observe the mind of Heaven. Now, the Way of Heaven puts warmth first and cold afterward, relaxation first and severity afterward—is not what it loves already abundantly clear? The ruler of men takes the mind of Heaven as his own mind, and thus loves what Heaven loves. Therefore, symbolic punishments such as straw hat-ribbons and pale green knee-covers were praised as the highest achievement of governance. When there was no alternative and people fell under deliberation for offenses, the ruler still instructed them in loyalty, roused them through conduct, taught them their duties, and employed them with harmony. And when there was still no alternative and they violated the law, he further sought out clear-sighted and discerning officials, loyal and trustworthy elders, and compassionate and benevolent teachers to hear their cases with clarity. Was this because he was fond of laxity in order to win a reputation for generous magnanimity? Heaven's mind loves life; the ruler of men, being the Son of Heaven, simply loves those whom Heaven has brought into life.

Alas! When the fettered minister [Zou Yan] was imprisoned, frost fell in summer; when the Clerk [Make-up/Subordinate Official] was executed, blood flowed backward. Such is the principle of resonance between Heaven and man. How much more so when officials unleash the poison of burning and branding, brandish the terror of thunderous [?] stringing-up, spread the devouring jaws of tigers and wolves, sharpen the strikes of hawks and falcons, and drive pitiable people…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
陷必死之穽雖國士有不勝其酷而自誣者此
則苛密擬於吹毛操切等於束濕圜扉夜哭棘
林晝嘯戾氣蒸而不散陰霾鬱而不解三光震
動二曜薄蝕其所關豈細故哉虞舜著典眚災
肆赦禹巡會稽遇罪流泣姬公作戒勿誤庶獄
伯夷折民惟刑惟敬武丁明罰不敢怠遑之數
君者皆審慎遲留而不敢專決乃其中固自有
所好耳當時之政穆於春風暄於冬日五刑式
序萬品畢設厥德顧不懋哉若晚近世墨劓剕
割之制鑿頂文額拆脅之條一切不係咎繇所
設呂侯所記則皆所以欿君德而干天和者也
胡可好也是故夏以刑顛秦以慘裂非殃及一
身則孽流數世其理彰灼而不爽而况人主撫
齊萬方一歲中擊斷無數少逞雷霆之威重以
摧折之勢則其隕越生人取讎造物者何可勝
計此削木畫地之議所以諄復於綜核之朝也
戒之哉雖然刑之立也所以生人故郭璞氏謂
重之以死者正所以求其生而罰輕則民易犯
punctuated: 陷必死之穽，雖國士有不勝其酷而自誣者。此則苛密擬於吹毛，操切等於束濕；圜扉夜哭，棘林晝嘯，戾氣蒸而不散，陰霾鬱而不解，三光震動，二曜薄蝕，其所關豈細故哉！虞舜著典，眚災肆赦；禹巡會稽，遇罪流泣；姬公作戒，勿誤庶獄；伯夷折民，惟刑惟敬；武丁明罰，不敢怠遑。之數君者，皆審慎遲留而不敢專決，乃其中固自有所好耳。當時之政，穆於春風，暄於冬日，五刑式序，萬品畢設，厥德顧不懋哉！若晚近世，墨、劓、剕、割之制，鑿頂、文額、拆脅之條，一切不係咎繇所設、呂侯所記，則皆所以欿君德而干天和者也，胡可好也？是故夏以刑顛，秦以慘裂，非殃及一身，則孽流數世，其理彰灼而不爽。而况人主撫齊萬方，一歲中擊斷無數，少逞雷霆之威，重以摧折之勢，則其隕越生人、取讎造物者，何可勝計！此削木畫地之議，所以諄復於綜核之朝也，戒之哉！雖然，刑之立也，所以生人。故郭璞氏謂重之以死者，正所以求其生，而罰輕則民易犯，
translation_en: …plunging them into pits of certain death, so that even worthy gentlemen of the state cannot bear the cruelty and falsely incriminate themselves. In such cases, the harshness and minuteness of the law are like blowing apart hairs to seek blemishes, and its urgent severity is like tying up wet firewood. In the round-door prisons there is weeping at night; in the thorn-forest courts there is wailing by day. Perverse qi steams upward without dispersing; dark gloom accumulates without clearing. The three luminaries—sun, moon, and stars—quake, and the sun and moon suffer eclipses. How could what is at stake here be a trifling matter! When Yu Shun 虞舜 set forth his canons, offenses of inadvertence and misfortune were pardoned; when Yu 禹 toured Kuaiji 會稽, he wept upon encountering criminals; when the Duke of Zhou (Jigong 姬公) composed his admonitions, he warned against mishandling the multitude of judicial cases; when Boyi 伯夷 restrained the people through punishments, he urged reverence in penal matters; when Wuding 武丁 clarified punishments, he dared not be indolent or remiss. All these several rulers were circumspect and deliberative, not daring to make arbitrary decisions, because within their hearts they naturally had what they cherished—human life. The governance of those times was gentler than the spring breeze and warmer than the winter sun; the Five Punishments were properly ordered, all things were fully arranged, and how great indeed was their virtue! As for later ages, the systems of tattooing, nose-cutting, foot-amputation, and castration, and the statutes for boring the crown of the head, branding the forehead, and breaking the ribs—none of which belonged to what Gaoyao 咎繇 established or what the Marquis of Lü (Lühou 呂侯) recorded—were all things that diminished the ruler's virtue and violated the harmony of Heaven. How could one take pleasure in them? Therefore, the Xia 夏 dynasty toppled through its punishments, and the Qin 秦 dynasty was torn apart through its brutality; if calamity did not befall their own persons, the evil consequences flowed down for several generations—this principle is manifest and unfailing. How much more so when the ruler governs and orders the myriad regions, striking down and deciding countless cases within a single year! If he slightly indulges his thunderous wrath and compounds it with crushing force, then the number of living people he destroys and the enmity he incurs from the Creator will be beyond reckoning! This is why the plea against dealing with officials drawn on the ground or carved of wood was earnestly repeated during a dynasty devoted to strict verification of nominal and actual performance. Let one beware of this! Even so, punishments are established in order to preserve human life. Thus Guo Pu 郭璞 said that imposing the heavy penalty of death is precisely the means of seeking to keep people alive, whereas when punishments are light, the people easily violate the law…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
在昔議之五服五流誰能去刑則彼所稱好生
云者無乃非齊法之大准哉蓋君人權斷主者
守文權斷則恩歸於主上守文則法立於有司
二者固自不偏廢也故削秋荼之令解凝脂之
網而後能爲君蔽淮南之獄執郭解之斷而後
能爲臣君養其德臣守其職而民稱平矣善乎
龜山氏之言曰天子以好生爲德有司以執法
爲公嗚呼盡之矣
表
擬輔臣應
制恭詠玄兔圖詩
進呈表
陳良心
同考試官教諭趙批對揚之辭類多勦襲此作事核
詞麗懇懇忠愛之心溢于言表得士如此可爲
國家慶矣
同考試官教諭顧批聲藻竝隆雅正不乏而遣詞使
事綽有體度可以式矣
punctuated:
在昔議之，五服五流，誰能去刑？則彼所稱好生云者，無乃非齊法之大准哉？蓋君人權斷，主者守文。權斷則恩歸於主上，守文則法立於有司，二者固自不偏廢也。故削秋荼之令，解凝脂之網，而後能爲君；蔽淮南之獄，執郭解之斷，而後能爲臣。君養其德，臣守其職，而民稱平矣。善乎龜山氏之言曰：「天子以好生爲德，有司以執法爲公。」嗚呼，盡之矣！

表
擬輔臣應制恭詠《玄兔圖》詩進呈表
陳良心
同考試官教諭趙批：對揚之辭，類多勦襲。此作事核詞麗，懇懇忠愛之心，溢于言表。得士如此，可爲國家慶矣。
同考試官教諭顧批：聲藻竝隆，雅正不乏，而遣詞使事，綽有體度，可以式矣。
translation_en:
… was discussed in antiquity. With the five punishments and the five grades of banishment, who could abolish punishment altogether? Then is what they call "loving life" not perhaps contrary to the great standard of uniform law? In general, the ruler of men exercises discretionary judgment, while the officials in charge abide by the letter of the law. When discretionary judgment is exercised, grace emanates from the sovereign above; when the letter of the law is observed, the law is upheld by the authorities below. The two certainly do not exclude each other. Therefore, only after paring away ordinances as dense as autumn weeds and loosening nets as thick as congealed fat can one act as a true ruler; only after adjudicating the case of the King of Huainan and holding firm to the sentencing of Guo Jie can one act as a true minister. When the ruler cultivates his virtue and the ministers guard their duties, the people will praise the fairness of the realm. How well put are the words of Master Guishan (Yang Shi 楊時): "The Son of Heaven takes loving life as his virtue; the authorities take enforcing the law as their public duty." Alas, that says it all!

Memorial
A Draft Memorial by Grand Secretaries Presenting Poems Respectfully Composed at Imperial Command on the "Picture of the Dark Hare"
Chen Liangxin 陳良心
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhao: Words composed in response to the sovereign are mostly plagiarized and derivative. In this piece, the allusions are accurate and the diction is elegant, while an earnest heart of loyalty and affection overflows beyond the words. To obtain a scholar such as this is a cause for congratulating the state!
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Gu: Sound and rhetorical ornament are equally lofty, elegance and correctness are not lacking, and the choice of words and use of allusions possess ample poise and measure. It can serve as a model.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭楊批莊重典則四六之佳者
考試官教諭湯批典雅駢儷宜錄以式
考試官教諭王批藻麗中有典則錄之
萬曆九年某月某日具官臣某等謹以所
撰應
制玄兔圖詩上
進者伏以
聖囿呈祥繪景爰留乎
宸鑒
===
天綃煥采摛辭共鬯乎
皇情蓋質秉玉衡歷千齡而始就而色分玄圃
應
萬壽以無疆覩玆舞獸之遺容披圖若見慚爾
雕蟲之末技表瑞難工臣等誠惶誠恐稽
首頓首竊惟治內治外國家以一統爲弘
規來享來王夷夏以同文爲盛世故寄象
鞮譯獻琛不却於湯廷鱗革羽毛圖貌兼
收於禹鼎獒來西旅雉進越裳旣顯異而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭楊批：莊重典則，四六之佳者。
考試官教諭湯批：典雅駢儷，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭王批：藻麗中有典則，錄之。

萬曆九年某月某日，具官臣某等謹以所撰《應制玄兔圖詩》上進者。伏以聖囿呈祥，繪景爰留乎宸鑒；天綃煥采，摛辭共鬯乎皇情。蓋質秉玉衡，歷千齡而始就；而色分玄圃，應萬壽以無疆。覩玆舞獸之遺容，披圖若見；慚爾雕蟲之末技，表瑞難工。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟治內治外，國家以一統爲弘規；來享來王，夷夏以同文爲盛世。故寄象鞮譯，獻琛不却於湯廷；鱗革羽毛，圖貌兼收於禹鼎。獒來西旅，雉進越裳，旣顯異而…
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yang: Grave and canonical in form, this is a fine example of parallel prose.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang: Classically elegant and finely paired; it should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: Amidst its ornate beauty there is canonical regularity; record it.

On a certain day of a certain month in the ninth year of the Wanli reign (1581), your servant So-and-so, holding full official title, and others respectfully present the "Poems on the Painting of the Black Hare Composed by Imperial Command" that we have written.

We humbly reflect that when the Sacred Park displays an auspicious omen, its painted likeness is kept for the Imperial gaze; when the heavenly silk shines with splendor, the verses spread forth upon it all the more gladden the August heart. For its substance derives from the Jade Heng star, taking a thousand years to reach completion; and its color is shared with the Mystic Garden of Kunlun, responding to a myriad longevities without bound. Beholding the preserved likeness of this dancing beast, as we unroll the painting it seems to appear before us; yet ashamed of our petty skill in carving insects, we find it hard to do justice in celebrating this auspicious sign.

Your servants, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground and knock our heads to the earth. We humbly consider that in governing both the interior and the exterior, the state takes grand unification as its far-reaching plan; in coming to offer tribute and acknowledge suzerainty, non-Chinese and Chinese alike take shared script as the hallmark of a flourishing age. Thus through interpreters of the four quarters, offerings of treasure were not spurned at the court of Tang; and creatures of scales, hides, feathers, and fur had their pictured forms all gathered upon the tripods of Yu. When the mastiff came from the Western Lü and the pheasant was presented by Yuechang, having manifested wonders and…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
效靈率登歌而獻奏覩赤驃以作頌岑參
之讃詠猶存感玄猿以吮豪吳筠之絺飾
可翫乃若星精月彩益為地寶天符俯封
卯而毓形仰瑶華以孕質歷稽往牒罕覿
奇章白者僅著嘉名赤焉巳為上應然未
有毳染緇林之色體分漆澤之光若此者
也惟
祖功
宗德柔懷誕格於遐夷而航海梯山賓貢充盈
===
於
禁苑蟾蜍玉魄無煩罝罘而自來霄漢玄猊
不待筌蹄而畢至在永樂甲申之歲受筐
篚於北陲暨宣德巳酉之年報
璽書於邊將付圉人慎加馴養宣畫史式繪英
標緇涅無加掃就若玄珠在掌鉛華弗著
瞻來如蒼璧盈眸兩勤侍從之歌章夙表
泰階之禎應聲詩巳光於往冊
繼述復慶於
punctuated: 效靈，率登歌而獻奏。覩赤驃以作頌，岑參之讃詠猶存；感玄猿以吮豪，吳筠之絺飾可翫。乃若星精月彩，益為地寶天符，俯封卯而毓形，仰瑶華以孕質。歷稽往牒，罕覿奇章：白者僅著嘉名，赤焉巳為上應；然未有毳染緇林之色，體分漆澤之光，若此者也。惟祖功宗德，柔懷誕格於遐夷；而航海梯山，賓貢充盈於禁苑。蟾蜍玉魄，無煩罝罘而自來；霄漢玄猊，不待筌蹄而畢至。在永樂甲申之歲，受筐篚於北陲；暨宣德巳酉之年，報璽書於邊將。付圉人慎加馴養，宣畫史式繪英標。緇涅無加，掃就若玄珠在掌；鉛華弗著，瞻來如蒼璧盈眸。兩勤侍從之歌章，夙表泰階之禎應。聲詩巳光於往冊，繼述復慶於
translation_en:
… manifest their numinous efficacy, all are celebrated in songs and presented in memorials. Seeing the red charger and composing an ode, the encomium of Cen Shen 岑參 still survives; moved by the black gibbon to moisten the brush-tip, the finely wrought verses of Wu Yun 吳筠 can still be savored. As for the essence of stars and the radiance of the moon, they are all the more treasures of earth and tallies of heaven—looking down upon the domain of Mao [the hare] to nurture their form, and looking up to the jade-like splendor to conceive their substance. Examining the records of the past, one rarely sees such extraordinary markings: the white ones merely established an auspicious name, and the red ones were already deemed a supreme response; yet never has there been one whose down is dyed the color of a dark forest and whose body shares the luster of black lacquer, such as this one.

Only through the meritorious achievements of our Ancestors and the virtuous power of our Forebears did gentle conciliation broadly reach the distant蠻夷 [non-Chinese peoples]; and crossing the seas and scaling the mountains, guest tribute filled the Imperial Park to overflowing. The jade spirit of the lunar toad came of its own accord without the trouble of rabbit-nets; the black lion of thecelestial expanse arrived in full without waiting for traps and snares. In the jiashen year of the Yongle 永樂 era (1404), baskets of tribute were received from the northern frontier; and when it came to the jiyou year of the Xuande 宣德 era (1429), an imperial letter under the dynastic seal was reported to the frontier generals. They were handed over to the grooms to be carefully tamed and raised, and court painters were summoned to depict their heroic bearing. Without adding black dye, when swept by the brush it is like a dark pearl in the palm; without applying lead powder, when gazed upon it is like a deep-green jade bi disk filling the eyes. Twice they engaged the poetic compositions of the imperial attendants, early on manifesting the auspicious response of the Grand Staircase [cosmic harmony]. Melodious poems have already shed luster upon the records of the past, and the continuation and transmission of our forebears' enterprise is once again celebrated on…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
令辰恭惟
皇帝陛下
功參五德
道際九玄
心合四始之奇葩
政列三驅之疎網
神營閱武近知沙漠來威
王會成編遠羨丹青馳譽求賢無類登庸取
駿於中林繩
===
===
祖有懷清燕探奇於
內府毛蟲獻狀清暉長護以玄雲冰縠傳神
黝質疑來於北極明視炯然而日映僊儀
颯矣其風旋擘春練以規摹爰爰故態織
秋煙而點綴躍躍馴姿霜杵澄鮮彷彿瑶
臺傳碧墨花摇動分明玉宇飛毫輕縑拂
而喜動
天顏華軸展而光昭
帝業卷藏惟舊宜卜世以卜年
punctuated: 令辰。恭惟皇帝陛下：功參五德，道際九玄。心合四始之奇葩，政列三驅之疎網。神營閱武，近知沙漠來威；王會成編，遠羨丹青馳譽。求賢無類，登庸取駿於中林；繩祖有懷，清燕探奇於內府。毛蟲獻狀，清暉長護以玄雲；冰縠傳神，黝質疑來於北極。明視炯然而日映，僊儀颯矣其風旋。擘春練以規摹，爰爰故態；織秋煙而點綴，躍躍馴姿。霜杵澄鮮，彷彿瑶臺傳碧；墨花摇動，分明玉宇飛毫。輕縑拂而喜動天顏，華軸展而光昭帝業。卷藏惟舊，宜卜世以卜年；
translation_en: …this auspicious day. We humbly reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor possesses achievements that stand alongside the Five Virtues and a Way that reaches the Nine Heavens. Your mind harmonizes with the wondrous blossoms of the Four Beginnings of the Odes, and Your governance sets out the wide-meshed net of the Three Drives. Inspecting military prowess at the Divine Camp, we recently see the desert tribes submitting to Your awe; compiling the record of the Royal Audience, distant lands admire the renown spread by painted portraits. Seeking worthies without distinction of class, You elevate and employ fine steeds taken from the deep forests (as in the ode "Rabbit Net"); mindful of carrying on the work of Your ancestors, in moments of serene leisure You explore the rarities of the Inner Treasury. The furry creature presents its form, its pure radiance ever guarded by dark clouds; the icy silk captures its spirit, its sable substance seeming to have come from the North Pole. The "bright-gazer" (hare) gleams brilliantly as if reflecting the sun, and its immortal bearing swirls briskly with the wind. Splitting spring silk to trace its likeness, there is its unhurried original manner; weaving autumn mist to add touches of detail, there is its leaping tamed posture. The frost-pestle (of the moon hare) is limpid and fresh, as though transmitting emerald light from the Jasper Terrace; the ink-blossoms quiver with life, clearly showing the flying hair in the Jade Firmament. When the light silk is dusted off, joy moves the Imperial Countenance; when the splendid scroll is unrolled, glory illuminates the Imperial Enterprise. Though the scroll has long been stored away, fitting for divining generations and divining years,…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賞鑒重新可得名而得象豈留情於翫物將
適意於研詮宛文囿之游觀卑哉漢獵恍
鎬京之輸賁陋矣梁園方期侈詠以揚
休特奉
溫綸而應
制稽昔揄揚之作多歸鉛槧之流故庾信拜表
於周墀徒誇藻富而張浚颺言於宋室未
闡猷謨睠玆十館之詞林恭讚
累朝之瑞牒臣等業專班馬才愧左狐乏南山
===
隱豹之文負東郭驚盧之懼矢志敢營乎
三窟持身寧守乎一株目翫金精神怡月
德按圖而知上瑞均騰躍雀之歡搦管以
掞清辭殊切戴鰲之懼雕龍技殫徒云下
里裁歌繡虎心勞自謂上林借色蕪綴諸
臣之什繕塵
一夜之觀詞莫罄其鋪張意自關於對育瀟灑
煙霞之性難盡品題迷離毛穎之情粗能
描寫苟有裨於龜鑑良莫遏於蛩吟伏願
punctuated: 賞鑒重新，可得名而得象。豈留情於翫物，將適意於研詮。宛文囿之游觀，卑哉漢獵；恍鎬京之輸賁，陋矣梁園。方期侈詠以揚休，特奉溫綸而應制。稽昔揄揚之作，多歸鉛槧之流。故庾信拜表於周墀，徒誇藻富；而張浚颺言於宋室，未闡猷謨。睠玆十館之詞林，恭讚累朝之瑞牒。臣等業專班、馬，才愧左、狐；乏南山隱豹之文，負東郭驚盧之懼。矢志敢營乎三窟，持身寧守乎一株。目翫金精，神怡月德。按圖而知上瑞，均騰躍雀之歡；搦管以掞清辭，殊切戴鰲之懼。雕龍技殫，徒云下里裁歌；繡虎心勞，自謂上林借色。蕪綴諸臣之什，繕塵一夜之觀。詞莫罄其鋪張，意自關於對育。瀟灑煙霞之性，難盡品題；迷離毛穎之情，粗能描寫。苟有裨於龜鑑，良莫遏於蛩吟。伏願
translation_en:
… As connoisseurship is renewed, both its name and its likeness can be grasped. How could this be lingering affection for trifling with curiosities? Rather, it is taking pleasure in probing the deeper meaning. It is just like roaming and viewing in King Wen's park—how base were the Han hunts! Or like the tribute of splendor brought to the capital of Hao—how crude was the Liang garden! Just as we were hoping to compose lavish verses to extol this auspiciousness, we specially received Your gracious decree to write in response to imperial command.

Examining the eulogistic works of the past, they mostly belonged to men of writing tablets and brushes. Thus, when Yu Xin 庾信 presented his memorial at the court of Northern Zhou, he merely boasted of florid abundance; and when Zhang Jun 張浚 spoke forth at the house of Song, he did not expound grand counsels. Looking fondly upon the forest of literati in the ten historiographical halls, we respectfully praise the auspicious records of successive reigns.

Your servants specialize in the craft of Ban Gu 班固 and Sima Qian 司馬遷, yet our talents fall shamefully short of Zuo Qiuming 左丘明 and Dong Hu 董狐. Lacking the literary patterning of the leopard hidden in the Southern Mountains, we harbor the fear of the Dongguo 東郭 hare startled by the hound Hanlu 韓盧. In swearing our resolve, how would we dare scheme for three burrows? In conducting ourselves, we would rather guard a single tree trunk. Our eyes delight in the Essence of Metal, and our spirits rejoice in the Virtue of the Moon. Examining the painting, we recognize a supreme omen, and all alike leap with the joy of sparrows; grasping our brushes to spread forth pure phrases, we feel most keenly the dread of a turtle bearing a mountain. Our skill at carving dragons is exhausted—we can merely say we have fashioned rustic songs of Xiali; our minds are weary from embroidering tigers—we tell ourselves we have borrowed splendor from the Shanglin Park.

Clumsily stringing together the verses of the various officials, we have copied them out to befoul Your Majesty's perusal for an evening. Words cannot exhaust its grand display, yet the meaning naturally pertains to responding to Heaven's nurturing [?]. Its carefree nature amid mist and rosy clouds is difficult to evaluate in full; the elusive disposition of the furred creature—and of our writing brushes—we can only roughly depict. Yet if it may offer some small aid as a mirror for governance, truly we could not suppress our cricket-like chirping. We humbly wish that…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
緝熙懋學得心頓造於忘蹄
寤寐求才式燕頻歌乎斯首
斡旋元氣長收百鍊之眞精培養性靈不藉
千年之僊搗治以不治躋
上治俾漢賦絶筆於長楊玄之又玄格
重玄令虞舞再儀乎箭管臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹以所撰玄兎圖詩隨
表上
===
進以
聞
第參塲
策
第一問
段蓋國
同考試官訓導趙批祝願
皇儲具見忠愛之至而條對內御祈祀莫不一秉于正庶幾乎藎臣用心哉
同考試官教諭尹批守靜葆和乃根本之論
punctuated:
緝熙懋學，得心頓造於忘蹄；寤寐求才，式燕頻歌乎斯首。斡旋元氣，長收百鍊之眞精；培養性靈，不藉千年之僊搗。治以不治，躋上治，俾漢賦絶筆於長楊；玄之又玄，格重玄，令虞舞再儀乎箭管。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屛營之至。謹以所撰《玄兎圖詩》隨表上進以聞。

第參塲
策
第一問
段蓋國
同考試官訓導趙批：祝願皇儲，具見忠愛之至；而條對內御、祈祀，莫不一秉于正，庶幾乎藎臣用心哉！
同考試官教諭尹批：守靜葆和，乃根本之論。
translation_en:
…may Your Majesty continuously brighten Your diligent learning, grasping the essence so instantly as to forget the snare; and seek talent waking and sleeping, holding joyful banquets and frequently singing the ode "The White-Headed Hare" (Hu Ye). Revolving the primordial vitality, may You forever gather the true essence refined a hundredfold; nurturing Your spiritual nature, You have no need of the elixir pounded for a thousand years by the immortals. Governing through non-governance, ascend to supreme governance, causing the rhapsodies of Han to lay down their brushes at the Changyang Palace; mysterious and yet more mysterious, reach the doubly mysterious, making the dances of Yu bring the phoenixes to court once more to the music of flute and pipe. Your servants are overcome with the utmost awe, trepidation, and earnest emotion as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacred Majesty. We reverently present the "Poems on the Picture of the Black Hare" that we have composed, accompanying this memorial, to bring them to Your Majesty's attention.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Duan Gaiguo
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao: In his prayers and wishes for the Imperial Heir, one fully sees the utmost loyalty and affection; and in his point-by-point responses regarding the regulation of the inner palace and prayers and sacrifices, there is nothing that does not adhere strictly to orthodoxy. How close this is to the devoted mindfulness of a loyal subject!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yin: Preserving tranquility and cherishing harmony is indeed a fundamental argument…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭湯批寓規於祝頌宜錄
考試官教諭王批條答甚悉而忠藎藹然
人主荷
天地
祖宗之託念承祧主器之重則稽典禮以迓
神休非本本原原至計哉夫
君猶天也頌天者以不息故曰重光而乾道昌
祝
君者以無疆故明兩作而
===
皇圖鞏其克配均也欲隆無疆之業必先本原
之地故遐則監於成憲而法古之道備焉
邇則稽諸舊章而率
祖之心盡焉六職備脩三靈孚祐古之誼辟所
以式壼則而衍胤祥者事莫大於此矣執
事軫重
皇儲而以內御祈祀之典策諸生蓋爲
國本慮殷且亟也敢不稽古以復夫大君非
命於天者哉其冢嗣則天之宗子也其諸
punctuated:
考試官教諭湯批：「寓規於祝頌，宜錄。」
考試官教諭王批：「條答甚悉，而忠藎藹然。」
人主荷天地、祖宗之託，念承祧主器之重，則稽典禮以迓神休，非本本原原至計哉！夫君猶天也。頌天者以不息，故曰重光，而乾道昌；祝君者以無疆，故明兩作，而皇圖鞏。其克配均也。欲隆無疆之業，必先本原之地。故遐則監於成憲，而法古之道備焉；邇則稽諸舊章，而率祖之心盡焉。六職備脩，三靈孚祐，古之誼辟所以式壼則而衍胤祥者，事莫大於此矣。執事軫重皇儲，而以內御、祈祀之典策諸生，蓋爲國本慮殷且亟也，敢不稽古以復？夫大君非命於天者哉？其冢嗣，則天之宗子也；其諸
translation_en:
Examiner Instructor Tang 湯 comments: "He embeds admonition within prayers and praise; this should be selected for recording."
Examiner Instructor Wang 王 comments: "His point-by-point responses are thorough, and his loyal devotion shines forth."

When the ruler bears the trust of Heaven, Earth, and the Ancestors, and reflects upon the weighty responsibility of succeeding to the ancestral temple and presiding over the sacrificial vessels, then examining the canons of ritual in order to welcome divine blessings—is this not the supreme plan rooted in fundamental principles? Now, the Sovereign is like Heaven. Those who praise Heaven do so for its ceaselessness; thus it is called "redoubled brilliance," and the Way of Qian 乾 flourishes. Those who pray for the Sovereign do so for his boundlessness; thus "brightness is doubled in rising," and the imperial enterprise is consolidated. Their capacity to match one another is equal. If one wishes to exalt a boundless enterprise, one must first attend to the fundamental ground. Therefore, looking far back, one takes the established constitutions as a mirror, and the way of emulating antiquity is made complete; looking near at hand, one examines the old statutes, and the heart devoted to following the Ancestors is fully realized. When the six offices of the palace are fully cultivated and the three spiritual powers respond with blessings—that whereby the righteous sovereigns of antiquity modeled the rules of the inner quarters and multiplied the auspiciousness of posterity had no greater basis than this. Your Excellency, out of deep concern for the Imperial Heir, has posed a policy question to us candidates regarding the canons of inner palace regulation and prayers and sacrifices. This is surely because your concern for the foundation of the dynasty is both earnest and urgent; how could I dare not examine antiquity in order to reply? Now, is the Great Sovereign not mandated by Heaven? His eldest heir is the lineal son of Heaven; his various…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
王以下則天所茂衍爲宗子支也而紫薇
垣象之矣太乙座其宸極乎第一星以象
冢嗣餘三星以象庶子森羅列置互爲維
亘夫使二星隱曜弗彰則光芒與紫宮不
相包絡而何以烜奕宸極乎故天必耦地
王必耦后其道相須而後成而天神効順
地軸發靈其機亦相感而類應繇斯以譚
所以樹茲
儲寳克昌來業者其道槩可覩已甞攷敻古
===
后稷之生寔自元妃下之則簡狄生契慶
都生堯娀訾生摯維時閫職未建掖位尚
乏烏覩所謂六宮哉自四妃始於帝嚳而
成周廣之爲王宮之令立之后以配天子
立之三夫人以象三公立之九嬪以象九
卿立之二十七世婦以象大夫立之八十
一御妻以象元士六宮之位與外班等而
翬珩褕組自是稍稍充椒塗也然而未濫
也載按禮文天地之祭主自天子次之則
punctuated: 王以下，則天所茂衍爲宗子支也，而紫薇垣象之矣。太乙座其宸極乎，第一星以象冢嗣，餘三星以象庶子，森羅列置，互爲維亘。夫使二星隱曜弗彰，則光芒與紫宮不相包絡，而何以烜奕宸極乎？故天必耦地，王必耦后，其道相須而後成；而天神効順，地軸發靈，其機亦相感而類應。繇斯以譚，所以樹茲儲寳、克昌來業者，其道槩可覩已。甞攷敻古，后稷之生，寔自元妃；下之，則簡狄生契，慶都生堯，娀訾生摯。維時閫職未建，掖位尚乏，烏覩所謂六宮哉？自四妃始於帝嚳，而成周廣之爲王宮之令：立之后以配天子，立之三夫人以象三公，立之九嬪以象九卿，立之二十七世婦以象大夫，立之八十一御妻以象元士。六宮之位與外班等，而翬珩褕組自是稍稍充椒塗也，然而未濫也。載按禮文，天地之祭，主自天子；次之，則
translation_en:
…princes and below are those whom Heaven causes to flourish and multiply as branches of the principal son, and the Purple Forbidden Enclosure (Ziwei yuan) symbolizes this in the heavens. Does not the Great One (Taiyi) sit at the imperial pole? The first star symbolizes the eldest heir, and the remaining three stars symbolize the sons of concubines; arrayed in serried ranks, they mutually uphold and extend one another. Now, suppose those stars hid their brilliance and did not shine forth—then their radiance would not envelop and connect with the Purple Palace, and how could the imperial pole be made resplendent and illustrious? Therefore, Heaven must be paired with Earth, and the King must be paired with the Queen; their Ways depend on each other to reach completion. And when the spirits of Heaven render obedience and the axis of Earth manifests its numinous power, their subtle mechanisms likewise move one another and respond according to kind. Speaking from this perspective, the Way by which to establish the precious Heir Apparent and make prosperous the future patrimony can in general be seen.

When we examine remote antiquity, the birth of Hou Ji (Lord Millet) truly came from the principal consort; below her, Jiandi gave birth to Xie, Qingdu gave birth to Yao, and Changzi gave birth to Zhi. At that time, the offices of the inner quarters were not yet established and the ranks of the side-apartments were still lacking—where could one see the so-called Six Palaces? Beginning with Emperor Ku, there were the four consorts, and the flourishing Zhou expanded this into the regulations of the royal palace: establishing the Queen to match the Son of Heaven, establishing the Three Ladies (san furen) to symbolize the Three Dukes, establishing the Nine Concubines of the First Rank (jiu pin) to symbolize the Nine Chief Ministers, establishing the Twenty-Seven Hereditary Consorts (ershiqi shifu) to symbolize the Grand Masters, and establishing the Eighty-One Attendant Wives (bashiyi yuqi) to symbolize the Servicemen of the First Class. The ranks of the Six Palaces corresponded to the outer court hierarchy, and pheasant-patterned robes, jade pendants, feathered garments, and silk cords from this time gradually filled the pepper-plastered halls—and yet there was no excess.

Furthermore, examining the ritual texts: sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were presided over by the Son of Heaven; next to these,…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
秩於山川禋於六宗徧於羣神維時祝史
未繁祭義尚質烏覩所謂高禖哉自簡狄
見於商詩而秦官述之爲祈嗣之文期之
仲春以適生機候之玄鳥以符靈契主之
高禖以重始合從之嬙嬪以配陰陽授之
韣矢以徵先兆禖祀之典與先蠶竝而龍
斾鳳蹕自是往往列春郊也然而未瀆也
後世闇帷房之戒廣事采擇而婦制莫釐
昧告虔之儀徒飾虛文而精意未協則去
===
古遠矣譚內御者每藉口於周官以自遂
其狎昵之私有增級十四者焉漢之武元
是已而巫蠱燕啄內釁相尋不可長也有
爵視外朝者焉晉之武帝是已而下逮散
位盈溢至萬不可訓也有分列八品者焉
唐之襲隋是已而貽謀不善素舒失德不
可道也此惟端容麗服陪從宴閒內鮮求
賢審官之助外叢德纖偾長之譏吁可鑒
哉譚祀典者又藉口於秦官以自文其不
punctuated: 秩於山川，禋於六宗，徧於羣神。維時祝史未繁，祭義尚質，烏覩所謂高禖哉？自簡狄見於《商詩》，而秦官述之爲祈嗣之文：期之仲春以適生機，候之玄鳥以符靈契，主之高禖以重始合，從之嬙嬪以配陰陽，授之韣矢以徵先兆。禖祀之典與先蠶竝，而龍斾鳳蹕自是往往列春郊也，然而未瀆也。後世闇帷房之戒，廣事采擇，而婦制莫釐；昧告虔之儀，徒飾虛文，而精意未協，則去古遠矣。譚內御者，每藉口於《周官》以自遂其狎昵之私。有增級十四者焉，漢之武、元是已，而巫蠱、燕啄，內釁相尋，不可長也；有爵視外朝者焉，晉之武帝是已，而下逮散位，盈溢至萬，不可訓也；有分列八品者焉，唐之襲隋是已，而貽謀不善，素舒失德，不可道也。此惟端容麗服，陪從宴閒，內鮮求賢審官之助，外叢德纖偾長之譏。吁，可鑒哉！譚祀典者，又藉口於秦官以自文其不
translation_en:
…ordered sacrifices to the mountains and rivers, pure offerings to the Six Honored Ones, and sacrifices extending to all the spirits. At that time, invocation scribes were not yet numerous, and the principles of sacrifice valued simplicity—where did one ever see the so-called Supreme Matchmaker (Gaomei 高禖)? Beginning with Jiandi 簡狄 appearing in the Odes of Shang (Shang shi 商詩), Qin ritual officials transmitted this to establish the liturgical forms for praying for an heir: scheduling it in mid-spring to accord with the vitality of generation, awaiting the arrival of the dark bird (swallow) to match the numinous tally, presiding over it at the altar of the Supreme Matchmaker to honor the original union, attending it with the palace consorts and concubines to pair yin and yang, and bestowing a bow-case and arrows tobetoken the auspicious omen beforehand. The canon of the Matchmaker sacrifice stood alongside that of the First Sericulturist (Xiancan 先蠶), and from then on dragon banners and phoenix processions were often arrayed in the spring suburbs—yet this was not irreverent profanation.

Later ages grew blind to the admonitions of the bedchamber, engaging broadly in the selection of palace women while failing to regulate the system of consorts; they grew ignorant of the rites of reverent supplication, merely adorning empty forms while failing to harmonize with the essential meaning. Thus they departed far from antiquity.

Those who discuss the management of the inner palace always use the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官) as a pretext to indulge their private desires for familiar favoritism. There were those who increased the ranks of consorts to fourteen—Emperors Wu 武 and Yuan 元 of the Han were such cases—yet witch-gu poisoning (wugu 巫蠱) and the "swallow's pecking" [imperial infanticide by Zhao Feiyan] brought domestic crises one after another; this must not be fostered. There were those who made consort ranks correspond to the titles of the outer court—Emperor Wu 武帝 of the Jin was such a case—yet extending down to unranked positions, they overflowed to ten thousand women; this cannot serve as a model. There were those who divided them into eight ranks—the Tang following the Sui was such a case—yet the counsels bequeathed to posterity were poor, and licentious indulgence and loss of virtue are unspeakable. These women merely composed their countenances in splendid attire to attend the ruler in banquets and leisure; within, they rarely offered the assistance of seeking the worthy and examining officials [as praised in the Ode "Juan'er"], while without, they gathered criticisms of petty virtue and ruining the hierarchy. Alas, how worthy of serving as a warning!

Those who discuss the sacrificial canons, moreover, use the Qin officials as a pretext to gloss over their un…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
經之說有設壇城南者焉則漢武以誕生
皇子之故而有報無祈何簡也有建立石
主者焉則晉采束晳高堂隆之議而瘞埋
破石何陋也有增置配帝者焉則北齊以
太昊爲配而義無所取何褻也此皆典禮
未稱明神不享徒事苟簡攟摭之儀罔識
前星少海之重吁可鄙哉
高皇帝詫業發祥外自堦墀內逮房闥靡匪雝
雝肅肅以貽
===
神孫令則洪武初年卽
命禮官詳定女職設立六局尚宮則司紀司言
司簿司闈也尚儀則司籍司樂司賓司賛
也尚服則司寳司衣司仗司飾也尚食則
司饌司醞司藥司供也尚寢則司設司輿
司苑司燈也尚功則司製司珍司綵司計
也戒正責罰則董之宮正而其秩無踰六
品法何具也或疑六尚之設雜就唐儀不
知唐沿隋者也隋沿宇文周者也宇文氏
punctuated:
經之說。有設壇城南者焉，則漢武以誕生皇子之故，而有報無祈，何簡也！有建立石主者焉，則晉采束晳、高堂隆之議，而瘞埋破石，何陋也！有增置配帝者焉，則北齊以太昊爲配，而義無所取，何褻也！此皆典禮未稱，明神不享，徒事苟簡攟摭之儀，罔識前星少海之重。吁，可鄙哉！
高皇帝詫業發祥，外自堦墀，內逮房闥，靡匪雝雝肅肅，以貽神孫令則。洪武初年，卽命禮官詳定女職，設立六局：尚宮，則司紀、司言、司簿、司闈也；尚儀，則司籍、司樂、司賓、司賛也；尚服，則司寳、司衣、司仗、司飾也；尚食，則司饌、司醞、司藥、司供也；尚寢，則司設、司輿、司苑、司燈也；尚功，則司製、司珍、司綵、司計也。戒正責罰，則董之宮正，而其秩無踰六品，法何具也！或疑六尚之設，雜就唐儀，不知唐沿隋者也，隋沿宇文周者也，宇文氏
translation_en:
…unorthodox theories. There were those who set up an altar south of the city: such was Emperor Wu of Han (漢武), who because of the birth of an imperial son offered thanksgiving without prior supplication—how perfunctory! There were those who erected a stone spirit-tablet: such was the Jin dynasty, which adopted the proposals of Shu Xi (束晳) and Gaotang Long (高堂隆) and buried a broken stone—how vulgar! There were those who added a coadjutor deity: such was the Northern Qi, which made Taihao (太昊) the coadjutor without any basis in principle—how irreverent! In all these cases, the canonical rites were unmatched to their purpose and the bright spirits did not accept the offerings; they merely engaged in careless and cobbled-together ceremonies, failing to recognize the gravity of the Heir Apparent—the Fore-star and Lesser Sea. Alas, how contemptible!

When the Exalted Emperor (高皇帝, Ming Taizu) founded the imperial enterprise [詫業, for 創業?] and initiated auspicious blessings, from the outer court steps in to the palace chambers, there was nothing that was not harmonious and reverent, so as to bequeath an admirable model to his divine descendants. In the early years of the Hongwu (洪武) reign, he immediately ordered the ritual officials to determine in detail the offices of the palace women, establishing the Six Bureaus: the Palace Service Bureau (尚宮), comprising the Services of Registers (司紀), Messages (司言), Accounts (司簿), and Gates (司闈); the Ceremonial Service Bureau (尚儀), comprising the Services of Books (司籍), Music (司樂), Guests (司賓), and Praise-giving (司賛); the Wardrobe Service Bureau (尚服), comprising the Services of Treasures (司寳), Robes (司衣), Regalia (司仗), and Ornaments (司飾); the Food Service Bureau (尚食), comprising the Services of Delicacies (司饌), Brews (司醞), Medicines (司藥), and Provisions (司供); the Bedchamber Service Bureau (尚寢), comprising the Services of Furnishings (司設), Palanquins (司輿), Gardens (司苑), and Lamps (司燈); and the Handicraft Service Bureau (尚功), comprising the Services of Tailoring (司製), Jewels (司珍), Silks (司綵), and Auditing (司計). Admonition, correction, and punishment were supervised by the Rectifier of the Palace (宮正), and none of their ranks exceeded the sixth grade—how complete the regulations were! Some suspect that the establishment of the Six Bureaus was indiscriminately modeled on Tang ceremony, not knowing that the Tang followed the Sui, the Sui followed the Northern Zhou of the Yuwen (宇文) clan, and what the Yuwen clan…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所定又皆本周官者也洪武儒臣采而用
之奚嘗不循周制耶
肅皇帝鑠勳恢烈大自
兩郊細及百祀靡匪皇皇奕奕以光
聖祖遐武嘉靖初年卽
命禮官議崇禖祀設壇震方南鄉則
皇天上帝也西鄉則
獻皇作配也牲則三品也禮則三獻也樂則九
奏也舞則八佾也
===
帝位則壇下北鄉也
后妃則以次稍南也弓矢弓韣則陳之壇下而
其數視乎
妃嬪制何詳也或疑禮文之縟半益周制不
知壇居東方震繼離也主以
上帝荅元貺也配以
皇考本自出也
帝后異位坤承乾也嘉靖儒臣變而通之又奚
必泥古法耶夫攷之往古參以
punctuated:
所定，又皆本《周官》者也。洪武儒臣采而用之，奚嘗不循周制耶？
肅皇帝鑠勳恢烈，大自兩郊，細及百祀，靡匪皇皇奕奕，以光聖祖遐武。嘉靖初年，卽命禮官議崇禖祀：設壇震方，南鄉則皇天上帝也，西鄉則獻皇作配也；牲則三品也，禮則三獻也，樂則九奏也，舞則八佾也，帝位則壇下北鄉也，后妃則以次稍南也；弓矢、弓韣則陳之壇下，而其數視乎妃嬪。制何詳也！或疑禮文之縟，半益周制；不知壇居東方，震繼離也；主以上帝，荅元貺也；配以皇考，本自出也；帝后異位，坤承乾也。嘉靖儒臣變而通之，又奚必泥古法耶？夫攷之往古，參以
translation_en:
… established were in turn all based upon the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). When the Confucian officials of the Hongwu era selected and adopted them, how did they ever fail to follow the institutions of the Zhou?

Emperor Su [the Jiajing Emperor], of shining merit and expansive achievements, in matters great from the two suburban sacrifices and small down to the hundred sacrifices, left nothing that was not grand and resplendent, thereby glorifying the distant footsteps of the Sacred Ancestor. In the early years of the Jiajing era, he promptly ordered the ritual officials to deliberate on exalting the Gaomei sacrifice [to the Matchmaker Deity for imperial heirs]: an altar was erected in the eastern quarter [the direction of the trigram Zhen]; facing south was Sovereign Heaven Supreme Emperor (Huangtian Shangdi), and facing west was Emperor Xian as correlate; the sacrificial victims were of the three kinds, the ritual consisted of three offerings, the music was performed in nine movements, and the dance was of eight rows; the Emperor's place was below the altar facing north, and the Empress and consorts were arranged in order slightly to the south; bows, arrows, and bow-cases were set out below the altar, their number corresponding to that of the consorts and concubines. How detailed the institution was! Some may suspect that theelaborateness of the ritual forms added half again to the institutions of the Zhou. They do not know that locating the altar in the east means that Zhen [the eldest son] succeeds Li [radiance/the sovereign]; making the Supreme Emperor the principal deity answers the primordial blessing; making the Imperial Deceased Father the correlate honors the source from which one came; and placing the Emperor and Empress in distinct positions signifies that Kun [Earth/the female] submissively receives Qian [Heaven/the male]. When the Confucian officials of the Jiajing era adapted and carried them through, why would they have needed to cling rigidly to ancient methods?
