Now, if we examine the distant past and compare it with…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
昭代時之升降可燭已禮之汙隆可鏡已方今
兩宮慈範齊軌姜嫄
中闈壼德方駕任姒且登九列而充六尚者非
良家之婉嫕則待年之淑女也簪珥成行
環珮振響肅
坤儀而脩四善體柔範以弘六義俔天之烈小
星之歌豈乏哉而
郊廟必親海岳必祀祈求胤嗣之典
兩宮尤惓惓焉然海內臣民之望又有出于廣
===
內御崇禋祀二者之外蓋亦有說矣夫禮
言時御易著貫魚非獨均恩嗇寵也將以
助
天資生也奈之何桂殿迎春則情與愛遷蘭房
侍夜則事為私奪或嬖而專席以妨廣胤
之理或溺而濫幸以虧生息之原此豈可
不為長慮哉詩紀玄鳥禮述高禖非尚禨
祥小數也將以翊
運承祧也奈之何內政未脩而專事徼福玄釐
punctuated: 昭代，時之升降可燭已，禮之汙隆可鏡已。方今兩宮慈範，齊軌姜嫄；中闈壼德，方駕任姒。且登九列而充六尚者，非良家之婉嫕，則待年之淑女也。簪珥成行，環珮振響，肅坤儀而脩四善，體柔範以弘六義，「俔天」之烈、「小星」之歌，豈乏哉？而郊廟必親，海岳必祀，祈求胤嗣之典，兩宮尤惓惓焉。然海內臣民之望，又有出于廣內御、崇禋祀二者之外，蓋亦有說矣。夫《禮》言時御，《易》著貫魚，非獨均恩嗇寵也，將以助天資生也。奈之何桂殿迎春，則情與愛遷；蘭房侍夜，則事為私奪。或嬖而專席，以妨廣胤之理；或溺而濫幸，以虧生息之原。此豈可不為長慮哉？《詩》紀玄鳥，《禮》述高禖，非尚禨祥小數也，將以翊運承祧也。奈之何內政未脩，而專事徼福；玄釐
translation_en:
… our illustrious dynasty, the rise and fall of the times can be illuminated, and the decline and flourishing of ritual can be mirrored. At present, the compassionate example of the Two Palaces [the Empresses Dowager] matches the track of Jiang Yuan; the inner-palace virtue of the Central Apartments [the Empress] rides abreast with Tai Ren and Tai Si. Moreover, those who ascend to the Nine Concubines and fill the Six Bureaus of the Palace Women are either gentle and compliant daughters of good families or virtuous maidens awaiting the age of marriage. Hairpins and ear-ornaments form ranks; jade pendants ring out in harmony. They reverence the Earthly model to cultivate the four virtues, and embody the gentle norm to broaden the six principles—how could there be any lack of the illustrious merit of "Like Heaven" [in the Odes] or the song of "Little Stars"? Furthermore, the suburban and ancestral altars are invariably attended in person, and the seas and sacred peaks are invariably sacrificed to; to the rites of praying for imperial posterity, the Two Palaces are especially devoted. Yet the hopes of officials and subjects within the seas go beyond merely expanding the roster of inner attendants and exalting the pure sacrifices—and for this, indeed, there is an explanation.

Now, when the Book of Rites speaks of timely attendance in the bedchamber, and the Book of Changes sets forth the image of "stringing fishes," this is not merely to equalize favor and economize on doting affection; it is intended to assist Heaven in giving birth to life. How is it, then, that when welcoming spring in the cassia halls, feelings shift along with infatuation, and when attending at night in the orchid chambers, duties are usurped by private partiality? Either a favorite monopolizes the mat, thereby obstructing the principle of multiplying heirs; or one indulges in excessive visitation, thereby impairing the source of generative vitality. How can one not take long-term thought for this? When the Book of Odes records the "Dark Bird" and the Book of Rites recounts the Supreme Matchmaker (Gaomei), this is not to prize the petty arts of omens and portents; it is intended to assist the dynastic destiny and continue the ancestral line. How is it, then, that when inner governance is not yet cultivated, one engages exclusively in seeking after fortune; when mysterious blessings…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
濫乞而惑志媚神或假符緯以求赤虹白
魚之驗或弔詭幽以要吞鳥履跡之奇此
豈可爲後訓哉
人主惟致虛守靜以儀刑於內嗇神葆和以考
祥於天則何福不應何瑞不臻故旣醉之
什曰釐爾女士從以孫子而假樂亦言子
孫千億干祿百福應感之機從可識矣乃
茲旣
明愼聘納虔脩祀事天下已望
===
明德於造舟爲梁之時而愚生今日則又竊效
封人之祝而推廣之詩序不云天下和平
斯婦人樂有子焉藉令軒殿以內凝采髫
年賁章笄歲者風流行而雨窈窕而民間
多關於伉儷后宮翡翠火齊膏脣耀首而
里巷士女不免葛屨杼軸之困則內外咨
怨終傷理道故夙夜幾康以薦天和而施
祉孫子者宜講也天道葆光於秋伏精於
冬而噢咻於春然後百昌殖萬彙作
punctuated:
濫乞而惑志媚神？或假符緯以求赤虹、白魚之驗，或弔詭幽以要吞鳥、履跡之奇，此豈可爲後訓哉？
人主惟致虛守靜以儀刑於內，嗇神葆和以考祥於天，則何福不應，何瑞不臻？故《旣醉》之什曰：「釐爾女士，從以孫子。」而《假樂》亦言：「子孫千億。」干祿百福，應感之機，從可識矣。乃茲旣明愼聘納，虔脩祀事，天下已望明德於「造舟爲梁」之時，而愚生今日則又竊效封人之祝而推廣之。《詩序》不云「天下和平，斯婦人樂有子」焉？藉令軒殿以內，凝采髫年，賁章笄歲者，風流行而雨窈窕，而民間多關於伉儷；后宮翡翠火齊，膏脣耀首，而里巷士女，不免葛屨杼軸之困；則內外咨怨，終傷理道。故夙夜幾康，以薦天和而施祉孫子者，宜講也。天道葆光於秋，伏精於冬，而噢咻於春，然後百昌殖、萬彙作。
translation_en:
… [dark blessings are] extravagantly begged for while deluding the mind in flattering the spirits? Whether borrowing from prognostic apocrypha to seek the portents of the red rainbow or the white fish, or indulging in bizarre occultism to court the marvels of swallowing a bird's egg or treading in a giant's footprint—how could such practices serve as lessons for posterity?

If only the sovereign attains emptiness and preserves tranquility so as to set a model within the inner court, and husbands his spirit and cherishes harmony so as to secure auspiciousness from Heaven, then what blessing will not respond, and what auspicious sign will not arrive? Thus the ode "Already Drunk" (Jizui) in the Book of Odes says: "You are granted heroic women, followed by grandsons and sons." And "Felicitous and Joyous" (Jiale) likewise speaks of "sons and grandsons in thousands and ratusan millions." Seeking emoluments and a hundred blessings—the mechanism of resonance and response can be understood from this.

Now, since Your Majesty has already shown discerning caution in the betrothal and selection of consorts and has reverently performed the sacrificial rites, the realm already looks up to your illustrious virtue at this moment of "joining boats to form a bridge" [i.e., the royal wedding]. Yet today, I, a foolish student, venture to imitate the border warden's prayer of Hua and expand upon it. Does not the Preface to the Odes (Shi xu) say that "when the realm is at peace, women delight in bearing children"? Suppose that within the palace halls, those chosen for their beauty in childhood or adorned with insignia upon reaching the age of the hairpin enjoy favors spreading like wind and grace falling like rain upon their secluded elegance, while among the common people many are deprived of a spouse; or suppose the rear palace is decked in kingfisher feathers and fire-pearls, with anointed lips and gleaming heads, while the men and women of the village lanes cannot escape the hardships of weaving hemp sandals and empty looms—then sighs and resentment within and without would ultimately harm the way of governance. Therefore, attending with vigilance from dawn to night to the subtle springs of peace and order, so as to present heavenly harmony and bestow blessings upon sons and grandsons, is something that ought to be carefully studied.

The Way of Heaven treasures its light in autumn, conceals its vital essence in winter, and warms and nurtures in spring; only then do the hundred things flourish and the myriad categories of beings arise. …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人主法陰陽之運養性命之精非堇堇焉習熊
經鳥伸以耽靜息也語曰天子不處全不
處極不處盈
皇皇上帝挈
大寶而屬之而以不貲之身靡曼於佚慾如子
孫黎民何如天意何故素封之家有材千
章而刳情約志無敢馳奢重弃糈也矧
至尊哉則上荅
蒼穹俯順人心往鑒流湎而來茂
===
鼎祚者宜講也樛木螽斯其小者也聖人刪詩
直取以美后妃則何以張之蓋樛木下垂
葛藟得附焉以豐其末螽斯不妬則天氣
全而種類繁滋后妃者法樛木之慈以逮
衆法螽斯之仁以馭下則蟄蟄振振之感
固可操左契而責之償則今之脩陰敎以
章内則者可講也古者御幸之禮至嚴且
肅將侍君所無論后若夫人息燭以告行
易服以告虔奏雞鳴於太師以告時鳴珮
punctuated: 人主法陰陽之運，養性命之精，非堇堇焉習熊經鳥伸以耽靜息也。語曰：「天子不處全，不處極，不處盈。」皇皇上帝，挈大寶而屬之，而以不貲之身靡曼於佚慾，如子孫黎民何？如天意何？故素封之家，有材千章，而刳情約志，無敢馳奢，重弃糈也，矧至尊哉？則上荅蒼穹，俯順人心，往鑒流湎而來茂鼎祚者，宜講也。樛木、螽斯，其小者也，聖人刪《詩》，直取以美后妃，則何以張之？蓋樛木下垂，葛藟得附焉以豐其末；螽斯不妬，則天氣全而種類繁滋。后妃者，法樛木之慈以逮衆，法螽斯之仁以馭下，則蟄蟄振振之感，固可操左契而責之償。則今之脩陰敎以章内則者，可講也。古者御幸之禮，至嚴且肅。將侍君所，無論后若夫人，息燭以告行，易服以告虔，奏《雞鳴》於太師以告時，鳴珮
translation_en:
The ruler takes the cycle of yin and yang as his model and nurtures the essence of his nature and vital endowment—not merely practicing the exercises of the hanging bear and stretching bird in order to indulge in quiet repose. As the saying goes: "The Son of Heaven does not dwell in completeness, does not dwell in the extreme, and does not dwell in fullness." August Lord on High has taken the Great Treasure and entrusted it to him; yet if he wears away his priceless person in licentious desires, what will become of his descendants and the black-haired people? What will become of the will of Heaven? Even an unofficially wealthy family possessing a thousand timbers of fine wood will pare down its passions and restrain its ambitions, not daring to run wild in extravagance, because it is reluctant to squander its sustenance—how much more so the Most Venerable! Therefore, how to answer the Azure Vault above, accord with human hearts below, take warning from past dissipation, and bring flourishing to the dynastic fortune in the future is something that ought to be expounded.

The "Drooping Boughs" (Jiumu) and the "Locusts" (Zhongsi) are minor things; yet when the Sage edited the Classic of Odes, he directly selected them to praise the Empress and consorts—how did he magnify them so? It is because when the boughs droop downward, the vines and creepers are able to cling to them and make their tips luxuriant; and because the locusts are free of jealousy, their heavenly endowment remains intact and their kind multiplies abundantly. If the Empress and consorts model themselves on the kindness of the drooping boughs in reaching out to the multitude, and imitate the benevolence of the locusts in governing their subordinates, then the response of harmonious clustering and numerous progeny may indeed be claimed as surely as holding the left tally to demand repayment of a debt. Thus, how at present to cultivate the Yin teachings so as to make manifest the regulations of the inner palace is something that may be expounded.

In antiquity, the rites of royal attendance in the bedchamber were most strict and solemn. When about to attend at the ruler's place, whether the Empress or a consort, she would extinguish the candles to announce her departure, change her garments to express her reverence, have the Grand Musician perform the "Cockcrow" (Jiming) to announce the hour, sound her girdle…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
玉於房中以告去應門擊柝以告闢其禮
恭愼而不苟而又有女史簪彤管書其環
以進退之此非好瑣煩其令所以謹競榮
之防而杜色授之漸則今之昵第裯而越
矩矱者可講也大任之身文王目無邪視
耳無淫聽口無敖言文王生而褒然聖明
爲周宗太姒生十子自少至長恒以正道
押持之用成武王周公至德則古昔所稱
胎敎內敎者可講也審能是則陰陽順序
===
恩寵均齊慶澤綿遠本支千億以此格天
而上神歆以此格
廟而百靈契揚
太母徽音之烈成
中宮脫珥之賢刑家之化爰達寰宇重輪之
貺且延萬葉奚止
掖庭永巷之脩職哉宋魏鶴山氏言之矣
人君居內之日常少居外之日常多所以養壽
命之源雖子孫千億亦自此始此祈嗣之
punctuated: 玉於房中以告去，應門擊柝以告闢。其禮恭愼而不苟，而又有女史簪彤管，書其環以進退之。此非好瑣煩其令，所以謹競榮之防，而杜色授之漸。則今之昵第裯而越矩矱者，可講也。大任之身文王，目無邪視，耳無淫聽，口無敖言，文王生而褒然聖明，爲周宗。太姒生十子，自少至長，恒以正道押持之，用成武王、周公至德。則古昔所稱胎敎、內敎者，可講也。審能是，則陰陽順序，恩寵均齊，慶澤綿遠，本支千億。以此格天而上神歆，以此格廟而百靈契，揚太母徽音之烈，成中宮脫珥之賢，刑家之化爰達寰宇，重輪之貺且延萬葉，奚止掖庭、永巷之脩職哉？宋魏鶴山氏言之矣：「人君居內之日常少，居外之日常多，所以養壽命之源。雖子孫千億，亦自此始。」此祈嗣之
translation_en:
… jade pendants in the bedchamber to announce her departure, and watchmen struck wooden clappers at the Gate of Response (Yingmen) to announce the opening of the palace doors. These rites were respectful, circumspect, and never lax. Moreover, female scribes wearing red-tube brushes in their hair recorded the silver rings of the consorts in order to regulate their advancement and withdrawal. This was not out of a fondness for making regulations petty and burdensome; rather, it was the means to guard the dike against vying for favor and to stop the gradual rise of promotion through sensual allure. Thus, how today we might address the problem of being overly intimate with bedcurtains and bedding [?] and overstepping the proper rules and standards is something that should be discussed.

When Tairen 太任 was pregnant with King Wen 文王, her eyes looked at nothing improper, her ears listened to nothing licentious, and her mouth spoke nothing arrogant; King Wen was born preeminently sage and enlightened, becoming the founder of Zhou grandeur. Taisi 太姒 gave birth to ten sons, and from their youth to maturity she constantly upheld and guided them [?] with the correct Way, thereby bringing to completion the supreme virtue of King Wu 武王 and the Duke of Zhou 周公. Thus, what antiquity called fetal instruction and domestic instruction is something that should be discussed.

If this can truly be achieved, then yin and yang will follow their proper order, favor and grace will be evenly distributed, auspicious blessings will stretch far into the future, and the main and collateral lineages will number in the hundreds of millions. Through this, one will reach Heaven and the spirits above will delight in the offerings; through this, one will reach the Ancestral Temple and the hundred numina will be in harmony. It will exalt the illustrious legacy of the Empress Dowager's admirable reputation and fulfill the worthiness of the Empress in removing her earrings in remonstrance. The transforming influence of regulating the family will thereupon reach the entire world, and the blessing of the "double-ringed moon"—the Heir Apparent—will extend for ten thousand generations. How could this merely be a matter of cultivating duties within the lateral courts and the Long Lanes of the inner palace?

Wei Heshan 魏鶴山 (Wei Liaoweng 魏了翁) of the Song dynasty said it well: "When a ruler spends fewer days residing in the inner quarters and more days residing in the outer court, it is the means to nourish the source of longevity; even having descendants numbering in the hundreds of millions also begins from this." This is the… [foundation] of praying for heirs…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
本也而非特宋臣有是說也
高皇帝初定女職亦嘗言古者建設過多宜防
女寵垂法將來以故六局外無復剩員然
當時篤生二十四
王迄今稱親郡諸府及中尉將軍以下二萬
有竒天下比於鳳毛麟趾以為上瑞然則
繼體守成之盛果在内御之繁與禋祀之勤耶
詩曰昭兹來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天
之祜以
===
高皇
世祖之功耀於日月長於天地神祇降康俾有
土者世世明章之矧
今上應昌期孚世德雲物告符鍾祥厥後一卜
於
瑶圖之曆再稽於大人之占多男之慶且旦
暮睹之矣
第二問
陳良心
punctuated:
本也。而非特宋臣有是說也，高皇帝初定女職，亦嘗言古者建設過多，宜防女寵，垂法將來，以故六局外無復剩員。然當時篤生二十四王，迄今稱親、郡諸府，及中尉、將軍以下，二萬有竒，天下比於鳳毛麟趾，以為上瑞。然則繼體守成之盛，果在内御之繁與禋祀之勤耶？《詩》曰：「昭兹來許，繩其祖武。於萬斯年，受天之祜。」以高皇、世祖之功，耀於日月，長於天地，神祇降康，俾有土者世世明章之。矧今上應昌期，孚世德，雲物告符，鍾祥厥後，一卜於瑶圖之曆，再稽於大人之占，多男之慶，且旦暮睹之矣。

第二問
陳良心
translation_en:
…foundation. And it was not only the minister of the Song who held this view. When the August Emperor Taizu (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝) first established the female palace offices, he also remarked that in antiquity too many positions had been set up and that one ought to guard against female favoritism so as to hand down a model for the future; for this reason, beyond the Six Bureaus (liuju 六局) there were no surplus personnel. Yet at that time he was blessed with the birth of twenty-four princes, and down to the present day the various establishments of Imperial Princes (qinwang 親王) and Commandery Princes (junwang 郡王), together with those of the rank of Defender-in-Chief (zhongwei 中尉) and General (jiangjun 將軍) and below, number more than twenty thousand. The realm compares them to phoenix feathers and unicorn footprints, regarding this as the highest auspiciousness. This being so, does the flourishing of dynastic succession and conservation really lie in the profusion of palace consorts in attendance or the assiduousness of sacrificial rites? The Book of Odes (Shi 詩) says: "Brilliant is this continuation, following in the footsteps of the ancestors; for ten thousand years, receiving the blessings of Heaven." Through the merits of the August Founder (Gaohuang 高皇, i.e. Emperor Taizu) and the Epochal Founder (Shizu 世祖, i.e. Emperor Shizong), which shine like the sun and moon and endure as long as heaven and earth, the spirits of Heaven and Earth send down peace and prosperity, enabling those who hold territories to make them illustrious from generation to generation. How much more so now that the Reigning Sovereign answers to a flourishing era and embodies the hereditary virtue of the dynasty! Auspicious clouds and phenomena announce the signs, concentrating good fortune upon his descendants. Divining once by the calendar of the jade chart and consulting again the prognostications of the great diviner, the celebration of many sons shall be witnessed morning and evening!

Second Question
Chen Liangxin 陳良心

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭趙批是能留心
國計者就所條畫次第施行殷富立致矣經濟材也錄之
同考試官教諭顧批以儉德立論足識時務者
同考試官教諭楊批會計始末闡揚殆盡
考試官教諭湯批是策有裨主計者宜錄
考試官教諭王批斟酌時事劈畫允當
財蓋難言哉聽而不爲之筴則大耗驟起
而持之則裒刻難行循故牘則盈縮無稽
而間爲陽驅陰脅之法則又近於籍外取
===
而讎民然則理財固無術乎財猶水也疏
則流泰疏則涸蓄則止泰蓄則滯故制其
出者毋若制其入而已數口之家日有膳
月有儲主者手屈心計握其奇贏而量用
焉終身可以無困朝得而夕散之廢其什
九而不知其存者什一卽計然猗頓立窘
耳況天下之廣其所仰給又千百億萬而
倍之乎夫天地之道至紘以大尚猶節其
章光愛其神明宇宙之財幾何而乃以填
punctuated:
同考試官教諭趙批：是能留心國計者，就所條畫次第施行，殷富立致矣，經濟材也，錄之。
同考試官教諭顧批：以儉德立論，足識時務者。
同考試官教諭楊批：會計始末，闡揚殆盡。
考試官教諭湯批：是策有裨主計者，宜錄。
考試官教諭王批：斟酌時事，劈畫允當。
財蓋難言哉！聽而不爲之筴，則大耗；驟起而持之，則裒刻難行；循故牘，則盈縮無稽；而間爲陽驅陰脅之法，則又近於籍外取而讎民。然則理財固無術乎？財猶水也，疏則流，泰疏則涸；蓄則止，泰蓄則滯。故制其出者，毋若制其入而已。數口之家，日有膳，月有儲，主者手屈心計，握其奇贏而量用焉，終身可以無困。朝得而夕散之，廢其什九，而不知其存者什一，卽計然、猗頓立窘耳。況天下之廣，其所仰給，又千百億萬而倍之乎？夫天地之道，至紘以大，尚猶節其章光，愛其神明，宇宙之財幾何，而乃以填…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: This is one who pays close attention to the fiscal administration of the state. If what he has systematically outlined were put into practice step by step, abundance and wealth would be achieved immediately. He is a talent in statecraft; record this.

Associate Examiner and Instructor Gu comments: Grounding his argument in the virtue of frugality, he sufficiently understands the affairs of the times.

Associate Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: The whole story of fiscal accounting is expounded almost exhaustively.

Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: This policy essay is beneficial to those in charge of fiscal administration; it ought to be recorded.

Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Weighing current affairs, his analysis and planning are sound and appropriate.

Wealth is indeed difficult to speak of! If one leaves it alone and makes no plan for it, there is great depletion; if one suddenly rises to tighten control over it, harsh exactions are difficult to carry out; if one merely follows old registers, surpluses and deficits cannot be verified; and if at times one resorts to methods of overt coercion and covert intimidation, that comes close to extracting revenue beyond the registers and making enemies of the people. That being so, is there truly no art to managing wealth?

Wealth is like water: when channeled it flows, but if channeled excessively it runs dry; when stored it stays still, but if stored excessively it stagnates. Therefore, regulating expenditures is simply a matter of matching them to the regulation of revenues. In a household of several mouths, with daily meals and monthly savings, if the master counts on his fingers and calculates in his mind, grasping the surplus and measuring out expenses accordingly, he can go his whole life without hardship. If what is gained in the morning is squandered by evening, wasting nine parts out of ten without knowing whether even one part in ten remains, then even Ji Ran 計然 or Yi Dun 猗頓 would immediately fall into distress—how much more so the vastness of the Empire, where those who depend on provisions multiply it by thousands, millions, and tens of thousands of millions? Now, the Way of Heaven and Earth is supremely vast and great, yet it still moderates its radiant light and cherishes its numinous vitality. How much wealth is there in the universe, that it should be used to fill…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
谿壑之欲塞江湖之漏哉古今言理財者
始於成周考之地官所隸若府史胥徒師
瞽眠瞭廩遺稍委之官以保養萬民者甚
設而大司空總土地所生料人民所出復
辨其山林川澤丘陵墳衍原隰之名物而
登之籍是會計之祖也間嘗按而求之兵
非不足也而比閭族黨遞相爲伍則犒食
不煩民官非不具也而卿大夫士等其功
緒以次而世之土爲祿入則廩餼不外索
===
其所爲上供者自祭祀宴饗匪頒好用公
旬之外不及焉固非如後世餒其家鬼而
淫於外神糜其祿食而疲民於枯魚之肆
也乃周公猶心憂之九賦以斂財賄自邦
中以至幣餘屬焉九式以節財用自祭祀
以至匪頒好用屬焉上自王后王世子下
至有司百執事經用具有等差無羨額此
雖不名爲會計而會計之防密於毫毛所
以約人主之侈德禁有司之苛征者無餘
punctuated: 谿壑之欲、塞江湖之漏哉！古今言理財者，始於成周。考之地官所隸，若府史、胥徒、師瞽、眠瞭、廩遺、稍委之官，以保養萬民者甚設；而大司空總土地所生，料人民所出，復辨其山林、川澤、丘陵、墳衍、原隰之名物而登之籍，是會計之祖也。間嘗按而求之：兵非不足也，而比閭族黨遞相爲伍，則犒食不煩民；官非不具也，而卿大夫士等其功緒，以次而世之土爲祿入，則廩餼不外索；其所爲上供者，自祭祀、宴饗、匪頒、好用、公旬之外不及焉。固非如後世餒其家鬼而淫於外神，糜其祿食而疲民於枯魚之肆也。乃周公猶心憂之：九賦以斂財賄，自邦中以至幣餘屬焉；九式以節財用，自祭祀以至匪頒、好用屬焉。上自王后、王世子，下至有司、百執事，經用具有等差，無羨額。此雖不名爲會計，而會計之防密於毫毛，所以約人主之侈德、禁有司之苛征者，無餘…
translation_en: …desires as insatiable as deep ravines, or plug leaks as vast as rivers and lakes? In ancient and modern times, discussions of fiscal management began with the flourishing Zhou dynasty. Examining those subordinate to the Minister of Education (Diguan), such as the officials in charge of archives, clerks, petty runners, blind musicians, sighted assistants, granaries, relief, and provisions, the offices established to nurture the myriad people were thoroughly instituted; meanwhile, the Minister of Works (Da Sikong) summarized what the land produced, calculated what the people yielded, and further distinguished the names and products of its mountains and forests, rivers and marshes, hills and mounds, embankments and plains, and plateaus and lowlands, entering them into the registers—this was the ancestor of accounting. I have at times examined and investigated this: troops were not insufficient, yet because the neighborhoods, villages, clans, and districts formed military units in turn, rewarding and feeding them did not trouble the people; officials were not lacking, yet because the ministers, grand masters, and servicemen were graded by their meritorious achievements and sequentially granted hereditary lands as their emoluments, their grain rations were not sought from outside; and what was provided as tribute to the ruler did not extend beyond sacrifices, banquets, discretionary distributions, favored uses, and public corvée. Truly, it was not like later ages, which starve their ancestral spirits while indulging excessively in extraneous deities, or waste their official emoluments while exhausting the people in the market of dried fish! Even so, the Duke of Zhou still worried about this in his heart: the Nine Exactions (jiufu) were used to collect wealth and goods, to which everything from the capital district down to surplus revenues belonged; the Nine Regulations (jiushi) were used to regulate expenditures, to which everything from sacrifices down to discretionary distributions and favored uses belonged. From the Queen and the Heir Apparent above, down to the authorities and the hundred functionaries below, regular expenditures all had graded distinctions without any surplus quota. Although this was not explicitly named "accounting," the safeguards of accounting were finer than the tip of a hair; as a means to restrain the extravagant inclinations of the ruler and prohibit harsh exactions by the authorities, there was no remaining…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
術矣漢稱去古未遠而周官典籍一逸於
十六國之分裂再逸於七國之從衡巳再
逸於祖龍之坑焚其所存什一於千伯者
厪厪副秦之博士官與藥醫種樹諸書竝
不茀廢故蕭相國營緝關中得以裪其殘
斷而張蒼爲計相更以列侯居公府領郡
國上計覆其出入猶有周官之遺焉自漢
以來言利者衆而利始鷙賦式良法蕩然
無存嗣是若曹璠李吉甫之上計於唐則
===
國計圖國計簿是巳若丁謂林特田况韓
絳蘇轍之上計於宋則景德祥符皇祐治
平元祐錄是巳顧當時淮蔡構兵澶淵要
幣靑苗變法則出利之孔或不勝其入利
之孔而元和靖康以後生齒蜉蝣於戈鋌
金繒罄而宗祚移卽具簿書奚裨哉
高皇帝戡定海內一統志所轄盡屬之版曹三
司使所條悉入之典故二百年來庶府淸
明黎氓蕃阜乃自嘉靖之季北迫胡南結
punctuated:
術矣。漢稱去古未遠，而《周官》典籍一逸於十六國之分裂，再逸於七國之從衡，巳再逸於祖龍之坑焚；其所存什一於千伯者，厪厪副秦之博士官，與藥醫、種樹諸書竝不茀廢。故蕭相國營緝關中，得以裪其殘斷；而張蒼爲計相，更以列侯居公府，領郡國上計，覆其出入，猶有《周官》之遺焉。自漢以來，言利者衆，而利始鷙，賦式良法蕩然無存。嗣是，若曹璠、李吉甫之上計於唐，則《國計圖》、《國計簿》是巳；若丁謂、林特、田况、韓絳、蘇轍之上計於宋，則《景德》、《祥符》、《皇祐》、《治平》、《元祐錄》是巳。顧當時淮蔡構兵，澶淵要幣，靑苗變法，則出利之孔或不勝其入利之孔；而元和、靖康以後，生齒蜉蝣於戈鋌，金繒罄而宗祚移，卽具簿書，奚裨哉！
高皇帝戡定海內，《一統志》所轄，盡屬之版曹；三司使所條，悉入之典故。二百年來，庶府淸明，黎氓蕃阜。乃自嘉靖之季，北迫胡，南結
translation_en:
…method left unused. The Han dynasty is said to have been not far removed from antiquity, yet the canonical records of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) were first lost during the division of the sixteen states, lost a second time amid the vertical and horizontal alliances of the Seven Warring States, and lost once again in the burying of scholars and burning of books by the Ancestral Dragon [Qin Shi Huang]. What survived—scarcely one part in a thousand or a hundred—was barely preserved as duplicate copies among the Erudites (boshi guan) of Qin, alongside books on medicine and arboriculture that were not discarded or destroyed. Thus, when Chancellor of State Xiao [Xiao He] administered and brought order to Guanzhong, he was able to gather up their broken fragments; and when Zhang Cang served as Accounting Chancellor (jixiang), and further resided in the ducal offices as a ranked marquis to oversee the annual accounts (shangji) submitted by the commanderies and kingdoms and verify their revenues and expenditures, there still remained something of the legacy of the Offices of Zhou. Since the Han dynasty, those who speak of profit have grown numerous, and the pursuit of profit began to turn rapacious, while the sound laws of taxation and expenditure vanished completely. Thereafter, as for the accounts submitted in the Tang dynasty by figures such as Cao Fan and Li Jifu, these were the Charts of State Finances (Guoji tu) and Registers of State Finances (Guoji bu); and as for the accounts submitted in the Song dynasty by figures such as Ding Wei, Lin Te, Tian Kuang, Han Jiang, and Su Zhe, these were the Accounting Records of the Jingde, Xiangfu, Huangyou, Zhiping, and Yuanyou Eras. Yet at those times, with military campaigns waged in Huai and Cai, tribute payments demanded at Chanyuan, and the New Policies of the Green Sprouts (qingmiao) enacted, the channels through which wealth flowed out perhaps could not keep pace with the channels through which wealth flowed in; and after the Yuanhe and Jingkang eras, the common people were as ephemeral as mayflies beneath spears and halberds, gold and silk were exhausted, and the imperial mandate shifted—even if accounting registers were complete, what help were they!

When the Exalted Emperor [Hongwu] pacified the realm within the seas, all territories under the jurisdiction of the Comprehensive Gazetteer (Yitong zhi) were assigned entirely to the Ministry of Revenue (bancao), and all regulations itemized by the Finance Commissioners (sansi shi) were incorporated into the statutory precedents. For two hundred years, the various government offices were pure and well-ordered, and the common people were numerous and prosperous. Yet since the end of the Jiajing reign, pressed in the north by the Hu nomads and entangled in the south with…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
越大司馬苦兵事士卒暴露赤白之囊一
日十道八輩上之旦夕仰急縣官土木嗣
興大司農調度不給自顧策亡出則使者
在道分部趣督亡休沐暇已而瓠子歌文
成進而水衡司宰所積若掃蓋物盛而詘
時極而轉固其當也賴
先皇帝行義未過德澤有加我
皇上踐祚首下奉天子民之
詔以節儉發聲於天下當軸者又條上故事督
===
考成嚴殿責核邊實省傜役汰冗員恤傳
置不數年間而
內庫之貫可朽太倉之粟可腐已乃主計大
臣猶然長慮却顧手編會計錄呈之
燕覽頒之天下綜理詳密仰符六典有非漢唐
宋可班者夫處全盛之時當阜殖之世胡
以若斯過計也蓋歲月旣久時勢漸殊條
例雖存沿革數易田額之有增與減也賦
額之有盈與縮也中外之需有約與浮也
punctuated: 越，大司馬苦兵事，士卒暴露，赤白之囊一日十道八輩上之，旦夕仰急縣官；土木嗣興，大司農調度不給，自顧策亡出，則使者在道，分部趣督，亡休沐暇。已而瓠子歌，文成進，而水衡、司宰所積若掃。蓋物盛而詘，時極而轉，固其當也。賴先皇帝行義未過，德澤有加。我皇上踐祚，首下奉天子民之詔，以節儉發聲於天下；當軸者又條上故事，督考成，嚴殿責，核邊實，省傜役，汰冗員，恤傳置。不數年間，而內庫之貫可朽，太倉之粟可腐已。乃主計大臣猶然長慮却顧，手編《會計錄》，呈之燕覽，頒之天下，綜理詳密，仰符《六典》，有非漢、唐、宋可班者。夫處全盛之時，當阜殖之世，胡以若斯過計也？蓋歲月旣久，時勢漸殊，條例雖存，沿革數易。田額之有增與減也，賦額之有盈與縮也，中外之需有約與浮也，
translation_en:
… the Yue in the south. The Minister of War (Da Sima) suffered under military affairs, while troops were exposed in the field; red-and-white emergency dispatch pouches were sent up to the throne ten times a day in eight batches, looking morning and evening to the imperial government for urgent relief. Major construction projects followed one after another, and the Minister of Revenue (Da Sinong) could not meet the demands of allocation and provisioning. Seeing no other policy recourse, envoys were constantly on the roads, dispatched by their respective bureaus to press and supervise collections without even a day's leave for rest and bathing. Before long, the Song of Huzi was sung [as the Yellow River breached its dikes] and "General Wencheng" [Daoist magicians and adepts] were advanced at court, so that the reserves accumulated by the Offices of Waters and Parks and the Directorate for Imperial Manufactories were swept clean. Indeed, when things reach their peak they decline, and when times reach an extreme they turn; this is naturally how it must be.

Thankfully, the Late Emperor practiced righteousness without excess and bestowed ever greater virtuous beneficence. When Our August Emperor ascended the throne, he first issued an edict on honoring Heaven and cherishing the people as his children, proclaiming frugality across the empire. Those at the pivot of government also submitted itemized precedents: supervising the verification of official accomplishments (kaocheng), strictly enforcing penalties for poor performance, auditing frontier realities, reducing corvée labor, eliminating superfluous personnel, and showing compassion for the postal relay system. Within a few years, the strings of cash in the Inner Treasuries were left to rot and the grain in the Grand Granaries was left to spoil.

Yet the chief ministers in charge of fiscal administration still took long-term thought and looked back with caution, personally compiling the Record of Fiscal Accounting (Kuaiji lu), presenting it for the Emperor's leisure perusal, and promulgating it throughout the realm. Its comprehensive organization is detailed and precise, conforming above to the Six Statutes (Liudian), such that the Han, Tang, and Song cannot be ranked alongside it. Now, situated in an age of complete flourishing and an era of abundant prosperity, why should one take such seemingly excessive precautions? It is because as the years and months have grown long, the times and circumstances have gradually changed; although the regulations remain, institutional evolutions have repeatedly altered them. Land quotas have experienced increases and decreases; tax quotas have experienced surpluses and shortfalls; expenditures within the court and in the provinces have been sometimes thrifty and sometimes extravagant; …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
内庫之類如
上供也賜給也奉養之類如
宗藩也戚里也武臣也歲餉之類如繕邊也
贍兵也市虜也
會典所載幾踰倍半自玆年愈久則費愈增
費愈增則賦愈急加以吏胥舞文豪强去
籍即欲考核往昔而且茫然矣况
會典統志非均輸專籍也不足以盡戸事項
故通計萬曆十年之例編爲是錄勒成四
===
十三卷首之以舊額見額繼之以歲入歲
出大者若邊鎮漕屯小者若茶鹽鈔課靡
不畢舉冀
皇上一覽瞭然在目且
頒行中外所司以垂永據即所稱九賦九式奚
遜焉愚甞伏而思之今天下度田非加損
也山林川陂非減於昔也稅侯王之廬筭
筐販之緡差量非不纖悉也而其中消息
興革月異歲殊數年間領度支者旦暮案
punctuated:
内庫之類，如上供也、賜給也；奉養之類，如宗藩也、戚里也、武臣也；歲餉之類，如繕邊也、贍兵也、市虜也，《會典》所載，幾踰倍半。自玆年愈久則費愈增，費愈增則賦愈急，加以吏胥舞文，豪强去籍，即欲考核往昔，而且茫然矣。况《會典》、《統志》非均輸專籍也，不足以盡戸事。頃故通計萬曆十年之例，編爲是錄，勒成四十三卷，首之以舊額、見額，繼之以歲入、歲出，大者若邊鎮、漕屯，小者若茶鹽、鈔課，靡不畢舉。冀皇上一覽，瞭然在目，且頒行中外所司，以垂永據，即所稱九賦、九式，奚遜焉？

愚甞伏而思之，今天下度田非加損也，山林川陂非減於昔也，稅侯王之廬、筭筐販之緡，差量非不纖悉也，而其中消息興革，月異歲殊。數年間，領度支者旦暮案…
translation_en:
…In the category of the Palace Treasuries, there are items such as imperial supplies and bestowal grants; in the category of stipends and maintenance, there are the imperial clansmen and princely establishments, the imperial relatives by marriage, and the military officials; in the category of annual military provisions, there are frontier repairs, the support of troops, and horse-markets and subsidies for the northern tribes. Compared to what is recorded in the Collected Statutes (Huidian), these have nearly more than doubled or increased by half again. From now on, the longer the years pass, the more expenditures will grow; and the more expenditures grow, the more urgent taxation will become. Add to this the manipulation of documents by clerks and subofficial functionaries and the destruction of registers by the powerful and local magnates—even if one wished to investigate and verify the past, one would be completely at a loss. Moreover, the Collected Statutes and the Comprehensive Gazetteer (Tongzhi) are not specialized registers of equitable transport and fiscal administration; they are insufficient to exhaustively cover the affairs of the Ministry of Revenue. Therefore, a comprehensive accounting has recently been made of the precedents and quotas up to the tenth year of the Wanli reign (1582) to compile this record, arranged into forty-three chapters (juan). It begins with the old quotas and current quotas, and continues with annual revenues and annual expenditures. Great matters such as the frontier commands, grain transport, and military state farms, and small matters such as tea, salt, and paper-money commercial taxes—none fail to be completely listed. The hope is that with a single glance His Majesty will have everything clearly before his eyes, and that by promulgating it to the responsible authorities in the capital and the provinces to serve as a permanent standard of reference, how should it be any inferior to what antiquity called the Nine Tributary Revenues and Nine Fiscal Formulas?

I have humbly pondered this: today, the measured lands of the empire have not been diminished; the mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes have not decreased from what they were in the past; taxing the lodges of marquises and princes and reckoning the strings of cash of basket-peddlers—such differential assessments are by no means lacking in minute thoroughness. Yet within all this, the waxing and waning, the initiatives and abolitions, differ from month to month and vary from year to year. Over the course of several years, those in charge of revenues and expenditures morning and night examine…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
計簿持金錢左盻操其贏右盻操其奇所
以佐縣官之緩急沃黎民之貨鏹備不冀
之虞遏無經之費者無不切至胡海內氓
庶富者日就朘削貧者不厭糟糠質子貸
穗以供租稅笞肉棰骨以急攀斂此其故
莫之能詰矣嗟夫財非天雨也賦非神輸
也陸輓川漕有時而息山冶海釜有時而
窮私求曲獻有時而禁而軍國有司經費
則旦暮歲月無巳時度支惡能不告困哉
===
然當內空外乏之時而求足國裕民之道
則當論其所以耗財者而不當復論其所
以興利者非謾也耗財之路可塞而興利
之計巳窮也
主上御寓以來十餘年間師旅未聞有所征發
禮樂未聞有所脩舉
諸侯王未聞與之剖符有所封建而纔一欲
謁
昭陵上
punctuated:
計簿，持金錢，左盻操其贏，右盻操其奇，所以佐縣官之緩急、沃黎民之貨鏹、備不冀之虞、遏無經之費者，無不切至。胡海內氓庶，富者日就朘削，貧者不厭糟糠，質子貸穗以供租稅，笞肉棰骨以急攀斂？此其故莫之能詰矣。嗟夫！財非天雨也，賦非神輸也。陸輓川漕，有時而息；山冶海釜，有時而窮；私求曲獻，有時而禁。而軍國有司經費，則旦暮歲月無巳時，度支惡能不告困哉？

然當內空外乏之時，而求足國裕民之道，則當論其所以耗財者，而不當復論其所以興利者，非謾也，耗財之路可塞，而興利之計巳窮也。主上御寓以來，十餘年間，師旅未聞有所征發，禮樂未聞有所脩舉，諸侯王未聞與之剖符有所封建，而纔一欲謁昭陵、上
translation_en:
…accounting ledgers and clutching cash, looking left to seize the surplus and looking right to grasp the remainder; in their efforts to assist the imperial government in emergencies, enrich the common people's stores of coin, prepare for unexpected crises, and curb unregulated expenditures, they have left nothing undone. Why then, among the common people within the seas, are the rich daily pared down and exploited, while the poor cannot even get their fill of dregs and husks, pawning their children and borrowing grain on the stalk to pay their land taxes, their flesh flogged and their bones beaten to hasten the exactions? The reason for this is something no one can fathom. Alas! Wealth does not rain down from heaven, nor are taxes delivered by spirits. Overland carting and riverine transport must at times cease; mountain smelters and sea-salt cauldrons must at times be exhausted; private solicitations and devious presentations of tribute must at times be prohibited. Yet the regular expenditures of the military, the state, and the authorities go on morning and night, month and year, without end—how then could the fiscal administration avoid declaring itself in distress?

Yet when the inner treasuries are empty and the outer provinces are depleted, if we seek the way to make the state sufficient and the people prosperous, we ought to discuss what drains wealth, and ought no longer to discuss what generates profit. This is no idle talk: the avenues that drain wealth can be blocked, whereas the schemes for generating profit have already been exhausted. In the more than ten years since the reigning sovereign assumed rule over the realm, we have not heard of armies being mobilized for campaigns, nor have we heard of rites and music being revived and instituted, nor have we heard of tallies being split with feudal princes to establish new enfeoffments; yet the moment there is a single wish to pay a visit to the Zhaoling Mausoleum, to present…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
太后壽及爲公主治裝卽三
詔稱乏至取司宰不足取冏寺又不足取太倉
借續之則連年進奉是果安在提空名自
炫而內自虛以畜百姓之怨失今不謹必
不支矣且司宰猶曰
皇上減膳之遺也冏寺所儲馬政所關已不可
輕秏而太倉則內贍百司外厭四夷
國家根本繫焉卽貫朽粟陳積空虛不用猶
日懇其匱今讀尚書洎臺省言事諸臣疏
===
===
則一歲所入未贍所出是何可以片語單
詞借也況頻歲河幸安瀾有如一日遷徙
胡以策之虜幸款塞今順義王且死有如
一日生心又胡以策之
親王封國諸公主第旦夕次第舉矣又胡以
策之故爲今計莫若矯之以儉矯之以儉
莫若倡之以
上奈之何
人君富有四海其尊無上其快意當前疇能咈
punctuated: 太后壽、及爲公主治裝，卽三詔稱乏。至取司宰不足，取冏寺，又不足，取太倉借續之。則連年進奉，是果安在？提空名自炫，而內自虛，以畜百姓之怨，失今不謹，必不支矣。且司宰猶曰皇上減膳之遺也；冏寺所儲，馬政所關，已不可輕秏；而太倉則內贍百司，外厭四夷，國家根本繫焉，卽貫朽粟陳，積空虛不用，猶日懇其匱。今讀尚書洎臺省言事諸臣疏，則一歲所入未贍所出，是何可以片語單詞借也！況頻歲河幸安瀾，有如一日遷徙，胡以策之？虜幸款塞，今順義王且死，有如一日生心，又胡以策之？親王封國、諸公主第，旦夕次第舉矣，又胡以策之？故爲今計，莫若矯之以儉；矯之以儉，莫若倡之以上。奈之何人君富有四海，其尊無上，其快意當前，疇能咈
translation_en: … present birthday felicitations to the Empress Dowager, or prepare a trousseau for a princess, three imperial edicts were immediately issued declaring a shortage of funds. It came to the point of drawing from the Imperial Butchery (Court of Imperial Entertainments), and when that was not enough, drawing from the Court of the Imperial Stud, and when that too was not enough, borrowing from the Taicang Treasury to make up the shortfall. Where, then, have all the tribute offerings submitted year after year actually gone? To flaunt an empty name while depleting oneself within, thereby accumulating the resentment of the common people—if we fail to exercise caution now, it will surely become unsustainable. Moreover, while the savings of the Imperial Butchery may still be called the surplus from Your Majesty's reduction of imperial meals, the reserves of the Court of the Imperial Stud are vital to the horse administration and already should not be lightly squandered. As for the Taicang Treasury, internally it supports the hundred agencies and externally it keeps the four barbarian peoples in check; the very foundation of the state depends upon it. Even if strings of cash were rotting and grain mouldering, piled up unused in idle spaces, one would still worry daily about its exhaustion. Yet today, reading the memorials of the Minister and the speaking officials of the Censorate and the Six Offices of Scrutiny, the revenues of an entire year do not suffice to cover the expenditures—how then can its funds be borrowed away with a mere phrase or a single word! Furthermore, in recent years the Yellow River has fortunately remained calm; if one day it should shift its course, with what strategy will we meet it? The northern caitiffs have fortunately submitted at the frontier, yet now the Shunyi Prince (Altan Khan) is dead; if one day they should conceive treacherous intentions, with what strategy will we meet it? The enfeoffment of Imperial Princes into their princedoms and the construction of mansions for the various princesses will soon be carried out one after another; with what strategy will we meet that? Therefore, in planning for the present, nothing is better than correcting this with frugality; and to correct it with frugality, nothing is better than having it initiated from above. Yet how can it be helped that the ruler of men possesses the wealth of the four seas and a dignity above all others; when his heart's pleasure is right before him, who could oppose…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
小制度而左右瞽御輩非從臾以侈無以
希寵售恩則儉之一言乃
人主之所慊而左右瞽御見以爲恡者故一二
大臣寓諷於會計庶幾量天地之數參
祖宗之規審
內府之盈虛察下里之疾苦節一朝之予而
存中人數十家之產節一事之費而留縣
官數十年之藏自是不侈於色則是編也
醉踞之屛女戎之戒也自是不侈於讒則
===
是編也蘇公之章巷伯之雅也自是不侈
於征討則是編也玉關之謝朱崖之罷也
自是不侈於馳射則是編也銜蹶之虞羗
夷之警也其益
主德裨
國計豈在周官下哉
聖天子旣躬行儉德於上賢公卿百執事孰不
奉清節以風四方而輶軒使者復明禁令
以導之約脩刑章以黜之浮丹青刻畫醲
punctuated:
小制度，而左右瞽御輩非從臾以侈，無以希寵售恩。則儉之一言，乃人主之所慊，而左右瞽御見以爲恡者。故一二大臣寓諷於會計，庶幾量天地之數，參祖宗之規，審內府之盈虛，察下里之疾苦，節一朝之予，而存中人數十家之產；節一事之費，而留縣官數十年之藏。自是不侈於色，則是編也，醉踞之屛、女戎之戒也；自是不侈於讒，則是編也，蘇公之章、巷伯之雅也；自是不侈於征討，則是編也，玉關之謝、朱崖之罷也；自是不侈於馳射，則是編也，銜蹶之虞、羗夷之警也。其益主德、裨國計，豈在《周官》下哉？
聖天子旣躬行儉德於上，賢公卿百執事孰不奉清節以風四方？而輶軒使者復明禁令以導之約，脩刑章以黜之浮。丹青刻畫、醲
translation_en:
…belittle institutional regulations [?], while the blind musicians and attendants at his side have no way to curry favor and peddle his grace except by egging him on to extravagance. Thus the single word "frugality" is something with which the ruler is dissatisfied, and which the attendants around him regard as stinginess. Therefore, one or two grand ministers have lodged remonstrance within the accounting records, in the hope that he will measure the resources of Heaven and Earth, consult the regulations of the Imperial Ancestors, examine the surpluses and deficits of the Inner Treasury, and observe the sufferings of the humble villages—curtailing the bestowals of a single morning to preserve the patrimony of dozens of middle-class families, and curtailing the expenditures of a single affair to retain decades of reserves for the state. If from this he is no longer extravagant in sensual pleasures, then this compilation will serve as a screen depicting drunken sprawling and a warning against the warfare of women. If from this he is no longer extravagant in heeding slander, then this compilation will serve as the stanzas of Duke Su and the "Xiangbo" ode of the Minor Odes. If from this he is no longer extravagant in military expeditions, then this compilation will serve as the refusal at the Jade Gate and the abandonment of Zhuya. If from this he is no longer extravagant in galloping and archery, then this compilation will serve as a precaution against abroken bit and a stumbling horse, and an admonition against the Qiang and Yi barbarians. In enhancing the ruler's virtue and benefiting the state's finances, how could it rank below the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan)?

Once the Sacred Son of Heaven personally practices the virtue of frugality above, who among the worthy dukes, ministers, and hundred officials will not uphold pure restraint in order to influence the four quarters? Moreover, the light-carriage emissaries will again clarify prohibitions and ordinances to guide the people toward restraint, and cultivate the penal statutes to dismiss their frivolity. Those who indulge in painted decorations, carved engravings, rich…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
肥綺靡者必法而後財不耗於奢緇黃技
巧聲色邪欹者必法而後財不耗於蠹蛇
賦鼠斂虎噬鷹摶者必法而後財不耗於
墨如是則生之有道用之有度委遺山積
泉貨川流成周九府之贏可立致耳釋此
不講而區區於膚剝髓啄之術民就窮而
賦日急國與民竝困雖驅管晏以握筭走
桑孔以運籌末之能矣
第三問
===
同考試官訓導范 批 遣求書之官專校書之任此編
購要務也經生能一一條對足覘博洽
同考試官訓導范 批 敘圖書興廢散合詞腴意博
考試官教諭湯 批 博古通今之士錄之以風後學
考試官教諭王 批 有裨右文之治者宜錄
天苞地符顯而圖書出焉蘭臺石室啓而
圖書聚焉夫圖書者豈世所稱纖眇長物
哉在人爲國華而在天則爲東壁宿東壁
banxin: 鄉試錄 七十五 孟養浩
punctuated:
肥、綺靡者必法，而後財不耗於奢；緇黃、技巧、聲色、邪欹者必法，而後財不耗於蠹；蛇賦、鼠斂、虎噬、鷹摶者必法，而後財不耗於墨。如是則生之有道，用之有度，委遺山積，泉貨川流，成周九府之贏可立致耳。釋此不講，而區區於膚剝髓啄之術，民就窮而賦日急，國與民竝困，雖驅管、晏以握筭，走桑、孔以運籌，末之能矣。

第三問
同考試官訓導范 〔批：遣求書之官，專校書之任，此編購要務也。經生能一一條對，足覘博洽。〕
同考試官訓導范 〔批：敘圖書興廢散合，詞腴意博。〕
考試官教諭湯 〔批：博古通今之士，錄之以風後學。〕
考試官教諭王 〔批：有裨右文之治者，宜錄。〕

天苞地符顯而圖書出焉，蘭臺石室啓而圖書聚焉。夫圖書者，豈世所稱纖眇長物哉？在人爲國華，而在天則爲東壁宿。東壁
translation_en:
… rich meats, and ornate silks must be subjected to the law, and only then will wealth not be wasted on extravagance; Buddhist monks and Daoist priests, clever artisans, sensual pleasures, and crooked and heterodox practices must be subjected to the law, and only then will wealth not be wasted on parasites; those who exact like snakes, gather like rats, devour like tigers, and seize like hawks must be subjected to the law, and only then will wealth not be wasted on corruption. If things are done in this manner, then wealth will be produced according to principle and expended with moderation; surplus grain will pile up like mountains and coined money will flow like rivers, so that the abundance of the Nine Treasuries of the accomplished Zhou dynasty can be immediately achieved. If we set this aside without discussing it, and busy ourselves exclusively with techniques that flay the skin and peck at the marrow, the people will fall into poverty while tax demands grow daily more urgent. With both the state and the people simultaneously in distress, even if one drove Guan Zhong 管仲 and Yan Ying 晏嬰 to ply the counting rods, or sent Sang Hongyang 桑弘羊 and Kong Jin 孔僅 to devise fiscal strategies, nothing could be done about it.

Third Question
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Fan 范 [comment: Dispatching officials to seek out books and assigning dedicated responsibilities for collating them are the essential tasks of compilation and acquisition. That the examination candidate is able to reply to each point item by item is sufficient to show his broad learning.]
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Fan 范 [comment: In recounting the rise and decline, dispersion and gathering of books and charts, the diction is rich and the meaning expansive.]
Examiner Instructor Tang 湯 [comment: A scholar conversant with both antiquity and the present; record this essay to inspire later students.]
Examiner Instructor Wang 王 [comment: This is beneficial to a governance that esteems civil culture; it ought to be recorded.]

When the auspices of Heaven and the tallies of Earth were manifested, charts and writings emerged; when the Orchid Terrace and the Stone Chamber were opened, charts and books were gathered together. Now, are charts and books merely what the world calls trivial and superfluous things? Among men, they are the splendor of the state, while in Heaven, they correspond to the Eastern Wall (Dongbi 東壁) constellation. The Eastern Wall …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
次奎室二星之中爲天下圖書秘府其星
明潤則圖書集道術行而世常泰其星失
色則圖書隱文士賤而世常否否泰汙隆
之運于圖書占之是惡可令一日廢哉然
是物也購之則蝟集匪購則散逸潛藏而
莫見編之則鱗次匪編則訛贋舛雜而無
章況未嘗求之而謂缺軼焉未嘗任之而
謂乏才焉謾也執事稱儒先語人有存歿
而學不息世有變故而書不亡誠然哉夫
===
典籍天下之神物也玉在山而草木潤珠
在淵而崖不枯典籍所聚不啻珠玉當有
卿雲輪囷金寶扶疎之氣時呵護焉是非
典籍之能爲神也古人往矣其精神在竹
素今雖去古遠甚而其神亦未嘗不日與
人俱所以炳日月流江河而不息不亡者
以此乃孔壁酉巖之藏或廢或興或聚或
散代異而世殊何哉惟其爲天下之神物
也物神則變見幻化猶干將莫邪焉俄而
punctuated: 次奎、室二星之中，爲天下圖書秘府。其星明潤，則圖書集，道術行，而世常泰；其星失色，則圖書隱，文士賤，而世常否。否泰汙隆之運，于圖書占之，是惡可令一日廢哉？然是物也，購之則蝟集，匪購則散逸潛藏而莫見；編之則鱗次，匪編則訛贋舛雜而無章。況未嘗求之而謂缺軼焉，未嘗任之而謂乏才焉，謾也。執事稱儒先語：「人有存歿而學不息，世有變故而書不亡。」誠然哉！夫典籍，天下之神物也。玉在山而草木潤，珠在淵而崖不枯。典籍所聚，不啻珠玉，當有卿雲輪囷、金寶扶疎之氣，時呵護焉。是非典籍之能爲神也，古人往矣，其精神在竹素，今雖去古遠甚，而其神亦未嘗不日與人俱。所以炳日月、流江河而不息不亡者，以此。乃孔壁、酉巖之藏，或廢或興，或聚或散，代異而世殊，何哉？惟其爲天下之神物也。物神則變見幻化，猶干將、莫邪焉，俄而
translation_en: …is situated between the two lunar mansions Kui and Shi, serving as the secret repository of books and charts for the entire realm. When its stars are bright and lustrous, books and charts gather together, the Way and its arts flourish, and the world is ever in harmony; when its stars lose their luster, books and charts go into hiding, men of letters are despised, and the world is ever in stagnation. Since the cycles of stagnation and harmony, of decline and flourishing, are divined from books and charts, how could they be allowed to fall into neglect for even a single day? Yet with these things, if one seeks to acquire them, they gather as thick as hedgehog spines; if one does not acquire them, they scatter and lie hidden where none can see them. If one compiles them, they are arranged as orderly as fish scales; if one does not compile them, they become corrupted, forged, confused, and devoid of order. Moreover, to claim that books are missing and lost without ever having sought them, or to claim that there is a lack of talent without ever having entrusted anyone with the task, is sheer deception. Your Excellency cites the words of a former Confucian worthy: "Men may live or die, yet learning does not cease; the world may undergo upheavals, yet books do not perish." How true indeed! Now, canonical texts and records are the numinous objects of the world. When jade is in the mountain, the grasses and trees are nourished; when pearls are in the deep pool, the banks do not wither. Where canonical texts and records gather, they are far more than pearls and jade; there is surely an aura of auspicious clouds curling upward and golden treasures branching out, constantly breathing protection over them. This is not because the physical texts themselves are able to be numinous. The ancients are gone, yet their spirit abides in bamboo slips and silk scrolls. Although the present is very far removed from antiquity, their spirit has never ceased to be with men day by day. The reason they shine like the sun and moon and flow like the Yangzi and Yellow River, never ceasing and never perishing, lies in this. Why is it, then, that the collections hidden in the wall of Confucius's house and in the caves of Mount You have at times fallen into ruin and at times flourished, at times gathered and at times scattered, varying from dynasty to dynasty and differing from age to age? It is precisely because they are the numinous objects of the world. When an object is numinous, its appearances and transformations are wondrous and unpredictable—just like the legendary swords Ganjiang and Moye, which in an instant…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
飛俄而沉俄而合俄而離張華雷煥不能
測也矧圖書者抉天地之秘洩元會之精
通陰陽鬼神之靈當其時則見不當其時
則隱乃其神則晶晶熒熒雖千百禩如一
日焉粵自上古俯龜疇以布畫仰鳥跡以
成文書契之設所從來遠矣周外史掌三
皇五帝之書楚左史讀墳典索丘之籍後
世藏書之祖校書之原此始睹矣哲人萎
而微言絕諸家百氏各以其說背馳而爭
===
鳴至於秦乃燔滅文章以愚黔首漢興除
挾書律開獻書路建藏書策置寫書官始
稱彬彬焉時歆承父業為輯略六藝略諸
子略詩賦兵書略術數方技略凡七至唐
兩都書分為四部曰經部史部子部集部
而裒帙至開元盛矣宋崇文館書設為六
庫曰東昭文一南集賢一西史館四而裒
帙至太平興國又盛矣歷代所藏靡有遺
佚而君子猶不能無訾議則以類例不明
punctuated: 飛，俄而沉，俄而合，俄而離，張華、雷煥不能測也。矧圖書者，抉天地之秘，洩元會之精，通陰陽鬼神之靈，當其時則見，不當其時則隱，乃其神則晶晶熒熒，雖千百禩如一日焉。粵自上古，俯龜疇以布畫，仰鳥跡以成文，書契之設，所從來遠矣。周外史掌《三皇》《五帝》之書，楚左史讀《墳》《典》《索》《丘》之籍，後世藏書之祖、校書之原，此始睹矣。哲人萎而微言絕，諸家百氏各以其說背馳而爭鳴。至於秦，乃燔滅文章以愚黔首。漢興，除挾書律，開獻書路，建藏書策，置寫書官，始稱彬彬焉。時歆承父業，為《輯略》、《六藝略》、《諸子略》、《詩賦》、《兵書略》、《術數》、《方技略》，凡七。至唐，兩都書分為四部，曰經部、史部、子部、集部，而裒帙至開元盛矣。宋崇文館書設為六庫，曰東昭文一、南集賢一、西史館四，而裒帙至太平興國又盛矣。歷代所藏，靡有遺佚，而君子猶不能無訾議，則以類例不明、
translation_en: …soaring up, now sinking down, now uniting, now parting—even Zhang Hua 張華 and Lei Huan 雷煥 could not fathom them. How much more so with charts and books, which unlock the secrets of heaven and earth, reveal the essence of cosmic epochs, and communicate with the numinous power of yin and yang, ghosts and spirits! When the time is right, they appear; when the time is not right, they remain hidden. Yet their spirit shines brightly and radiantly, remaining as if a single day even across hundreds and thousands of years. Ever since high antiquity, when sages looked down at the tortoise-shell divisions to lay out the trigrams and looked up at bird tracks to form written characters, the institution of writing and tallies has had a long history indeed. The External Scribe (waishi) of Zhou took charge of the books of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, and the Left Scribe (zuoshi) of Chu could read the Three Fen, Five Dian, Eight Suo, and Nine Qiu; here we first see the ancestors of book-collecting and the origins of text-collation in later ages. When the wise men withered away and subtle words ceased, the various schools and hundred masters each ran counter to one another with their doctrines and contended for a voice. Coming down to Qin, they burned and destroyed literary writings in order to keep the black-headed commoners in ignorance. When the Han arose, it repealed the statute against possessing books, opened the way for presenting books to the throne, established plans for storing books, and instituted officials for copying books; only then could culture be described as flourishing in balanced refinement. At the time, Liu Xin 劉歆 carried on his father's enterprise and compiled the "General Summary" (Jilüe), "Summary of the Six Arts" (Liuyi lüe), "Summary of the Masters" (Zhuzi lüe), "[Summary of] Songs and Rhapsodies" (Shifu [lüe]), "Summary of Military Books" (Bingshu lüe), "[Summary of] Divination and Calculations" (Shushu [lüe]), and "Summary of Recipes and Techniques" (Fangji lüe)—seven in all. By the Tang dynasty, the books in the two capitals were divided into four divisions—namely the Classics division, Histories division, Masters division, and Collected Works division—and the gathering of volumes reached its peak in the Kaiyuan era (713–741). In the Song dynasty, the books of the Institute for the Veneration of Literature (Chongwen guan) were arranged in six storehouses—namely one in the east for the Institute for the Glorification of Literature (Zhaowen guan), one in the south for the Academy of Scholarly Worthies (Jixian yuan), and four in the west for the Historiography Institute (Shiguan)—and the gathering of volumes reached another peak in the Taiping Xingguo era (976–984). What was stored across successive dynasties left nothing omitted or lost, yet gentlemen still could not help finding fault; this was because the classification principles were unclear and…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
圖書失記也夫書之類例若將兵然部伍
嚴雖多亦治部伍失雖寡亦紛禮一也凡
七種而以儀禮雜周官者非也春秋一也
凡五家而以啖趙雜公穀者非也推此而
它可知矣惟不明於類例其勢必至脫略
唐部有星書而無風雲氣候書宋庫有風
雲氣候書而無日月書推此而它可知矣
夾漈鄭氏謂七略苟簡六庫荒唐蓋有激
於此乎巳自別爲一十二類散之爲四百
===
三十二種科條縷析覽者病焉則又不若
七略之疎而簡矣又謂書有名亡而實不
亡者如文言寓於周易鼓吹寄於樂府之
類是也有闕於前而完於後者如淵明集
梁僅五卷隋增於梁而唐又倍於隋之類
是也有不出於當時而出於後代者如孔
安國舜典出晉連山易出唐之類是也鄭
氏之意以求書者未得其方校書者或失
其職故詳示凡例俾後代知倣而緝之其
punctuated: 圖書失記也。夫書之類例，若將兵然：部伍嚴，雖多亦治；部伍失，雖寡亦紛。禮一也，凡七種，而以《儀禮》雜《周官》者，非也；《春秋》一也，凡五家，而以啖、趙雜公、穀者，非也。推此而它可知矣。惟不明於類例，其勢必至脫略。唐部有星書，而無風雲氣候書；宋庫有風雲氣候書，而無日月書。推此而它可知矣。夾漈鄭氏謂「七略苟簡，六庫荒唐」，蓋有激於此乎？巳自別爲一十二類，散之爲四百三十二種，科條縷析，覽者病焉，則又不若七略之疎而簡矣。又謂：書有名亡而實不亡者，如《文言》寓於《周易》、《鼓吹》寄於《樂府》之類是也；有闕於前而完於後者，如《淵明集》梁僅五卷，隋增於梁，而唐又倍於隋之類是也；有不出於當時而出於後代者，如孔安國《舜典》出晉、《連山易》出唐之類是也。鄭氏之意，以求書者未得其方，校書者或失其職，故詳示凡例，俾後代知倣而緝之，其…
translation_en: …and charts and books were left unrecorded. Now, the classification principles of books are like commanding troops: when the ranks and files are strict, even if numerous they are in order; when the ranks and files are lost, even if few they are in confusion. The Rites (Li) are one, comprising seven kinds in all, yet to mix the Ceremonials (Yili) with the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) is wrong; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) are one, comprising five schools in all, yet to mix Dan [Zhu 啖助] and Zhao [Kuang 趙匡] with Gongyang and Guliang is wrong. Reasoning from this, the rest can be known. Only when one is unclear about classification principles will the trend inevitably lead to omissions. The Tang divisions had books on stars, yet lacked books on wind, clouds, and weather; the Song repositories had books on wind, clouds, and weather, yet lacked books on the sun and moon. Reasoning from this, the rest can be known. When Master Zheng of Jiaji [Zheng Qiao 鄭樵] said that "the Seven Summaries (Qilüe) are careless and simplistic, and the Six Repositories (Liuku) are absurd," was he not provoked by this? He himself distinguished them into twelve main classes, subdividing them into four hundred and thirty-two subcategories; the headings were analyzed in such minute detail that readers found it burdensome, so in turn it was not as good as the broad simplicity of the Seven Summaries. He also said: there are books whose titles are lost while their substance is not lost, such as the "Commentary on the Words of the Text" (Wenyan) being lodged within the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi), or the "Drum and Flute Songs" (Guchui) being attached to the Music Bureau Poems (Yuefu); there are those that were incomplete in earlier times and complete in later times, such as the Collected Works of [Tao] Yuanming (Yuanming ji), which in the Liang dynasty was only five juan, increased in the Sui over the Liang, and doubled again in the Tang over the Sui; and there are those that did not appear in their own time but appeared in later ages, such as Kong Anguo's 孔安國 "Canon of Shun" (Shundian) appearing in the Jin, or the Lianshan Changes (Lianshan yi) appearing in the Tang. Master Zheng's intention was that because those who sought out books had not grasped the proper method and those who collated books had sometimes failed in their duty, he set forth the general principles in detail so that later generations would know how to model themselves on them and compile them—how…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
勤與嗟夫求書者能體鄭氏之志必無掛
漏之虞校書者能循鄭氏之法必無紕繆
之患奚至泯棼失傳也
高皇以馬上得天下不欲以馬上治改元未幾
命有司訪求古今書籍藏之
祕室又
遣使購遺書
頒行天下及脩治太學藏本
文皇奠鼎之初徵召名儒輯四書五經大全梓
===
布中外又開局纂著
永樂大典繕寫寶貯以備
昭代制作
二祖稽古右文之心皇皇若弗及而當時名山
石屋之遺物充
天府較漢唐宋去萬矣然子史百家撰記諸書
行於世者攷之宋崇文總目十無一焉攷
之漢唐藝文志所載百無一焉誠有如執
事所云者此其故謂何大都天下之物不
punctuated:
勤與！嗟夫！求書者能體鄭氏之志，必無掛漏之虞；校書者能循鄭氏之法，必無紕繆之患，奚至泯棼失傳也！

高皇以馬上得天下，不欲以馬上治。改元未幾，命有司訪求古今書籍，藏之祕室。又遣使購遺書，頒行天下，及脩治太學藏本。文皇奠鼎之初，徵召名儒，輯《四書》《五經大全》，梓布中外；又開局纂著《永樂大典》，繕寫寶貯，以備昭代制作。二祖稽古右文之心，皇皇若弗及，而當時名山石屋之遺，物充天府，較漢、唐、宋去萬矣。然子、史、百家撰記諸書行於世者，攷之宋《崇文總目》，十無一焉；攷之漢、唐《藝文志》所載，百無一焉。誠有如執事所云者，此其故謂何？大都天下之物，不
translation_en:
…how diligent indeed! Alas! If those who seek out books can embody Master Zheng's [Zheng Qiao's] intention, there will surely be no worry of omissions; if those who collate books can follow Master Zheng's methods, there will surely be no trouble of errors and discrepancies. How then could books ever fall into oblivion and confusion or be lost to transmission!

The Exalted Emperor [Emperor Taizu, Hongwu] won the empire on horseback, yet he did not wish to govern it from horseback. Not long after proclaiming his reign era, he ordered the authorities to search for ancient and modern books and store them in the Imperial Library. He also dispatched envoys to purchase surviving books, promulgated them throughout the empire, and restored the editions held in the Directorate of Education (Taixue). At the beginning of the Cultured Emperor's [Emperor Chengzu, Yongle] establishment of his reign, he summoned renowned Confucian scholars to compile the Complete Meaning of the Four Books and Five Classics (Sishu Wujing daquan), printing and distributing them inside and outside the capital. He also opened a bureau to compile the Grand Canon of the Yongle Era (Yongle dadian), having it finely copied and treasured in storage to provide for the literary and institutional productions of our illustrious dynasty. The minds of our Two Progenitors in investigating antiquity and esteeming culture were urgently solicitous, as if fearing they could not do enough; and at that time, the surviving works from famous mountains and stone chambers filled the imperial storehouses, surpassing those of the Han, Tang, and Song by ten thousandfold. Yet among the writings and records of the Masters, the Histories, and the Hundred Schools currently circulating in the world, if one checks them against the Song General Catalogue of the Venerating Literature Library (Chongwen zongmu), not one in ten remains; if one checks them against what is recorded in the "Treatises on Literature" (Yiwen zhi) of the Han and Tang histories, not one in a hundred remains. It is truly just as Your Excellency has stated—and what may be said to be the reason for this? Broadly speaking, as for the things of the world, without…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有廢何以興不有散何以合昔奇章公謂
自周迄隋書籍已遭五厄况隋唐以後變
故滋多胡元以還散亡益甚書缺簡脫奚
惑哉
國初購募雖張搜訪未廣一旦欲遺編逸錄
林軸麗麗而與前代埒固難矣第至
今日文教大明而武庫所儲猶然絀焉則購
求之法未講而校讎之職未脩也夫求書
之官不可不遣校書之任不可不專乃自
===
古記矣蓋縕緗未富貴在弋蒐故漢遣陳
農唐遣牛弘已而又遣苗發宋遣孫逢吉
李龜祥歷歷可指也今二百年來有奉
詔購募者乎則知求書猶未廣矣典籍旣彙貴
在讎勘故司馬遷世爲史官劉歆卒父前
業虞世南顏師古相繼爲秘書監令狐德
棻三朝脩史班班可覩也今二百年來有
世守專官者乎則知校書猶未精矣夫謂
求書之道有八曰卽類以求也旁類以求
punctuated: 有廢何以興？不有散何以合？昔奇章公謂自周迄隋，書籍已遭五厄。况隋唐以後，變故滋多；胡元以還，散亡益甚。書缺簡脫，奚惑哉？國初購募雖張，搜訪未廣，一旦欲遺編逸錄，林軸麗麗，而與前代埒，固難矣。第至今日，文教大明，而武庫所儲猶然絀焉，則購求之法未講，而校讎之職未脩也。夫求書之官不可不遣，校書之任不可不專，乃自古記矣。蓋縕緗未富，貴在弋蒐，故漢遣陳農，唐遣牛弘，已而又遣苗發，宋遣孫逢吉、李龜祥，歷歷可指也。今二百年來，有奉詔購募者乎？則知求書猶未廣矣。典籍旣彙，貴在讎勘，故司馬遷世爲史官，劉歆卒父前業，虞世南、顏師古相繼爲秘書監，令狐德棻三朝脩史，班班可覩也。今二百年來，有世守專官者乎？則知校書猶未精矣。夫謂求書之道有八：曰卽類以求也，旁類以求
translation_en:
… fall into ruin, how can they flourish? If they do not scatter, how can they be gathered together? In the past, the Duke of Qizhang (Niu Hong 牛弘) remarked that from the Zhou down to the Sui, books had already suffered five great catastrophes. How much more so since the Sui and Tang, when upheavals and calamities multiplied, and from the Mongol Yuan onward, when dispersion and loss grew even more severe! That books are incomplete and bamboo slips have come unbound—what is there to wonder at?

At the founding of the dynasty, although calls to purchase and solicit books were issued, the search and inquiry were not yet wide-ranging. To wish all at once that surviving compilations and lost records should stand in resplendent forests of scrolls to rival those of former dynasties was assuredly difficult. Yet down to the present day, when civil teaching shines in full brilliance, what is stored in the imperial repositories remains scanty. This is because the methods for purchasing and seeking books have not been thoroughly studied, and the office of collation has not been properly cultivated.

Indeed, that officials must be dispatched to seek out books, and that the responsibility for collating books must be made specialized, has been recorded since antiquity. When the store of books and scrolls is not yet rich, what matters most is hunting them down and gathering them in. Thus the Han dispatched Chen Nong 陳農; the Tang dispatched Niu Hong 牛弘 [Note: historically Sui, here attributed to Tang], and later again dispatched Miao Fa 苗發; and the Song dispatched Sun Fengji 孫逢吉 and Li Guixiang 李龜祥—all of which can be pointed to one by one. Over the past two hundred years, has there been anyone who received an imperial decree to purchase and solicit books? From this we know that the search for books is still not wide-ranging.

Once canonical and historical texts have been assembled, what matters most is collating and verifying them. Thus Sima Qian 司馬遷 held the office of Grand Astrologer from generation to generation; Liu Xin 劉歆 completed his father's prior undertaking; Yu Shinan 虞世南 and Yan Shigu 顏師古 succeeded one another as Director of the Palace Library (Bishu jian); and Linghu Defen 令狐德棻 compiled histories across three reigns—all of which can be clearly observed. Over the past two hundred years, has there been anyone holding a specialized office preserved across generations? From this we know that the collation of books is still not precise.

Now, as for the statement that there are eight ways of seeking books: they are called seeking by direct category, seeking by adjacent category, …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也因地以求也因家以求也因人以求也
因代以求也求之公也求之私也大要謂
旣得於此復參於彼旣得於遠復取諸近
旣得於官復採諸民旣得於專門復徵諸
雜見務在收貯博富耳此求書之官不可
不知也謂編書之難有五曰傳記之難也
雜家之難也小說之難也雜史之難也故
事之難也大要疑其可以合可以無合可
以分可以無分可以釋注可以無釋注可
===
以人類書亦可以書類人務在用心精密
耳此校書之官不可不講也今大行人所
至循故購求歸
朝之日彙寘本署則周官外史之遺也第問
其書果探之禹穴乎果索之汲冢而搜之
廬嶽乎萬一灾朽蕪穢而令之充東觀之
儲必無當矣為今計者宜分地遣官設格
置募或藩邸如河間之好古者購之或世
家如鄴侯之挿架者購之或博物家如張
punctuated: 也，因地以求也，因家以求也，因人以求也，因代以求也，求之公也，求之私也。大要謂：旣得於此，復參於彼；旣得於遠，復取諸近；旣得於官，復採諸民；旣得於專門，復徵諸雜見，務在收貯博富耳。此求書之官不可不知也。謂編書之難有五：曰傳記之難也，雜家之難也，小說之難也，雜史之難也，故事之難也。大要疑其可以合，可以無合；可以分，可以無分；可以釋注，可以無釋注；可以人類書，亦可以書類人，務在用心精密耳。此校書之官不可不講也。今大行人所至，循故購求，歸朝之日，彙寘本署，則《周官》外史之遺也。第問其書，果探之禹穴乎？果索之汲冢而搜之廬嶽乎？萬一灾朽蕪穢，而令之充東觀之儲，必無當矣。為今計者，宜分地遣官，設格置募：或藩邸如河間之好古者購之，或世家如鄴侯之挿架者購之，或博物家如張
translation_en:
… searching according to region, searching according to school or family, searching according to person, searching according to dynasty, searching in public collections, and searching in private collections. The general principle is that once one has obtained a work here, one cross-checks it against those there; once one has obtained works from afar, one also draws them from nearby; once one has obtained works from the government, one also gathers them from the common people; and once one has obtained works from specialized masters, one also seeks them in miscellaneous sources—all with the aim of making the collection broad and rich. This is what officials charged with seeking books must not fail to understand.

As for the assertion that there are five difficulties in compiling and cataloging books: they are the difficulty of biographies and records, the difficulty of miscellaneous thinkers, the difficulty of minor talks and tales, the difficulty of unofficial histories, and the difficulty of precedents and old affairs. The general issue is the uncertainty over whether works may be combined or not combined, whether they may be divided or not divided, whether they may be annotated or not annotated, and whether books should be classified by person or persons classified by book—all requiring that one apply one's mind with utmost precision. This is what officials charged with collating books must not fail to study carefully.

Nowadays, wherever Messengers go, they follow established precedent in purchasing and seeking out books, and on the day they return to court they assemble and deposit them in their office; this is a vestige of the Scribes for External Affairs in the *Offices of Zhou* (Zhouguan). Yet if we ask about these books: were they truly explored from the Cave of Yu? Were they truly sought from the Tomb of Ji or searched out from Mount Lu? Should the woodblocks be ruined and rotted [?] or the texts coarse and corrupt, allowing them to fill the stores of the Eastern Pavilion would surely be inappropriate.

To plan for the present, we ought to dispatch officials by region and establish regulations and rewards to solicit books: whether from princely establishments like Prince Xian of Hejian, who loved antiquity, we should acquire them; or from hereditary houses like the Marquis of Ye (Li Mi 李泌), with his packed bookshelves, we should acquire them; or from men of broad learning like Zhang…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
華之縹乗者購之或著述家如司馬談之
藏名山者購之或學究家如伏生之匿壁
間者購之或勳臣家如侯君集之好書者
購之或隱逸家如惠施之五車者購之或
編氓家如越裴氏白下曹氏之聚書者購
之其檢括不稱者若蕭穎士即聽劾免而
又若唐之或以爵勸或以鏹購或以縑易
即有偽贋毋遽斥罰所謂與其過而廢之
也寧過而立之則異典畢出而燦然充棟
===
矣今學士舍人所居稱玉堂清秘而十館
列置纂脩不計歲月則唐宋校書之任也
第考其實果能紬金匱之藏乎果能秉太
乙之藜而訂金根之誤乎萬一驕駁謬戾
而令之部西崑之帙必不勝矣為今計者
宜分館列職計日受函業經術者專之如
梁丘賀夏侯勝董仲舒匡衡大小戴之於
五經業韜鈐者專之如任宏之於兵書業
博雜者專之如尹咸之於數術李柱國之
punctuated: 華之縹乗者購之，或著述家如司馬談之藏名山者購之，或學究家如伏生之匿壁間者購之，或勳臣家如侯君集之好書者購之，或隱逸家如惠施之五車者購之，或編氓家如越裴氏、白下曹氏之聚書者購之。其檢括不稱者，若蕭穎士，即聽劾免；而又若唐之或以爵勸，或以鏹購，或以縑易，即有偽贋，毋遽斥罰，所謂「與其過而廢之也，寧過而立之」，則異典畢出而燦然充棟矣。今學士、舍人所居稱玉堂清秘，而十館列置，纂脩不計歲月，則唐、宋校書之任也。第考其實，果能紬金匱之藏乎？果能秉太乙之藜而訂金根之誤乎？萬一驕駁謬戾，而令之部西崑之帙，必不勝矣。為今計者，宜分館列職，計日受函：業經術者專之，如梁丘賀、夏侯勝、董仲舒、匡衡、大小戴之於《五經》；業韜鈐者專之，如任宏之於兵書；業博雜者專之，如尹咸之於數術、李柱國之
translation_en:
… Hua's (張華) carts of pale-blue silk scrolls; or from the families of authors, such as Sima Tan (司馬談), who hid his works in famous mountains; or from the families of pedants and classicists, such as Master Fu (伏生), who concealed his texts inside a wall; or from the families of meritorious ministers, such as Hou Junji (侯君集), who was fond of books; or from the families of recluses, such as Hui Shi (惠施), who possessed five cartloads of books; or from the families of registered commoners, such as the Pei clan (裴氏) of Yue and the Cao clan (曹氏) of Baixia, who amassed book collections. Those who fail to perform their duties in searching and collecting, like Xiao Yingshi (蕭穎士), should immediately be impeached and dismissed. Moreover, as in the Tang dynasty, we should encourage contributors with official rank, purchase books with strings of cash, or trade fine silk for them. Even if there are forgeries among them, do not hastily reject or punish the bringers—following the saying, "Rather than erring on the side of abolishing it, it is better to err on the side of establishing it." Then rare canons will all emerge and brilliantly fill the rafters.

Today, the quarters where the Academician (學士) and Drafters (舍人) reside are called the Jade Hall and Pure Secretariat, and the ten historiographical institutes are arrayed in place, compiling and editing without reckoning the months and years—this is the book-collating duty of the Tang and Song dynasties. Yet if we examine the reality, are they truly able to draw out the treasures of the Golden Coffer? Are they truly able to hold the cane of the Great Unity and correct the error of "Golden Root" (金根)? If by some chance they are arrogant,雜-minded [unruly/heterogeneous], and perverse, and we have them classify the volumes of Xikun, they will certainly not be equal to the task. In planning for the present, we should divide the institutes, array the posts, and have them receive book-cases according to a daily schedule. Let those who specialize in classical scholarship have exclusive charge of their field, just as Liangqiu He (梁丘賀), Xiahou Sheng (夏侯勝), Dong Zhongshu (董仲舒), Kuang Heng (匡衡), and the Elder and Younger Dai (大小戴) did with the Five Classics; let those who specialize in military strategy have exclusive charge of theirs, just as Ren Hong (任宏) did with military treatises; let those who specialize in broad and miscellaneous learning have exclusive charge of theirs, just as Yin Xian (尹咸) did with the arts of calculation and Li Zhuguo (李柱國) did…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於方伎乃意見齟齬者倣白虎石渠
親制臨决而又如唐之月給楮季給墨歲給賴
材即有異同毋相標榜人自為荀楊家自
為政駿則汗青可就而釐然成帙矣然此
猶陳其末耳至本原之地又在
人主注意典籍崇尚文儒勤甲乙之觀辨萍釗
之誤而後奉購求司校讎者靡不淬厲興
起耳譚者又謂
帝王之學與韋布殊不宜雜亂耳目
===
經筵講讀自四書五經外無復以它書進夫
凡謂之書皆可益人智意羽翼聖道宣鬯
皇猷苟非旁搜遠觀何以籠宇宙羅古今窮幽
索賾標綵散縟以新
一代文治乎夫上不好則下不習即今博士弟
子六館諸生誰非業文者哉顧日事呫嗶
工帖括以求速化而兄勉其弟父課其子
羣然以博古通今為謬世戾俗之具青緗
素業蕩然亡有沿至於今將併經傳之旨
punctuated: 於方伎。乃意見齟齬者，倣白虎、石渠，親制臨决；而又如唐之月給楮、季給墨、歲給賴材。即有異同，毋相標榜，人自為荀、楊，家自為政、駿，則汗青可就，而釐然成帙矣。然此猶陳其末耳，至本原之地，又在人主注意典籍，崇尚文儒，勤甲乙之觀，辨萍釗之誤，而後奉購求、司校讎者，靡不淬厲興起耳。譚者又謂帝王之學與韋布殊，不宜雜亂耳目，經筵講讀，自《四書》、《五經》外，無復以它書進。夫凡謂之書，皆可益人智意，羽翼聖道，宣鬯皇猷。苟非旁搜遠觀，何以籠宇宙、羅古今、窮幽索賾、標綵散縟，以新一代文治乎？夫上不好則下不習，即今博士弟子、六館諸生，誰非業文者哉？顧日事呫嗶，工帖括以求速化，而兄勉其弟、父課其子，羣然以博古通今為謬世戾俗之具，青緗素業蕩然亡有，沿至於今，將併經傳之旨…
translation_en:
… over medicine and divination. As for cases where opinions conflict, one should follow the precedent of the White Tiger Hall (Baihu) and the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu), with the sovereign personally presiding to render a final decision; and furthermore, as in the Tang dynasty, supply paper monthly, ink quarterly, and official stipends [?] and materials annually. Even if there are differences and similarities in view, they should not form rival factions for mutual self-promotion; when each person strives to be a Xun Kuang 荀況 or Yang Xiong 揚雄, and each household a Liu Xiang 劉向 (Zizheng 子政) or Liu Xin 劉歆 (Zijun 子駿), then the bamboo slips can be completed and neatly arranged into volumes. Yet this still merely sets forth the secondary details. When it comes to the fundamental source, it lies in the ruler fixing his attention upon canonical texts and historical records, esteeming literary scholars, being diligent in the nightly reading of the A and B divisions of books, and distinguishing scribal errors like "ping" 萍 for "ping" 苹 or "zhao" 釗 for "jian" 劍; only then will those charged with procuring books and overseeing collation all be spurred to rouse themselves to action.

Commentators also claim that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoners in coarse cloth and leather, and that their ears and eyes should not be cluttered and confused; thus in the Classics Colloquium (jingyan) lectures and readings, apart from the Four Books and Five Classics, no other books are presented. Yet anything called a book can enlarge a person's wisdom and thought, serve as wings to the Way of the Sages, and propagate and expand the august plan of the sovereign. If one does not search widely and observe far, how can one encompass the cosmos, net antiquity and the present, fathom the obscure and probe the arcane, and display brilliance and scatter richly adorned patterns so as to renew the civil governance of an entire era?

Now if the superior does not care for something, those below will not practice it. Even today, among the disciples of the Erudites (boshi dizi) and the students of the Six Halls (liuguan zhusheng) in the Directorate of Education, who is not engaged in literary studies? Yet they spend their days merely droning over texts and perfecting stereotypical examination essays (tiegua) in pursuit of rapid advancement, while elder brothers urge their younger brothers and fathers drill their sons, all together regarding broad knowledge of antiquity and comprehension of the present as instruments that mislead the age and offend against custom. The time-honored scholarly heritage bound in blue silk has been completely swept away, and continuing down to the present, they are about to treat even the meaning of the Classics and commentaries…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
藐若土苴駕名懸解則爲斵輪之談飾言
無用則爲覆瓿之談詭詞官守則爲兼兩
之談委過剞劂則爲災木之談間有締章
繪句擷英咀華者未必皆有本之學廼知
亡書之故奚獨祖龍能燎而滅之
皇上受圖凝籙嚅嚌道眞左經右史不廢朝夕
牙籤玉軸之貯固已
紬覽無餘矣它如奇篇秘籍副在名山石室者
安可不按而求也亟宜倣往代之故章廣
===
===
二祖之遺志俾經生藝士洗滌故習一意嚮道
人人知貴典籍而後別鳩聚之林類辨魚
豕之訛舛整蟬斷之緹囊祛蠹餘之籤帙
徵蠅頭之繕寫則東觀崇文之盛且在下
風而聲名文物禮樂之化顯揚百禩愚生
何幸身親覩之
第四問
劉承芳
同考試官訓導王 批 讓固處令九原可作固亦無以
punctuated:
藐若土苴：駕名懸解，則爲斵輪之談；飾言無用，則爲覆瓿之談；詭詞官守，則爲兼兩之談；委過剞劂，則爲災木之談。間有締章繪句、擷英咀華者，未必皆有本之學。廼知亡書之故，奚獨祖龍能燎而滅之？皇上受圖凝籙，嚅嚌道眞，左經右史，不廢朝夕，牙籤玉軸之貯，固已紬覽無餘矣。它如奇篇秘籍，副在名山石室者，安可不按而求也？亟宜倣往代之故章，廣二祖之遺志，俾經生藝士，洗滌故習，一意嚮道，人人知貴典籍。而後別鳩聚之林類，辨魚豕之訛舛，整蟬斷之緹囊，祛蠹餘之籤帙，徵蠅頭之繕寫，則東觀、崇文之盛，且在下風，而聲名文物、禮樂之化，顯揚百禩，愚生何幸身親覩之！
第四問
劉承芳
同考試官訓導王批：讓固處，令九原可作，固亦無以
translation_en:
…slighted as mere dross. Those who falsely claim transcendent awakening engage in talk of the wheelwright's chisel [dismissing books as the dregs of the ancients]; those who gloss over their ignorance by calling books useless engage in talk of covering醬 jars; those who make specious excuses about official duties engage in talk of cartloads of books; and those who shift blame onto woodblock carvers engage in talk of ruining timber. Occasionally there are those who weave chapters and paint sentences, plucking the blossoms and savoring the essence, yet this is not necessarily learning rooted in fundamentals. Thus we know that as for the reasons books are lost, how could it only be the First Emperor of Qin (Zulong) who was able to burn and destroy them?

His Majesty has received the prophetic charts and consolidated the imperial mandate, savoring the true Way. With the Classics to his left and the Histories to his right, he does not neglect them morning or evening; the collections fitted with ivory tags and jade rollers have indeed already been perused in their entirety. As for other rare writings and secret texts whose duplicate copies rest in famous mountains and stone chambers, how can we fail to investigate and seek them out? We should urgently model ourselves on the established precedents of past dynasties and broaden the bequeathed intentions of our Two Ancestors [Taizu and Taizong], causing students of the Classics and men of letters to wash away their old habits, turn single-mindedly toward the Way, and ensure that everyone knows to value the canonical texts and records. Only after that should we classify the gathered forests of books, distinguish the scribal errors of "fish" and "pigs," mend the silk pouches of broken bindings, brush away the bookworms from the tagged cases, and commission fine-script transcriptions. Then the flourishing of the Eastern Pavilion (Dongguan) and the Hall for Venerating Literature (Chongwen yuan) will fall behind us, while the transformative influence of our renown, cultural artifacts, rites, and music will be gloriously manifest for a hundred generations. How fortunate is this foolish student to witness it in person!

Fourth Question
Liu Chengfang 劉承芳
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wang, comments: In the passages where he reproaches Ban Gu 班固, even if Ban Gu could be raised from the Nine Springs, he too would have no way to…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
自解足稱雄辨
考試官教諭湯批評隲人物表詳核
考試官教諭王批掊擊精當不獨其詞攉古也
論一人而欲盡一人之槩也易論百代之
人而欲盡百代之人之槩也難何者以一
人獨觀則其呈德有象專才有形情貌可
以洞原顛末得以旋究如夷吾有釁浴之
恥許之以仁展禽有裸裎之褒闡之為介
此謂以一言而蓋一人之生平不難也以
===
百代之人竝觀則歲歷綿曖稽覈難周派
别多端參伍寡決上斯人乎猶有上於斯
者下斯人乎猶有下於斯者是故辨二叔
非難也辨十六族難也然又安知五觀之
何如次乎辨四凶非難也辨十二牧難也
然又安知十亂之何如次乎使非稱博雅
之極精綜覈之方協總會之宜定銓次之
經其孰能進退古今悉當其則哉此班孟
堅古今人表所以不能無遺論也夫史之
punctuated:
自解，足稱雄辨。
考試官教諭湯批：評隲《人物表》詳核。
考試官教諭王批：掊擊精當，不獨其詞攉古也。
論一人而欲盡一人之槩也，易；論百代之人而欲盡百代之人之槩也，難。何者？以一人獨觀，則其呈德有象，專才有形，情貌可以洞原，顛末得以旋究。如夷吾有釁浴之恥，許之以仁；展禽有裸裎之褒，闡之為介。此謂以一言而蓋一人之生平，不難也。以百代之人竝觀，則歲歷綿曖，稽覈難周，派别多端，參伍寡決。上斯人乎？猶有上於斯者；下斯人乎？猶有下於斯者。是故辨二叔非難也，辨十六族難也，然又安知五觀之何如次乎？辨四凶非難也，辨十二牧難也，然又安知十亂之何如次乎？使非稱博雅之極，精綜覈之方，協總會之宜，定銓次之經，其孰能進退古今，悉當其則哉？此班孟堅《古今人表》所以不能無遺論也。夫史之
translation_en:
… vindicate himself. It fully deserves to be called a powerful argument.

Examiner Instructor Tang comments: Its evaluation of the "Table of Personages" (Renwu biao) is detailed and verified.

Examiner Instructor Wang comments: Its criticisms are precise and fitting; it is not merely that its diction captures the antique style [?].

To discuss a single person and wish to exhaust the general measure of that single person is easy; to discuss the people of a hundred generations and wish to exhaust the general measure of the people of a hundred generations is difficult. Why is this? When one observes a single person in isolation, the virtues he manifests have a clear image and his specialized talents have a distinct form; his disposition and demeanor can be thoroughly traced to their source, and his story from beginning to end can be readily investigated. For instance, Yi Wu [Guan Zhong 管仲] suffered the humiliation of being anointed and bathed as a captive, yet he was granted recognition for his humanity; Zhan Qin [Liuxia Hui 柳下惠] was praised for his forbearance even toward someone standing naked beside him, yet his character was elucidated as one of firm integrity. This means that summing up a person's entire life with a single word is not difficult. When one observes the people of a hundred generations side by side, however, the passage of years is long and obscure, making comprehensive verification difficult; their lineages and categories are manifold, leaving few decisive answers when comparing and cross-checking them. Should one rank this person high? There are still others higher than he. Should one rank this person low? There are still others lower than he. Therefore, to distinguish the Two Royal Uncles [Guan and Cai] is not difficult, whereas to distinguish the Sixteen Worthy Clans is difficult; and yet how can one know where to rank the Five Guan brothers? To distinguish the Four Miscreants is not difficult, whereas to distinguish the Twelve Pastors is difficult; and yet how can one know where to rank the Ten Capable Ministers? Unless one attains the utmost in broad learning and refinement, masters the methods of comprehensive verification, harmonizes what is fitting in an overarching synthesis, and establishes the standard for grading and ranking, who could elevate and demote the figures of antiquity and the present so that every one conforms to the proper rule? This is why Ban Mengjian's (Ban Gu 班固) "Table of Ancient and Modern Personages" (Gujin renbiao) cannot be free from lingering criticisms. Now, as for the [difficulty] of history …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
難難在一代良也史之良良在一代盡也
孟堅不惟欲盡一代而且欲盡百代是以
此表之作有三科焉謂上中下也三科之
中又各有上中下焉於是九等分矣自帝
皇而侯伯自師輔而臣僕自伎巧而隱佚
卽閨閤之流亦靡弗劈肌分理採摭而並
著有淑者有愚者有淑淑而愚愚者有媺
者有惡者有媺媺而惡惡者一等斷自宓
義而後凡一十五人二等斷自女媧而後
===
凡一百七十五人三等斷自倉頡而後凡
二百四人四等斷自胤靡而後凡三百二
十三人五等斷自昌若而後凡三百三十
六人六等斷自仲康而後凡三百五人七
等斷自玄妻而後凡二百四十三人八等
斷自虞賔而後凡二百三十二人九等斷
自蚩尤而後凡一百二十四人仰包億載
旁貫百家竭馳鶩之力以成閎博之規斯
其爲籍亦巳勤矣跨略舊筴剏始新詮洞
punctuated: 難，難在一代良也；史之良，良在一代盡也。孟堅不惟欲盡一代，而且欲盡百代，是以此表之作，有三科焉，謂上、中、下也。三科之中，又各有上、中、下焉，於是九等分矣。自帝皇而侯伯，自師輔而臣僕，自伎巧而隱佚，卽閨閤之流，亦靡弗劈肌分理，採摭而並著。有淑者，有愚者，有淑淑而愚愚者；有媺者，有惡者，有媺媺而惡惡者。一等斷自宓義而後，凡一十五人；二等斷自女媧而後，凡一百七十五人；三等斷自倉頡而後，凡二百四人；四等斷自胤靡而後，凡三百二十三人；五等斷自昌若而後，凡三百三十六人；六等斷自仲康而後，凡三百五人；七等斷自玄妻而後，凡二百四十三人；八等斷自虞賔而後，凡二百三十二人；九等斷自蚩尤而後，凡一百二十四人。仰包億載，旁貫百家，竭馳鶩之力，以成閎博之規，斯其爲籍亦巳勤矣。跨略舊筴，剏始新詮，洞
translation_en: … difficulty lies in being good for a single dynasty; the excellence of a history lies in being exhaustive for a single dynasty. Mengjian [Ban Gu 班固] not only wished to be exhaustive for a single dynasty, he also wished to be exhaustive for a hundred generations. Therefore, in composing this table [the Table of Ancient and Modern Persons, Gujin renbiao 古今人表], he set up three categories: upper, middle, and lower. Within each of the three categories, there are again upper, middle, and lower subdivisions, and thus nine grades are distinguished. From emperors and sovereigns down to marquises and earls, from grand tutors and辅佐 [assistants] down to ministers and servants, from artisans and technicians down to recluses, and even women of the inner quarters—none are not dissected to the finest grain, gathered up, and recorded together. There are the virtuous and the foolish, and those who are virtuous among the virtuous or foolish among the foolish; there are the admirable and the wicked, and those who are admirable among the admirable or wicked among the wicked. The first grade begins from Fuxi 宓義 [伏羲] onward, totaling fifteen persons; the second grade begins from Nüwa 女媧 onward, totaling one hundred and seventy-five persons; the third grade begins from Cangjie 倉頡 onward, totaling two hundred and four persons; the fourth grade begins from Yin Mi 胤靡 onward, totaling three hundred and twenty-three persons; the fifth grade begins from Changruo 昌若 onward, totaling three hundred and thirty-six persons; the sixth grade begins from Zhongkang 仲康 onward, totaling three hundred and five persons; the seventh grade begins from Xuanqi 玄妻 onward, totaling two hundred and forty-three persons; the eighth grade begins from Yu Bin 虞賔 [Dan Zhu 丹朱, guest of Yu] onward, totaling two hundred and thirty-two persons; and the ninth grade begins from Chiyou 蚩尤 onward, totaling one hundred and twenty-four persons. Looking up to encompass myriad ages and reaching out sideways to thread through the hundred schools, he exhausted the strength of his wide-ranging pursuits to achieve a grand and broad design—truly, as a work of compilation, it was a diligent labor indeed! Stepping beyond the old bamboo records and initiating a new mode of evaluation, he penetrated …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
性靈之奧區啓耳目之茫昧其義例昭乎
若日月之光華其包括森乎若星辰之錯
落蔚宗氏稱其贍且詳也豈溢美哉第一
則聖之二則仁之三則智之九則愚之自
四以下自八以上卽孟堅亦不能揭而號
之矣不能揭而號之也豈非雄白之名可
詫而雌黃之義難施乎是以劉知幾史通
之作每每興慨於斯以爲其篇列之不類
於敘言也胡曾參之後伯牛也冉有之後
===
仲弓也抑鄧侯而又果進聃𨾏諸甥也
晉文諸臣若舟之僑陽處父士會而其班
殊舛燕丹諸客若高漸離荆軻秦舞陽而
厥次不倫珍瓴甀而賤璠璵策駑駘而舍
騏驥以是爲監安所取衷哉至張晏氏又
以爲老子與文伯之母奈何四之而不知
老子已巍然聖列也田單魯仲連藺相如
奈何五之而不知魯藺二公原以二之而
單又未嘗五也大姬與寺人孟子奈何三
punctuated: 性靈之奧區，啓耳目之茫昧；其義例昭乎若日月之光華，其包括森乎若星辰之錯落。蔚宗氏稱其「贍且詳」也，豈溢美哉？第，一則聖之，二則仁之，三則智之，九則愚之；自四以下，自八以上，卽孟堅亦不能揭而號之矣。不能揭而號之也，豈非雄白之名可詫，而雌黃之義難施乎？是以劉知幾《史通》之作，每每興慨於斯，以爲其篇列之不類於敘言也。胡曾參之後伯牛也？冉有之後仲弓也？抑鄧侯，而又果進聃、𨾏諸甥也？晉文諸臣若舟之僑、陽處父、士會，而其班殊舛；燕丹諸客若高漸離、荆軻、秦舞陽，而厥次不倫。珍瓴甀而賤璠璵，策駑駘而舍騏驥，以是爲監，安所取衷哉？至張晏氏又以爲老子與文伯之母奈何四之，而不知老子已巍然聖列也；田單、魯仲連、藺相如奈何五之，而不知魯、藺二公原以二之，而單又未嘗五也；大姬與寺人孟子奈何三
translation_en: … the esoteric realms of human nature and spirit, and opening up the dim obscurity of sight and hearing; its principles and conventions are as radiant as the brilliance of the sun and moon, and its comprehensive scope is as arrayed as the scattered stars and constellations. When Fan Ye 范曄 (Weizong 蔚宗) praised it as "rich and detailed," how could that be excessive praise?
