Yet while he designated the first grade as Sages, the second as the Benevolent, the third as the Wise, and the ninth as the Foolish, from the fourth grade down and the eighth grade up, even Ban Gu 班固 (Mengjian 孟堅) himself could not hold up a specific label for them. That he could not hold up a label for them—is it not because grand and dazzling titles are easy to boast of, whereas precise critical judgments are difficult to apply? For this reason, when Liu Zhiji 劉知幾 wrote the Comprehensive Perspectives on Historiography (Shitong 史通), he frequently sighed over this very point, holding that the actual arrangement of the table did not match its prefatory remarks. Why was Zeng Shen 曾參 placed after Ran Geng 冉耕 (Boniu 伯牛)? Why was Ran Qiu 冉求 (Ranyou 冉有) placed after Ran Yong 冉雍 (Zhonggong 仲弓)? Why did he demote the Marquis of Deng 鄧侯, and yet resolutely promote the nephews Dan 聃 and Yao 𨾏 [Huan 雚]? Among the ministers of Duke Wen of Jin 晉文公, such as Zhou Zhiqiao 舟之僑, Yang Chufu 陽處父, and Shi Hui 士會, their rankings are wildly discrepant; among the retainers of Prince Dan of Yan 燕太子丹, such as Gao Jianli 高漸離, Jing Ke 荆軻, and Qin Wuyang 秦舞陽, their sequence is devoid of coherence. Treasuring roof tiles and jars while despising fine fanyu 璠璵 jade, whipping on worn-out nags while abandoning thoroughbred steeds—if one takes this as a mirror, where is one to find a balanced standard? As for Zhang Yan 張晏, he further asked how Laozi 老子 and the mother of Gongfu Wenbo 公父文伯 could be placed in the fourth grade—not knowing that Laozi already stood loftily in the rank of Sages; he asked how Tian Dan 田單, Lu Zhonglian 魯仲連, and Lin Xiangru 藺相如 could be placed in the fifth grade—not knowing that the two worthies Lu and Lin were originally placed in the second grade, while Tian Dan was never in the fifth; and he asked how Tai Ji 太姬 (Daji 大姬) and the Eunuch Mengzi 寺人孟子 could be placed in the third…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之而不知寺人固已四之嫪毐奈何七之
則表所不及吾又不知安所據而云然若
晏者可謂寙囈之語非旦晝之見也則又
何怪乎顏師古之議其後哉夫洪濛之世
昊古之初跡其人若有若無論其事若存
若亡繇斯以還上下千載文獻紛糅心術
幽秘夫孰能衡程而鏡照焉吾以爲姓氏
存而行事無所考見與行事可考而有之
不足爲勸無之不足爲戒者卽不錄可也
===
顓頊之世不可必明孟堅猶且難之孟堅
固且以爲備乎何夏禹之時脫一庚辰老
君之時脫一尹喜鄹紇之時脫一徵在魯
莊公時曾誅縣賁父而不書荆莊王時曾
執珪佽飛而不書序西乞術而不及白乙
丙收江上丈人而不及激絮女又何也錄
倉頡謂其肇字也乃始皇時王次仲作隸
傳於世胡勿錄也錄奚仲謂其服駕也乃
黃帝時胡曹爲衣伯余爲裳荀始爲冠于
punctuated: 之，而不知寺人固已四之；嫪毐奈何七之，則表所不及，吾又不知安所據而云然。若晏者，可謂寙囈之語，非旦晝之見也，則又何怪乎顏師古之議其後哉！夫洪濛之世，昊古之初，跡其人若有若無，論其事若存若亡。繇斯以還，上下千載，文獻紛糅，心術幽秘，夫孰能衡程而鏡照焉？吾以爲姓氏存而行事無所考見，與行事可考而有之不足爲勸、無之不足爲戒者，卽不錄可也。顓頊之世不可必明，孟堅猶且難之；孟堅固且以爲備乎？何夏禹之時脫一庚辰，老君之時脫一尹喜，鄹紇之時脫一徵在？魯莊公時曾誅縣賁父而不書，荆莊王時曾執珪佽飛而不書，序西乞術而不及白乙丙，收江上丈人而不及激絮女，又何也？錄倉頡，謂其肇字也；乃始皇時王次仲作隸傳於世，胡勿錄也？錄奚仲，謂其服駕也；乃黃帝時胡曹爲衣、伯余爲裳、荀始爲冠、于…
translation_en:
… the third tier, not realizing that Eunuch Mengzi is in fact already placed in the fourth tier; and as for his asking why Lao Ai 嫪毐 is placed in the seventh tier—that is someone the Table does not even include, so I do not know on what basis he makes such a claim. Someone like Zhang Yan 張晏 may be said to utter lazy sleep-talk rather than clear-sighted daytime observations; what wonder is it, then, that Yan Shigu 顏師古 criticized him afterward!

Now, in the age of primordial chaos and the beginning of remote antiquity, if one traces the people, they seem at once to have existed and not existed; if one discusses their deeds, they seem at once preserved and lost. From that time onward, across thousands of years, documents and authorities have become tangled and confused, and the inner workings of the mind remain dark and hidden—who could possibly weigh and measure them on a balance or illuminate them in a mirror? In my view, those whose surnames and clan names survive but whose deeds cannot be verified by examination, as well as those whose deeds can be examined but whose inclusion suffices not to encourage virtue and whose omission suffices not to warn against vice, may simply be left unrecorded.

Even the lineage of the era of Zhuanxu 顓頊 cannot be known with certainty, and Mengjian 孟堅 (Ban Gu 班固) himself found it difficult; yet did Mengjian truly consider his own work complete? Why, in the time of Yu of Xia 夏禹, did he omit Gengchen 庚辰; in the time of Laojun 老君 (Laozi), omit Yin Xi 尹喜; and in the time of Zou He 鄹紇 (Shuliang He), omit Zhengzai 徵在? In the time of Duke Zhuang of Lu 魯莊公, Xian Benfu 縣賁父 received a formal eulogy, yet he is not recorded; in the time of King Zhuang of Jing 荆莊王 (Chu), Cifei 佽飛 was granted the rank of Baton-holder, yet he is not recorded; Xiqishu 西乞術 is listed, yet Baiyibing 白乙丙 is not mentioned; the Old Man on the River 江上丈人 is included, yet the Silk-bleaching Woman 激絮女 is not mentioned—why is this as well? He records Cang Jie 倉頡 because he originated written characters; yet in the time of the First Emperor, Wang Cizhong 王次仲 created clerical script and transmitted it to the world—why not record him? He records Xi Zhong 奚仲 because he yoked horses to carriages; yet in the time of the Yellow Emperor, Hu Cao 胡曹 made upper garments, Bo Yu 伯余 made lower garments, Xun Shi 荀始 made caps, Yu…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則爲扉延鼓爲鐘貨狄爲舟堯時羽壽爲
鏡母句爲琴瑟質以靡爲擊甌胡勿錄也
既有九黎不妨及偃師矣既有長狄僑如
不妨及夸父矣既有醫緩和不妨及桐雷
矣孟堅皆略之又何也士會非范文子乎
夔非后夔韋非豕韋乎而兩書之漁父非
屈平寓言之稱計然非范蠡著書之名乎
而竝列之又何也且一者聖之無庸議也
二者仁之無甚相懸也至於智品則有不
===
可解者矣朱英而得與樂毅同駕樊遲而
得與老彭竝鑣至於四則史魚之直也而
祝鮀亦參之賓須無之諒也而優孟亦參
之至於五則包胥不得竝於伍員穰苴李
牧不得比於白起至於六而所尤冤者叔
梁紇穎考叔也至於九而獨昂桀而置紂
與幽厲於其評意者以其虐猶未甚與然
均之失天下者耳且以毒痡之夫而肩於
太康六以下何舛也吾又且究言之伯禽
punctuated: 則爲扉、延鼓爲鐘、貨狄爲舟，堯時羽壽爲鏡、母句爲琴瑟、質以靡爲擊甌，胡勿錄也？既有九黎，不妨及偃師矣；既有長狄僑如，不妨及夸父矣；既有醫緩、和，不妨及桐、雷矣。孟堅皆略之，又何也？士會非范文子乎？夔非后夔，韋非豕韋乎？而兩書之。漁父非屈平寓言之稱，計然非范蠡著書之名乎？而竝列之，又何也？且一者，聖之無庸議也；二者，仁之無甚相懸也。至於智品，則有不可解者矣。朱英而得與樂毅同駕，樊遲而得與老彭竝鑣。至於四，則史魚之直也，而祝鮀亦參之；賓須無之諒也，而優孟亦參之。至於五，則包胥不得竝於伍員，穰苴、李牧不得比於白起。至於六，而所尤冤者，叔梁紇、穎考叔也。至於九，而獨昂桀，而置紂與幽、厲於其評。意者以其虐猶未甚與？然均之失天下者耳。且以毒痡之夫而肩於太康，六以下何舛也！吾又且究言之：伯禽、
translation_en:
… Ze made sandals, Yan Gu [Yanbu 延部?] made bells, and Huodi 貨狄 made boats; in the time of Yao 堯, Yu Shou 羽壽 made mirrors, Muju 母句 made zithers, and Zhi [Nü 女?] and Mi 靡 made clay drums for striking—why did he not record them? Since he already included the Jiuli 九黎, there was no harm in mentioning Master Yan (Yanshi 偃師); since he already included the giant Di (Chang Di 長狄) Qiaoru 僑如, there was no harm in mentioning Kuafu 夸父; since he already included the physicians Huan 緩 and He 和, there was no harm in mentioning Tong Jun 桐君 and Lei Gong 雷公. Why is it that Mengjian 孟堅 (Ban Gu 班固) omitted all of them? Was Shi Hui 士會 not Fan Wenzi 范文子 [note: historically Shi Xie 士燮 was Fan Wenzi and Shi Hui was Fan Wuzi 范武子]? Was Kui 夔 not Hou Kui 后夔, and was Wei 韋 not Shiwei 豕韋? Yet he recorded each of them twice. Was "The Fisherman" (Yufu 漁父) not an allegorical figure invented by Qu Ping 屈平 (Qu Yuan 屈原), and was Jiran 計然 not the title of a book written by Fan Li 范蠡? Why, then, did he list them alongside real people?

Furthermore, as for the first grade—that of the sages—there is no need for dispute; as for the second grade—that of the benevolent—there are no great discrepancies. When we come to the grade of the wise (the third grade), however, there are placements that are inexplicable. Zhu Ying 朱英 is allowed to ride in the same yoke as Yue Yi 樂毅, and Fan Chi 樊遲 is allowed to run neck and neck with Lao Peng 老彭. When we come to the fourth grade, there is the uprightness of Historian Yu (Shi Yu 史魚), yet Priest Tuo (Zhu Tuo 祝鮀) is placed alongside him; there is the trustworthiness of Bin Xuwu 賓須無, yet the jester Meng (You Meng 優孟) is placed alongside him. When we come to the fifth grade, Shen Baoxu 申包胥 is not allowed to stand equal to Wu Yuan 伍員 (Wu Zixu 伍子胥), and Sima Rangju 司馬穰苴 and Li Mu 李牧 are not allowed to compare with Bai Qi 白起. When we come to the sixth grade, those who are most unjustly treated are Shuliang He 叔梁紇 and Ying Kaoshu 穎考叔. When we come to the ninth grade, he elevates Jie 桀 alone [into the eighth grade], while placing Zhou 紂 as well as Kings You 幽 and Li 厲 in this [ninth] category. Could his idea have been that Jie's tyranny was not yet so extreme? Yet they were all equally rulers who lost the Empire. Moreover, to take a man who inflicted such poison and suffering and place him shoulder to shoulder with Tai Kang 太康 [in the eighth grade]—how perverse are the rankings from the sixth grade downward! Let me examine and speak of this still further: Boqin 伯禽…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
吕伋何遽不及酆郇應而置之五徐偃
王宋襄公比於諸樊必有分矣而皆置之
六樂正子優於公孫丑辨在其師較若白
黑而置克丑下充程嬰杵臼之懿心也豈
不曰誠仁哉充輔果之蚤見也豈不曰誠
智哉然四之則恐泥也巢許卞務荷蕢接
輿之流豈不皆高蹈哉而巢許二之卞務
三之荷蕢接輿四之何也夫史名漢書乃
叙曠遠而脫本朝表載女士乃詳通顯而
===
略幽微則所謂體又安在乎故曰以山澤
量者不盡其珍也垢亦受之以鍾釜量者
不盡其粲也糲亦納之孟堅之史贍而不
免於穢詳而不免於體之紕也則此表之
謂也或者謂大家爲其兄卒成之則以孟
堅旣下請室而八表多出昭之手故遂意
之耳雖然吾無暇質此也所爲孟堅計者
寄昂抑於一字如麟經之簡辭以立體上
也寓斷决於微言如遷史之卽事以該情
punctuated: 吕伋何遽不及酆、郇、應，而置之五？徐偃王、宋襄公比於諸樊，必有分矣，而皆置之六。樂正子優於公孫丑，辨在其師，較若白黑，而置克丑下。充程嬰、杵臼之懿心也，豈不曰誠仁哉？充輔果之蚤見也，豈不曰誠智哉？然四之則恐泥也。巢、許、卞、務、荷蕢、接輿之流，豈不皆高蹈哉？而巢、許二之，卞、務三之，荷蕢、接輿四之，何也？夫史名《漢書》，乃叙曠遠而脫本朝；表載女士，乃詳通顯而略幽微，則所謂體又安在乎？故曰：以山澤量者，不盡其珍也，垢亦受之；以鍾釜量者，不盡其粲也，糲亦納之。孟堅之史，贍而不免於穢，詳而不免於體之紕也，則此表之謂也。或者謂大家爲其兄卒成之，則以孟堅旣下請室，而八表多出昭之手，故遂意之耳。雖然，吾無暇質此也。所爲孟堅計者，寄昂抑於一字，如《麟經》之簡辭以立體，上也；寓斷决於微言，如遷史之卽事以該情，
translation_en:
… and Lü Ji 呂伋 (Duke Ding of Qi) so suddenly inferior to the lords of Feng 酆, Xun 郇, and Ying 應 that they are placed in the fifth grade? King Yan of Xu 徐偃王 and Duke Xiang of Song 宋襄公, when compared to Zhufan 諸樊 of Wu, surely have distinctions between them, yet all are placed in the sixth grade. That Yuezhengzi 樂正子 (Yuezheng Ke 樂正克) was superior to Gongsun Chou 公孫丑 is discernible from their master's words, as clear as black and white, yet Ke is placed below Chou. If one extends the admirable intentions of Cheng Ying 程嬰 and Gongsun Chujiu 公孫杵臼, how could one not call them truly humane? If one extends the early foresight of Fu Guo 輔果, how could one not call him truly wise? Yet to place them in the fourth grade is, I fear, overly rigid. Were not men of the ilk of Chao Fu 巢父, Xu You 許由, Bian Sui 卞隨, Wu Guang 務光, the Basket-Carrier (Hekui 荷蕢), and Jieyu 接輿 all lofty recluses? Yet Chao and Xu are placed in the second grade, Bian and Wu in the third, and the Basket-Carrier and Jieyu in the fourth—why is this?

Now, the history is titled the History of the Former Han (Hanshu 漢書), yet this table recounts the distant past while omitting the reigning dynasty; the table records women and gentlemen, yet it details the prominent and illustrious while neglecting the obscure and humble—where, then, is its so-called structural principle? Therefore it is said: that which measures by mountains and marshes does not contain only treasures, for it receives dirt as well; that which measures by the zhong and fu vessels does not hold only fine white grain, for it admits coarse grain as well. That Ban Mengjian's 班孟堅 (Ban Gu 班固) history is rich yet cannot avoid impurity, detailed yet cannot avoid structural flaws—this is precisely what is meant by this table.

Some say that Cao Dajia 曹大家 (Ban Zhao 班昭) completed it for her brother, simply guessing this because after Mengjian was cast into the prison for officials, the eight tables mostly came from Zhao's hand. Even so, I have no leisure to verify this. What I would reckon as the best plan for Mengjian is this: to lodge praise and censure in a single word, like the concise phrasing of the Classic of the Unicorn (Linjing 麟經, the Spring and Autumn Annals) in establishing its form, is the highest way; to embed judgments in subtle words, like Sima Qian's 司馬遷 history (Shiji 史記) using the events themselves to encompass the circumstances, is the…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
次也智不出此而既立之傳復系之表表
而良也且不免於文之駢枝說之疣贅況
其舛駁脫漏若是是奚取焉夫聖固無二
品也如仁則夷齊是也微箕比干亦是也
雖然以方之孔甲伶倫則姱張貌象而失
其真也如智則樗里鴟夷是也五羖大夫
亦是也雖然以方之方叔召虎則圖寫毫
毛而迷其似也夫表之言標也所以標世
系詔來許也而棕核名實評隲神理不與
===
焉乃其褒以單辭寵踰爵賞貶以隻字辱
過鞭箠則固檃括於紀載間而等列自具
矣故先儒謂列傳之中美惡備著足示鑒
誡表可無作信然哉遷史嘗作十表以倣
剛柔十日以定歷代系年而百世而下莫
之能易亦莫之能議者無它曰探研博而
考核精也曰總會周而銓配當也孟堅之
作是表果有得於此否耶嘗攷之孟堅在
漢以浮華剽獵稱故肅宗問禮樂而固對
punctuated: 次也。智不出此，而既立之傳，復系之表。表而良也，且不免於文之駢枝、說之疣贅，況其舛駁脫漏若是，是奚取焉？夫聖固無二品也。如仁，則夷、齊是也，微、箕、比干亦是也；雖然，以方之孔甲、伶倫，則姱張貌象而失其真也。如智，則樗里、鴟夷是也，五羖大夫亦是也；雖然，以方之方叔、召虎，則圖寫毫毛而迷其似也。夫表之言標也，所以標世系、詔來許也，而棕核名實、評隲神理不與焉。乃其褒以單辭，寵踰爵賞；貶以隻字，辱過鞭箠，則固檃括於紀載間，而等列自具矣。故先儒謂列傳之中，美惡備著，足示鑒誡，表可無作，信然哉！遷史嘗作十表，以倣剛柔十日，以定歷代系年，而百世而下，莫之能易，亦莫之能議者，無它，曰探研博而考核精也，曰總會周而銓配當也。孟堅之作是表，果有得於此否耶？嘗攷之，孟堅在漢，以浮華剽獵稱。故肅宗問禮樂，而固對
translation_en: …is second best. His wisdom did not reach this; instead, having already established biographies for them, he further appended a table. Even if the table were good, it still would not escape being a superfluous appendage in writing and a redundant excrescence in explanation; how much more so when its errors, contradictions, and omissions are like this—what is there to take from it? Now, the sages certainly cannot be divided into two grades. As for benevolence, Boyi and Shuqi are examples, and the Viscount of Wei, the Viscount of Ji, and Bigan are also examples; even so, if one places them alongside Kong Jia and Ling Lun, that is exaggerating outward appearances and losing their true nature. As for wisdom, Shuli Zi and Chiyi [Fan Li] are examples, and the Five-Ramskins Grandee [Baili Xi] is also an example; even so, if one places them alongside Fang Shu and Shao Hu, that is sketching fine hairs while losing the true likeness. Now, "table" (biao) means "to mark" (biao); it is the means by which to mark genealogies and inform future generations, whereas comprehensively verifying names and realities [reading 棕 as 綜] and evaluating subtle principles have no part in it. As for praising with a single phrase so that the honor surpasses noble rank and reward, or censuring with a lone character so that the disgrace exceeds the whip and rod, these are naturally framed within the annals and narrative records, and the gradations are inherently present there. Therefore, when former scholars said that within the biographies, good and evil are fully manifested, sufficient to serve as a mirror and warning, so that the table need not have been made—how true that is! Sima Qian's history once made ten tables, in imitation of the ten strong and weak celestial stems, to fix the chronological succession of the generations; and that for a hundred generations below no one has been able to alter them, nor has anyone been able to criticize them, is for no other reason than this: namely, that his inquiry and research were broad and his investigation and verification were precise; namely, that his synthesis was comprehensive and his evaluation and arrangement were fitting. In making this table, did Mengjian [Ban Gu] truly grasp any of this or not? If we examine into it, Mengjian in the Han was known for showy superficiality and plagiarism. Thus, when Emperor Suzong asked about rites and music, Ban Gu replied…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以在京諸儒必能知之及諸儒奏記固第
取叔孫通十二篇以上無乃探研之未博
與史稱孟堅掠人之美竊鍾揜耳自武帝
以上凡六世則皆彷彿遷書自昭帝以後
凡六世則皆憑藉賈劉無乃考核之未精
與旁行邪上固且未達漢紹堯運談更無
稽周秦旣不相因古今斯成間隔無乃統
會之未周與帝王儒老方駕並驅人物姓
名層出疊見聖賢之詳略不倫品格之低
===
昂失較無乃銓配之未當與夫是四者旣
皆不出遷右而徒欲以矯遷之失舉古今
人物彊立差等惡在其不穢與有體焉夫
漢孝肅固已窺其疎矣乃其語竇憲曰公
愛班固而忽崔駟此葉公之好龍耳而夾
漈氏至謂遷之與固猶龍之與豕則固不
逮遷遠甚諸史弃遷而用固劉知幾之徒
尊班而抑馬又不知其何說也愚因得而
評之遺親攘美徵賄鬻筆先儒之所以責
punctuated: 以在京諸儒必能知之；及諸儒奏記，固第取叔孫通十二篇以上，無乃探研之未博與？史稱孟堅掠人之美，竊鍾揜耳：自武帝以上凡六世，則皆彷彿遷書；自昭帝以後凡六世，則皆憑藉賈、劉，無乃考核之未精與？旁行邪上，固且未達；漢紹堯運，談更無稽；周、秦旣不相因，古今斯成間隔，無乃統會之未周與？帝王、儒、老方駕並驅，人物姓名層出疊見，聖賢之詳略不倫，品格之低昂失較，無乃銓配之未當與？夫是四者，旣皆不出遷右，而徒欲以矯遷之失，舉古今人物彊立差等，惡在其不穢與有體焉？夫漢孝肅固已窺其疎矣，乃其語竇憲曰：「公愛班固而忽崔駟，此葉公之好龍耳。」而夾漈氏至謂「遷之與固，猶龍之與豕」，則固不逮遷遠甚！諸史弃遷而用固，劉知幾之徒尊班而抑馬，又不知其何說也？愚因得而評之：遺親攘美，徵賄鬻筆，先儒之所以責
translation_en: …that the various Confucian scholars in the capital would surely know of them; yet when the scholars submitted their memoranda, Gu merely took the twelve chapters of Shusun Tong 叔孫通 and presented them to the throne. Was his investigation and research not lacking in breadth? History states that Mengjian (Ban Gu 班固) plagiarized the merits of others, like stealing a bell while covering one's own ears: for the six reigns up to Emperor Wu, he closely imitated Qian's (Sima Qian's 司馬遷) book; for the six reigns from Emperor Zhao onward, he relied entirely on Jia (Jia逵/Jia Shan?) and Liu (Liu Xiang 劉向 and Liu Xin 劉歆). Was his critical verification not lacking in precision? As for the format of horizontal rows and diagonal upward lines, Gu did not even grasp it; his talk of the Han succeeding the destiny of Yao 堯 was even more unfounded; and since the Zhou and Qin were not treated as continuous, antiquity and the present became severed from one another. Was his comprehensive synthesis not lacking in thoroughness? Emperors and kings, Confucians and Daoists ride abreast together; the names of historical figures appear repeatedly in profusion; the relative detail or brevity accorded to sages and worthies is out of proportion; and the elevation or demotion of their moral rankings fails of proper measure. Was his evaluation and classification not lacking in appropriateness? Now, in these four respects he in no way surpassed Qian, yet he vainly sought to rectify Qian's faults by taking the figures of antiquity and the present and forcibly establishing graded ranks for them—how could this be considered free of vulgarity and possessed of proper form? Indeed, Emperor Xiaosu of Han (Emperor Zhang) had already seen through his superficiality, for he said to Dou Xian 竇憲: "You are fond of Ban Gu yet neglect Cui Yin 崔駟—this is nothing more than Lord Ye's fondness for dragons." And Mr. Jiaji (Zheng Qiao 鄭樵) even went so far as to say that "Qian compared to Gu is like a dragon compared to a pig," showing that Gu fell far short of Qian! That the various later histories abandoned Qian and followed Gu, and that men like Liu Zhiji 劉知幾 revered Ban while disparaging Ma (Sima Qian)—one truly does not know on what grounds they argued this. I am therefore able to offer this appraisal: neglecting his own father to appropriate the credit for himself, and soliciting bribes to sell his brush—the grounds on which former scholars reproached…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
班史者當矣然十志該富讚序弘麗宗經
以救遷之謬旨豐贍以掩遷之疏落如固
者是胡可盡訾哉乃或曰班彪有其業而
班固不能讀父書又不能保其身安在其
言爲天下法噫是又以固之冤古今人者
而冤固也
第五問
樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批書生譚田賦利弊犁然若指掌
===
而等畫詳悉其經世之才耶錄之
考試官教諭王批洞析弊源而條畫鑿鑿可用
今天下田賦之當均未有甚於楚者也田
賦均矣而爲之圖善後之策亦未有急於
楚者也何也禹貢荆州之域厥土惟泥塗
厥田惟下中厥賦上下大都與揚州壤埒
而田有加焉則以淖濕同而人力異也楚
在春秋稱最彊大歲出兵車與秦晉爭雄
長非盡倚辦地利哉厥後揚州稱隩區而
punctuated:
班史者當矣。然十志該富，讚序弘麗，宗經以救遷之謬旨，豐贍以掩遷之疏落，如固者，是胡可盡訾哉？乃或曰：「班彪有其業，而班固不能讀父書，又不能保其身，安在其言爲天下法？」噫！是又以固之冤古今人者，而冤固也。

第五問
樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批：書生譚田賦利弊，犁然若指掌，而等畫詳悉，其經世之才耶？錄之。
考試官教諭王批：洞析弊源，而條畫鑿鑿可用。

今天下田賦之當均，未有甚於楚者也；田賦均矣，而爲之圖善後之策，亦未有急於楚者也。何也？《禹貢》荆州之域，厥土惟泥塗，厥田惟下中，厥賦上下，大都與揚州壤埒，而田有加焉，則以淖濕同而人力異也。楚在春秋稱最彊大，歲出兵車，與秦、晉爭雄長，非盡倚辦地利哉？厥後揚州稱隩區，而
translation_en:
… Ban’s History (Ban shi) is indeed justified. Yet his ten treatises are comprehensive and rich, and his eulogies and prefaces are grand and ornate. He upheld the Classics to remedy Sima Qian’s erroneous purport, and used copiousness to cover Sima Qian’s sketchiness and omissions. How can someone like Ban Gu be completely disparaged? Still, some say: "Ban Biao 班彪 laid the foundation of the work, yet Ban Gu was unable to truly read his father’s writings and furthermore could not preserve his own life; how then could his words serve as a model for the world?" Alas! This is in turn to wrong Ban Gu in the very manner in which Ban Gu wronged the people of antiquity and the present.

Question Five
Fan Yuheng 樊玉衡
Comment by Examiner Instructor Tang: A scholar discussing the advantages and abuses of land taxation as clearly as pointing to his own palm, with detailed and thorough planning—is he not a talent for statecraft? Recorded.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wang: Penetratingly analyzes the sources of abuse, and his point-by-point plans are concrete and practicable.

In the empire today, nowhere is the need to equalize land taxes more acute than in Chu [Huguang]; and once the land taxes are equalized, nowhere is the need to devise a policy for future maintenance more urgent than in Chu. Why is this? In the "Tribute of Yu" (Yu gong), the region of Jingzhou had soil that was miry mud, fields of the middle-lower grade, and revenues of the upper-lower grade. On the whole its territory was comparable to that of Yangzhou, yet its fields were graded higher; this was because while both shared the same marshy dampness, human effort differed. During the Spring and Autumn period, Chu was renowned as the most powerful state, sending out war chariots year after year to contend for supremacy with Qin and Jin—did this not rely entirely upon the productivity of its land? Thereafter, Yangzhou came to be celebrated as a fertile and prosperous region, whereas…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
瀉鹵瘠空楚用以絀故漢人之論荆楊曰
伐木而樹穀燔萊而播粟呰窳而偷生民
亦大困戹矣
高皇帝起自田間稔識地事據天下所上墾額
定立賦貢其土脉膏磽封畛𦵇溢疆畆登
耗載在圖冊可鏡已弘成之際民物殷富
稱全盛焉斯去今未遠也而田賦剌戾若
是其故蓋難言矣夫楚疆遼逖度一邑地
可當東南一大郡天下初定井廬寥闊原
===
野蕪穢故經界靡及焉計今闢地十倍𢓺
於
國初而籍額歲縮德靖以來遞削至數十萬
夫土無盈虛避新闢之稅匿已定之田此
大不均者一鄂州中廬沙羡常武南交麋
蘄之間皆
諸侯王封國也分茅之始錫以土疆其籍藏
於
內府有司不得闚虞芮之田往往沒入其國
punctuated: 瀉鹵瘠空，楚用以絀。故漢人之論荆楊曰：「伐木而樹穀，燔萊而播粟，呰窳而偷生。」民亦大困戹矣。高皇帝起自田間，稔識地事，據天下所上墾額，定立賦貢，其土脉膏磽、封畛𦵇溢、疆畆登耗，載在圖冊，可鏡已。弘、成之際，民物殷富，稱全盛焉，斯去今未遠也，而田賦剌戾若是，其故蓋難言矣。夫楚疆遼逖，度一邑地可當東南一大郡。天下初定，井廬寥闊，原野蕪穢，故經界靡及焉。計今闢地十倍𢓺於國初，而籍額歲縮，德、靖以來，遞削至數十萬。夫土無盈虛，避新闢之稅，匿已定之田，此大不均者一。鄂州、中廬、沙羡、常武、南交、麋、蘄之間，皆諸侯王封國也。分茅之始，錫以土疆，其籍藏於內府，有司不得闚。虞、芮之田，往往沒入其國，
translation_en:
…saline, barren, and depleted, so that Chu became impoverished as a result. Thus, when people of the Han dynasty discussed Jingzhou and Yangzhou, they said: "They fell trees to plant grain and burn off weeds to sow millet; they are indolent and merelyeke out a living." The people were indeed in great distress.

The Exalted Emperor arose from among the fields and was thoroughly familiar with agricultural affairs. Based on the quotas of reclaimed land submitted from across the realm, he established the land taxes and tribute. The fertility or barrenness of the soil veins, the constriction or expansion of the boundaries, and the increase or decrease of the acreage were all recorded in the Yellow Registers and Fish-Scale Maps, where they can be clearly seen as in a mirror. During the Chenghua (1465–1487) and Hongzhi (1488–1505) eras, the populace and goods were abundant and prosperous, which was hailed as the peak of flourishing. That time is not far removed from the present, yet the land taxes have become so perverse and disordered—the reasons for this are indeed difficult to speak of!

Now, the territory of Chu is vast and distant; if one measures the land of a single county there, it is equivalent to a large prefecture in the southeast. When the realm was first pacified, settlements and cottages were sparse and scattered, and the plains and wilds were overgrown with weeds, so boundary surveys did not reach everywhere. It is calculated that the land opened to cultivation today is more than ten times that at the founding of the dynasty, yet the registered tax quota shrinks year by year; since the Zhengde (1506–1521) and Jiajing (1522–1566) eras, it has been successively whittled down by several hundred thousand [mu]. Now, the land itself neither expands nor contracts; rather, people evade taxes on newly reclaimed land and conceal fields that were already assessed. This is the first great inequity.

The region spanning Ezhou, Zhonglu, Shaxian, Changwu, Nanjiao, Mi, and Qi is all the enfeoffed territories of Imperial Princes. At the beginning of their investiture with the sacred thatch, they were granted lands and territories. Their registers are stored in the Inner Treasury, where local authorities are not permitted to peer into them. Disputed fields like those of Yu and Rui are frequently confiscated and absorbed into their princedoms,…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
比於湯沐食邑不可勝數皆各爲私奉養
焉不領於天下之經費此大不均者二楚
故饒湖利而滄桑徙易靡常昔爲沮洳今
稱沃衍者不啻萬萬荆郢尤甚大姓與游
民彊有力者據之計畝歲入數鍾專其厚
積坐攫齊民食亡租稅而苦積逋者曾不
得以塗足而收半穗彼獨非王土哉而吏
不敢問如河南南陽此大不均者三屯非
獨楚有也而楚之屯非昔之屯矣按
制每軍給屯五十畝有奇今屯浮者什伯其額
此非獨依山濱水之地耕新墾遺也蓋亦
有占射焉夫屯軍不能世其業輒質之民
民利其賦薄無他役即以巳所有之民田
更籍爲軍歷十數傳不可窮竟所謂民竄
於屯屯竄於民者非邪此大不均者四先
是山澤之羨率弃不理今則皐濕原阪耕
者鱗集甚之叢菁幽葦人力所不能通者
亦皆纍纍象耕鳥耘稱常稔焉乃聽其封
punctuated: 比於湯沐食邑，不可勝數。皆各爲私奉養焉，不領於天下之經費。此大不均者二。楚故饒湖利，而滄桑徙易靡常，昔爲沮洳，今稱沃衍者，不啻萬萬，荆、郢尤甚。大姓與游民彊有力者據之，計畝歲入數鍾，專其厚積，坐攫齊民，食亡租稅；而苦積逋者，曾不得以塗足而收半穗。彼獨非王土哉？而吏不敢問，如河南、南陽。此大不均者三。屯非獨楚有也，而楚之屯非昔之屯矣。按制：每軍給屯五十畝有奇；今屯浮者，什伯其額。此非獨依山濱水之地耕新墾遺也，蓋亦有占射焉。夫屯軍不能世其業，輒質之民；民利其賦薄無他役，即以巳所有之民田更籍爲軍，歷十數傳不可窮竟。所謂民竄於屯、屯竄於民者，非邪？此大不均者四。先是，山澤之羨率弃不理；今則皐濕原阪，耕者鱗集。甚之叢菁幽葦，人力所不能通者，亦皆纍纍象耕鳥耘，稱常稔焉。乃聽其封
translation_en:
…comparable to bath-towns and revenue estates, beyond all counting. All are used by each prince for his own private maintenance and are not directed toward the regular expenditures of the empire. This is the second great inequality.

Chu [Huguang] has long been rich in the bounty of its lakes, yet its waters and lands shift and change without constancy. Places that were once marshy lowlands and are now acclaimed as fertile expanses number in the tens of millions of mu, most acutely in Jingzhou and Yingzhou. Great clans and powerful vagrants seize hold of them, taking in several zhong of grain per mu each year. Monopolizing these rich stores and sitting idly while fleecing the common people, they live off the land without paying land tax; meanwhile, those suffering under accumulated arrears cannot so much as muddy their feet in those fields to harvest half an ear of grain. Are those lands alone not the King's territory? Yet officials dare not inquire into them, just as in Henan and Nanyang. This is the third great inequality.

Military colonies (tun) are not unique to Chu, yet the military colonies of Chu are no longer what they were of old. According to the dynastic system, each soldier is allotted slightly more than fifty mu of colony land; today, the surplus colony land is ten or a hundred times the statutory quota. This is not merely a matter of cultivating newly opened land or reclaiming abandoned fields along the hills and waters; rather, there is also fraudulent engrossment and tax evasion. When colony soldiers are unable to pass their holdings down through the generations, they readily mortgage them to civilians. Civilians, taking advantage of the light tax rate and the exemption from other corvée labor, then re-register their own civilian fields as military holdings; after ten or more generations have passed, the matter can no longer be traced to the bottom. Is this not what is meant by "civilians slipping into the military colonies, and military colonies slipping into civilian hands"? This is the fourth great inequality.

Previously, the marginal lands of mountains and marshes were generally abandoned and left untended; now, across damp bottomlands, plateaus, and hillsides, cultivators gather thick as fish scales. Even in dense thickets and secluded reed-beds where human strength could scarcely penetrate, people now till and weed in droves—as if elephants were plowing and birds weeding—and these places are acclaimed as yielding regular harvests. Yet they are left to enclose and…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
殖自利幾世幾年不問所收此大不均者
五五者弊也而非所以弊也其失在庸有
司與舞文之吏不軌之民曰飛詭曰影射
曰虛懸曰那移曰隱沒曰兼并其姦狀若
蝟毛起務欺謾以逃其課以故富者連阡
陌而嫁稅於貧貧者或不厭糠粞而代富
人輸此大不均者六故曰今日田賦之當
均未有甚於楚者也議者不勝其憤輒曰
井田井田夫井田法黃虞氏以前尚矣靡
===
===
得而記云至周始備亦子輿氏所謂大略
也自李悝商鞅出而其法決裂廢滅不復
存二人誠萬世戎首然秦漢迄今英君誼
辟與竒謀石畫之臣莫之能變即有變者
或至紕戾無稽此豈商李之法有加於三
代聖人耶譚者謂戰國干戈之後丘陵城
郭墳壠廬舍鞠爲茂草即有平原亦半荆
棘漢去秦無幾已不能比次而經紀之顧
處千載之下而欲籠其業以授民踵新莽
punctuated: 殖自利，幾世幾年，不問所收。此大不均者五。五者，弊也，而非所以弊也。其失在庸有司與舞文之吏、不軌之民。曰飛詭，曰影射，曰虛懸，曰那移，曰隱沒，曰兼并。其姦狀若蝟毛起，務欺謾以逃其課。以故富者連阡陌而嫁稅於貧，貧者或不厭糠粞而代富人輸。此大不均者六。故曰：今日田賦之當均，未有甚於楚者也。議者不勝其憤，輒曰：「井田！井田！」夫井田法，黃虞氏以前尚矣，靡得而記云。至周始備，亦子輿氏所謂大略也。自李悝、商鞅出，而其法決裂廢滅，不復存。二人誠萬世戎首！然秦、漢迄今，英君誼辟與竒謀石畫之臣，莫之能變。即有變者，或至紕戾無稽。此豈商、李之法有加於三代聖人耶？譚者謂戰國干戈之後，丘陵、城郭、墳壠、廬舍鞠爲茂草，即有平原，亦半荆棘。漢去秦無幾，已不能比次而經紀之。顧處千載之下，而欲籠其業以授民，踵新莽
translation_en:
…amass wealth for their own profit for generations and years without anyone inquiring into their harvest. This is the fifth great inequity. These five are abuses, yet they are not the root cause of the abuses. The fault lies with mediocre officials, pettifogging clerks, and lawless commoners. There is what is called fraudulent transfer (feigui), sheltering under others' names (yingshe), unattached registration (xuxuan), illicit shifting (nuoyi), concealment (yinmo), and engrossment (jianbing). Their fraudulent tricks spring up like hedgehog bristles, all aimed at deception in order to evade their tax quotas. Consequently, the rich own contiguous tracts of land across the paths and ridges yet shift their taxes onto the poor, while the poor cannot even get their fill of chaff and broken grain yet pay taxes in place of the rich. This is the sixth great inequity. Therefore it is said: Today, nowhere is the need to equalize land taxes more urgent than in Chu [Huguang].

Commentators, overcome with indignation, immediately cry, "The well-field system! The well-field system!" Now, prior to the Yellow Emperor and Yu [Shun], the well-field system was of remote antiquity, and nothing could be recorded of it. Only in the Zhou dynasty did it become complete, though even that was what Master Ziyu [Mencius] called merely a general outline. Once Li Kui and Shang Yang emerged, the system was torn apart, abolished, and destroyed, never to exist again. Those two men were truly the arch-offenders of ten thousand generations! Yet from the Qin and Han dynasties down to the present, heroic rulers and righteous sovereigns, along with ministers of extraordinary counsel and rock-solid plans, have been unable to change this. Even when someone attempted to change it, it resulted in perversity and absurdity. Could this mean that the laws of Shang Yang and Li Kui surpassed those of the sages of the Three Dynasties? Discussants say that after the warfare of the Warring States period, hills, city walls, burial mounds, and cottages were all overgrown with rank grass, and even where flat plains remained, they were half covered in brambles. The Han dynasty was not far removed in time from the Qin, yet it was already unable to arrange and regulate the land in order. To stand instead a thousand years later and wish to monopolize people's property in order to parcel it out to the populace, following in the overturned tracks of Wang Mang of the Xin dynasty…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之覆轍吁亦迂矣是井田之不能復也勢
也議者無已又有限田均田之說董仲舒
倡限田於元狩而武帝不果行師丹請限
田於鴻嘉而成帝不能用乾興初詔限公
卿以下與衙前將吏田而任事者以為不
便夫井地旣廢富民業已肥殖長子孫傳
襲擬於封國而遽欲於歲月間盡褫其所
有此亦非人情矣是限田之不能行也亦
勢也由周而來七百年而魏孝文納李安
===
===
世之疏均授民田然不再傳而廢又百二
十年而唐太宗定口分世業之法然行未
久而報罷又二百三十年而周世宗詔行
元稹均田圖法然世族羣起而撓之夫周
制旣遠生齒錯出民之遷徙靡定田之給
代亡常而履畝握算官且不勝其鑿矣是
均田之不能久也亦勢也夫田不能井又
不能限又不能均均亦不能久第建步立
畝括田均賦此為至策邇者八閩守臣議
punctuated: 之覆轍，吁，亦迂矣！是井田之不能復也，勢也。議者無已，又有限田、均田之說。董仲舒倡限田於元狩，而武帝不果行；師丹請限田於鴻嘉，而成帝不能用；乾興初，詔限公卿以下與衙前將吏田，而任事者以為不便。夫井地旣廢，富民業已肥殖，長子孫，傳襲擬於封國，而遽欲於歲月間盡褫其所有，此亦非人情矣。是限田之不能行也，亦勢也。由周而來七百年，而魏孝文納李安世之疏，均授民田，然不再傳而廢；又百二十年，而唐太宗定口分、世業之法，然行未久而報罷；又二百三十年，而周世宗詔行元稹《均田圖》法，然世族羣起而撓之。夫周制旣遠，生齒錯出，民之遷徙靡定，田之給代亡常，而履畝握算，官且不勝其鑿矣。是均田之不能久也，亦勢也。夫田不能井，又不能限，又不能均，均亦不能久，第建步立畝，括田均賦，此為至策。邇者，八閩守臣議
translation_en: …overturned cart—alas, how impractical that would be! Thus, that the well-field system (jingtian) cannot be restored is a matter of prevailing circumstance. Having no other recourse, commentators have also proposed the doctrines of limiting landholdings (xiantian) and equalizing landholdings (juntian). Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 advocated limiting landholdings during the Yuanshou reign (122–117 BCE), yet Emperor Wu (Han Wudi) did not carry it out; Shi Dan 師丹 requested the limitation of landholdings during the Hongjia reign (20–17 BCE), yet Emperor Cheng (Han Chengdi) could not adopt it; at the beginning of the Qianxing reign (1022), an imperial decree limited the landholdings of high court officials (gongqing) and below, as well as prefectural officers and sub-official functionaries (yaqian jiangli), yet those in charge of affairs deemed it inconvenient. Now, once the well-field lands were abolished, wealthy commoners had already enriched and multiplied their estates, raising their sons and grandsons and passing down their holdings in a manner comparable to enfeoffed principalities; to suddenly wish within the space of a few months or years to strip them completely of all they possess—this too goes against human nature. Thus, that the limitation of landholdings cannot be practiced is also a matter of prevailing circumstance. Seven hundred years after the Zhou, Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei (Wei Xiaowendi) accepted the memorial of Li Anshi 李安世 and equally distributed land to the people, yet before two generations had passed it fell into abeyance; another one hundred and twenty years later, Emperor Taizong of Tang (Tang Taizong) established the law of personal-share (koufen) and hereditary-estate (shiye) lands, yet not long after being put into practice it was declared abolished; another two hundred and thirty years later, Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou (Zhou Shizong) decreed the implementation of the method in Yuan Zhen's 元稹 Chart for Equalizing Landholdings (Juntian tu), yet hereditary clans rose up in droves to obstruct it. Now, when the institutions of the Zhou are already remote, the population grows unevenly, the migrations of the people are unsettled, and the granting and succession of fields lack constancy, for officials to pace out the acres (mu) and hold the counting rods is more contrivance than they can bear. Thus, that the equalization of landholdings cannot endure is also a matter of prevailing circumstance. Now, since land cannot be arranged into well-fields, nor can it be limited, nor can it be equalized—and even if equalized, it cannot endure—simply establishing paces and setting up acres, surveying the fields and equalizing the taxes, is the supreme policy. Recently, the provincial officials in charge of the Eight Prefectures of Fujian (Bamin) deliberated on…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
括民田書奏
天子覽焉顧哀蒸庶失業天下罷匱乃下其議
於是太宰司農御史大夫言便宜者衆乃
下令檢括兩都十三部如閩部條章甚具
維時楚大小臣工罔不稟稟承
德意矢公矢毖分視督趣量山澤之入視莊屯
之額塞飛詭之竇責無籍之戶令所輸者
與所入相當取他羨補崩決償失額無嫁
稅匿逋者卽驗問嘉與更始弛其罰無論
===
世世偏累疲癃之民驩然若更生卽大姓
游民豪有力者亦喜過望謂千載始此一
睹則田不必井而井之之法存田不必均
而均之之法寓之役也楚壤數百年之積
蠹已去楚人數百年之沉痼已瘳當事諸
臣亦不遺餘力矣執事者猶以人窮吏弊
爲言而疑其難乂復爲楚人規萬世長守
之策愚以爲法本無弊也其始也議之難
其旣也守之尤難人情狃於故常驟而語
punctuated: 括民田。書奏，天子覽焉，顧哀蒸庶失業、天下罷匱，乃下其議。於是太宰、司農、御史大夫言便宜者衆，乃下令檢括兩都十三部，如閩部，條章甚具。維時，楚大小臣工罔不稟稟承德意，矢公矢毖，分視督趣：量山澤之入，視莊屯之額，塞飛詭之竇，責無籍之戶，令所輸者與所入相當，取他羨補崩決、償失額，無嫁稅，匿逋者卽驗問，嘉與更始，弛其罰。無論世世偏累、疲癃之民驩然若更生，卽大姓、游民、豪有力者，亦喜過望，謂千載始此一睹。則田不必井而井之之法存，田不必均而均之之法寓。之役也，楚壤數百年之積蠹已去，楚人數百年之沉痼已瘳，當事諸臣亦不遺餘力矣。執事者猶以人窮吏弊爲言，而疑其難乂，復爲楚人規萬世長守之策。愚以爲法本無弊也，其始也議之難，其旣也守之尤難。人情狃於故常，驟而語
translation_en: … surveying the people's land. When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven perused it; looking with compassion upon the common folk who had lost their livelihoods and the exhaustion and impoverishment of the realm, he handed down the proposal for deliberation. Thereupon, as the Minister of Personnel, the Minister of Revenue, and the Censor-in-Chief, along with many others, spoke of its advantages and suitability, an order was issued to inspect and survey the two capitals and thirteen provinces just as had been done in the province of Fujian, with the regulations and articles drawn up in full detail. At that time, the officials of Chu [Huguang], great and small alike, all reverently upheld the Emperor's benevolent intent; swearing to be impartial and diligent, they divided the regions to inspect and urge the work forward: measuring the yields of mountains and marshes, examining the quotas of estates and military farms, stopping up the loopholes of fraudulent registration and falsified ownership, and holding unregistered households accountable. They ensured that what was paid in tax matched what was taken in yield, used surpluses from elsewhere to make up for land lost to collapses and floods and to compensate for shortfalls in quotas, prevented the shifting of tax burdens onto others, and even when tax evaders and defaulters were verified and interrogated, graciously allowed them to make a fresh start and remitted their punishments. Not only did the exhausted and infirm commoners who had suffered from unequal burdens for generations rejoice as if given a new lease on life, even the great clans, floating population, and powerful magnates were pleased beyond their expectations, declaring that such a thing was seen only once in a thousand years. Thus, the land need not be divided into nine-square fields, yet the principle of the well-field system is preserved; the land need not be equalized, yet the principle of land equalization is embodied therein. Through this undertaking, the accumulated abuses of several hundred years in the lands of Chu have been removed, the chronic ailments of several hundred years among the people of Chu have been cured, and the officials in charge have spared no effort. Yet you, the Examiner, still speak of the exhaustion of the people and the malfeasance of clerks, doubting whether order can easily be maintained, and once again seek to plan for the people of Chu a policy that can be preserved for ten thousand generations. In my humble opinion, the law itself has no flaws; at the outset, it is difficult to deliberate upon, and afterward, it is even more difficult to maintain. Human nature is accustomed to old routines; if one suddenly speaks…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之以更革則必譸張駭愕而不吾信故議
之雖然利不十不苟興害不百不苟祛卽
興且祛矣有一不當於衆心則條格未下
而訾者隨其後亟議亟罷鯈興鯈廢福端
未試而禍孽萌矣故守之尤難宋景祐中
命郭諮均田賦已而重擾民遂罷怵於害
也皇祐中田京蔡挺均田而滄州民言不
便詔如舊摇於衆也嘉祐間遣包拯等分
按諸路行方田法而高本獨言不便甫均
===
數郡尋罷敗於私也三君子皆任事臣而
橫罹多口議亦垂寢法可易守哉顧守之
難者其弊不在下而在上其端不在未行
而在已行惟當事者弗爲害怵弗爲衆摇
弗爲私敗持獨斷之意操必然之畫法斯
久而無弊耳請卽一二所目覩者商之兼
幷濫冒
詔旨嘗懲之而今偷玩繩約狃習故智者何衆
也楚
punctuated: 之以更革，則必譸張駭愕而不吾信，故議之難。然利不十不苟興，害不百不苟祛。卽興且祛矣，有一不當於衆心，則條格未下而訾者隨其後，亟議亟罷，鯈興鯈廢，福端未試而禍孽萌矣，故守之尤難。宋景祐中，命郭諮均田賦，已而重擾民，遂罷，怵於害也；皇祐中，田京、蔡挺均田，而滄州民言不便，詔如舊，摇於衆也；嘉祐間，遣包拯等分按諸路，行方田法，而高本獨言不便，甫均數郡尋罷，敗於私也。三君子皆任事臣，而橫罹多口，議亦垂寢，法可易守哉？顧守之難者，其弊不在下而在上，其端不在未行而在已行。惟當事者弗爲害怵，弗爲衆摇，弗爲私敗，持獨斷之意，操必然之畫，法斯久而無弊耳。請卽一二所目覩者商之：兼幷濫冒，詔旨嘗懲之，而今偷玩繩約、狃習故智者，何衆也！楚
translation_en: … to them of reform, they will certainly become agitated, startled, and distrustful of us; therefore, deliberating on it is difficult [reading 雖 as 難]. Yet if the benefit is not tenfold, one does not lightly initiate a measure; if the harm is not a hundredfold, one does not lightly abolish it. Even when a measure has been initiated and the harm removed, if there is a single point that does not suit popular sentiment, then before the regulations have even been handed down, detractors will follow right behind. Quickly proposed and quickly abandoned, suddenly arising and suddenly abolished [reading 鯈 as 倏], before the beginnings of good fortune are even tested, the seeds of disaster have already sprouted; therefore, maintaining it is even more difficult. During the Jingyou era (1034–1038) of the Song dynasty, Guo Zi 郭諮 was ordered to equalize land taxes, but soon thereafter, out of concern that it would heavily disturb the people, the measure was abandoned—this was being intimidated by potential harm. During the Huangyou era (1049–1054), Tian Jing 田京 and Cai Ting 蔡挺 equalized landholdings, but when the people of Cangzhou 滄州 said it was inconvenient, an imperial edict ordered things restored to how they were before—this was being swayed by the multitude. During the Jiayou era (1056–1063), Bao Zheng 包拯 and others were dispatched to inspect the various circuits and implement the "square-fields" cadastral survey method (fangtian fa 方田法), yet Gao Ben 高本 alone argued that it was inconvenient; having barely equalized a few prefectures, it was soon abandoned—this was being ruined by private bias. All three gentlemen were ministers who shouldered responsibility for state affairs, yet they were perversely subjected to the carping of many mouths, and their proposals were nearly put to rest; how could a law be easily maintained? Yet as for the difficulty of maintaining a law, the fault lies not below but above, and its critical juncture lies not before its implementation, but after it has already been put into effect. Only if the officials in charge are not intimidated by harm, not swayed by the multitude, and not ruined by private bias, holding to a resolve of independent judgment and grasping an unshakeable plan, will the law endure for a long time without abuse. Allow me to discuss one or two matters that I have witnessed with my own eyes: annexation of land and fraudulent tax evasion have previously been punished by imperial edicts, yet today how numerous are those who laxly trifle with the legal restraints and cling to their old tricks! In Chu…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
諸侯王誠賢顧貴倨不習外事閹豎取累代
園奪者以為故籍而豪氓巨隷挾高貲以
相凌詡不可殫記彼單門孱戶厪厪以身
守世業者百無一焉豈惟違兩觀之束偪
有司之權將漫漶
恩澤之謂何矣宜令憲使者明勅條章無論士
若民按一切匿產亂籍隱畝避役之罰廉
其尤者下之吏以顯示
天子指夫然後倣限田均田之議以稍稍品節
===
之法庶幾可守哉墾荒招流
詔旨嘗督之而今草莽封盈戶口銷亡者何衆
也攷之
令甲荒閒以業貧民占籍以附流徙畸零以
寄寒細良規美政具在邇來里社漸縮於
舊占籍畸零按圖百不存一而墾田之數
率皆便文以罔上則勸罰之未明而招徠
之未至也夫荒閒易闢而不易守亡徙易
還而不易安鑄銍未施有司已履畝而稅
punctuated:
諸侯王誠賢，顧貴倨不習外事。閹豎取累代園奪者以為故籍，而豪氓巨隷挾高貲以相凌詡，不可殫記。彼單門孱戶，厪厪以身守世業者，百無一焉。豈惟違兩觀之束、偪有司之權，將漫漶恩澤之謂何矣！宜令憲使者明勅條章，無論士若民，按一切匿產亂籍、隱畝避役之罰，廉其尤者下之吏，以顯示天子指。夫然後倣限田、均田之議，以稍稍品節之，法庶幾可守哉！
墾荒招流，詔旨嘗督之，而今草莽封盈、戶口銷亡者，何衆也！攷之令甲，荒閒以業貧民，占籍以附流徙，畸零以寄寒細，良規美政具在。邇來里社漸縮於舊，占籍、畸零按圖百不存一，而墾田之數，率皆便文以罔上，則勸罰之未明，而招徠之未至也。夫荒閒易闢而不易守，亡徙易還而不易安。鑄銍未施，有司已履畝而稅
translation_en:
… The imperial princes and kings [of Chu] are truly worthy, yet being noble and haughty they are unfamiliar with external affairs. Eunuchs and palace attendants take lands seized for estates over successive generations and treat them as old registered holdings, while powerful commoners and prominent underlings rely on their vast wealth to bully and boast over one another, to an extent that cannot be fully recounted. As for those isolated families and weak households who barely manage to preserve their hereditary property in person, there is not one in a hundred. How does this merely violate the restraints promulgated from the palace watchtowers and encroach upon the authority of the local officials? What then becomes of the imperial grace that is thus blurred and squandered! Surveillance Commissioners and Censors should be ordered to clearly enforce the statutory regulations: regardless of whether gentry or commoner, they should apply all penalties for concealing property, falsifying registers, hiding land acreage, and evading labor service, investigating the most egregious offenders and handing them over to the judicial officials so as to clearly manifest the Son of Heaven's intent. Only after that, by emulating the proposals for limiting landholdings and equalizing land distribution so as to gradually regulate and restrict them, may the laws perhaps be upheld!

Reclaiming wasteland and attracting displaced people are matters that imperial decrees have previously urged; yet today, how numerous are the places overgrown with weeds and brush and the registered households that have dwindled and vanished! Examining the state statutes, wasteland and idle land were used to give livelihoods to poor commoners, local registration was used to attach wandering migrants, and odd-lot auxiliary categories were used to lodge the impoverished and humble—these fine rules and admirable policies are all extant. Recently, the rural communities have gradually shrunk compared to before; when checking the yellow registers for attached migrants and odd-lot households, not one in a hundred remains, while the reported figures for reclaimed land are mostly just convenient paperwork used to deceive superiors. This is because incentives and punishments have not been made clear, and efforts to attract and settle people have not reached their mark. Now, idle wasteland is easy to open up, but not easy to keep; fled migrants are easy to bring back, but not easy to settle in peace. Before plowshares and sickles have even been put to use, the authorities already pace off the acres to tax…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之堗突未黔有司已按籍而驅之民是以
憚於歸耕而溺於偷惰有卒汙萊耳宜
嚴飭所司嚴偽增之罰科重開疆之勸格土曠
矣召佃以廣其來召佃矣免租以固其存
免租矣弛役以優其力則歸耕之民纍纍
而至而地力有不盡者否也法庶幾可守
哉蠲逋省贖
詔旨嘗申之而今邑里蕭條徙弃故業者何衆
也語曰竭澤無魚焚田無獸往見寬仁
===
令下小民輒枵腹願須臾無死歡相勞也已
乃郡縣按簿而索吏一切夤緣為姦利烏
覩所謂蠲耶縣官之捃摭毋慮兩稅以上
如期徴發而無名之擾雜然竝生墨吏之
侵鈔毋但羨鍰即受賕納餉劀剃蒸人者
項相望也烏覩所謂省耶兩者妨農廢業
之本也自今憲使者宜宣
天子命持三尺以肅百屬取其所朘民脂奪民
時者劾而汰之使
punctuated:
之，堗突未黔，有司已按籍而驅之。民是以憚於歸耕，而溺於偷惰，有卒汙萊耳。宜嚴飭所司，嚴偽增之罰科，重開疆之勸格。土曠矣，召佃以廣其來；召佃矣，免租以固其存；免租矣，弛役以優其力。則歸耕之民纍纍而至，而地力有不盡者否也？法庶幾可守哉！
蠲逋省贖，詔旨嘗申之，而今邑里蕭條、徙弃故業者何衆也？語曰：「竭澤無魚，焚田無獸。」往見寬仁令下，小民輒枵腹願須臾無死，歡相勞也。已乃郡縣按簿而索，吏一切夤緣為姦利，烏覩所謂蠲耶？縣官之捃摭，毋慮兩稅以上如期徴發，而無名之擾雜然竝生；墨吏之侵鈔，毋但羨鍰，即受賕納餉，劀剃蒸人者項相望也，烏覩所謂省耶？兩者，妨農廢業之本也。自今憲使者宜宣天子命，持三尺以肅百屬，取其所朘民脂、奪民時者，劾而汰之，使
translation_en:
… them; before their stove chimneys have even turned black with soot, the authorities are already consulting the registers to press them into service. Because of this, the people dread returning to the plow and sink into idleness, leaving the fields to end up as flooded weeds. The relevant authorities should be strictly instructed to enforce severe penalty classifications for fabricated increases in acreage and to give weight to the reward standards for opening up new land. Where the land lies vast and empty, call in tenants to broaden the influx of settlers; once tenants have been called in, exempt them from land rent to secure their remaining; once they have been exempted from rent, relax their labor service to give ease to their strength. Then people returning to the plow will arrive in continuous streams—and will the productivity of the soil not be fully realized? In this way, the laws may perhaps be upheld!

Remitting tax arrears and reducing redemption fines have previously been reiterated in imperial decrees, yet why are there now so many bleak towns and villages, and so many people who migrate and abandon their ancestral livelihoods? The proverb says: "Drain the marsh and there will be no fish; burn the hunting grounds and there will be no beasts." In the past, when a benevolent and lenient order was handed down, the common people, even on empty stomachs, would wish to hold off death for a moment longer and joyfully comfort one another. Yet before long, the prefectures and counties demand payment according to the registers, and the subofficial functionaries use every opportunity to collude for illicit profit—where does one see any so-called remission? As for the exactions of the county magistrates, not only are the twice-yearly taxes and upward levied on schedule, but unscheduled disturbances arise all at once in great confusion; as for the depredations of corrupt officials, it is not merely a matter of surplus redemption money, for those who take bribes, accept provisions, and scrape and fleece the multitude can be seen one after another—where does one see any so-called reduction? These two things are the root causes of hindering agriculture and ruining livelihoods. From now on, the surveillance commissioners should proclaim the commands of the Son of Heaven, uphold the law code to bring order to the hundred subordinate officials, and impeach and weed out those who drain the fat of the people and rob them of their seasonal agricultural time, causing…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
詔令信而野沾必至之澤吏所至廉平與民休
息黎庶堵安而業皆世保法庶幾可守哉
崇本殿末
詔旨嘗言之而今農祥罔候稼政不脩者何衆
也夫督耕勉植趨穫勸藏非有司上務哉
其次莫若驅末作以緣南畝故
國初治農有定職水利有專官其重田事如
此後世計其所由入而不計其所由生則
見以為剩員而悉裁之舟車繁而耒耜銷
===
緇黃衆而桑柘稀溝洫堙而灌溉廢罪獨
在民哉宜推古建設之意稍復職事令之
朝脩夕舉日考旬會吏家子弟弃田作者
輒斥罷之如邵信臣之在南陽民挾漁獵
具者盡屛之使業耕蠶如文翁之在下蔡
披荊棘載酒食勞民甽畝如張全義之在
河南則農事勸課地力豐贏磽瘠可為良
沃孰忍輕弃之法庶幾可守哉夫是四者
其一常在下而上不問也其三常在上而
punctuated: 詔令信而野沾必至之澤，吏所至廉平，與民休息。黎庶堵安，而業皆世保，法庶幾可守哉！崇本殿末，詔旨嘗言之，而今農祥罔候，稼政不脩者，何衆也！夫督耕勉植、趨穫勸藏，非有司上務哉？其次莫若驅末作以緣南畝。故國初治農有定職，水利有專官，其重田事如此。後世計其所由入，而不計其所由生，則見以為剩員而悉裁之。舟車繁而耒耜銷，緇黃衆而桑柘稀，溝洫堙而灌溉廢，罪獨在民哉？宜推古建設之意，稍復職事，令之朝脩夕舉，日考旬會。吏家子弟弃田作者輒斥罷之，如邵信臣之在南陽；民挾漁獵具者盡屛之使業耕蠶，如文翁之在下蔡；披荊棘，載酒食勞民甽畝，如張全義之在河南。則農事勸課，地力豐贏，磽瘠可為良沃，孰忍輕弃之？法庶幾可守哉！夫是四者，其一常在下而上不問也，其三常在上而
translation_en:
…imperial edicts be trusted and the countryside be moistened by blessings that are sure to arrive, and wherever officials go, let them be incorruptible and fair, allowing the people to rest and recuperate. When the common people live in security within their walls and their livelihoods are preserved for generations, then the laws can perhaps be maintained!

Revering the fundamental occupation [agriculture] and placing secondary pursuits [commerce and crafts] last has previously been stated in imperial edicts, yet today how numerous are those who fail to observe the auspicious stars for farming and neglect agricultural administration! Are not supervising plowing and encouraging planting, hastening the harvest and urging storage, the supreme duties of the local authorities? Next to this, nothing is better than driving those in secondary pursuits back to the southern acres [the fields]. Thus, at the founding of our Dynasty, there were fixed posts for managing agriculture and specialized officials for water conservancy; such was the importance attached to farming matters. Later generations calculated whence revenue came in, without calculating whence it was produced; thus they viewed these posts as superfluous personnel and abolished them all. When boats and carts multiply while plowshares melt away, when Buddhist monks and Daoist priests grow numerous while mulberry and cudrania trees become sparse, and when ditches and channels silt up while irrigation falls into disuse, does the fault lie solely with the people?

We ought to extend the intent behind the ancient establishment of offices and somewhat restore these duties, ordering officials to attend to them from morning to night, examining them daily and tallying results every ten days. Sons and younger brothers of official families who abandon fieldwork should be promptly dismissed, just as Shao Xinchen 邵信臣 did in Nanyang 南陽; commoners carrying fishing and hunting gear should all be turned away and made to practice farming and sericulture, just as Wen Weng 文翁 did in Xiacai 下蔡; and officials should clear away brambles and carry wine and food to reward and comfort the people in the ditches and fields, just as Zhang Quanyi 張全義 did in Henan 河南. Then agricultural work will be encouraged and supervised, the productivity of the land will be abundant and yield a surplus, and barren and stony soil can be turned into fine, fertile land—who would bear to lightly abandon it? Thus the laws can perhaps be maintained!

Now, of these four matters, one always lies with those below while those above do not inquire into it; three always lie with those above while…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
下不筴也要皆
君相所常軫念爲之三令五申者直有司廢格
不用耳今之謀楚事者不求之上而求之
下舛也不求之已行而求之未行悖也卽
悖且舛而欲圖萬世之慮能乎記有曰地
廣大荒而不治士之辱也又曰虞芮之間
地有餘而人不足君子恥之假令郡縣長
吏人人懷恥辱之念而承奉
明詔若救火追亡子無敢後則弊無不祛利無
===
不興善後之圖宜無出此矣
punctuated: 下不筴也。要皆君相所常軫念，爲之三令五申者，直有司廢格不用耳。今之謀楚事者，不求之上而求之下，舛也；不求之已行而求之未行，悖也。卽悖且舛，而欲圖萬世之慮，能乎？《記》有曰：「地廣大，荒而不治，士之辱也。」又曰：「虞、芮之間，地有餘而人不足，君子恥之。」假令郡縣長吏人人懷恥辱之念，而承奉明詔，若救火、追亡子，無敢後，則弊無不祛，利無不興，善後之圖宜無出此矣。
translation_en: … the lower levels fail to plan for them. In sum, these are all matters over which the ruler and his chief ministers constantly show anxious concern, issuing repeated orders and injunctions on their behalf—it is simply that the local authorities set them aside and fail to carry them out. Those who deliberate on the affairs of Chu (Huguang) today do not seek the solution from above, but instead seek it from below: this is misguided. They do not seek it in measures already enacted, but instead seek it in measures not yet enacted: this is perverse. Being at once perverse and misguided, yet wishing to devise a plan for ten thousand generations—is that possible? The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "When the land is vast and extensive, yet left overgrown and uncultivated, this is the disgrace of the officer." And it is also said: "Between Yu and Rui, there is a surplus of land and a shortage of people; the gentleman is ashamed of this." Suppose the senior officials of the prefectures and counties every one harbored this sense of shame and disgrace, and received and upheld the illustrious imperial edicts as urgently as if fighting a fire or pursuing a runaway child, none daring to lag behind—then no abuse would go unremoved, no benefit would go unpromoted, and any plan for future reconstruction surely would not go beyond this.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
御史旣大比楚士錄成將籍
奏之不佞有光以職事載牘宜
敘末端則思以
國家致士之意與
君臣大義明告多士迺後敢受成
也洪武初以弓矢平一海內
===
遭
明初定未遑庠序之事
高皇帝委心精意思爲天下作新
更始喟然歎興於學疾文言
之無實乃
詔中外博士弟子人各守受一經
三歲輒試非受業身通六藝
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
御史旣大比楚士，錄成，將籍奏之。不佞有光以職事載牘，宜敘末端，則思以國家致士之意與君臣大義明告多士，迺後敢受成也。洪武初，以弓矢平一海內，遭明初定，未遑庠序之事。高皇帝委心精意，思爲天下作新更始，喟然歎興於學，疾文言之無實，乃詔中外博士弟子，人各守受一經，三歲輒試。非受業身通六藝
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

After the Censor had conducted the triennial examination of the scholars of Chu [Huguang] and the record was completed and about to be registered and presented to the throne, I, the unworthy Youguang, having my name recorded in the documents by virtue of my official duties, ought to write a postface at the end. I therefore reflected that I should clearly proclaim to the many scholars the state's intention in recruiting scholars and the great principle binding ruler and minister, before daring to accept the completed work.

At the beginning of the Hongwu era [1368–1398], when all within the seas was pacified and unified by bow and arrow, and encountering the initial stabilization of the Ming, there was not yet leisure for the affairs of schools. The High Emperor [Hongwu], devoting his heart and concentrating his thoughts, wished to bring about renewal and a fresh start for the empire. With a deep sigh, he sought to promote learning, and detesting the emptiness of ornate words, he thereupon decreed that Erudites and Government Students inside and outside the capital should each receive and hold fast to one Classic, and be examined every three years. Those who had not received instruction and personally mastered the Six Arts…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
者弗以名聞著爲
功令其它空語虚稱若詞賦諸
不在
令中者禁不得用卽漢所設孝
廉賢良明經茂才諸科皆一
切罷去若曰
國家所以致士非曉暢六經大
===
義莫可通今古分際備
任使耳
列聖承流道化熙洽二百年餘百
舉百全海內異能之士材懷
伊呂行若周孔靡不以此發
冢焉誦義無窮蓋
高皇帝聖神文武於天下萬世皆
punctuated: 者，弗以名聞，著爲功令。其它空語虚稱，若詞賦諸不在令中者，禁不得用。卽漢所設孝廉、賢良、明經、茂才諸科，皆一切罷去。若曰國家所以致士，非曉暢六經大義，莫可通今古分際，備任使耳。列聖承流，道化熙洽，二百年餘，百舉百全。海內異能之士，材懷伊、呂，行若周、孔，靡不以此發冢焉，誦義無窮。蓋高皇帝聖神文武，於天下萬世，皆
translation_en:
… were not to have their names reported, and this was enacted into the examination regulations. As for other empty talk and hollow praise, such as rhapsodies and poetic expositions and all other genres not included in the ordinances, their use was forbidden. Even the various categories established in the Han dynasty—such as the Filially Pious and Incorrupt (xiaolian), the Worthy and Upright (xianliang), Experts in the Classics (mingjing), and Flourishing Talents (maocai)—were all completely abolished. It was as if to say that the means by which the dynasty recruits scholars requires that unless they thoroughly understand the great principles of the Six Classics, none can comprehend the distinctions and connections between past and present or be ready for official appointment and service.

The successive sage emperors carried forward this tradition, and moral transformation flourished in harmony. For more than two hundred years, every measure taken has been wholly complete. Scholars of extraordinary ability within the seas—harboring talents like those of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, and conducting themselves like the Duke of Zhou and Confucius—have without exception risen to prominence [?] through this system, praising its righteousness without end. Truly, the High Emperor (Hongwu), in his sagely divinity and civil and martial splendor, for the empire and for ten thousand generations…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有以灼睹其竅會而豫徵其
微眇旣已著爲
功令欲以制科網羅儁乂豈其
使在野猶有遺賢乎哉不佞
應御史聘而來也旣卒業多
士所爲文則見人人標本經
術根柢大義纚纚洋洋足聽
===
===
聞矣意者楚於
今日獨稱最盛山川靈爽默牖
其衷以保定
王國又其仰承
主上廣厲學官至意耳目歡感潛
潤臭味以是莫不雲蒸龍變
應
punctuated: 有以灼睹其竅會，而豫徵其微眇。旣已著爲功令，欲以制科網羅儁乂，豈其使在野猶有遺賢乎哉？不佞應御史聘而來也，旣卒業多士所爲文，則見人人標本經術、根柢大義，纚纚洋洋，足聽聞矣。意者楚於今日獨稱最盛，山川靈爽默牖其衷以保定王國；又其仰承主上廣厲學官至意，耳目歡感，潛潤臭味，以是莫不雲蒸龍變，應
translation_en: …had the means to clearly perceive the key junctures and foresee the subtle essentials. Since this has already been established in the regulations for evaluating merit, with the aim of gathering men of outstanding talent through the examination system, how could worthy men still be left neglected in the wilderness? In my unworthiness, I came in response to the Censor's invitation; having finished reading through the essays composed by the many scholars, I saw that every one of them took classical learning as both branch and root, grounding themselves in the great principles—flowing continuously and grandly, well worth hearing! Perhaps it is that Chu today alone is acclaimed as the most flourishing: the numinous spirits of its mountains and rivers silently enlighten their hearts so as to safeguard the royal state; and furthermore, looking up to receive our Sovereign's supreme intention to broadly encourage the Confucian schools, their ears and eyes are joyfully moved and they are quietly steeped in its influence, so that none fail to rise like clouds and transform like dragons in response to…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
明詔與雖然臣道至難言也事使
之義非細故矣名爲事君而
不造其極謂之不忠苞舉其
道告人而不語其至謂之不
盡請爲子多士畢陳之今夫
士伏處嵓巖究徧六經本指
不稱君臣之分無所逃於天
===
地乎事是君也雖以神州赤
縣之大至欲有所之而卒無
逃焉卽終其身猶在日月照
臨之內其義可睹已人臣委
質事君道固多端總之不自
有其身者近是老生豎儒守
其師說白首不能窺見聖道
punctuated: 明詔與？雖然，臣道至難言也，事使之義非細故矣。名爲事君而不造其極，謂之不忠；苞舉其道告人而不語其至，謂之不盡。請爲子多士畢陳之。今夫士伏處嵓巖，究徧六經本指，不稱君臣之分無所逃於天地乎？事是君也，雖以神州赤縣之大，至欲有所之而卒無逃焉，卽終其身猶在日月照臨之內，其義可睹已。人臣委質事君，道固多端，總之不自有其身者近是。老生豎儒守其師說，白首不能窺見聖道
translation_en: … the enlightened decree? Even so, the Way of the minister is most difficult to speak of, and the principle of serving a ruler and employing a minister is no trivial matter. To be said to serve one's ruler in name yet fail to reach the utmost limit of devotion is called disloyalty; to encompass this Way in speaking to others yet fail to tell them of its highest perfection is called falling short of completeness. Allow me to set this forth in full for you, the many scholars. Now when a scholar lives in retirement among crags and cliffs and thoroughly investigates the fundamental purport of the Six Classics, does he not declare that there is nowhere between heaven and earth to escape the moral bond between ruler and minister? In serving this ruler, vast though the sacred realm of China may be, even if one wished to go elsewhere, in the end there is nowhere to escape; even to the end of one's life one remains within the illumination of the sun and moon—from this, its principle can be clearly seen. When a minister pledges himself to serve his ruler, though the ways of doing so are assuredly manifold, in sum it comes closest to no longer regarding his person as his own. Old pedants and petty Confucians cling to the doctrines of their teachers and even into white-haired old age are unable to catch a glimpse of the sage's Way…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之大全一當利害輒掉臂不
顧以此爲稟於古昔夫聖人
之道具在六經可考鏡也平
生誦讀詩書豈眞未嘗決擇
異同探厥閫奧哉彼其心以
爲此可博名此可規利此可
遠嫌而避咎以故處其便於
===
厥躬而遺其難於
君父有所託而逃耳嗟乎
國家舉士之謂何廼重自愛惜
如此卽有緩急安所賴之爾
多士舉矣其務一乃心定乃
志毋持祿養交毋詭飾干譽
毋相眉睫與時浮沉毋矯矯
punctuated: 之大全，一當利害，輒掉臂不顧，以此爲稟於古昔。夫聖人之道，具在《六經》，可考鏡也。平生誦讀《詩》《書》，豈眞未嘗決擇異同、探厥閫奧哉？彼其心以爲：此可博名，此可規利，此可遠嫌而避咎。以故處其便於厥躬，而遺其難於君父，有所託而逃耳。嗟乎！國家舉士之謂何？廼重自愛惜如此，卽有緩急，安所賴之？爾多士舉矣，其務一乃心，定乃志，毋持祿養交，毋詭飾干譽，毋相眉睫與時浮沉，毋矯矯
translation_en:
… in its entirety; as soon as they confront personal advantage or harm, they swing their arms and walk away without looking back, claiming that in doing so they are adhering to antiquity. Yet the Way of the Sages is fully set forth in the Six Classics and can be examined there as in a mirror. Throughout their lives they recite the Odes and the Documents—have they truly never weighed the differences and similarities among doctrines or plumbed their deepest mysteries? Rather, in their hearts they calculate: "This will win me fame; this will secure me profit; this will keep me clear of suspicion and allow me to escape blame." And so they reserve what is convenient for themselves while leaving the difficulties to their ruler and father, finding some pretext under which to abscond. Alas! For what purpose does the state select scholars? If instead they cherish and spare themselves to such a degree, then should an emergency arise, what reliance can be placed upon them?

You many scholars have now been selected as provincial graduates. Strive to unify your hearts and fix your resolve! Do not merely cling to your emoluments and cultivate personal connections; do not practice deceitful posturing to fish for praise; do not watch others' expressions and drift up and down with the times; do not affectedly…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以一節自好毋以利害付諸
身以成敗付諸
國事矢心殫誠事
上使凡所爲唯
天地鬼神實臨之其道詎不偉與
不佞道襄樊望隆中知諸葛
忠武侯楚產也彼當漢末造
===
國步多艱成敗利鈍非所逆
睹猶然鞠躬盡瘁今讀其言
忠貞之心千古如一日焉矧
皇上嚮意文學每飯側席天下賢
者百司庶府少有功能罔不
畢敘有
君如此其忍負之夫結綠蘊山懸
punctuated: 以一節自好，毋以利害付諸身、以成敗付諸國事。矢心殫誠事上，使凡所爲唯天地鬼神實臨之，其道詎不偉與？不佞道襄樊，望隆中，知諸葛忠武侯楚產也。彼當漢末造，國步多艱，成敗利鈍非所逆睹，猶然鞠躬盡瘁。今讀其言，忠貞之心，千古如一日焉。矧皇上嚮意文學，每飯側席，天下賢者、百司庶府，少有功能，罔不畢敘。有君如此，其忍負之？夫結綠蘊山，懸
translation_en:
… to pride yourselves on a single narrow virtue; do not weigh personal advantage and harm for yourselves while leaving success or failure to the affairs of the state. Pledge your hearts and exhaust your sincerity in serving the Sovereign, so that in all you do, Heaven, Earth, and the spirits and gods truly oversee you—would this way not be magnificent?

As I, an unworthy man, traveled by way of Xiangyang and Fancheng and gazed toward Longzhong, I reflected that Zhuge, Marquis Zhongwu (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮), was associated with the lands of Chu. Facing the waning days of the Han, when the fortunes of the state were beset with difficulties and success or failure, smooth progress or setback could not be foreseen, he nonetheless bowed his body and exhausted his strength to the utmost. Today, when we read his words, his loyal and steadfast heart remains as vivid across a thousand ages as if it were a single day. How much more so now, when His Majesty turns his mind toward learning and letters, leaving his seat unoccupied at every meal in eager anticipation of the worthy; among the worthies of the realm and the officials of all offices and bureaus, anyone with the slightest merit and capability is without exception duly recognized and promoted. Having a Sovereign such as this, how could you bear to fail Him? Now, the Jielü jade lies hidden in the mountains, and the Xuan…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
黎匿頷良工嬰距爪披逆鱗
以求之亡所自愛重適用也
士人少負四方之志長試之
藝類能剌剌道天下計至令
受事則舉其生平而弁髦之
斯則燕石魚目末之若矣即
工人者安所傅眊臊之誅焉
今多士挾筴登途方日夜裝
而見
天子趨
日月之末光非抱空質矣
上幸止輦而聽將試之庶官使得
自見有日也其尚誦說所聞
大義蘄自盡其經術以無負
punctuated: 黎匿頷，良工嬰距爪、披逆鱗以求之，亡所自愛，重適用也。士人少負四方之志，長試之藝，類能剌剌道天下計；至令受事，則舉其生平而弁髦之，斯則燕石、魚目末之若矣，即工人者安所傅眊臊之誅焉？今多士挾筴登途，方日夜裝而見天子，趨日月之末光，非抱空質矣。上幸止輦而聽，將試之庶官，使得自見有日也。其尚誦說所聞大義，蘄自盡其經術，以無負
translation_en: … and the Xuanli jade is hidden beneath the dragon's chin, yet a master craftsman will brave spurs and claws and stroke the inverted scales in order to obtain them, without sparing himself, because he values their practical utility. When scholars are young, they harbor ambitions to serve throughout the realm, and when grown, they are tested in the literary arts; they are generally able to discourse endlessly on plans for the empire. Yet when they are given office and take up their duties, they cast aside everything they have learned in their lives as if it were a useless child's cap. In that case, they are not even equal to a worthless stone from Yan or a fish-eye pearl—and how then can the craftsman escape the blame for being dim-sighted and blind [?]? Now, as you many scholars pack your books and set out on the road, preparing day and night to go for an audience with the Son of Heaven and hasten toward the lingering light of the sun and moon, you do not come holding mere empty substance. Should His Majesty graciously halt his imperial carriage to listen, and soon test you in various official posts, the day when you will be able to manifest your abilities is at hand. May you continue to recite and expound the great principles you have learned, striving to exhaust your mastery of the classics and their practical application, so as not to betray…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國家設科求材意不佞竝有榮
施哉
山東東昌府莘縣儒學敎諭
湯有光謹序
punctuated:
國家設科求材意，不佞竝有榮施哉！
山東東昌府莘縣儒學敎諭湯有光謹序。
translation_en:
… the Dynastic State's intent in establishing the examinations to seek out talent. Would I not then share in the glorious bestowal of honor as well!

Respectfully written as a postface by Tang Youguang 湯有光, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shen County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
萬曆歲壬午復當比士於鄉
上以士文不中程多鉤棘語以衒
竒袤非
盛世典詔有司學官凡諸不類者
亟斥之謬進者罰於是御史
錢岱奉
===
詔按湖廣綱紀其事御史嘗比士
東省所錄文足為士程士斌
斌皆適用惟楚眎東省其地
廣倍之而士額多四之一御
史於是皇皇益毖脊秉憲申
要求所以祇若
明詔則戒環聚檺幾非常侍不時
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序
萬曆歲壬午，復當比士於鄉。上以士文不中程，多鉤棘語以衒竒袤，非盛世典，詔有司、學官：凡諸不類者，亟斥之；謬進者，罰。於是御史錢岱奉詔按湖廣，綱紀其事。御史嘗比士東省，所錄文足為士程，士斌斌皆適用。惟楚眎東省，其地廣倍之，而士額多四之一。御史於是皇皇益毖，脊秉憲申要，求所以祇若明詔。則戒環聚、檺幾微，常侍不時，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the renwu year of the Wanli reign (1582), it was once again time to examine and select scholars in the provinces. Because the compositions of scholars did not conform to standard models and were filled with convoluted and thorny phrasing meant to show off strange and deviant ideas—which was not appropriate for the institutions of a flourishing age—His Majesty issued an edict to the relevant authorities and Confucian school officials: all those whose writings are improper must be promptly rejected, and officials who mistakenly advance them shall be punished. Accordingly, Investigating Censor Qian Dai 錢岱 received the imperial edict to tour Huguang as Regional Inspector and take overall charge of the affair. The Censor had previously examined scholars in the eastern province (Shandong), where the essays he selected for the record were worthy of serving as model answers for scholars, and the refined scholars chosen were all suited for practical service. Yet compared to the eastern province, Chu (Huguang) has twice the territory, and its quota of scholars is greater by a quarter. The Censor was therefore ever more anxious and exercised even greater caution, upholding the statutory regulations and reiterating the essential rules [?], seeking every means to reverently comply with the illustrious edict. Thus he guarded against the gathering of crowds, watched closely for subtle irregularities [?], and kept constant attendance at irregular hours [?], …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
簾以内外無弗飭者内則幣
聘遴暨教諭湯有光爲考試
官教諭楊鳳鳴顧爲麟尹禮
繼趙永祿訓導王廷俊范調
元范時芳趙嘉猷爲同考試
官外則自提調官左布政使
錢藻右布政使賈待問監試
===
官按察使馬文煒僉事王圻
而下咸矢心矢慎如御史指
乃合提學副使曹慎管大勳
僉事龍宗武所簡士二千七
百三試之得雋九十人籍奏
上御史授簡於遴屬遴當有稱說
遴謂諸生令稱選士於鄉不
punctuated: 簾以内外，無弗飭者。内則幣聘遴暨教諭湯有光爲考試官，教諭楊鳳鳴、顧爲麟、尹禮繼、趙永祿，訓導王廷俊、范調元、范時芳、趙嘉猷爲同考試官；外則自提調官左布政使錢藻、右布政使賈待問，監試官按察使馬文煒、僉事王圻而下，咸矢心矢慎，如御史指。乃合提學副使曹慎、管大勳，僉事龍宗武所簡士二千七百，三試之，得雋九十人，籍奏上。御史授簡於遴，屬遴當有稱說。遴謂諸生：「令稱選士於鄉，不
translation_en: … both inside and outside the curtain, there was nothing not put in strict order. For the inner administration, gifts were sent to invite me, [Xie] Lin 遴, together with County Director of Studies Tang Youguang 湯有光, to serve as Examiners; and County Directors of Studies Yang Fengming 楊鳳鳴, Gu Weilin 顧爲麟, Yin Liji 尹禮繼, and Zhao Yonglu 趙永祿, along with Assistant Instructors Wang Tingjun 王廷俊, Fan Tiaoyuan 范調元, Fan Shifang 范時芳, and Zhao Jiayou 趙嘉猷, to serve as Associate Examiners. For the outer administration, from the Proctors—Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Qian Zao 錢藻 and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Jia Daiwen 賈待問—and the Surveillance Officials—Surveillance Commissioner Ma Wenwei 馬文煒 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qi 王圻—on down, all pledged their hearts and exercised the utmost caution, in accordance with the Censor's instructions. Thereupon, bringing together the two thousand seven hundred scholars selected by Education-intendant Vice Commissioners Cao Shen 曹慎 and Guan Daxun 管大勳 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Long Zongwu 龍宗武, we tested them in three sessions and obtained ninety outstanding men, whose roster was submitted to the throne in a memorial. The Censor handed the writing slips to me, Lin, charging that I should have words of counsel. I say to the students: "The statutes state that scholars selected from the local districts are exempted from…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
征矣諸生知爾鄕乎視
今日之籍天下雖其鄕之視
今日之統天下實莫敢鄕也
肅皇帝纘有
大命寔肇爾南服其更朔元寔始
諸壬午壬者任也於行爲水
萬物莫弗任養焉午南位於
===
卦爲離萬物莫弗明盛焉荆
故天地之中南水火旣濟之
繇也在列宿則麗翼軫爲鶉
尾之次東揚西雍南粤北豫
在九州則稱闊衍表介二嶽
江漢九江潜沱雲夢苞絡衡
貫其中名神區巳自雲陽氏
punctuated: 征矣。諸生知爾鄕乎？視今日之籍，天下雖其鄕之；視今日之統，天下實莫敢鄕也。肅皇帝纘有大命，寔肇爾南服，其更朔元，寔始諸壬午。壬者，任也，於行爲水，萬物莫弗任養焉；午，南位，於卦爲離，萬物莫弗明盛焉。荆故天地之中南，水火旣濟之繇也。在列宿則麗翼、軫，爲鶉尾之次。東揚、西雍、南粤、北豫，在九州則稱闊衍，表介二嶽，江、漢、九江、潜、沱、雲、夢苞絡衡貫其中，名神區巳。自雲陽氏
translation_en: … exempt from levies. Do you students truly know your native region? Viewed from today's registers, although the realm regards it as a local region; viewed from today's imperial lineage, no region in the realm would dare treat it as merely another local region! When the Augustus Shizong (Emperor Su 肅皇帝, the Jiajing Emperor) succeeded to the Great Mandate, he actually rose from your southern domain; and when he changed the calendar era to its first year, it indeed began in a renwu year (1522). Ren means "to bear and nurture" (ren); among the Five Phases it corresponds to Water, by which there is nothing among the myriad things that is not sustained and nourished. Wu is the southern position; among the trigrams it corresponds to Li (Fire and Brightness), by which there is nothing among the myriad things that does not flourish in brilliance. Jingzhou (Huguang) is inherently the central south of Heaven and Earth, embodying the hexagram pronouncement of Water and Fire in "Already Fording" (Jiji). Among the constellations, it is aligned with the Wings (Yi) and Chariot-Platform (Zhen) mansions, forming the celestial station of the Quail's Tail (Chunwei). Bordered by Yangzhou to the east, Yongzhou to the west, Baiyue to the south, and Yuzhou to the north, among the Nine Provinces it is renowned for its vast expanse. Marked out and bounded by two sacred peaks, with the Yangzi, the Han, the Nine Rivers (Jiujiang), the Qian, the Tuo, and the Yun and Meng marshes encompassing and traversing its interior, it is truly famed as a numinous precinct! Since the time when the Yunyang clan …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
創都沙丘赫然列於神明之
紀其太上則離光氏因是以
官天地遂皇氏因是以燭萬
物昆吾雄諸侯熊氏長五覇
皆綿暦千百流祚無窮雖夷
陵至於楚卽不與中國會盟
乃墳典丘索國人類能識之
===
智謀勇鬭獨衡乎天下其次
濯靈耀采紛載丹青重黎佐
嚳以司燿鬻熊師文以新命
尹吉二甫弘弼亮於周莫敖
鬭穀競勛華於族三閭以忠
憤寤主陳良以文學顯名左
史檮杌媲義春秋雞次鐸氏
punctuated: 創都沙丘，赫然列於神明之紀。其太上，則離光氏因是以官天地，遂皇氏因是以燭萬物；昆吾雄諸侯，熊氏長五覇，皆綿暦千百，流祚無窮。雖夷陵至於楚，卽不與中國會盟，乃《墳》、《典》、《丘》、《索》，國人類能識之，智謀勇鬭，獨衡乎天下。其次，濯靈耀采，紛載丹青：重黎佐嚳以司燿，鬻熊師文以新命，尹、吉二甫弘弼亮於周，莫敖、鬭穀競勛華於族，三閭以忠憤寤主，陳良以文學顯名，左史《檮杌》媲義《春秋》，雞次、鐸氏……
translation_en: …established his capital at Shaqiu 沙丘, standing illustriously in the annals of the divine sovereigns. In highest antiquity, Liguangshi 離光氏 relied on this region to govern heaven and earth, and Suihuangshi 遂皇氏 relied on it to illuminate the myriad things. Kunwu 昆吾 held sway among the feudal lords, and the Xiong 熊 clan led the Five Hegemons; both endured for hundreds and thousands of years, passing down boundless blessings. Even when prestige declined down to the era of Chu 楚, though it did not join in the covenants and alliances of the Central States, the people of the state were generally able to understand the Three Fen (San Fen 三墳), Five Dian (Wu Dian 五典), Eight Qiu (Ba Qiu 八丘), and Nine Suo (Jiu Suo 九索), and in strategic wisdom and brave combat they alone counterbalanced the rest of the realm. Next, those who cleansed their spirits and shone in brilliance are abundantly recorded in the histories: Chongli 重黎 assisted Emperor Ku 嚳 as Director of Fire; Yuxiong 鬻熊 served as preceptor to King Wen 文王 in renewing the Mandate; Yin Jifu 尹吉甫 and仲山甫 [? "the two Fu, Yin and Ji"] broadly assisted and brought clarity to the Zhou 周; the Mo'ao 莫敖 and Dou Guwutu 鬭穀於菟 vied in meritorious glory within their clans; the Minister of the Three Lanes (Sanlü Dafu 三閭大夫, Qu Yuan 屈原) sought to awaken his ruler through loyal indignation; Chen Liang 陳良 became renowned for his learning and scholarship; the Left Scribe's (Zuoshi 左史) Taowu 檮杌 matched the moral principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋); Jici 雞次 and Duoshi 鐸氏…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有文武勳著常彝故天下傾
心楚材以為地王也垂六十
年而為
穆皇
今上得道之秉處乎中央治瑩化
醇無文不懷六幕為一諸生
幸生斯世孕之以泰清奠之
===
以泰寧范無形甞無味譬大
造之育萬物其雨露猶偏焉
履不諱之
朝戴無垓之宇出即危言處即
危行譬大明之燭萬物其照
臨猶偏焉是楚人士所任養
於
punctuated: 有文武勳，著常彝，故天下傾心楚材，以為地王也。垂六十年而為穆皇、今上，得道之秉，處乎中央，治瑩化醇，無文不懷，六幕為一。諸生幸生斯世，孕之以泰清，奠之以泰寧，范無形，甞無味，譬大造之育萬物，其雨露猶偏焉；履不諱之朝，戴無垓之宇，出即危言，處即危行，譬大明之燭萬物，其照臨猶偏焉。是楚人士所任養於
translation_en: …had civil and military accomplishments recorded on the ceremonial banners and bronze vessels; thus the entire realm admired the talents of Chu, taking this land to be supreme. Nearly sixty years passed down to Emperor Mu [the Longqing Emperor] and His Present Majesty, who have grasped the handle of the Way and dwell at the center. Their governance is lustrous and their transformation pure; there is no literary culture they do not cherish, and the six directions are united as one. The students are fortunate to be born in this age, nurtured in supreme clarity and settled in supreme peace, molded by the formless and tasting the flavorless—just as the Great Creator nourishes the myriad things, yet His rain and dew favor them all the more. Treading a court that shuns no candid speech and sheltered beneath a boundless canopy, when going forth to serve they may speak boldly, and when remaining in retirement they may act with lofty integrity—just as the great luminaries illuminate the myriad things, yet their shining presence favors them all the more. Thus, the way the scholars of Chu have been nurtured by…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皇澤所嚮注於
上意者亦至渥巳夫亭毒羣彙昭
蘇化工納於南訛者天地之
養物也旁羅民秀奕孚教澤
示以周行者聖人之養士也
萬物養於天地人養於聖人
聖人養士使自養以養天下
===
今主上南面而聽嚮明以治
神功暉曜洪洞朗天當其所
面之方昭燭休爽尤爲焜顯而士
衣被
耿光揚景炎騰茂實發攄詩書禮
樂之緒宣鬯道德仁義之精
炳如蔚如雲蒸龍變以翼戴
punctuated: 皇澤，所嚮注於上意者，亦至渥巳！夫亭毒羣彙，昭蘇化工，納於南訛者，天地之養物也；旁羅民秀，奕孚教澤，示以周行者，聖人之養士也。萬物養於天地，人養於聖人，聖人養士，使自養以養天下。今主上南面而聽，嚮明以治，神功暉曜，洪洞朗天。當其所面之方，昭燭休爽，尤爲焜顯。而士衣被耿光，揚景炎，騰茂實，發攄《詩》、《書》、禮、樂之緒，宣鬯道德、仁義之精，炳如蔚如，雲蒸龍變，以翼戴
translation_en: … imperial grace, and that toward which the Sovereign's favor is directed, are most abundant indeed! Now, shaping and maturing the myriad categories of beings, reviving them through the transformative work of nature, and ordering the summer transformations in the south—this is how Heaven and Earth nurture things. Gathering the finest of the people from all sides, deeply imbuing them with the blessings of moral instruction, and showing them the Great Way—this is how the Sage nurtures scholars. The myriad things are nurtured by Heaven and Earth, and human beings are nurtured by the Sage; the Sage nurtures scholars, causing them to nurture themselves so as to nurture the whole world. Now the Reigning Sovereign faces south and listens to his ministers, turning toward the light to govern; his divine achievements shine brightly, vast and clear as the luminous sky. In the direction that he faces, the radiant illumination and auspicious clarity are especially resplendent. And scholars, clothed in this brilliant light, exalt the great radiance and send soaring their flourishing substance, setting forth the traditions of the Odes, the Documents, Rites, and Music, and proclaiming the essence of the Way, Virtue, Benevolence, and Righteousness—resplendent and luxuriant, rising like clouds and transforming like dragons, so as to support and uphold…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
休烈弼成
文明之治固士所自養以答我
主上宜莫先楚士諸士毋亦攷九
丘之伊始集三管之所述追
蹤前賢流聞來嗣以不負
國家煦養以佐
主上明盛之理庶幾哉稱天下士
===
亦庶幾稱所爲壬午所舉士
乎乃足以塞楚名若其追琢
之不文鞭策之不進即有和
璧天馬夫誰與羣使天下嗤
和氏盲玉九方皐盲馬也亦
宜是役也巡撫湖廣兵部右
侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史
punctuated:
休烈，弼成文明之治，固士所自養以答我主上，宜莫先楚士。諸士毋亦攷九丘之伊始，集三管之所述，追蹤前賢，流聞來嗣，以不負國家煦養，以佐主上明盛之理。庶幾哉，稱天下士，亦庶幾稱所爲壬午所舉士乎！乃足以塞楚名。若其追琢之不文，鞭策之不進，即有和璧、天馬，夫誰與羣？使天下嗤和氏盲玉、九方皐盲馬也，亦宜。

是役也，巡撫湖廣兵部右侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史
translation_en:
… splendid achievements and assist in bringing to perfection a civil and enlightened rule—this is surely how scholars cultivate themselves in order to repay our Sovereign, and in this none should take precedence over the scholars of Chu. Should you scholars not examine the origins of the Nine Mounds (Jiuqiu), gather what is recounted by the Three Brushes (Sanguan), follow in the footsteps of former worthies, and pass down a renowned reputation to future generations, so as not to betray the nurturing care of the State and to assist in our Sovereign's bright and flourishing governance? How close indeed would you then come to being worthy of the title of scholars of the realm, and how close to being worthy of what it means to be scholars selected in the renwu year (1582)! Only then will it suffice to fulfill the reputation of Chu. If, however, in carving and polishing one fails to achieve refinement, or under the whip and spur one fails to advance, then even if there were a Jade of He (Hebi) or a Heavenly Horse, who would associate with them? And if the world were to laugh at Master He (Heshi) for being blind to jade and Jiufang Gao for being blind to horses, it would also be fitting.

In this undertaking, the Grand Coordinator of Huguang, Right Vice Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
陳省首振聲猷聿倡文教巡
撫貴州兼制湖北軍務右副
都御史劉庠提督南贛軍務
右副都御史王緝共綏疆土
翊宣士風其守備地方則太
監王禎奉使地方則翰林院
編修王懋德刑部郎中王任
===
戶部主事于文熙工部主事
程奎中書舍人吳嶽秀効勞
棘外則左參政沈子木沈伯
龍陶大順喬懋敬右參政衷
貞吉許守謙項思教右參議
蕭九成馬鳴鑾梁問孟副使
曹子朝李天植侯堯封僉事
punctuated: 陳省，首振聲猷，聿倡文教；巡撫貴州兼制湖北軍務右副都御史劉庠、提督南贛軍務右副都御史王緝，共綏疆土，翊宣士風。其守備地方則太監王禎；奉使地方則翰林院編修王懋德、刑部郎中王任、戶部主事于文熙、工部主事程奎、中書舍人吳嶽秀；効勞棘外則左參政沈子木、沈伯龍、陶大順、喬懋敬，右參政衷貞吉、許守謙、項思教，右參議蕭九成、馬鳴鑾、梁問孟，副使曹子朝、李天植、侯堯封，僉事
translation_en: … Chen Sheng 陳省 took the lead in rousing renown and grand plans, thereby promoting cultural education; Grand Coordinator of Guizhou concurrently Controlling Military Affairs of Northern Huguang and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiang 劉庠, and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Nan'gan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Ji 王緝, jointly pacified the territory and assisted in spreading the ethos of the literati. As for those defending the region, there was Eunuch Director Wang Zhen 王禎; as for those serving on imperial commissions in the region, there were Hanlin Academy Historiographer Wang Maode 王懋德, Ministry of Justice Director Wang Ren 王任, Ministry of Revenue Secretary Yu Wenxi 于文熙, Ministry of Works Secretary Cheng Kui 程奎, and Drafter Wu Yuexiu 吳嶽秀; as for those rendering service outside the examination compound, there were Left Administration Vice Commissioners Shen Zimu 沈子木, Shen Bolong 沈伯龍, Tao Dashun 陶大順, and Qiao Maojing 喬懋敬; Right Administration Vice Commissioners Zhong Zhenji 衷貞吉, Xu Shouqian 許守謙, and Xiang Sijiao 項思教; Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Xiao Jiucheng 蕭九成, Ma Mingluan 馬鳴鑾, and Liang Wenmeng 梁問孟; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Cao Zichao 曹子朝, Li Tianzhi 李天植, and Hou Yaofeng 侯堯封; Assistant Surveillance Commissioner …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
夏良心署都指揮僉事周印
范恩而左參議田樂義僉事
王廷稷署都指揮僉事張應
奎則以入
賀行例得並書書之
河南歸德府鹿邑縣儒學教
諭王遴謹序
punctuated:
夏良心，署都指揮僉事周印、范恩，而左參議田樂義、僉事王廷稷、署都指揮僉事張應奎，則以入賀行，例得並書，書之。

河南歸德府鹿邑縣儒學教諭王遴謹序。
translation_en:
…Xia Liangxin 夏良心, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Zhou Yin 周印 and Fan En 范恩; while Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Tian Leyi 田樂義, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Tingji 王廷稷, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Zhang Yingkui 張應奎 were away on a mission to present congratulations at court—by precedent they are all entitled to be recorded together, and so I record them.

Respectfully prefaced by Wang Lin 王遴, Instructor in the Confucian School of Luyi County 鹿邑縣, Guide Prefecture 歸德府, Henan 河南.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
萬曆十年湖廣鄉試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史錢岱〔汝瞻直隸常熟縣人辛未進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使錢藻〔自文直隸如皋縣人己未進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右布政使賈待問〔學叔直隸威縣人戊辰進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使馬文煒〔仲韜山東安丘縣人壬戌進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事王圻〔元翰直隸上海縣人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官
河南歸德府鹿邑縣儒學教諭王遴〔惟俊雲南寧州人癸酉貢士〕
山東東昌府莘縣儒學教諭湯有光〔子韜直隸常熟縣人癸酉貢士〕
