title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
明四目達四聰
終始惟一時乃日新任官惟賢才左右惟
其人臣爲上爲德爲下爲民其難其愼
惟和惟一
皇建其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥庶民
夏商官倍亦克用乂
詩
漢之廣矣不可泳思江之永矣不可方思
靺鞈有奭以作六師
===
乃及王季維德之行大任有身生此文王
無曰高高在上陟降厥士日監在茲
春秋
齊師宋師曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕春王正月
城楚丘〔僖公二年〕春諸侯城緣陵〔僖公〕
〔十有四年〕
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕吳子使札來聘〔襄公〕
〔二十有九年〕
夏五月宋人及楚人平〔宣公十有五年〕夏
punctuated:
「明四目，達四聰。」
「終始惟一，時乃日新。任官惟賢才，左右惟其人。臣爲上爲德，爲下爲民；其難其愼，惟和惟一。」
「皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。」
「夏商官倍，亦克用乂。」

《詩》
「漢之廣矣，不可泳思；江之永矣，不可方思。」
「靺鞈有奭，以作六師。」
「乃及王季，維德之行。大任有身，生此文王。」
「無曰高高在上，陟降厥士，日監在茲。」

《春秋》
「齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。」〔僖公元年〕「春，王正月，城楚丘。」〔僖公二年〕「春，諸侯城緣陵。」〔僖公十有四年〕
「秦人伐晉。」〔文公三年〕「吳子使札來聘。」〔襄公二十有九年〕
「夏，五月，宋人及楚人平。」〔宣公十有五年〕「夏，
translation_en:
"[From the Classic of Documents:]
'He saw clearly with the eyes of the four quarters, and heard distinctly with the ears of the four quarters.'
'Be always the same from beginning to end, and so shall you be daily renewed. In appointing to office, let it be only the worthy and talented; let those around you be only the right men. The minister, in relation to his sovereign above, promotes his virtue; in relation to the people below, he seeks their welfare. How hard it is! How cautious he must be! There must be harmony; there must be unity.'
'The Sovereign establishes his supreme standard of perfection; he gathers together these five blessings, and then diffuses and bestows them upon his common people.'
'Under the Xia and Shang, the number of officials was doubled, and yet they were still able to achieve good governance.'

Classic of Poetry (Shijing):
'Broad is the Han River—it cannot be swum across; long is the Yangzi River—it cannot be crossed by raft.'
'With red knee-covers of madder-dyed leather, to rouse the Six Armies.'
'And so it came down to King Ji, whose conduct was solely of virtue. Tai Ren became pregnant, and gave birth to this King Wen.'
'Do not say that Heaven is high, high above; it ascends and descends about our doings, and daily inspects us right here.'

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
'The army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Cao walled Xing.' [First year of Duke Xi] 'In spring, in the King's first month, they walled Chuqiu.' [Second year of Duke Xi] 'In spring, the feudal lords walled Yuanling.' [Fourteenth year of Duke Xi]
'The men of Qin attacked Jin.' [Third year of Duke Wen] 'The Viscount of Wu sent Zha to come on a mission of friendly inquiry.' [Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang]
'In summer, in the fifth month, the men of Song and the men of Chu made peace.' [Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan] 'In summer, …'"

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
公會晉侯衛侯于瑣澤〔成公十有二年〕
冬築郎囿〔昭公九年〕
禮記
凡聽五刑之訟必原父子之親立君臣之
義以權之意論輕重之序慎測淺深之
量以别之悉其聰明致其忠愛以盡之
疑獄氾與眾共之眾疑赦之必察小大
之比以成之
固封疆備邊竟完要塞謹關梁塞徯徑
===
故樂也者動於内者也禮也者動於外者
也樂極和禮極順
夙夜其命宥密無聲之樂也威儀逮逮不
可選也無體之禮也
第貳場
論
天子以好生為德
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢春和議振貸詔〔文帝元年〕
punctuated:
公會晉侯、衛侯于瑣澤。〔成公十有二年〕
「冬，築郎囿。」〔昭公九年〕

《禮記》
「凡聽五刑之訟，必原父子之親，立君臣之義以權之；意論輕重之序，慎測淺深之量以别之；悉其聰明，致其忠愛以盡之。疑獄，氾與眾共之；眾疑，赦之；必察小大之比以成之。」
「固封疆，備邊竟，完要塞，謹關梁，塞徯徑。」
「故樂也者，動於内者也；禮也者，動於外者也。樂極和，禮極順。」
「『夙夜其命宥密』，無聲之樂也；『威儀逮逮，不可選也』，無體之禮也。」

第貳場
論
「天子以好生為德」

詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢《春和議振貸詔》〔文帝元年〕
translation_en:
…the Duke met the Marquis of Jin and the Marquis of Wei at Suoze.” [Twelfth Year of Duke Cheng]
“In winter, the deer-park at Lang was built.” [Ninth Year of Duke Zhao]

Record of Rites (Liji)
“In all hearing of lawsuits involving the five punishments, one must trace the affection between father and son and establish the righteousness between ruler and minister in order to weigh them; judge the intention in order of gravity and carefully gauge the measure of shallowness or depth in order to distinguish them; exhaust one’s intelligence and clarity and extend one’s utmost loyalty and love in order to get to the bottom of them. In doubtful cases, broadly deliberate them with the multitude; if the multitude is in doubt, pardon them; and always examine precedents both small and great in order to conclude them.”
“Secure the boundaries and frontiers, prepare the borderlands, repair strategic fortresses, guard passes and bridges, and block up bypaths.”
“Therefore, music is that which stirs within; rites are that which moves without. Music culminates in harmony; rites culminate in compliance.”
“‘Day and night he enlarged the foundations of his destiny in quietude and profundity’—this is music without sound. ‘His dignified demeanor was utterly composed and nothing could be faulted in it’—this is ritual without form.”

Second Session
Discourse (Lun)
“The Son of Heaven Takes the Love of Life as His Virtue”

Proclamation, Mandate, and Memorial [Candidates answer one]
Imitation of the Han Dynasty “Proclamation Deliberating Relief and Loans in theGenial Spring” [First Year of Emperor Wen]

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
擬輔臣應
制恭詠玄兔圖詩
進呈表〔萬曆九年〕
判語〔五條〕
無故不朝參公座
見任官輒自立碑
禁經斷人充宿衞
從征守禦官軍逃
===
聞有恩赦而故犯
第叁場
策五道
問
帝作儲述記之往牒重
國本也成周內立六宮外崇禖祀廣御幸而
祈嗣續重可知矣秦漢以降內御非不
廣也有增級十四者有爵視外朝者有
分列八品者此與姬周之數將無同與
punctuated:
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
擬輔臣應制恭詠《玄兔圖》詩進呈表〔萬曆九年〕

判語〔五條〕
無故不朝參公座
見任官輒自立碑
禁經斷人充宿衞
從征守禦官軍逃
聞有恩赦而故犯

第叁場
策五道
問：《帝作》、《儲述》，記之往牒，重國本也。成周內立六宮，外崇禖祀，廣御幸而祈嗣續，重可知矣。秦、漢以降，內御非不廣也：有增級十四者，有爵視外朝者，有分列八品者，此與姬周之數將無同與？
translation_en:
Draft of a Tang Mandate Appointing Wei Zheng 魏徵 as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent (Sixteenth year of the Zhenguan reign [642])
Draft of a Memorial by the Grand Secretaries Presenting Poems Composed at Imperial Command respectfully Celebrating the Painting of the Black Rabbit (Ninth year of the Wanli reign [1581])

Legal Judgments (Five Items)
Failing without Cause to Attend Court Audience or Official Sessions
Incumbent Officials Arbitrarily Erecting Steles for Themselves
Prohibiting Convicted Persons from Serving in the Palace Guard
Desertion by Officers and Soldiers on Campaign or in Defense Commands
Deliberately Committing Offenses upon Hearing of an Imperial Amnesty

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: The *Imperial Enterprises* (Di zuo) and *Accounts of the Heir Apparent* (Chu shu) are recorded in past documents because the foundation of the state is held in high importance. In the flourishing Zhou dynasty, within the palace they established the Six Palaces, and outside they venerated the sacrifice to the Matchmaker Deity (Meisi), broadening the royal consorts' attendance in the bedchamber and praying for the continuation of the lineage—from this, its importance can be known. From the Qin and Han dynasties onward, the inner consorts were not unbroadened: there were those who increased the ranks to fourteen, those whose noble titles matched the outer court, and those who divided them into eight ranks. Are these not similar to the numbers of the Zhou house of Ji? …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
禖祀非不舉也有設壇城南者有議建
石主者有增置配帝者此與月令之儀
得無戾與
太祖高皇帝御寓之初卽
命禮部詳定女職六局之外無復剩員謂皆循
用周制然與否與
世宗肅皇帝虔祀高禖壇位有所陪祀有配牲
牢有品果與周禮有所損益與
皇上踐祚十載
===
儲位未蕃
兩宮軫念
命選九嬪充位
掖庭又
遣禮官禱祀名山夫欲延
重光而衍萬葉慮至周也然螽斯樛木之詩鳴
雞佩玉之典彤管書環之法胎教內教
之則古所稱述有出於
宮寢弓韣之外者豈少哉夫多男之頌封人
punctuated: 禖祀非不舉也，有設壇城南者，有議建石主者，有增置配帝者，此與《月令》之儀得無戾與？太祖高皇帝御寓之初，卽命禮部詳定女職，六局之外無復剩員，謂皆循用周制，然與否與？世宗肅皇帝虔祀高禖，壇位有所，陪祀有配，牲牢有品，果與周禮有所損益與？皇上踐祚十載，儲位未蕃，兩宮軫念，命選九嬪充位掖庭，又遣禮官禱祀名山，夫欲延重光而衍萬葉，慮至周也。然《螽斯》、《樛木》之詩，鳴雞、佩玉之典，彤管、書環之法，胎教、內教之則，古所稱述有出於宮寢、弓韣之外者，豈少哉？夫多男之頌，封人
translation_en:
Nor was the sacrifice to the Matchmaker Deity (Meisi) left unperformed: there were those who erected an altar to the south of the capital, those who deliberated on establishing a stone spirit tablet, and those who added a coadjutor deity. Does this not run counter to the ceremonial prescribed in the Monthly Ordinances (Yueling)? When Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), first took reign over the realm, he immediately commanded the Ministry of Rites to determine the offices of the palace women in detail; beyond the Six Bureaus (liuju), there were no superfluous personnel. It is said that all of this followed the institutions of the Zhou—is this so or not? Emperor Su, the Epochal Ancestor (Shizong), reverently sacrificed to the Supreme Matchmaker (Gaomei), with a designated site for the altar, coadjutors for the auxiliary sacrifices, and graded offerings of sacrificial livestock. Did this indeed involve additions to or subtractions from the rites of the Zhou?

His Majesty has occupied the throne for ten years, yet the heir-apparent's line has not yet proliferated. The Two Empresses Dowager (Lianggong), in their deep solicitude, commanded the selection of the Nine Imperial Concubines (jiupin) to fill the ranks of the Lateral Courts (yeting), and furthermore dispatched officials of the Ministry of Rites to pray and offer sacrifices at famous mountains. In desiring to prolong the successive radiance of the dynasty and propagate it for ten thousand generations, their consideration is comprehensive indeed. Yet the odes "Locusts" (Zhongsi) and "Drooping Branches" (Jiumu), the canons regarding the crowing of the cock and the wearing of jade pendants, the methods of the red brush and the ring-inscription, and the rules of prenatal instruction and inner-palace education—among the things praised and recounted in antiquity, are there few that go beyond the palace bedchambers and the bow-case rites [of the Matchmaker sacrifice]? Now, the chúc blessing for "many sons" was something the borderwarden…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所不廢也諸士其詳述於篇以爲
宗社億萬年無疆之助
問經費國家大計也成周養兵以私田而
不餉養士以公田而不廩歲出不過祭
祀宴享匪頒好用數者而已周公方且
憂之立九賦九式之法上自王后世子
下至有司百官經用具有等差無令浮
額以裨人主儉德意何深哉嗣後有上
郡國籍者有上元和國計圖若簿者有
===
上景德祥符皇祐治平元祐會計錄者
要在使人主審其所以入察其所以出
節用裕民已耳而民反大困此何以說
與我
朝自洪武來歷代講求大氐皆損上益下之
政
國浸饒民浸殷矣嘉隆之際嬴絀不常厥咎
何繇頃者嚴考成之法定降罰之例閱
邊餉省傜役汰冗員恤傳置十餘年間
punctuated:
所不廢也。諸士其詳述於篇，以爲宗社億萬年無疆之助。
問：經費，國家大計也。成周養兵以私田而不餉，養士以公田而不廩，歲出不過祭祀、宴享、匪頒、好用數者而已。周公方且憂之，立九賦、九式之法，上自王、后、世子，下至有司百官，經用具有等差，無令浮額，以裨人主儉德，意何深哉！嗣後有上《郡國籍》者，有上《元和國計圖》若《簿》者，有上《景德》、《祥符》、《皇祐》、《治平》、《元祐會計錄》者，要在使人主審其所以入，察其所以出，節用裕民已耳；而民反大困，此何以說與？我朝自洪武來，歷代講求，大氐皆損上益下之政，國浸饒，民浸殷矣。嘉、隆之際，嬴絀不常，厥咎何繇？頃者嚴考成之法，定降罰之例，閱邊餉，省傜役，汰冗員，恤傳置，十餘年間…
translation_en:
…did not neglect. May you gentlemen set this forth in detail in your essays, as an aid to the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain for tens of thousands of years without bound.

Question: Regular expenditures are a great plan of the state. In the era of Completed Zhou, soldiers were maintained through private fields without being paid rations, and officials were maintained through public fields without being given granary stipends. Annual outlays were nothing more than a few items: sacrifices, banquets, discretionary distributions, and benevolent bestowals. Even so, the Duke of Zhou was concerned about them and established the laws of the Nine Revenues and Nine Expenditure Formulas. From the King, Queen, and Heir Apparent above, down to the various officials and hundred functionaries below, regular expenses all had their graded distinctions, and none were permitted to exceed their quotas, so as to assist the sovereign's virtue of frugality—how profound was his intention! Thereafter, there were those who presented Registers of Commandery and Kingdom Accounts (Junguo ji), those who presented the Yuanhe Charts (or Registers) of State Finances (Yuanhe guoji tu / bu), and those who presented the Accounting Records (Kuaiji lu) of the Jingde (1004–1007), Xiangfu (1008–1016), Huangyou (1049–1054), Zhiping (1064–1067), and Yuanyou (1086–1094) eras. The essential point was simply to cause the ruler to examine whence revenues entered and inspect whither expenditures went out, economizing on expenses and enriching the people; yet the people on the contrary suffered great distress—how is this to be explained? In our dynasty, since the Hongwu era (1368–1398), successive reigns have investigated and sought out measures that were, in the main, policies of diminishing those above to benefit those below; the state gradually grew abundant and the people gradually grew prosperous. During the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras, surpluses and deficits were erratic—from what did this fault arise? Recently, the government has tightened the law for evaluating performance, fixed the regulations for demotion and punishment, audited frontier military rations, reduced corvée labor, eliminated superfluous personnel, and relieved the postal relay system; over the course of ten or more years, …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國用稍紓乃主計之臣又作萬曆會計錄以
獻無亦九賦九式遺意與第是錄所載如
內庫祿餉諸條視
會典不啻倍半將來歲乆費增度支所領猶
然縮也胡以應之說者謂
皇上躬節儉慎出入庶幾可捄萬一則舍此誠
無善後之策與諸生脫有懷耿耿者即
言多寡有無庸何傷
問先儒云人有古今而學不息世有代謝
===
而書不亡審若是孔壁酉巖之藏雖至
今存可耳胡秘閣所儲碩儒所業乃百
不一二覩也嬴秦煨燼姑勿譚已若漢
之七略唐之四部宋之六庫簡帙疑靡
逸矣說者猶以類例不明圖書失敘少
之而自編為十二類其優劣可別言歟
夫書有名亡而實不亡者有闕於前而
完於後者有隱於當世而出於異代者
豈當時編次無法坐令泯棼失傳與抑
punctuated:
國用稍紓。乃主計之臣，又作《萬曆會計錄》以獻，無亦九賦、九式遺意與？第是錄所載，如內庫、祿餉諸條，視《會典》不啻倍半。將來歲乆費增，度支所領，猶然縮也，胡以應之？說者謂皇上躬節儉，慎出入，庶幾可捄萬一，則舍此誠無善後之策與？諸生脫有懷耿耿者，即言多寡有無，庸何傷？

問：先儒云：「人有古今而學不息，世有代謝而書不亡。」審若是，孔壁、酉巖之藏，雖至今存可耳。胡秘閣所儲、碩儒所業，乃百不一二覩也？嬴秦煨燼，姑勿譚已；若漢之《七略》、唐之四部、宋之六庫，簡帙疑靡逸矣，說者猶以類例不明、圖書失敘少之，而自編為十二類，其優劣可別言歟？夫書有名亡而實不亡者，有闕於前而完於後者，有隱於當世而出於異代者。豈當時編次無法，坐令泯棼失傳與？抑
translation_en:
…state finances have been somewhat relieved. Moreover, the officials in charge of fiscal accounting have compiled and presented the Accounting Records of the Wanli Era (Wanli kuaiji lu); is this not also the legacy of the Nine Revenues (jiufu) and Nine Expenditure Regulations (jiushi) of the Rites of Zhou? Yet in what is recorded in this work, items such as the Inner Treasuries, official salaries, and military rations are more than one and a half times what is listed in the Collected Statutes (Huidian). In the future, as the years pass and expenses grow, the funds received by the Ministry of Revenue will still fall short; how can this be met? Commentators say that if His Majesty personally practices frugality and is cautious with revenues and expenditures, perhaps one part in ten thousand may be remedied—so apart from this, is there truly no other policy for the future? Should you students harbor earnest concerns in your hearts, even if you speak of abundances and shortages or of having and lacking, what harm could there be?

Question: A former Confucian scholar said: "Men belong to antiquity or the present, yet learning never ceases; ages succeed one another, yet books do not perish." If this is truly so, then the books hidden in Confucius's wall and the caverns of Mount You could well have survived down to the present day. Why then is it that of the collections stored in the imperial libraries and the works studied by great scholars, not even one or two out of a hundred are to be seen? Let us leave aside without discussion the ashes of the Qin burning of the books; as for the Seven Epitomes (Qilüe) of the Han, the Four Categories (sibu) of the Tang, and the Six Repositories (liuku) of the Song, one would suspect that no volumes were lost, yet commentators still disparaged them for unclear classification principles and disorderly arrangement of charts and books, and instead compiled their own systems into twelve classes—can their relative merits and defects be distinguished and stated? Now, among books there are those whose titles have perished yet whose substance has not perished; those that were defective in earlier times yet complete in later times; and those that were hidden in their own age yet emerged in another dynasty. Could it be that because the compilation and arrangement at the time lacked proper method, they were idly allowed to fall into confusion, oblivion, and loss of transmission? Or…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
在乃史通極不滿焉史通之議孟堅雖
不敢謂盡然然所糾正此表卽後世甚
愛孟堅者似未能曲諱也孟堅所稱良
一代史耳至欲盡百代而囊括之何與
夫古今人亦大相懸矣槩以三科列以
九等豈盡無一二佚顧又取閨閤之流
而襍評之與就中所掎摭又不特一史
通也史通凡四舉張晏凡五舉其說可
得聞與乃顏師古獨不然晏語又何與
===
或者謂大家爲其兄卒成之則固不宜
深攻孟堅矣顧於何證其爲大家筆也
夫論人欲盡不則無以定是非之準而
立勸懲之極明知其人之必可軒也然
或可稍輊焉明知其人之必可輊也然
或可稍軒焉談何容易哉諸士學古有
獲於玆擬議蓋已素矣其極著之卽使
孟堅再作唯唯稱謝而不敢抗吾之精
粹亦奚不可
punctuated: 在，乃《史通》極不滿焉。《史通》之議孟堅，雖不敢謂盡然，然所糾正此表，卽後世甚愛孟堅者，似未能曲諱也。孟堅所稱良，一代史耳，至欲盡百代而囊括之，何與？夫古今人亦大相懸矣，槩以三科，列以九等，豈盡無一二佚？顧又取閨閤之流而襍評之與？就中所掎摭，又不特一《史通》也。《史通》凡四舉，張晏凡五舉，其說可得聞與？乃顏師古獨不然晏語，又何與？或者謂大家爲其兄卒成之，則固不宜深攻孟堅矣，顧於何證其爲大家筆也？夫論人欲盡，不則無以定是非之準，而立勸懲之極。明知其人之必可軒也，然或可稍輊焉；明知其人之必可輊也，然或可稍軒焉。談何容易哉！諸士學古有獲，於玆擬議蓋已素矣，其極著之。卽使孟堅再作，唯唯稱謝，而不敢抗吾之精粹，亦奚不可？
translation_en: … exists, yet the Shitong (Comprehensive Perspectives on Historiography) is极ly dissatisfied with it. Although one would not dare say that the Shitong's criticisms of Mengjian [Ban Gu 班固] are entirely right, as for what it corrects in this table [the "Table of Ancient and Modern Persons" 古今人表 in the Book of Han], even those in later generations who greatly admire Mengjian seem unable to bend the truth to defend him. What Mengjian was praised as excelling at was merely the history of a single dynasty; why then did he wish to encompass all hundred generations within a single bag? Now, people of ancient and modern times differ vastly from one another. To summarize them under three categories and rank them into nine grades—how could this be entirely free of one or two omissions? And why, moreover, did he take women of the inner quarters and mingle them into the evaluations? Among the faults that have been picked out in it, it is not only the Shitong alone that does so. The Shitong raises four points in all, and Zhang Yan 張晏 raises five points in all; may we hear an account of their arguments? Yet Yan Shigu 顏師古 alone disagreed with Yan's remarks—why was that? Some say that Dajia [Ban Zhao 班昭, Cao Dajia 曹大家] completed it on behalf of her elder brother, and if so, one certainly ought not to attack Mengjian too severely; yet by what evidence can one prove that it came from Dajia's brush? Now, in evaluating people one wishes to be exhaustive, for otherwise there is no way to fix the standard of right and wrong and establish the ultimate criterion for encouragement and warning. Even when one clearly knows that a person certainly deserves to be elevated, perhaps he may be slightly lowered; even when one clearly knows that a person certainly deserves to be lowered, perhaps he may be slightly elevated. How could this be an easy matter to discuss! You scholars have gained much from your study of antiquity and have surely long deliberated over these questions. Set forth your views to the fullest. Even if we should cause Mengjian to rise again, say "Yes, yes" in acknowledgment, and not dare to contest the pure essence of our arguments—why would that not be possible?

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
問井法昉於黃虞至周大備然已上矣自
魏盡地力秦開阡陌而田制決裂殆盡
卽慨然有志復古者莫能盡舉而更之
何歟其間二三藎臣或請限民名田或
請上限田胡竟以沮格也乾興初毅然
下限田之詔而任事者謂不便太和貞
觀顯德間略倣三代均田遺意庶幾小
康第行未久輒報罷其咎安在
令甲十歲一籍丁業以稽贏耗是
===
國家所重而吏未稱田與賦大剌戾百姓失
職不贍楚尤告病
上甚憫焉邇
詔臺臣如八閩例綜覈民田乃今經界竣事戶
無羨畝人無虛賦羣生和樂方外蒙澤
已第慮始固難而守成亦不易欲令法
久而弊絕爲楚人規萬世之利復何施
而後可諸生楚產也當明習楚事願聞
所宜罷行之畫
punctuated: 問：井法昉於黃、虞，至周大備，然已上矣。自魏盡地力、秦開阡陌，而田制決裂殆盡。卽慨然有志復古者，莫能盡舉而更之，何歟？其間二三藎臣，或請限民名田，或請上限田，胡竟以沮格也？乾興初，毅然下限田之詔，而任事者謂不便；太和、貞觀、顯德間，略倣三代均田遺意，庶幾小康，第行未久輒報罷，其咎安在？令甲十歲一籍丁業，以稽贏耗，是國家所重，而吏未稱，田與賦大剌戾，百姓失職不贍，楚尤告病。上甚憫焉，邇詔臺臣如八閩例，綜覈民田。乃今經界竣事，戶無羨畝，人無虛賦，羣生和樂，方外蒙澤已。第慮始固難，而守成亦不易。欲令法久而弊絕，爲楚人規萬世之利，復何施而後可？諸生楚產也，當明習楚事，願聞所宜罷行之畫。
translation_en:
Question: The well-field system originated in the eras of the Yellow Emperor and Yu Shun, and reached complete perfection under the Zhou dynasty; yet that was already in high antiquity. Ever since Wei exhausted the productivity of the land and Qin opened up the field paths and ridges, the system of land tenure has been almost completely shattered. Even among those who were passionately resolved to restore antiquity, none could fully revive and reform it—why is that? During the intervening periods, two or three loyal ministers either requested to limit the amount of land registered in private names, or requested that the throne impose land limits—why were their proposals ultimately blocked and frustrated? At the beginning of the Qianxing reign (1022), an edict limiting landholding was resolutely handed down, yet those in charge of affairs claimed it was inconvenient; during the Taihe (477–499), Zhenguan (627–649), and Xiande (954–960) eras, rulers roughly imitated the surviving principles of the Three Dynasties' land-equalization system and nearly achieved modest prosperity, yet before these measures had been practiced for long they were repeatedly reported as discontinued—where did the fault lie?

Current statutory law requires a registration of adult males and property once every ten years in order to audit increases and decreases. This is a matter to which the State attaches great importance, yet officials have failed to live up to their duties. Landholdings and tax assessments have become gravely out of alignment, the common people have lost their livelihoods and lack sufficiency, and Chu [Huguang] especially reports distress. His Majesty took deep pity on this and recently decreed that Censorate officials, following the precedent of the Eight Min [Fujian], comprehensively verify the people's lands. Now the demarcation of boundaries has been completed: households have no unrecorded surplus acreage, individuals bear no fictitious tax burdens, the multitude of living beings are harmonious and happy, and the regions throughout the realm have received imperial grace. Yet while planning at the outset is certainly difficult, maintaining what has been accomplished is also not easy. If we wish to make the system endure for a long time and eradicate abuses, planning a benefit of ten thousand generations for the people of Chu, what further measures must be implemented before this can be achieved? You students are natives of Chu and ought to be clearly conversant with the affairs of Chu; I wish to hear your plans regarding what should be abolished and what should be put into practice.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
曾子曰十目所視十手所指其嚴乎富潤
屋德潤身心廣體胖故君子必誠其意
段藎國
同考試官訓導趙批發愼獨誠意貫串而潤身處輕
輕說過極得題旨
同考試官敎諭尹批命意精深措辭典雅
考試官敎諭湯批是析理之精者
===
考試官敎諭王批說題意簡當
傳者甚嚴夫獨而因驗誠之不可已也夫天下
之大可畏者獨也愼則意誠而身潤矣此君子
誠之爲貴與傳者釋誠意蓋曰夫學必自意始
矣意之已誠爲德而意之方動爲獨君子之愼
獨非徒鑒於小人也蓋亦有見於獨之嚴焉曾
子甞言獨矣以人之情唯視指則畏唯視指之
多則甚畏而至於獨則以爲莫予及也不知視
指之實生於意不生於形而幽獨之中無其形
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「曾子曰：『十目所視，十手所指，其嚴乎！』富潤屋，德潤身，心廣體胖，故君子必誠其意。」

段藎國

同考試官訓導趙批：發愼獨、誠意貫串，而潤身處輕輕說過，極得題旨。
同考試官敎諭尹批：命意精深，措辭典雅。
考試官敎諭湯批：是析理之精者。
考試官敎諭王批：說題意簡當。

傳者甚嚴夫獨，而因驗誠之不可已也。夫天下之大可畏者，獨也；愼則意誠而身潤矣。此君子誠之爲貴與！傳者釋誠意，蓋曰：夫學必自意始矣。意之已誠爲德，而意之方動爲獨。君子之愼獨，非徒鑒於小人也，蓋亦有見於獨之嚴焉。曾子甞言獨矣。以人之情，唯視指則畏，唯視指之多則甚畏，而至於獨，則以爲莫予及也。不知視指之實生於意，不生於形，而幽獨之中，無其形
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"Zengzi said: 'What ten eyes behold, what ten hands point to—how austere it is!' Wealth adorns the house; virtue adorns the person. The mind is broad and the body is at ease. Therefore, the superior man must make his intentions sincere."

Duan Jinguo 段藎國

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhao 趙, comments: It brings out being watchful over oneself when alone and making the intentions sincere in a connected thread, while touching lightly upon adorning the person; it thoroughly grasps the purport of the topic.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Yin 尹, comments: The conception is subtle and profound, and the phrasing is classical and elegant.
Examiner, Instructor Tang 湯, comments: This is one who analyzes principles with precision.
Examiner, Instructor Wang 王, comments: It explains the meaning of the topic concisely and aptly.

The commentator treats solitude with the utmost austerity, and thereby verifies that making the intentions sincere cannot be dispensed with. Now, what is most greatly to be feared in the world is solitude; if one is watchful over it, one's intentions become sincere and one's person is adorned. Is this not why the superior man prizes making them sincere! In explaining making the intentions sincere, the commentator in effect says: Learning must begin with the intentions. When the intentions have been made sincere, that is virtue; when the intentions are just stirring, that is solitude. That the superior man is watchful over himself when alone is not merely from taking warning from the petty man, for he also perceives the austerity of solitude. Zengzi once spoke of solitude. By human nature, people feel fear only when beheld and pointed at, and feel extreme fear only when beheld and pointed at by many; yet when it comes to being alone, they suppose that no one can reach them. They do not realize that the reality of being beheld and pointed at arises from the intentions, not from outward form, and that in hidden solitude, though there is no outward form…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭羅批〔氣象雄偉意義精徹〕
同考試官教諭楊批〔發有道與不議甚警拔〕
考試官教諭湯批〔莊重古雅盛世之文〕
考試官教諭王批〔遒勁雅馴非淺學可到〕
治出於道徵諸民而信從矣夫民之議議道之
失也有道則信而從矣奚議哉且夫上之人以
其權威福天下下之人亦以其意是非人主故
其得失莫掩於匹夫匹婦之公而其論議不廢
於至愚至賤之口庶人而議也勢也乃若天下
===
有道以君則哲紀法脩而皇極建以政則一體
統正而朝廷尊禮樂以勸征伐以懲莫不自大
君之裁斷而截然定命矣上不僭濫雖庶人將
奚議之諸侯以下陪臣以上莫不奉天王之明
聖而喁然傒志矣朝無異同况庶人又誰議之
天子方采之里巷之傳詢之商旅之論豈禁而
不議哉君之建立唯道則公亡可議耳庶人則
進無逢迎之意退無忌諱之思豈畏而不議哉
民之心志唯道則服亡容議耳謳歌咏歎之衆
punctuated:
同考試官教諭羅批：〔氣象雄偉，意義精徹。〕
同考試官教諭楊批：〔發有道與不議，甚警拔。〕
考試官教諭湯批：〔莊重古雅，盛世之文。〕
考試官教諭王批：〔遒勁雅馴，非淺學可到。〕

治出於道，徵諸民而信從矣。夫民之議，議道之失也；有道則信而從矣，奚議哉？且夫上之人以其權威福天下，下之人亦以其意是非人主。故其得失莫掩於匹夫匹婦之公，而其論議不廢於至愚至賤之口。庶人而議也，勢也。乃若天下有道，以君則哲，紀法脩而皇極建；以政則一，體統正而朝廷尊。禮樂以勸，征伐以懲，莫不自大君之裁斷，而截然定命矣。上不僭濫，雖庶人將奚議之？諸侯以下，陪臣以上，莫不奉天王之明聖，而喁然傒志矣。朝無異同，况庶人又誰議之？天子方采之里巷之傳，詢之商旅之論，豈禁而不議哉？君之建立唯道，則公亡可議耳。庶人則進無逢迎之意，退無忌諱之思，豈畏而不議哉？民之心志唯道，則服亡容議耳。謳歌咏歎之衆，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Luo: [Magnificent in spirit and atmosphere; precise and penetrating in meaning.]
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Yang: [Its exposition of "the Way prevailing" and "not criticizing" is remarkably incisive and striking.]
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Tang: [Dignified and classically elegant—writing worthy of a flourishing age.]
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Wang: [Vigorous, refined, and polished; beyond the reach of shallow scholarship.]

When governance proceeds from the Way, it is verified among the people through their trust and compliance. Now, when the people criticize, they criticize the loss of the Way; when the Way prevails, they trust and comply—what is there to criticize? Moreover, those above use their authority to dispense awe and fortune across the realm, while those below likewise use their judgment to approve or disapprove of the ruler. Thus, his successes and failures cannot be concealed from the impartial judgment of ordinary men and women, and discussion and criticism never cease on the lips of the most ignorant and lowly. That commoners should criticize is the natural course of things.

Yet when the Way prevails in the world: as for the ruler, he is wise, discipline and laws are cultivated, and the August Ultimate is established; as for governance, it is unified, the institutional hierarchy is rectified, and the court is revered. Rites and music to encourage, punitive expeditions to chastise—none fail to issue from the great sovereign's own decision, thereby setting down clear-cut mandates. When superiors neither usurp nor overstep, even among commoners, what will they find to criticize? From the feudal lords downward and from the subsidiary ministers upward, none fail to honor theHeavenly King's enlightened sagacity, looking up in eager anticipation of his will. When the court has no dissension, how much less will commoners have anyone to criticize?

The Son of Heaven is just then gathering traditions from the lanes and alleys and inquiring into the discussions of traveling merchants—how could he forbid them so that they do not criticize? Because the ruler's institutions rest solely on the Way, they are impartial and leave nothing to be criticized. As for the commoners, when coming forward they have no intention to flatter, and when retiring they harbor no fear of taboos—how could they be afraid and therefore not criticize? Because the minds and wills of the people rest solely on the Way, they submit and have no room for criticism. The multitudes who sing and chant in praise…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
旣頒而無間言耕鑿嬉遊之民且忘而不知議
大順之徵也極治之象也非世有道惡睹此乎
吁夫子之言其有思矣抑召公曰天子有道庶
人傳語則不議何稱焉夫宣之而下不議上也
議之而上不禁下也下固議之上固禁之則下
矣噫一庶人也唐虞忘商周頌春秋議而嬴秦
箝惟議故三世五世希不失也箝之則二世矣
故世治則庶人之私議不可有世亂則天下之
公議不可無
===
孟子曰惠而不知爲政歲十一月徒杠成
十二月輿梁成民未病涉也君子平其
政行辟人可也焉得人人而濟之故爲
政者每人而悅之日亦不足矣
孟養浩
同考試官訓導范批政惠二字辨論甚晳而裁剪呼
應處更佳可錄
同考試官訓導范批意透詞工不落塵格
punctuated:
旣頒而無間言，耕鑿嬉遊之民且忘而不知議。大順之徵也，極治之象也，非世有道，惡睹此乎？吁！夫子之言其有思矣。抑召公曰：「天子有道，庶人傳語。」則不議何稱焉？夫宣之而下不議，上也；議之而上不禁，下也；下固議之，上固禁之，則下矣。噫！一庶人也，唐、虞忘，商、周頌，春秋議，而嬴秦箝。惟議，故三世、五世希不失也；箝之，則二世矣。故世治則庶人之私議不可有，世亂則天下之公議不可無。

孟子曰：「惠而不知爲政。歲十一月徒杠成，十二月輿梁成，民未病涉也。君子平其政，行辟人可也，焉得人人而濟之？故爲政者，每人而悅之，日亦不足矣。」
孟養浩
同考試官訓導范批：政、惠二字，辨論甚晳，而裁剪呼應處更佳，可錄。
同考試官訓導范批：意透詞工，不落塵格。
translation_en:
…already proclaimed them and there are no dissenting words; the people who plow, dig wells, and play in joy even forget about them and do not know to criticize. This is the sign of great harmony and the image of ultimate good governance. If the world did not possess the Way, how could one witness this? Alas! The Master's words indeed carried deep thought. Yet the Duke of Shao (Shaogong 召公) said: "When the Son of Heaven possesses the Way, the common people pass along their words." Why then is not criticizing praised here? Now, when policies are promulgated and those below do not criticize them, that is the highest state; when they criticize them and those above do not prohibit it, that is a lower state; when those below insist on criticizing them and those above insist on prohibiting it, that is the lowest of all. Alas! They are the very same common people: under Tang 唐 and Yu 虞 they forgot, under Shang 商 and Zhou 周 they sang praises, in the Spring and Autumn period (Chunqiu 春秋) they criticized, and under the Ying-surnamed Qin (Ying Qin 嬴秦) they were gagged. Because there was criticism, after three or five generations it was rare for the rulers not to lose their power; when they gagged them, it lasted only two generations! Therefore, when the world is well-governed, private criticism among the common people should not exist; when the world is in disorder, public criticism across the realm must not be absent.

Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) said: "He was kind, but did not understand how to govern. When the footbridges are completed in the eleventh month of the year, and the carriage bridges are completed in the twelfth month, the people do not suffer from wading across rivers. If a gentleman makes his governance equitable, it is permissible for him to clear the people from his path as he travels; how can he ferry every single person across? Therefore, if one who governs tries to please every individual, there will not even be enough days to do so."
Meng Yanghao 孟養浩
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Fan 范: The distinction and argument concerning the two words "governance" (zheng 政) and "kindness" (hui 惠) are exceedingly clear, and the tailoring and structural echoes are even finer; worthy of selection.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Fan 范: The meaning is penetrating and the diction skillful, not falling into mundane conventions.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
濟而遺於濟者常多政不令人悅而無不悅者
自在則公私大小所繇相遠也此孟氏所以坊
焉爾也不然僑稱衆人之母也彼其口實辟人
置民之溺而秦越之視僑又何如人哉吁庸主
愛牛遽許保民賢相濟涉不與知政君子用意
微矣
易
六四觀國之光利用賓于王象曰觀國之
光尚賓也
===
徐成楚
同考試官教諭趙批意正詞精發士君子趨時尚禮
之心甚徹此可以式矣
同考試官教諭顧批言言典雅深於易者
同考試官教諭楊批精確明透
考試官教諭湯批雅勁有蘊藉
考試官教諭王批意深詞雅
二聖於觀爻有著其進以時者有原其進以禮
者夫時可以進進斯不括矣然非尚君之禮肯
punctuated:
濟，而遺於濟者常多；政不令人悅，而無不悅者自在，則公私大小所繇相遠也。此孟氏所以坊焉爾也。不然，僑稱「衆人之母」也，彼其口實辟人，置民之溺而秦越之視，僑又何如人哉？吁！庸主愛牛，遽許保民；賢相濟涉，不與知政。君子用意微矣！

《易》
「六四，觀國之光，利用賓于王。《象》曰：觀國之光，尚賓也。」
徐成楚
同考試官教諭趙批：意正詞精，發士君子趨時尚禮之心甚徹，此可以式矣。
同考試官教諭顧批：言言典雅，深於《易》者。
同考試官教諭楊批：精確明透。
考試官教諭湯批：雅勁有蘊藉。
考試官教諭王批：意深詞雅。

二聖於《觀》爻，有著其進以時者，有原其進以禮者。夫時可以進，進斯不括矣；然非尚君之禮，肯…
translation_en:
… ferried across, yet those left behind without being ferried across will always be many; governance does not seek to make every individual pleased, yet the fact that no one is displeased naturally remains. This is the reason why impartiality and partiality, great and small, are so far apart from one another. And this is simply why Mencius set up a dike against such notions. Otherwise, Qiao [Zichan] was praised as "the mother of the multitude"; if someone used clearing the way of people as a pretext, ignoring the drowning of the people and looking upon them with the indifference of Qin and Yue toward each other, what sort of person would he then make Qiao out to be? Alas! When a mediocre ruler pitied an ox, Mencius readily allowed that he could protect the people; when a worthy minister helped people across a river, he refused to grant that he understood governance. Subtle indeed were the intentions of the superior man!

Classic of Changes (Yi)
"Six in the fourth place: Contemplating the glory of the state, it is favorable to be the guest of the king. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Contemplating the glory of the state'—one honors the guest."
By Xu Chengchu.
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhao comments: The meaning is upright and the diction refined. It brings out most thoroughly the mind of the scholar-gentleman who seizing the proper time esteems ritual propriety. This can serve as a model.
Associate Examiner Instructor Gu comments: Every word is classically elegant—one who is profound in the Classic of Changes.
Associate Examiner Instructor Yang comments: Precise, accurate, clear, and penetrating.
Examiner Instructor Tang comments: Elegant and vigorous, with rich reserve.
Examiner Instructor Wang comments: The meaning is deep and the diction elegant.

Regarding this line of the hexagram "Contemplation" (Guan), the two sages [the Duke of Zhou and Confucius] on the one hand set forth that one's advancement is according to the time, and on the other hand traced the source of one's advancement to ritual propriety. Now, when the time allows one to advance, in advancing one is free of impediment; yet if it were not for esteeming the ruler's ritual courtesy, would one be willing to…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
遽進哉二聖所以交發其義也且君子之進旣
度其時又度其君道可用矣而時不吾遇時可
爲矣而君不吾禮皆未可進也周公有見於四
之進以應乎時也係之詞曰士無用賓之志非
自弃也養晦以待時耳四何時也最近於五明
王制作親炙而快覩之矣有時如此寧忍負之
故或自側微而賓興或自侯服而賓貢相時而
動者也豈躁進哉否則談不賓之操於雍熈之
朝則固矣奚其利夫子有見於四之進以應其
===
禮也申之象曰士無觀光之愿非違時也爲主
之輕士耳五之君何君也順巽成德天下豪傑
賓禮而羅致之矣有君如此寧忍負之故或以
尚其作賓之典或以尚其嘉賓之求爲禮而往
者也豈輕進哉否則高不屈之節於折節之主
則悖矣奚其利要之四之遇天下之盛王也而
禮賢下士又天下之盛節也士生而躬逢其盛
寧不爲斯道慶歟雖然蘧甯卷舒柳下三黜接
輿行歌仲連赴海坐不遇主也然堯舜在上下
punctuated: 遽進哉？二聖所以交發其義也。且君子之進，旣度其時，又度其君。道可用矣，而時不吾遇；時可爲矣，而君不吾禮，皆未可進也。周公有見於四之進以應乎時也，係之詞曰：士無用賓之志，非自弃也，養晦以待時耳。四何時也？最近於五，明王制作，親炙而快覩之矣。有時如此，寧忍負之？故或自側微而賓興，或自侯服而賓貢，相時而動者也，豈躁進哉？否則，談不賓之操於雍熈之朝，則固矣，奚其利？夫子有見於四之進以應其禮也，申之象曰：士無觀光之愿，非違時也，爲主之輕士耳。五之君何君也？順巽成德，天下豪傑，賓禮而羅致之矣。有君如此，寧忍負之？故或以尚其作賓之典，或以尚其嘉賓之求，爲禮而往者也，豈輕進哉？否則，高不屈之節於折節之主，則悖矣，奚其利？要之，四之遇，天下之盛王也；而禮賢下士，又天下之盛節也。士生而躬逢其盛，寧不爲斯道慶歟？雖然，蘧、甯卷舒，柳下三黜，接輿行歌，仲連赴海，坐不遇主也。然堯、舜在上，下
translation_en:
… advance hastily? This is why the two sages mutually elucidated its meaning.

Moreover, when a gentleman advances into office, he measures both his time and his ruler. Even if the Way can be put into practice, if the times do not favor us, or if the times allow for action, yet the ruler does not treat us with ritual propriety, in neither case may one advance. The Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) perceived that the Fourth line advances in response to the time, and so appended the line statement, meaning: when a scholar lacks the ambition to serve as a royal guest, it is not that he abandons himself; he is merely nurturing his obscurity while awaiting the right time. What sort of time is that of the Fourth line? It is closest to the Fifth line, where the institutions created by an enlightened king can be personally experienced and joyfully witnessed. Having such a time as this, how could one bear to turn one's back on it? Therefore, whether rising as a recommended guest from humble obscurity, or presented as a tribute-guest from the feudal domains, one moves by observing the time—how could this be rash advancement? Otherwise, to talk of the integrity of refusing to serve as a guest in a court of harmonious prosperity would be mere obstinacy; what benefit would there be in it?

The Master [Confucius] perceived that the Fourth line advances in response to ritual propriety, and so elaborated in the Commentary on the Images (Xiang 象), meaning: when a scholar lacks the desire to behold the glory of the realm, it is not that he goes against the times, but simply because the ruler slights scholars. What sort of ruler is the ruler of the Fifth line? With compliance and adaptability perfecting his virtue, he treats the heroes of the world with the ritual courtesy due to guests and gathers them into his net. Having such a ruler as this, how could one bear to turn one's back on him? Therefore, whether esteeming his canonical rites of receiving guests, or esteeming his earnest quest for honored guests, one goes forward for the sake of ritual propriety—how could this be frivolous advancement? Otherwise, to vaunt unbending integrity before a ruler who humbles himself would be perverse; what benefit would there be in it?

In sum, what the Fourth line encounters is a flourishing king of the world, and treating the worthy with ritual courtesy and humbling oneself before scholars is likewise the most flourishing virtue in the world. When a scholar is born and personally meets with such flourishing times, how could he not rejoice for the sake of this Way? Even so, that Qu [Boyu] (蘧伯玉) and Ning [Wuzi] (甯武子) rolled up or unfurled their talents, that Liuxia [Hui] (柳下惠) was dismissed three times, that Jieyu (接輿) walked along singing, and that [Lu] Zhonglian (魯仲連) was ready to cast himself into the sea—all this was because they failed to meet a true ruler. Yet when Yao (堯) and Shun (舜) were above, below…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有巢由則何以稱焉說者謂漢鼎繫於一絲則
不賓之士未必無補於大觀之治云
雷以動之風以散之雨以潤之日以晅之
艮以止之兌以說之乾以君之坤以藏
之
胡允寧
同考試官教諭趙批題本散渙是作聯絡𥠖綴種種
有法而詞旨復莊健可誦
同考試官教諭顧批不事雕刻蒼然有光
===
同考試官教諭楊批精透雅健
考試官教諭湯批精粹可式
考試官教諭王批詞簡意足
觀卦位於先天而造化備焉夫造化育物必有
生成而主藏之者卦位以之玆先天焉得天地
之用乎大傳之意曰天地自然之理運於氣機
天地自然之機昭於圖位吾觀方圖而知造化
之至妙矣彼圖之從中起者震巽也其雷風之
象乎而一動一散所以始物者由之圖之次震
punctuated:
有巢、由，則何以稱焉？說者謂漢鼎繫於一絲，則不賓之士，未必無補於大觀之治云。

「雷以動之，風以散之，雨以潤之，日以晅之，艮以止之，兌以說之，乾以君之，坤以藏之。」
胡允寧
同考試官教諭趙批：題本散渙，是作聯絡𥠖綴，種種有法，而詞旨復莊健可誦。
同考試官教諭顧批：不事雕刻，蒼然有光。
同考試官教諭楊批：精透雅健。
考試官教諭湯批：精粹可式。
考試官教諭王批：詞簡意足。

觀卦位於先天，而造化備焉。夫造化育物，必有生成而主藏之者，卦位以之。玆先天焉，得天地之用乎！《大傳》之意曰：天地自然之理，運於氣機；天地自然之機，昭於圖位。吾觀方圖，而知造化之至妙矣。彼圖之從中起者，震、巽也，其雷風之象乎！而一動一散，所以始物者由之。圖之次震、
translation_en:
… there were Chao Fu 巢父 and Xu You 許由; how then is that to be explained? Commentators say that the Han imperial tripods hung by a single thread [referring to Yan Guang 嚴光 fishing in seclusion]; thus, scholars who refuse to serve as guests at court are not necessarily without benefit to the governance of Great Observation (Daguan 大觀).

"Thunder to rouse them, wind to scatter them, rain to moisten them, the sun to dry them, Gen 艮 [Keeping Still] to stop them, Dui 兌 [The Joyous] to gladden them, Qian 乾 [The Creative] to rule over them, and Kun 坤 [The Receptive] to shelter them." [Book of Changes, Shuo gua 說卦]
By Hu Yunning 胡允寧.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhao 趙: The topic is inherently scattered and diffuse, yet this composition connects and stitches its parts together, methodical in every aspect, while its diction and purport are moreover dignified, vigorous, and worthy of recitation.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Gu 顧: Without indulging in artificial carving, it has a苍然 [venerable, antique] luster.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Yang 楊: Penetrating, refined, and vigorous.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Tang 湯: Pure and essential; worthy of serving as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wang 王: Concise in wording, complete in meaning.

Observe the positions of the trigrams in the Primordial (Xiantian 先天) arrangement, and the operations of Nature are complete therein. Now, in nurturing the myriad things, the creative and transformative forces of Nature must have that which generates and completes them, as well as that which rules over and stores them; the positions of the trigrams correspond to this. In this Primordial arrangement, how fully one grasps the functioning of Heaven and Earth! The meaning of the Great Commentary (Dazhuan 大傳) is as follows: The natural principle of Heaven and Earth operates through the mechanism of vital energy (qi 氣); the natural mechanism of Heaven and Earth is made manifest in the positions of the diagram. I observe the Square Diagram (Fangtu 方圖) and thereby know the ultimate subtlety of Nature's creative transformations. Those in the diagram that arise from the center are Zhen 震 and Xun 巽; are they not the images of thunder and wind? Through the one rousing and the other scattering, that by which things are begun derives from them. Those in the diagram that come next after Zhen…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
巽者坎離也其雨日之象乎而以潤以晅所以
通物者由之繼之以艮則真機謐而物賴以節
宣矣繼之以兌則真精凝而物賴以訢合矣夫
有動散而後有潤晅有潤晅而後有止說其序
不可紊也為動散不能為潤晅為潤晅不能為
止說其職不可兼也其惟乾坤乎六子各一其
氣而乾之元氣足以統之顯仁藏用惟其所樞
宰物之權則然耳謂乾以君之非耶六子各一
其能而坤之簡能足以成之育神復命皆其所
===
受養物之府則然耳謂坤以藏之非耶蓋迹其
生成人見六子之為而不見乾坤之為究其化
機人不曰六子之功而曰乾坤之功此圖位之
所以為妙與抑是天道也亦王道也君有獨制
而藏無專成內外之分也君職其要六卿職其
詳尊卑之等也雷不侵風之散風不奪雨之潤
日不兼艮兌之權官守之明也達於此者措之
天下易易矣
書
punctuated:
巽者，坎、離也。其雨、日之象乎？而以潤以晅，所以通物者由之。繼之以艮，則真機謐而物賴以節宣矣；繼之以兌，則真精凝而物賴以訢合矣。夫有動散而後有潤晅，有潤晅而後有止說，其序不可紊也；為動散不能為潤晅，為潤晅不能為止說，其職不可兼也。其惟乾、坤乎！六子各一其氣，而乾之元氣足以統之，顯仁藏用，惟其所樞，宰物之權則然耳，謂「乾以君之」，非耶？六子各一其能，而坤之簡能足以成之，育神復命，皆其所受，養物之府則然耳，謂「坤以藏之」，非耶？蓋迹其生成，人見六子之為，而不見乾、坤之為；究其化機，人不曰六子之功，而曰乾、坤之功。此圖位之所以為妙與！抑是天道也，亦王道也。君有獨制，而藏無專成，內外之分也；君職其要，六卿職其詳，尊卑之等也；雷不侵風之散，風不奪雨之潤，日不兼艮、兌之權，官守之明也。達於此者，措之天下，易易矣。
《書》
translation_en:
…and Xun in the diagram are Kan and Li. Are they not the images of rain and the sun? By moistening and by warming, that whereby things are brought into free circulation derives from them. Following these with Gen [Mountain], the true mechanism becomes tranquil, and things rely on it for regulation and release; following these with Dui [Lake], the true essence congeals, and things rely on it for joyful harmony. Now, only after there are stirring and scattering can there be moistening and warming; and only after there are moistening and warming can there be stopping and pleasing—their sequence cannot be disordered. That which acts to stir and scatter cannot act to moisten and warm, and that which acts to moisten and warm cannot act to stop and please—their functions cannot be combined. Is this not uniquely the province of Qian and Kun! The six children each possess a single aspect of vital energy, yet the primordial energy of Qian suffices to unify them; manifesting benevolence and concealing its workings, all hinges upon it—such is its authority in governing things. To say "Qian rules over them"—is this not so? The six children each possess a single capacity, yet the simple capacity of Kun suffices to bring them to completion; nurturing the spirit and returning to destiny, all is received within it—such is its storehouse for nourishing things. To say "Kun stores them"—is this not so? Indeed, if one traces the visible process of generation and completion, people see the actions of the six children without seeing the actions of Qian and Kun; yet if one investigates the underlying mechanism of transformation, people do not call it the achievement of the six children, but rather the achievement of Qian and Kun. Is this not wherein lies the subtlety of the positions in the diagram! Moreover, this is the Way of Heaven, and it is also the Kingly Way. The ruler exercises sole control, while the storehouse claims no independent completion: this is the distinction between inner and outer. The ruler attends to the essentials, while the Six Ministers attend to the details: this is the gradation of noble and base. Thunder does not encroach upon the scattering of wind, wind does not usurp the moistening of rain, and the sun does not combine the authorities of Gen and Dui: this is the clarity of official responsibilities. For one who comprehends this, putting it into practice throughout the realm is altogether easy!

Classic of History (Shu)

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
明四目達四聰
孟養浩
同考試官訓導范批詞簡義該發明達意殆盡可錄
以式浮靡者
同考試官訓導范批體格莊嚴超轍更有精思
考試官教諭湯批刊落陳言自爾典雅
考試官教諭王批虞帝求民瘼之意藹然言表
聖君謀治內臣欲其通天下之情也夫民情貴
周知也明目達聰而天下之情通矣宜舜首詢
===
此謂夫治天下者求賢要矣安民急焉故吾之
一身本天下之人之身則天下利病皆吾之利
病也但予一人居九重之上而欲達四方之隱
其勢恒難周爾四岳處君民之間而欲通上下
之情其機常甚便爾其率天下諸侯爲予明四
目焉太平之景象予所願見者固得而見之而
閭閻之艱難予所不願見者亦得而見之舉寒
者饑者疾首而蹙額者咸若集於吾前可矣又
率天下諸侯爲予達四聰焉盛治之謳歌予所
punctuated:
「明四目，達四聰。」
孟養浩
同考試官訓導范批：詞簡義該，發明「達」意殆盡，可錄以式浮靡者。
同考試官訓導范批：體格莊嚴，超轍更有精思。
考試官教諭湯批：刊落陳言，自爾典雅。
考試官教諭王批：虞帝求民瘼之意，藹然言表。
聖君謀治，內臣欲其通天下之情也。夫民情貴周知也。明目達聰，而天下之情通矣，宜舜首詢此。謂夫治天下者，求賢要矣，安民急焉。故吾之一身，本天下之人之身，則天下利病，皆吾之利病也。但予一人居九重之上，而欲達四方之隱，其勢恒難周；爾四岳處君民之間，而欲通上下之情，其機常甚便。爾其率天下諸侯，爲予明四目焉。太平之景象，予所願見者，固得而見之；而閭閻之艱難，予所不願見者，亦得而見之。舉寒者、饑者、疾首而蹙額者，咸若集於吾前可矣。又率天下諸侯，爲予達四聰焉。盛治之謳歌，予所
translation_en:
"Clarify the sight of the four quarters, and open up the hearing of the four quarters."

Meng Yanghao 孟養浩

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Fan comments: The diction is concise and the meaning comprehensive; it elucidates the idea of "opening up" almost exhaustively, and is worthy of being recorded as a model to correct florid and superficial writing.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Fan comments: The structure is庄嚴 (stately and solemn), transcending the usual ruts while possessing even more refined thought.
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Tang comments: Having pared away trite expressions, it is naturally classic and elegant.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: The Emperor of Yu's [Shun's] intention in seeking out the sufferings of the people shines warmly beyond the words.

When the sage ruler took counsel for governance, he desired his inner ministers to communicate the conditions of all under Heaven. Now, as for the conditions of the people, what is valued is knowing them comprehensively. When sight is clarified and hearing opened up, the conditions of all under Heaven are communicated; it was fitting that Shun inquired about this first. He said, in effect: For one who governs all under Heaven, seeking the worthy is essential, and giving rest to the people is urgent. Therefore, my own person is fundamentally the person of the people of all under Heaven, and the benefits and ills of all under Heaven are all my own benefits and ills. Yet I, the One Man, dwell above the ninefold gates of the palace, and when I wish to reach the hidden distresses of the four quarters, by the nature of my position it is constantly difficult to be comprehensive; you, the Four Peaks (Siyue), stand between ruler and people, and when you wish to communicate the feelings of those above and below, your position always makes the opportunity most convenient. Do you lead the feudal lords of all under Heaven to clarify the sight of the four quarters for me. The scenes of great peace, which I wish to see, I shall certainly be able to see; and the hardships of the village lanes, which I do not wish to see, I shall also be able to see. Let all who are cold, who are hungry, and who ache in the head and knit their brows be as though gathered before me—that will do. And again, lead the feudal lords of all under Heaven to open up the hearing of the four quarters for me. The songs of praise for flourishing governance, which I…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
樂聞者固得而聞之而下民之其咨予所不樂
聞者亦得而聞之舉號寒者啼饑者顛連而欲
告者咸若陳於吾前可矣其在下民有隱而未
達有抑而未伸而恒苦上人耳目之弗逮其在
天子隱而使必達抑而使必伸而不阻一人聞
見之無由庶治其可保乎吾想自古聰明之主
莫若堯舜彼其時皐夔稷契輩卽人號稱賢執
有如堯舜之耳目智慮者乃一則曰作股肱耳
目一則曰明目達聰何不自用而用人也夫不
===
自用而用人正其聲色不動而天下乂安者耳
彼見萬里察淵魚而曰吾能治天下也謬之謬
者也
皇建其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥庶民
張濤
同考試官訓導范批〔命意精深置辭雄渾宛然皇極〕
〔君民氣象可錄〕
同考試官訓導范批〔理會眞切詞更嚴整〕
考試官教諭湯批〔清謹之氣溢於辭□中選〕
punctuated:
樂聞者，固得而聞之；而下民之其咨，予所不樂聞者，亦得而聞之。舉號寒者、啼饑者、顛連而欲告者，咸若陳於吾前可矣。其在下民，有隱而未達，有抑而未伸，而恒苦上人耳目之弗逮；其在天子，隱而使必達，抑而使必伸，而不阻一人聞見之無由。庶治其可保乎！吾想自古聰明之主莫若堯、舜。彼其時，皐、夔、稷、契輩，卽人號稱賢，執有如堯、舜之耳目智慮者？乃一則曰「作股肱耳目」，一則曰「明目達聰」，何不自用而用人也？夫不自用而用人，正其聲色不動而天下乂安者耳。彼見萬里、察淵魚，而曰「吾能治天下」也，謬之謬者也。

「皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。」
張濤
同考試官訓導范批：〔命意精深，置辭雄渾，宛然皇極〕〔君民氣象。可錄。〕
同考試官訓導范批：〔理會眞切，詞更嚴整。〕
考試官教諭湯批：〔清謹之氣溢於辭□。中選。〕
translation_en:
…delighted to hear, I shall indeed be able to hear; and the groans of the common people, which I am not delighted to hear, I shall also be able to hear. All those who cry out from cold, weep from hunger, or are in distress with nowhere to turn for appeal—let it be as though all of them were set forth right before me! Among the common people below, there are grievances hidden and uncommunicated, wrongs suppressed and unredressed, and they ever suffer because the ears and eyes of their superiors do not reach them. For the Son of Heaven above, to ensure that what is hidden is必ず communicated and what is suppressed is必ず redressed, so that the One Man is never cut off from a means of hearing and seeing—through this, may good governance perhaps be preserved!”

I reflect that since antiquity, no rulers have been as perceptive and clear-sighted as Yao and Shun. In their day, although men such as Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Xie were acclaimed as worthy, who among them [執, for 孰] could match the ears, eyes, wisdom, and foresight of Yao and Shun? Yet one said, “You act as my limbs, my ears, and my eyes,” and the other said, “To see with the eyes and hear with the ears of all”—why did they not rely on themselves, but instead relied on others? Indeed, not relying on oneself and instead relying on others is precisely how, without altering countenance or raising one's voice, the empire was brought to peace and order. Those who boast of seeing ten thousand li away or peering into the fishes in the abyss, saying, “I am able to govern the empire,” are mistaken to the utmost degree.

“The Sovereign establishes his supreme standard; he gathers together these five blessings, and then broadly bestows them upon his common people.”

By Zhang Tao 張濤.

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Fan comments: 〔The conception is profound and the phrasing vigorous and grand; it vividly captures the spirit of ruler and people under the Supreme Standard. Worthy of recording.〕
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Fan comments: 〔The grasp of principle is genuine and incisive, and the diction is all the more rigorous and well-ordered.〕
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Tang comments: 〔An air of clarity and care brims throughout the diction [?]. Selected.〕

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭王批邃思古調書義之最佳者
王者立極以集福而因公諸天下也夫大君者
立人極者也以此集福而推以錫天下此見皇
極之道大矣且天人一機而感之者在人不在
天君民一理而孚之者在君不在民故皇者繼
天出治庶民環向而取則焉用感孚其間者極
也以典則惇朝廷立四方之準以禮則庸一人
樹天下之觀人君一動一靜無毫髮不通於天
而吾建極則已格於昭昭之表矣彼五福來同
===
若來於德也上天一視一聽無一息不注於君
而吾建極則已鑒於冥冥之中矣彼五福駢臻
若臻於德也然是福之錫也錫其所敷於民者
而非外天下以私一人則是福之斂也亦斂其
所敷於民者而不私吾身以後天下吾惇吾典
以迪吉而使民各惇典以自迪其吉是造德以
造福也而一夫無不獲矣吾庸吾禮以召順而
使民各庸禮以自召其順是布德以布福也而
羣黎無失所矣天人上下凝焉和氣而不乖朝
punctuated:
考試官敎諭王批：邃思古調，書義之最佳者。

王者立極以集福，而因公諸天下也。夫大君者，立人極者也。以此集福，而推以錫天下，此見皇極之道大矣。且天人一機，而感之者在人不在天；君民一理，而孚之者在君不在民。故皇者繼天出治，庶民環向而取則焉，用感孚其間者，極也。以典則惇，朝廷立四方之準；以禮則庸，一人樹天下之觀。人君一動一靜，無毫髮不通於天，而吾建極，則已格於昭昭之表矣；彼五福來同，若來於德也。上天一視一聽，無一息不注於君，而吾建極，則已鑒於冥冥之中矣；彼五福駢臻，若臻於德也。然是福之錫也，錫其所敷於民者，而非外天下以私一人；則是福之斂也，亦斂其所敷於民者，而不私吾身以後天下。吾惇吾典以迪吉，而使民各惇典以自迪其吉，是造德以造福也，而一夫無不獲矣；吾庸吾禮以召順，而使民各庸禮以自召其順，是布德以布福也，而羣黎無失所矣。天人上下，凝焉和氣而不乖；朝…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Profound thought and classical cadence; the finest among the expositions on the Classic of History (Shu).

The true king establishes the standard of perfection in order to concentrate blessings, and consequently shares them publicly with all under Heaven. Now, the great sovereign is he who establishes the standard of perfection for humankind. By this means he concentrates blessings and extends them to bestow upon all under Heaven; from this one sees how great is the Way of the Royal Perfection! Moreover, Heaven and humankind share a single mechanism, yet what moves it rests with humankind and not with Heaven; sovereign and people share a single principle, yet what inspires trust in it rests with the sovereign and not with the people. Therefore, when the August Sovereign succeeds Heaven in bringing forth governance, and the multitude of the common people turn toward him from all sides to take him as their model, that which acts to move and inspire trust between them is the standard of perfection. In terms of the constant norms, he gives weight to them, and the court establishes the standard for the four quarters; in terms of the rites, he practices them, and the One Man sets up an exemplar for all under Heaven to behold. In the ruler’s every movement and every stillness, there is not a hair’s breadth that does not communicate with Heaven; once I establish the standard of perfection, it already reaches beyond the bright expanse above, and those Five Blessings come together as if drawn by virtue. In High Heaven’s every glance and every listening, there is not a single breath when its attention is not fixed upon the ruler; once I establish the standard of perfection, it is already mirrored within the unseen realm, and those Five Blessings arrive side by side as if brought by virtue. Yet the bestowing of these blessings is a bestowing of that which is spread out to the people, rather than excluding all under Heaven in order to favor the One Man alone; thus the concentrating of these blessings is likewise a concentrating of that which is to be spread out to the people, rather than favoring my own person and putting all under Heaven last. I give weight to my constant norms in order to lead the way to good fortune, and cause the people each to give weight to the constant norms so as to lead themselves to their own good fortune—this is creating virtue in order to create blessings, and not a single man fails to obtain his share. I practice my rites in order to summon harmony, and cause the people each to practice the rites so as to summon their own harmony—this is spreading virtue in order to spread blessings, and none among the multitude of the people loses his proper place. Above and below, between Heaven and humankind, harmonious qi coalesces without discord; at court…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
野內外溢爲休風而無間極之義如此夫君人
之福與常人異常人福止一身君人福在天下
假令壽富康寧好德考終五福備君身矣彼貧
者夭者不寧居者敗德而匪彝者且載道路也
是可稱福乎故兆民戴德即君人之福必取效
五福猶二之矣
詩
韎鞈有奭以作六師
吳顯科
===
同考試官訓導趙批習安狃平二語起得作字明徹
而末段議論更有關係
同考試官教諭尹批得周王保泰之旨可錄
考試官教諭湯批莊雅可誦
考試官教諭王批意透詞雅
周王親講武之事而治道豫矣夫兵非治世所
諱也御戎服以作六師保治之圖豫矣哉且觀
兵非得已也天下之勢名爲治平而常伏不測
之憂是故明主慎焉東都之會人心同而福祿
punctuated:
野內外溢爲休風而無間，極之義如此。夫君人之福，與常人異；常人福止一身，君人福在天下。假令壽、富、康寧、好德、考終，五福備君身矣，彼貧者、夭者、不寧居者、敗德而匪彝者，且載道路也，是可稱福乎？故兆民戴德，即君人之福，必取效五福，猶二之矣。

《詩》
「韎鞈有奭，以作六師。」
吳顯科
同考試官訓導趙批：習安狃平二語，起得「作」字明徹，而末段議論更有關係。
同考試官教諭尹批：得周王保泰之旨，可錄。
考試官教諭湯批：莊雅可誦。
考試官教諭王批：意透詞雅。

周王親講武之事，而治道豫矣。夫兵，非治世所諱也；御戎服以作六師，保治之圖豫矣哉！且觀兵非得已也。天下之勢，名爲治平，而常伏不測之憂，是故明主慎焉。東都之會，人心同而福祿
translation_en:
… and outside the court, across the realm, an auspicious atmosphere overflows without gap—such is the meaning of the Supreme Standard. Now, the blessings of a ruler of men differ from those of an ordinary man. An ordinary man's blessings stop with his own person; a ruler's blessings lie in the whole world. Suppose longevity, wealth, health and peace, love of virtue, and a crowning end to life—all five blessings—were complete in the ruler's own person, yet the poor, the prematurely dying, those without peaceful dwellings, and those of ruined virtue and lawless conduct filled the roads: could this be called blessing? Therefore, when the millions of people cherish his virtue, that itself is the blessing of the ruler of men; if one insists on seeking proof in the five blessings, that is still to treat them as two separate things.

Book of Odes (Shi):
"The madder-dyed knee-covers are red, to rouse the Six Armies."
Wu Xianke 吳顯科
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao comments: The two parallel lines on being accustomed to safety and habituated to peace bring out the word "rouse" (zuo) with crystal clarity, and the argument in the final paragraph is of even greater consequence.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: It grasps the Zhou king's intent in preserving great peace; worthy of selection.
Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: Dignified and elegant, worthy of recitation.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: The thought is penetrating and the diction elegant.

When the King of Zhou personally attended to martial exercises, the way of governance was prepared in advance. Now, military affairs are not something tabooed in a well-governed age; by donning martial attire to rouse the Six Armies, how well-prepared in advance was his plan for preserving good order! Moreover, displaying military might is not done out of mere inclination. When the state of the realm is nominally one of order and peace, unforeseen anxieties often lie hidden within it; therefore, an enlightened ruler is cautious about this. At the assembly in the Eastern Capital, the hearts of the people were united and blessings and emoluments…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
聚矣乃君子則以理亂循環之幾不可忘戰家
邦久遠之計誰能去兵師徒方渙不作則不奮
也臨瀍洛以嚴簡閱之敎觀聽方新不親則不
肅也釋衮冕而躬韎鞈之章六師之氣習安而
靡矣則勗其止齊以示之勇伍兩軍師莫不起
而共武服者作其氣也六師之志狃平而偷矣
則申其誓戒以訓之忠文武將吏莫不起而敵
王愾者作其志也我周本以戎衣開國而維有
奭之御則大烈以揚列侯環視不益震於天威
===
而堅其翊戴之思哉先王甞以整旅戡亂而今
六師之作則顯謨以承六合風聞不將慴於王
靈而消其釁孽之萌哉蓋當是時天下之治日
趨於尚文不可不耀之以武國家之勢已見其
積弱不可不糾之以強玆役也保治之圖也周
道復興宜矣自周而後天子宿重兵於京師亦
古者六軍遺意彼五柞長楊豈不稱習戎哉而
久之漸替故其季也禁衞雖設而非習服遇小
警即不能受甲焉噫六師之作詎至此乎是故
punctuated: 聚矣。乃君子則以理亂循環之幾，不可忘戰；家邦久遠之計，誰能去兵？師徒方渙，不作則不奮也，臨瀍洛以嚴簡閱之敎；觀聽方新，不親則不肅也，釋衮冕而躬韎鞈之章。六師之氣，習安而靡矣，則勗其止齊以示之勇，伍兩軍師莫不起而共武服者，作其氣也；六師之志，狃平而偷矣，則申其誓戒以訓之忠，文武將吏莫不起而敵王愾者，作其志也。我周本以戎衣開國，而維有奭之御，則大烈以揚，列侯環視，不益震於天威而堅其翊戴之思哉？先王甞以整旅戡亂，而今六師之作，則顯謨以承，六合風聞，不將慴於王靈而消其釁孽之萌哉？蓋當是時，天下之治日趨於尚文，不可不耀之以武；國家之勢已見其積弱，不可不糾之以強。玆役也，保治之圖也，周道復興，宜矣！自周而後，天子宿重兵於京師，亦古者六軍遺意。彼五柞、長楊，豈不稱習戎哉？而久之漸替，故其季也，禁衞雖設，而非習服，遇小警即不能受甲焉。噫！六師之作，詎至此乎？是故
translation_en: …had gathered. Yet the noble men considered that in the cyclical turning point of order and disorder, one must not forget warfare; in the long-term plans for family and state, who can dispense with arms? When the troops are just beginning to slacken, if they are not roused they will not be spirited; thus he went to the Chan and Luo rivers to enforce the instruction of inspection and review. When the eyes and ears of the people are newly attentive, if the king does not attend in person there will be no solemnity; thus he laid aside his ceremonial robes and crown and personally put on the red-dyed knee-covers of military attire. The spirit of the Six Armies, accustomed to peace, had grown languid; so he exhorted them in halting and dressing ranks to show them courage, and none among the squads, platoons, regiments, and divisions failed to rise and attend to military service—this was rousing their spirit. The resolve of the Six Armies, habituated to tranquility, had grown lax; so he reiterated his oaths and warnings to instruct them in loyalty, and none among the civil and military officers failed to rise and oppose the objects of the king's wrath—this was rousing their resolve. Our Zhou dynasty originally founded the state in battle dress, and by wearing the red knee-covers, its great achievements were proclaimed; as the feudal lords looked on from all sides, would they not be all the more awed by the heavenly majesty and strengthened in their devotion to support and uphold the throne? The former kings once marshaled their troops to quell rebellion, and now by rousing the Six Armies, their illustrious plans were carried forward; as the whole realm heard the news on the wind, would they not tremble before the royal prestige and extinguish the buds of sedition and trouble? Indeed, at that time, the governance of the empire was daily inclining toward the prizing of civil culture, so it could not but be made resplendent with martial vigor; the state of the realm was already showing accumulated weakness, so it could not but be rectified with strength. This campaign was a plan for preserving good order; that the Way of Zhou revived was fitting indeed! From the Zhou onward, the Son of Heaven stationed heavy forces in the capital, which also preserved the legacy of the ancient Six Armies. Did not those hunts at the Five Oaks (Wuzuo) and Long Willows (Changyang) palaces claim to be military exercises? Yet over time they gradually declined, so that in their final years, although the imperial guards were established, they were not trained and accustomed to service, and upon encountering a minor alarm they were unable even to put on armor. Alas! Could the rousing of the Six Armies ever have come to such a pass? Therefore…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
周雅以頌漢賦以風
乃及王季維德之行大任有身生此文王
段藎國
同考試官訓導趙批上二句作者多以王季大任並
講殊失輕重下二句作者非枯淡則浮泛此作獨得之
同考試官教諭尹批典贍有體
考試官教諭湯批體格純正
考試官教諭王批詞意俱到
周有一德之配而聖人生矣蓋父作之母相之
===
天之所以開聖人也此文王所由生與詩人推
本以戒成王曰我周受命始於文王固矣而其
生豈偶然哉蓋國之將興天必生聖人以長發
其祥聖之將生天必厚聖人之所自生以竝鍾
其德故婦於京而思媚大任之婦道脩矣乃及
王季殆與其明類者有合德也嬪於周而思齊
大任之母道全矣乃及王季殆與其順比者無
違行也夫以德配德則帝祉集而大任身焉因
以凝醇和之氣以德育德則貞元會而文王生
punctuated:
周雅以頌，漢賦以風。

乃及王季，維德之行。大任有身，生此文王。
段藎國
同考試官訓導趙批：上二句作者多以王季、大任並講，殊失輕重；下二句作者非枯淡則浮泛，此作獨得之。
同考試官教諭尹批：典贍有體。
考試官教諭湯批：體格純正。
考試官教諭王批：詞意俱到。

周有一德之配，而聖人生矣。蓋父作之，母相之，天之所以開聖人也。此文王所由生與？詩人推本以戒成王曰：我周受命始於文王，固矣，而其生豈偶然哉？蓋國之將興，天必生聖人以長發其祥；聖之將生，天必厚聖人之所自生以竝鍾其德。故婦於京而思媚，大任之婦道脩矣；乃及王季，殆與其明類者有合德也。嬪於周而思齊，大任之母道全矣；乃及王季，殆與其順比者無違行也。夫以德配德，則帝祉集而大任身焉，因以凝醇和之氣；以德育德，則貞元會而文王生…
translation_en:
… the Zhou odes served as eulogies, whereas the Han rhapsodies served as admonitions.

"Then even unto King Ji, / Only virtue did she practice. / Tai Ren became with child, / And gave birth to this King Wen."
Duan Jinguo
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao: On the first two lines, most writers treat King Ji and Tai Ren equally, completely losing the proper emphasis; on the last two lines, writers are either dry and insipid or superficial and vague. This essay alone gets it right.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yin: Classical, rich, and well-structured.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang: Pure and upright in style and form.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: Both the phrasing and the meaning hit the mark.

The Zhou possessed a consort of united virtue, and thus a sage was born. Indeed, the father initiated it and the mother assisted it—this is how Heaven opens the way for a sage. Is this not how King Wen came to be born? Tracing things back to their roots in order to admonish King Cheng, the poet said: That our Zhou received the Mandate began with King Wen is certain, yet how could his birth have been a matter of chance? When a state is about to rise, Heaven necessarily brings forth a sage to long manifest its auspicious signs; and when a sage is about to be born, Heaven necessarily enriches those from whom the sage springs so as to jointly concentrate their virtue. Therefore, coming as a bride to the capital and thinking fondly of pleasing her elders, Tai Ren's way as a wife was cultivated; and extending to King Ji, she shared a matching virtue with his discerning and benevolent nature. Becoming a wife in Zhou and thinking of emulating her predecessors, Tai Ren's way as a mother was complete; and extending to King Ji, she had no conduct at variance with his compliant and harmonious ways. Now, when virtue is matched with virtue, the blessings of the Supreme Lord gather and Tai Ren conceives, thereby condensing the purest and most harmonious vital energy; when virtue nurtures virtue, the cycle of constancy and origination converges and King Wen is born…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
焉遂以協聖作之期胎敎於未生之初言敎於
已生之後人曰任之成厥子也而自其有身之
始則乾坤清淑之英已萃之矣近以拓三分之
基遠以貽八百之緖人曰文之肇厥家也而自
其有生之時則蒼姬靈長之籙已卜之矣故有
王季必不可無文王微文則孰爲之後生文王
必不可無大任微任則孰爲之先吁於此見聖
德之自而後王可繹思矣嘗謂聖人之生天也
而其所以聖則非天也人也不有肅雍臨保則
===
天生文王亦虛矣卽季任何稱焉故曰昭事上
帝聿懷多福此戒成王本指也不然述祖而第
夸其誕育之異則亦史臣之侈詞已耳何以爲
周公之詩
春秋
齊師宋師曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕春王正月
城楚丘〔僖公二年〕春諸侯城緣陵〔僖公
十有四年〕
劉承芳
punctuated:
焉，遂以協聖作之期。胎敎於未生之初，言敎於已生之後，人曰任之成厥子也，而自其有身之始，則乾坤清淑之英已萃之矣。近以拓三分之基，遠以貽八百之緖，人曰文之肇厥家也，而自其有生之時，則蒼姬靈長之籙已卜之矣。故有王季必不可無文王，微文則孰爲之後？生文王必不可無大任，微任則孰爲之先？吁！於此見聖德之自，而後王可繹思矣。嘗謂聖人之生，天也；而其所以聖，則非天也，人也。不有肅雍臨保，則天生文王亦虛矣，卽季、任何稱焉？故曰「昭事上帝，聿懷多福」，此戒成王本指也。不然，述祖而第夸其誕育之異，則亦史臣之侈詞已耳，何以爲周公之詩？

《春秋》
齊師、宋師、曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕；春王正月，城楚丘〔僖公二年〕；春，諸侯城緣陵〔僖公十有四年〕。
劉承芳
translation_en:
… and thereby fulfilled the appointed time for a sage to arise. With prenatal instruction before he was born and verbal instruction after his birth, people said that it was Tai Ren who brought her son to completion; yet from the very beginning of her pregnancy, the pure and virtuous essence of Heaven and Earth had already gathered in him. In the near term expanding the foundation of possessing two-thirds of the realm, and in the long term bequeathing an inheritance of eight hundred years, people said that it was King Wen who founded his house; yet from the moment of his birth, the enduring mandate of the illustrious Ji clan had already been foretold. Therefore, having King Ji, there could not but be King Wen—without Wen, who would have carried on after him? And to give birth to King Wen, there could not but be Tai Ren—without Ren, who would have preceded him? Ah! In this we see the source of sagely virtue, upon which later kings may well reflect. It has been said that the birth of a sage is a matter of Heaven, whereas that by which he becomes a sage is not of Heaven, but of man. Had he not possessed reverence and harmony in approaching and preserving, then Heaven's giving birth to King Wen would have been in vain, and what would there have been to praise in King Ji and Tai Ren? Thus it is said, "Brightly he served the Lord on High, and so secured abundant blessings"—this is the fundamental intent in admonishing King Cheng. Otherwise, to recount one's ancestors and merely boast of the marvels of their birth and rearing would be nothing more than the extravagant words of court historians; how could it be an ode by the Duke of Zhou?

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"The army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Cao walled Xing" [First year of Duke Xi]; "In spring, the king's first month, they walled Chuqiu" [Second year of Duke Xi]; "In spring, the feudal lords walled Yuanling" [Fourteenth year of Duke Xi].
By Liu Chengfang 劉承芳

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導王批敘三城書法得旨經義之佳者
宜錄以式
考試官教諭湯批格嚴詞鍊
考試官教諭王批整潔雅健
霸主專以存小春秋因事而示法焉夫善恤患
而惡專命春秋法也此三城之書詞所以異歟
齊桓之霸也存三亡國焉城邢而邢安城楚丘
而衞定城緣陵而杞無恙其事同矣春秋待之
異者何自城邢言之狄難殷而夷儀遷邢亡在
===
旦夕矣桓也卽以救邢之師而城以遷之是役
也謂之有命固不可獨不曰爲天子恤庶邦乎
邢之存桓之力也故詳列三師以著其善云自
楚丘言之狄師入而漕邑處衞亡已踰年矣桓
也爰度楚丘之地而城以戍之是役也謂之無
功固不可獨不曰無有封而不告乎衞之有周
之無也故沒諸侯不書以略其功云乃緣陵則
異是矣夷勢不若狄勢之張杞禍未若衞禍之
烈若之何自遷而自城之豈其知有杞不知有
punctuated:
同考試官訓導王批：敘三城書法得旨，經義之佳者，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭湯批：格嚴詞鍊。
考試官教諭王批：整潔雅健。
霸主專以存小，《春秋》因事而示法焉。夫善恤患而惡專命，《春秋》法也，此三城之書詞所以異歟！齊桓之霸也，存三亡國焉：城邢而邢安，城楚丘而衞定，城緣陵而杞無恙，其事同矣。《春秋》待之異者何？自城邢言之，狄難殷而夷儀遷，邢亡在旦夕矣。桓也，卽以救邢之師而城以遷之。是役也，謂之有命固不可，獨不曰爲天子恤庶邦乎？邢之存，桓之力也，故詳列三師以著其善云。自楚丘言之，狄師入而漕邑處，衞亡已踰年矣。桓也，爰度楚丘之地而城以戍之。是役也，謂之無功固不可，獨不曰「無有封而不告」乎？衞之有，周之無也，故沒諸侯不書以略其功云。乃緣陵則異是矣：夷勢不若狄勢之張，杞禍未若衞禍之烈，若之何自遷而自城之？豈其知有杞不知有
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang: The account of the historiographical principles regarding the walling of the three cities grasps the essential meaning. It is a fine piece of classical exegesis and ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang: Rigorous in structure and refined in diction.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: Neat, elegant, and vigorous.

The Hegemon acted on his own authority to preserve small states, and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) used these events to demonstrate its judgment. Indeed, to commend the relief of distress while condemning the usurpation of royal authority is the standard of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Is this not why the wording recorded for the walling of these three cities differs! In his hegemony, Duke Huan of Qi preserved three perishing states: he walled Xing and Xing was secured; he walled Chuqiu and Wei was stabilized; he walled Yuanling and Qi was kept unharmed. The deeds were the same. Why, then, did the Spring and Autumn Annals treat them differently?

Speaking of the walling of Xing: the Di threat was severe and Xing relocated to Yiyi; the fall of Xing was imminent at any moment. Huan thereupon used the very armies sent to rescue Xing to wall the city and relocate them there. Of this campaign, while one certainly cannot say that it had a royal mandate, could one not say that he was relieving the various states on behalf of the Son of Heaven? The preservation of Xing was due to Huan's strength; therefore, the Annals lists the three armies in detail in order to make manifest his goodness.

Speaking of Chuqiu: the Di army had invaded and the people of Wei were dwelling at the town of Cao; Wei had already been ruined for over a year. Huan thereupon surveyed the land of Chuqiu and walled it to garrison them. Of this campaign, while one certainly cannot say that it was without merit, does the rule not state, "There shall be no enfeoffment without reporting to the King"? That Wei existed as a state meant that the house of Zhou was treated as naught; therefore, the Annals suppresses the mention of the feudal lords and does not record them, in order to pass over his merit.

As for Yuanling, however, it differed from these: the power of the Yi tribes was not as rampant as that of the Di, and the disaster befalling Qi was not yet as fierce as that which befell Wei. Why, then, did he relocate them and wall a city for them on his own initiative? Could it be that he recognized the existence of Qi, yet did not recognize the existence of…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
周乎此其義不同於恤患而罪差薄於專封故
凡舉諸侯而不序與城邢楚丘異者聖人固權
之審矣吁此尊王賤伯意也雖然當周之季天
下之不胥為夷狄者賴有桓公在耳讀定中木
瓜之詩則衛之德齊甚矣奈何有意督過之蓋
春秋以道義而桓以功利無論緣陵楚丘即城
邢亦不能無議焉故聶北之次春秋譏之惡其
養亂為功也夫子大管仲之功而無道桓文之
事嗚呼其旨深矣
===
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕吳子使札來聘〔襄公二十有九年〕
梅森
同考試官訓導王批〔責穆公季札詞嚴義正深得聖人之旨〕
考試官教諭湯批〔語峻潔意委曲錄之〕
考試官教諭王批〔詞旨明確〕
春秋責備之義於賢君賢臣見之也此秦穆貳
過季札苦節皆賢者之累也春秋所以備責之
punctuated:
周乎？此其義不同於恤患，而罪差薄於專封。故凡舉諸侯而不序，與城邢、楚丘異者，聖人固權之審矣。吁！此尊王賤伯意也。雖然，當周之季，天下之不胥為夷狄者，賴有桓公在耳。讀《定中》、《木瓜》之詩，則衛之德齊甚矣，奈何有意督過之？蓋《春秋》以道義，而桓以功利；無論緣陵、楚丘，即城邢亦不能無議焉。故聶北之次，《春秋》譏之，惡其養亂為功也。夫子大管仲之功，而無道桓、文之事，嗚呼！其旨深矣。

秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕、吳子使札來聘〔襄公二十有九年〕
梅森
同考試官訓導王批：〔責穆公、季札，詞嚴義正，深得聖人之旨。〕
考試官教諭湯批：〔語峻潔，意委曲，錄之。〕
考試官教諭王批：〔詞旨明確。〕
《春秋》責備之義，於賢君、賢臣見之也。此秦穆貳過、季札苦節，皆賢者之累也，《春秋》所以備責之
translation_en:
… Zhou? Here the principle is not the same as relieving distress, while the offense is slightly less grave than unauthorizedly enfeoffing a state. Therefore, in referring collectively to the feudal lords without listing them in order—differing from the walling of Xing and Chuqiu—the Sage indeed weighed the matter with great care. Alas! This reflects the intent of honoring the King and disparaging the Hegemons. Even so, during the decline of the Zhou, that the realm did not sink altogether into barbarism depended solely on the presence of Duke Huan of Qi. When one reads the odes "Ding zhong" (Ding zhi fang zhong) and "Mugua" in the Classic of Odes, one sees how deeply grateful Wei was to Qi; why, then, deliberately find fault with him? It is because the Spring and Autumn Annals judges by moral principle, whereas Duke Huan acted out of utilitarian calculation; not to mention Yuanling and Chuqiu, even the walling of Xing is not beyond criticism. Thus, the halting of the troops at Niebei is criticized by the Spring and Autumn Annals, which despised his allowing disorder to fester so as to claim credit for himself. The Master praised the achievements of Guan Zhong, yet his disciples did not speak of the affairs of Dukes Huan and Wen. Alas! How profound was his meaning!

"The people of Qin attacked Jin" [3rd year of Duke Wen]; "The Viscount of Wu sent Zha to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [29th year of Duke Xiang]
Mei Sen 梅森
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Wang's comment: [In faulting Duke Mu and Jizha, the diction is stern and the reasoning upright; it deeply grasps the intent of the Sage.]
Examiner Instructor Tang's comment: [The language is crisp and pure, and the thought nuanced; selected for inclusion.]
Examiner Instructor Wang's comment: [The diction and purport are clear and precise.]

The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals in demanding perfection is seen in its treatment of worthy rulers and worthy ministers. Here, Duke Mu of Qin's repeating a fault and Jizha's extreme ascetic integrity were both blemishes upon worthy men; that is why the Spring and Autumn Annals held them to the fullest account…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其詞恕統全節而品隲之其法密故曰春秋聖
人之刑書也然觀黃鳥之詩穆眞少恩哉而季
札之讓猶有首陽之風焉此又不可以並論云
禮記
凡聽五刑之訟必原父子之親立君臣之
義以權之意論輕重之序愼測淺深之
量以別之悉其聰明致其忠愛以盡之
疑獄氾與眾共之眾疑赦之必察小大
之比以成之
===
樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批聽訟之權發揮明盡末歸於議
緩尤得欽恤之意
考試官教諭王批婉曲詳明可為司平龜鑑
王制言司理者必詳其聽而後成焉夫聽訟將
以成獄也聽之詳斯成之當矣焉往非公哉記
王制者有曰聖人貴無訟也訟而聽焉非其心
矣矧可弗公乎是故五刑之訟親與義其大矣
而輕重而淺深而法比非訟者所能自明也五
punctuated:
其詞恕；統全節而品隲之，其法密。故曰：《春秋》，聖人之刑書也。然觀《黃鳥》之詩，穆眞少恩哉！而季札之讓，猶有首陽之風焉，此又不可以並論云。

《禮記》
凡聽五刑之訟，必原父子之親，立君臣之義，以權之；意論輕重之序，愼測淺深之量，以別之；悉其聰明，致其忠愛，以盡之；疑獄，氾與眾共之，眾疑，赦之；必察小大之比，以成之。
樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批：聽訟之權，發揮明盡，末歸於議緩，尤得欽恤之意。
考試官教諭王批：婉曲詳明，可為司平龜鑑。

《王制》言司理者，必詳其聽而後成焉。夫聽訟將以成獄也，聽之詳斯成之當矣，焉往非公哉？記《王制》者有曰：聖人貴無訟也，訟而聽焉，非其心矣，矧可弗公乎？是故五刑之訟，親與義其大矣，而輕重、而淺深、而法比，非訟者所能自明也；五
translation_en:
… its wording is forgiving; when evaluating and ranking their conduct in its entirety, its rules are strict. Therefore it is said: The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) is the Sage's book of penal law. Yet when we look at the ode "Yellow Birds" (Huangniao), Duke Mu was truly lacking in grace! Whereas Jizha's yielding of the throne still retained the noble air of Mount Shouyang; thus the two cannot be discussed on the same footing.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"In hearing any case involving the five punishments, one must trace the affection between father and son and establish the righteous duty between ruler and minister in order to weigh it; thoughtfully consider the order of gravity and carefully gauge the degree of culpability in order to differentiate it; exhaust one's intelligence and discernment and extend one's utmost loyalty and compassion in order to get to the bottom of it; in doubtful cases, consult broadly with the multitude, and if the multitude is in doubt, pardon it; and one must examine precedents both small and great in order to bring the case to a conclusion."
Fan Yuheng
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Tang comments: The weighing of judicial hearings is expounded with clarity and thoroughness; concluding at the end with deliberation for leniency especially captures the spirit of reverent compassion in punishment.
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Wang comments: Nuanced, detailed, and clear; it can serve as a mirror and model for judicial officials.

The "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi) states that those in charge of administering justice must first be thorough in their hearing before finalizing a verdict. Now, the purpose of hearing litigation is to finalize a criminal case; only when the hearing is thorough will the final verdict be fitting—how then could it fail to be impartial in any instance? The author of the "Royal Regulations" as if to say: The Sage values the absence of litigation; when litigation arises and must be heard, it is already against his heart's wish—how much the less could one fail to be impartial? Therefore, in litigation involving the five punishments, affection and righteous duty are of the greatest moment, whereas gravity, degree of culpability, and legal precedents are not matters that the litigants can clarify for themselves; in the five …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
刑之聽赦與成其要矣而權之而別之而盡之
皆聽者所當致詳也故其始也原親於父子明
有恩也立義於君臣明有分也法常持於一定
用自妙於無方權其容巳乎然輕重無序淺深
無量未可也則論之以意而測之以慎務區別
而不爽者別此權也然論有遺究測有遁情未
可也又聰明是悉而忠愛是致求畢盡而無遺
者盡此權也於此而猶有疑赦可議矣敢任獨
見乎必氾稽於眾而輿論之皆同斯從而赦焉
===
刑無故縱也巳至是而無可疑獄斯成矣敢行
巳意乎必附比於法而小大之咸當斯從而成
焉刑無故入也巳自權以至於察而上無頗刑
由聽以至於成而下鮮濫獄古之公於蔽訟類
若此甞觀易言治獄者五而獨有取於巽與兌
也兌主其議巽主其緩議之以資吾斷緩之以
行吾仁中孚所爲取象蓋居然法銓也司刑者
毋好深文毋幸速成而服膺兌巽之訓幾矣哉
故樂也者動於內者也禮也者動於外者
punctuated:
刑之聽，赦與成其要矣；而權之，而別之，而盡之，皆聽者所當致詳也。故其始也，原親於父子，明有恩也；立義於君臣，明有分也。法常持於一定，用自妙於無方，權其容巳乎？然輕重無序，淺深無量，未可也；則論之以意，而測之以慎，務區別而不爽者，別此權也。然論有遺究，測有遁情，未可也；又聰明是悉，而忠愛是致，求畢盡而無遺者，盡此權也。於此而猶有疑，赦可議矣，敢任獨見乎？必氾稽於眾，而輿論之皆同，斯從而赦焉，刑無故縱也巳。至是而無可疑，獄斯成矣，敢行巳意乎？必附比於法，而小大之咸當，斯從而成焉，刑無故入也巳。自權以至於察，而上無頗刑；由聽以至於成，而下鮮濫獄。古之公於蔽訟，類若此。甞觀《易》言治獄者五，而獨有取於《巽》與《兌》也。《兌》主其議，《巽》主其緩；議之以資吾斷，緩之以行吾仁。《中孚》所爲取象，蓋居然法銓也。司刑者毋好深文，毋幸速成，而服膺《兌》、《巽》之訓，幾矣哉！

「故樂也者，動於內者也；禮也者，動於外者…
translation_en:
…in the hearing of the Five Punishments, pardon and final judgment are what is essential; yet weighing them, distinguishing them, and exhausting them are all matters to which the hearer of litigation must devote careful attention. Therefore, at the outset, one traces affection to father and son, making clear that there is grace; one establishes righteousness between ruler and minister, making clear that there is duty. The law is constantly upheld as something fixed, yet its application is naturally marvelous in having no set formula—how could weighing in the balance be dispensed with? Yet if轻 and heavy have no order, and shallow and deep have no measure, that will not do; thus one deliberates upon them with intent and gauges them with caution, striving to differentiate without error—this is distinguishing what has been weighed. Yet if deliberation leaves points uninvestigated and gauging lets true circumstances escape, that will not do; thus one further exhausts one's discernment and devotes one's loyalty and compassion, seeking to be thoroughly exhaustive without omission—this is exhausting what has been weighed. If at this point there is still doubt, a pardon may be deliberated; yet would one dare rely on a solitary view? One must broadly consult the multitude, and when public opinion is entirely in agreement, only then follow it and pardon the case; thus punishments are never deliberately縱 released. When it reaches the point where there is no longer any doubt, the case is then concluded; yet would one dare act upon one's own private wishes? One must match it by analogy to the law, and when great and small are all fittingly judged, only then follow it and finalize the verdict; thus punishments are never deliberately inflicted. From weighing in the balance to investigating, those above impose no biased punishments; from hearing to finalizing the verdict, those below suffer few unjust imprisonments. The impartiality of the ancients in deciding litigation was generally like this. I have observed that the Book of Changes (Yi) speaks of governing criminal cases in five places, yet particularly draws upon the trigrams Xun and Dui. Dui presides over deliberation, and Xun presides over leniency and delay; deliberating upon cases aids our judgment, and delaying them carries out our benevolence. The images taken for the hexagram Inner Trust (Zhongfu) are indeed a veritable standard of law. If those in charge of punishments do not delight in harsh application of the letter of the law, and do not seek quick closure, but instead take to heart the teachings of Dui and Xun, they will be near the mark indeed!

"Therefore, music is that which stirs within; ritual is that which stirs without…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也樂極和禮極順
王一鳴
考試官教諭湯批禮樂身心本爲一道是作探原
發奥殆造詣之深者
考試官教諭王批渾融精切絕無枝蔓
記者原禮樂所由動而各舉其妙焉夫禮樂以
和順爲本也隨所動而會其極治身心者惡能
去之且禮樂身心一道也夫人恒岐而二之此
功之或間而極未臻耳豈知樂之能治心非心
===
本無樂而以樂治也蓋樂由中出而鐘鼓干戚
特緣物以寄吾心耳故樂非動於聲容者乃未
有聲容之先而此心之和動即樂也動於內者
也禮之能治躬非身本無禮而以禮治也蓋禮
由身體而周旋裼襲特假物以彰吾軌耳故禮
非動於器數者乃未有器數之先而此身之順
動即禮也動於外者也夫樂動於內故宜治心
心苟斯須間焉猶難語和況和之極哉致樂而
至於安久天神是舉其動於內者而渾化之一
punctuated:
也。樂極和，禮極順。
王一鳴
考試官教諭湯批：禮樂身心，本爲一道。是作探原發奥，殆造詣之深者。
考試官教諭王批：渾融精切，絕無枝蔓。
記者原禮樂所由動，而各舉其妙焉。夫禮樂以和順爲本也，隨所動而會其極，治身心者惡能去之？且禮樂身心，一道也。夫人恒岐而二之，此功之或間而極未臻耳。豈知樂之能治心，非心本無樂而以樂治也？蓋樂由中出，而鐘鼓干戚，特緣物以寄吾心耳。故樂非動於聲容者，乃未有聲容之先，而此心之和動即樂也，動於內者也。禮之能治躬，非身本無禮而以禮治也。蓋禮由身體，而周旋裼襲，特假物以彰吾軌耳。故禮非動於器數者，乃未有器數之先，而此身之順動即禮也，動於外者也。夫樂動於內，故宜治心。心苟斯須間焉，猶難語和，況和之極哉？致樂而至於安久天神，是舉其動於內者而渾化之，一
translation_en:
… Music achieves the utmost harmony; ritual achieves the utmost compliance.”

Wang Yiming 王一鳴

Examiner and Instructor Tang 湯 comments: Ritual and music, body and mind, are fundamentally a single Way. This composition probes the source and brings forth profound subtleties; the author is surely one of deep attainment.

Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: Seamlessly integrated and precisely to the point, completely free of extraneous rambling.

The compiler of the Record of Rites traces that from which ritual and music are stirred into motion, and sets forth the subtle perfection of each. Now, ritual and music take harmony and compliance as their root. Following where they are stirred and converging upon their ultimate perfection—how could one who governs body and mind ever dispense with them? Moreover, ritual and music and body and mind are a single Way. People constantly separate them into two; this is why their effort is at times interrupted and the ultimate perfection is not reached. How could they fail to know that music’s ability to govern the mind is not a matter of the mind originally lacking music and then being governed by means of music? For music emerges from within, while bells, drums, shields, and battle-axes merely rely on external objects to lodge our mind. Therefore, music is not stirred into motion in sounds and appearances; rather, prior to the existence of any sounds and appearances, the harmonious stirring of this mind is itself music—it is that which stirs within. Ritual’s ability to govern the person is not a matter of the body originally lacking ritual and then being governed by means of ritual. For ritual is embodied through the person, while circling movements and baring or covering upper garments merely borrow external objects to manifest our deportment.
