Therefore, ritual is not stirred into motion in implements and numbers; rather, prior to the existence of any implements and numbers, the compliant stirring of this body is itself ritual—it is that which stirs without. Now, because music stirs within, it is fitting for governing the mind. If the mind experiences even a moment’s interruption, it is still difficult to speak of harmony, how much more so the utmost limit of harmony! To carry music to the point of serenity, endurance, and heavenly spirituality is to take all that stirs within and completely transform it, so that within a single…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
心之中無動非樂即無動非和也非極和耶禮
動於外故宜治身身苟斯須間焉猶難語順况
順之極哉致禮而至於莊敬威嚴是舉其動於
外者而嘉會之一身之中無動非禮即無動非
順也非極順耶吁此感人動物之基也抑樂在
心而求之秬黍禮在身而求之綿蕞迹耳舍迹
而求其眞則身心一動和順自充由是官天地
育萬物皆此之推耳故君子反觀於寂然不動
之天而禮樂固森然具也所謂斯須不可去者
===
存吾眞也
第貳場
論
天子以好生爲德
瞿甲
同考試官訓導趙批好生二字乃人君聯屬人心培
植國脉之本是篇以剴切之意命雋偉之詞是雅抱忠悃者
同考試官教諭尹批學識淵深文藻典雅
考試官教諭湯批發好生意明盡
punctuated:
心之中，無動非樂，即無動非和也，非極和耶？禮動於外，故宜治身。身苟斯須間焉，猶難語順，况順之極哉？致禮而至於莊敬威嚴，是舉其動於外者而嘉會之一身之中，無動非禮，即無動非順也，非極順耶？吁！此感人動物之基也。抑樂在心而求之秬黍，禮在身而求之綿蕞，迹耳。舍迹而求其眞，則身心一動，和順自充；由是官天地、育萬物，皆此之推耳。故君子反觀於寂然不動之天，而禮樂固森然具也。所謂斯須不可去者，存吾眞也。

第貳場
論
天子以好生爲德
瞿甲
同考試官訓導趙批：好生二字，乃人君聯屬人心、培植國脉之本。是篇以剴切之意，命雋偉之詞，是雅抱忠悃者。
同考試官教諭尹批：學識淵深，文藻典雅。
考試官教諭湯批：發好生意明盡。
translation_en:
… the mind, there is no movement that is not music, which means there is no movement that is not harmony—is this not the ultimate harmony? Ritual moves on the outside, and therefore it is fitting for regulating the person. If the person is interrupted from it even for a moment, it is difficult to speak of compliance, much less the ultimate compliance! When one carries ritual to the point of grave reverence and solemn dignity, one takes what moves on the outside and brings it into auspicious convergence within a single person: there is no movement that is not ritual, which means there is no movement that is not compliance—is this not the ultimate compliance? Ah! This is the foundation for moving people and stirring things. Yet when music resides in the mind and one seeks it in black millet pitch-standards, or when ritual resides in the person and one seeks it in roped-off ceremonial markers, those are merely outward traces. If one sets aside the traces and seeks their true reality, then at every movement of person and mind, harmony and compliance will naturally fill them; from this, presiding over Heaven and Earth and nurturing the myriad things are all simply extensions of this. Therefore, the gentleman turns his contemplation inward to the Heaven that is still and unmoving, where ritual and music are indeed already arrayed in full. What is meant by saying that they may not be left even for a moment is preserving our true reality.

Second Session
Discourse
"The Son of Heaven Takes the Love of Life as His Virtue"
Qu Jia
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao comments: The words "love of life" are the foundation by which a ruler binds together human hearts and cultivates the vital arteries of the state. This essay conveys incisive and earnest meaning through striking and lofty diction; its author is one who has long cherished loyal sincerity.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yin comments: His learning and insight are profound, and his literary style is refined and elegant.
Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: He brings out the meaning of the love of life with complete clarity.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭王批深得先王制刑本意
人主宰世以代天也必求全其天之所生而後
可夫民之生也天生之天能生民而不能使之
全其生乃舉而屬之人主以治之故四海八埏
奉曰天子天子一心仁庇億兆爲生生之本則
曰天君然而師心爲治終難以諧無厭之欲一
喜爭之志於是倚智而甞姦緣巧而構釁者業
纍纍起殆非所以齊衆濟治也不得已而設之
曰天刑而後世藉之以播其酷烈屠其生齒則
===
恣睢之法勝而矜全之意微矣聖人伏而思之
天下何尊何親也檢於刑故人相尊麗於仁故
人相親而奈何以區區督責之術收威於衆乎
是故解苛密之網流愷悌之聲弘欽恤之指副
樹牧之任而天下始鮮有伐生者嗚呼以好生
爲德斯可以爲天子矣甞遡觀皇王之時其動
也習其服也士刻畫衣冠而天下化君子有禮
樂之容野人脩曾史之行結繩亦治象刑亦治
punctuated:
考試官敎諭王批：深得先王制刑本意。

人主宰世以代天也，必求全其天之所生而後可。夫民之生也，天生之；天能生民，而不能使之全其生，乃舉而屬之人主以治之，故四海八埏奉曰「天子」。天子一心仁庇億兆，爲生生之本，則曰「天君」。然而師心爲治，終難以諧無厭之欲，一喜爭之志。於是倚智而甞姦、緣巧而構釁者，業纍纍起，殆非所以齊衆濟治也。不得已而設之，曰「天刑」。而後世藉之以播其酷烈，屠其生齒，則恣睢之法勝，而矜全之意微矣。聖人伏而思之，天下何尊何親也？檢於刑，故人相尊；麗於仁，故人相親。而奈何以區區督責之術，收威於衆乎？是故解苛密之網，流愷悌之聲，弘欽恤之指，副樹牧之任，而天下始鮮有伐生者。嗚呼！以好生爲德，斯可以爲天子矣。甞遡觀皇王之時，其動也習，其服也士，刻畫衣冠而天下化；君子有禮樂之容，野人脩曾、史之行，結繩亦治，象刑亦治，
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Wang's comment: Deeply grasps the fundamental intent of the former kings in instituting punishments.

A ruler governs the world on behalf of Heaven; he must seek to preserve whole all that Heaven has brought into life, and only then will he succeed. Now as for the life of the people, Heaven gives birth to them; Heaven is able to give birth to the people, yet cannot cause them to preserve their lives whole, and so it takes them up and entrusts them to the ruler of men to govern them. Therefore, within the four seas and to the eight utmost reaches, he is revered as the "Son of Heaven." When the Son of Heaven with single mind benevolently shelters the hundreds of millions, serving as the root of continuous generation and life, he is called the "Heavenly Sovereign." Even so, if he relies merely on his own heart to govern, in the end it is difficult to harmonize insatiable desires or unify minds that delight in strife. Thus, those who rely on cunning to test out wickedness and seizing upon artifice to stir up quarrels already arise one after another—which is hardly the way to bring order to the multitude and accomplish good governance. Having no alternative, he establishes punishments, calling them "Heaven's punishments." Yet later ages used them as a pretext to spread their cruelty and ferocity and to slaughter the living population, so that arbitrary and ruthless laws prevailed while the intent to pity and preserve grew faint. The sage bows his head and reflects upon this: Why does the world revere and why does it feel affection? Restrained by punishments, people revere one another; attached to benevolence, people feel affection for one another. Why then resort to petty arts of surveillance and reproach in order to gather awe over the multitude? Therefore, he loosens the harsh and closely woven net, spreads the sound of joyful kindness, broadens the principle of reverent compassion, and fulfills the duty of establishing pastors for the people—and only then are there few in the world who cut short their own lives. Alas! To take the love of life as one's virtue—by this indeed can one be the Son of Heaven. I have looked back upon the times of the august sovereigns and true kings: in their movements the people were compliant, and in their submission they acted like gentlemen [?]; merely by delineating symbolic patterns on robes and caps, the whole world was transformed. Gentlemen possessed the demeanor of ritual and music, while rustic folk cultivated the conduct of Zeng Shen 曾參 and Shi Yu 史魚; governance was achieved with knotted cords, and governance was achieved with symbolic punishments, …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國章也非以讎匹夫濟虓怒也中孚之象澤上
有風君子以議獄緩死夫水體虛故風能入之
心體虛故物能感之感於中而仁生焉是議獄
緩死之心非即好生之心哉心存而德不蝓矣
世主不曉競於煩苛之令搖於鋟薄之風囹圄
如市桎梏若林而有司奉上意指復深文巧詆
以塗民耳目而不知繁策急轡終不可語造父
之御也嚴刑促令終不可語三王之道也德何
以稱哉夫民之爭非其好也其所由來漸矣激
===
之則淫敦之則一激之也者動其爭機敦之也
者篤其古初則王者齊民豈堇堇在法制哉視
其所以激之敦之者耳故夏之肉辟殷之虔劉
鄭之刑書晉之執秩趙之國律楚之僕區法銓
愈備姦偽滋萌庸非任刑之過與任刑而至於
過皆人主欣嗜誅夷而無復以生為好故其下
麕附而景從也天生民而屬之人主欲生之耶
欲刑之耶人主不得已而用刑欲生之耶欲死
之耶夫介鯁之士以彊直加木羸窶之徒以單
punctuated: 國章也，非以讎匹夫、濟虓怒也。《中孚》之象，澤上有風，君子以議獄緩死。夫水體虛，故風能入之；心體虛，故物能感之。感於中而仁生焉，是議獄緩死之心，非即好生之心哉？心存而德不蝓矣。世主不曉，競於煩苛之令，搖於鋟薄之風，囹圄如市，桎梏若林。而有司奉上意指，復深文巧詆，以塗民耳目。而不知繁策急轡，終不可語造父之御也；嚴刑促令，終不可語三王之道也。德何以稱哉？夫民之爭，非其好也，其所由來漸矣。激之則淫，敦之則一。激之也者，動其爭機；敦之也者，篤其古初。則王者齊民，豈堇堇在法制哉？視其所以激之、敦之者耳。故夏之肉辟、殷之虔劉、鄭之《刑書》、晉之執秩、趙之《國律》、楚之僕區，法銓愈備，姦偽滋萌，庸非任刑之過與？任刑而至於過，皆人主欣嗜誅夷，而無復以生為好，故其下麕附而景從也。天生民而屬之人主，欲生之耶？欲刑之耶？人主不得已而用刑，欲生之耶？欲死之耶？夫介鯁之士以彊直加木，羸窶之徒以單
translation_en:
… are the statutes of the state, not means to take vengeance upon common men or to satisfy a roaring rage. In the Image of the hexagram Zhongfu (Inner Trust), "Wind is over the marsh; thus the superior man deliberates over legal cases and delays executions." Now, the substance of water is receptive, so wind can enter it; the substance of the mind is receptive, so things can move it. When moved within, benevolence is born therefrom. Is not this mind that deliberates over legal cases and delays executions precisely the mind that loves life? When this mind is preserved, virtue does not decay.

Rulers of the age do not understand this. They vie in issuing烦瑣 and harsh ordinances and are swayed by刻薄 (cutting and ungenerous) customs, until prisons are like marketplaces and fetters and stocks stand like forests. Meanwhile, the authorities follow the intentions and directives of their superiors, further applying severe interpretations of the law and artful slanders to blind the eyes and ears of the people. Yet they do not realize that with incessant whipping and tight reins, one can never speak of the charioteering of Zaofu; with severe punishments and urgent decrees, one can never speak of the Way of the Three Kings. How then can virtue be praised?

Now, contention among the people is not what they naturally delight in; its origins develop gradually. If you provoke them, they become licentious; if you cultivate them with generosity, they become unified. To provoke them is to stir up their impulses for contention; to cultivate them is to make them cleave to their ancient, pristine nature. In bringing order to the people, how could a true king rely merely on laws and regulations? It depends solely on that by which he provokes or cultivates them. Therefore, with the corporal punishments of the Xia, the severe slaughters of the Yin, the Book of Punishments (Xingshu) of Zheng, the office of the Administrator of Ranks (Zhi zhi) of Jin, the State Statutes (Guolü) of Zhao, and the Law of Concealment (Puqu) of Chu—as legal scales became ever more exhaustive, treachery and deceit sprouted all the more. Was this not the fault of relying on punishment? That relying on punishment reaches the point of excess is always because the ruler delights in execution and extermination and no longer holds life dear; therefore, his subordinates flock to him like deer and follow him like shadows.

When Heaven gives birth to the people and entrusts them to a ruler, does it wish them to live, or does it wish them to be punished? When a ruler has no choice but to use punishment, does he wish them to live, or does he wish them to die? Now, upright and outspoken gentlemen are placed in wooden cangues because of their unbending rectitude; weak and impoverished folk, because of their solitary…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
力寡控悃愿之眾以訥辨橫誣少年之子以孱
弱伏辜畜憤之夫以激昂賈罪膏梁之俊以遊
冶蒙辱豈其皆敢於弄法習於爲姦者而一切
寘之不原之典委命下吏情斷意訖目囑廷尉
愕若鬼魑身受黥掠痛甚湯火血流兩觀之下
聲徹九閽之關嗟嗟是亦重可哀矣哀之則必
有以生之矣先王之令烏無覆巢蟲無殺孩骼
則掩之胔則埋之乃至刑刈百姓竟若草菅則
視胞與賤於羽毛而戴髮含齒之倫不如一道
===
路朽枯之白骨德何衰也故仲尼譏鑄鼎端木
惡猛法要以明人主之所好在此不在彼耳夫
生者萬民系命之原也書稱其德好生易稱觀
我生觀民謂天子而可不好生哉是以古昔聽
民具以兩造詳以三刺孚以五辭俟以歷旬如
此乎矜其生也原以三宥寬以八議參以眾疑
設以二石贖以千鍰如此乎求其生也獄既成
爲之覆奏爲之籲天爲之垂泣爲之不舉樂不
視朝者凡三日如此乎重其生也故世有鉗灼
punctuated: 力寡控，悃愿之眾以訥辨橫誣，少年之子以孱弱伏辜，畜憤之夫以激昂賈罪，膏梁之俊以遊冶蒙辱。豈其皆敢於弄法、習於爲姦者？而一切寘之不原之典，委命下吏。情斷意訖，目囑廷尉，愕若鬼魑；身受黥掠，痛甚湯火。血流兩觀之下，聲徹九閽之關。嗟嗟！是亦重可哀矣！哀之則必有以生之矣。先王之令，烏無覆巢，蟲無殺孩，骼則掩之，胔則埋之。乃至刑刈百姓，竟若草菅，則視胞與賤於羽毛，而戴髮含齒之倫，不如一道路朽枯之白骨，德何衰也！故仲尼譏鑄鼎，端木惡猛法，要以明人主之所好在此不在彼耳。夫生者，萬民系命之原也。《書》稱「其德好生」，《易》稱「觀我生，觀民」，謂天子而可不好生哉！是以古昔聽民，具以兩造，詳以三刺，孚以五辭，俟以歷旬，如此乎矜其生也；原以三宥，寬以八議，參以眾疑，設以二石，贖以千鍰，如此乎求其生也。獄既成，爲之覆奏，爲之籲天，爲之垂泣，爲之不舉樂、不視朝者凡三日，如此乎重其生也。故世有鉗灼
translation_en: …strength have few means of appeal; the sincere and honest multitude, because of their halting speech, are wantonly slandered; young lads, because of their frailty and weakness, admit to guilt; men harboring indignation, because of their impassioned outbursts, incur blame; and the fine scions of wealthy families, because of their roaming and carousing, suffer disgrace. Could it be that all of them dare to toy with the law and are habituated to committing wickedness? Yet all alike are subjected to unforgiving statutes, their lives entrusted to low-ranking functionaries. With hope cut off and spirit exhausted, when their eyes gaze upon the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, they are terrified as though facing ghosts and goblins; when their bodies undergo tattooing and flogging, the pain is worse than boiling water or fire. Blood flows beneath the Twin Watchtowers, and cries pierce the gates of the ninefold palace. Alas! This is deeply to be pitied indeed! And if one pities them, one must surely find a way to keep them alive. According to the ordinances of the former kings, birds' nests were not to be overturned, larval insects were not to be killed, dry bones were to be covered, and decaying flesh was to be buried. When it comes instead to executing and mowing down the common people as though they were mere grass and reeds, then one regards one's fellow beings as cheaper than feathers and fur, and human beings—who wear hair and have teeth—as worth less than the rotting white bones along the roadside. How declined virtue has become! Therefore Confucius (Zhongni 仲尼) criticized the casting of the tripods [inscribed with penal laws], and Zigong (Duanmu 端木) abhorred harsh laws; the essential point was to make clear that what the ruler of men cherishes lies here [in life] and not there [in punishment]. Now life is the source upon which the destinies of the myriad people depend. The Book of Documents (Shu) praises "his virtue of loving life," and the Book of Changes (Yi) speaks of "contemplating my own life" and "contemplating the people." How could one be the Son of Heaven and not love life! Therefore in antiquity, when hearing the cases of the people, they required the presence of both parties, deliberated carefully through the three inquiries, verified the truth through the five modes of examining statements, and waited over the course of ten days—so greatly did they commiserate with their lives! They pardoned them through the three grounds for leniency, showed clemency through the eight deliberations, consulted the doubts of the multitude, set up the two boundary stones [to reform the errant], and allowed redemption by a thousand huan of bronze—so earnestly did they seek to preserve their lives! And when a criminal case was concluded, on their behalf they submitted repeated memorials, cried out to Heaven, shed tears, and refrained from playing music or holding court for a full three days—so deeply did they value their lives! Thus, when the world had a fondness for iron collars and branding…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之好而天子則曰寧覩法以毋殘其生世有窮
竟之好而天子則曰寧解嬈以毋傾其生世有
傅致之好而天子則曰寧文無害以毋傷其生
世有攓摭深故之好而天子則曰寧開改惡之
路以毋錮其生夫聖人所爲鰓鰓愍惻而不忍
言刑者好生故也攷之天官曰天西方句圜十
五星曰貫索曰天獄獄口星曰闢以示開也獄
事煩多則衆星畢見明王恥之此可以觀天心
矣夫天道先燠而後寒先舒而後慘其所好不
===
旣彰彰著耶人君心天之心則亦好天之好故
草纓艾韠稱爲上業不得已而罹於議則猶誨
之以忠聳之以行教之以務使之以和又不得
已而干於法則又求明察之官忠信之長慈惠
之師以明聽之豈其好爲姑息以博敦大之名
哉天心好生人君爲天之子亦好其天之所生
者巳耳嗚呼纍臣繫而夏隕霜令史殲而血逆
流天人感應之理若此況於逞燔灼之毒震轘
punctuated: 之好，而天子則曰：寧覩法以毋殘其生；世有窮竟之好，而天子則曰：寧解嬈以毋傾其生；世有傅致之好，而天子則曰：寧文無害以毋傷其生；世有攓摭深故之好，而天子則曰：寧開改惡之路以毋錮其生。夫聖人所爲鰓鰓愍惻而不忍言刑者，好生故也。攷之《天官》，曰天西方句圜十五星，曰貫索，曰天獄；獄口星曰闢，以示開也。獄事煩多，則衆星畢見，明王恥之，此可以觀天心矣。夫天道先燠而後寒，先舒而後慘，其所好不旣彰彰著耶？人君心天之心，則亦好天之好。故草纓艾韠，稱爲上業；不得已而罹於議，則猶誨之以忠，聳之以行，教之以務，使之以和；又不得已而干於法，則又求明察之官、忠信之長、慈惠之師以明聽之。豈其好爲姑息，以博敦大之名哉？天心好生，人君爲天之子，亦好其天之所生者巳耳。嗚呼！纍臣繫而夏隕霜，令史殲而血逆流，天人感應之理若此，況於逞燔灼之毒，震轘…
translation_en:
…of collar-irons and branding, the Son of Heaven says: "Better to observe the law fairly so as not to mutilate their lives." Though the world may have a fondness for pursuing cases to the bitter end, the Son of Heaven says: "Better to untangle petty vexations so as not to ruin their lives." Though the world may have a fondness for fabricating charges, the Son of Heaven says: "Better that legal statutes cause no harm, so as not to injure their lives." Though the world may have a fondness for seizing upon faults and harshly imputing deliberate guilt, the Son of Heaven says: "Better to open a path for reforming evil so as not to cut off their lives forever." Indeed, the reason the sages were so anxiously compassionate and could not bear to speak of punishments was because they loved life.

Examining the "Treatise on Celestial Officials" (Tianguan), it says that in the western sky there is a hooked circle of fifteen stars called the Coiled Thong (Guansuo), also called the Celestial Prison (Tianyu); the star at the mouth of the prison is called "Opening" (Pi), to signify that it should be kept open. When prison cases are numerous and burdensome, all the stars become fully visible, which enlightened kings regard as a disgrace; from this one may observe the mind of Heaven. Now, the Way of Heaven brings warmth first and cold afterward, gentle expansion first and grim severity afterward—is not what it loves already abundantly clear? The ruler of men takes the mind of Heaven as his own mind, and thus also loves what Heaven loves. Therefore, symbolic punishments like grass hat-strings and mugwort-dyed knee-covers were praised as the highest enterprise of antiquity. When, unavoidably, people fell under deliberation for offenses, rulers still instructed them in loyalty, roused them to good conduct, taught them their duties, and employed them with harmony. And when, again unavoidably, people violated the law, rulers sought out clear-sighted and discerning officials, loyal and trustworthy elders, and compassionate and benevolent teachers to hear the cases with clarity. Was this because they liked to practice lax indulgence in order to win a reputation for generous magnanimity? The mind of Heaven loves life, and the ruler of men, being the Son of Heaven, simply loves those whom Heaven has brought into life.

Alas! When a bound subject was imprisoned, frost fell in summer; when a Magisterial Scribe (lingshi) was executed, his blood flowed backward. If the principle of resonance between Heaven and man is like this, how much more so when unleashing the venom of burning and branding, shaking with the terror of tearing apart by chariots…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
陷必死之穽雖國士有不勝其酷而自誣者此
則苛密擬於吹毛操切等於束濕圜扉夜哭棘
林晝嘯戾氣蒸而不散陰霾鬱而不解三光震
動二曜薄蝕其所關豈細故哉虞舜著典眚災
肆赦禹巡會稽遇罪流泣姬公作戒勿誤庶獄
伯夷折民惟刑惟敬武丁明罰不敢怠遑之數
君者皆審慎遲留而不敢專决乃其中固自有
所好耳當時之政穆於春風暄於冬日五刑式
序萬品畢設厥德顧不懋哉若晚近世墨劓剕
===
宮之制鑿頂文額拆脅之條一切不係咎繇所
設呂侯所記則皆所以殃君德而干天和者也
胡可好也是故夏以刑顛秦以慘裂非殃及一
身則孽流數世其理彰灼而不爽而况人主撫
齊萬方一歲中擊斷無數少逞雷霆之威重以
摧折之勢則其隕越生人取讎造物者何可勝
計此削木畫地之議所以諄復於綜核之朝也
戒之哉雖然刑之立也所以生人故郭璞氏謂
重之以死者正所以求其生而罰輕則民易犯
punctuated: 陷必死之穽，雖國士有不勝其酷而自誣者。此則苛密擬於吹毛，操切等於束濕；圜扉夜哭，棘林晝嘯，戾氣蒸而不散，陰霾鬱而不解，三光震動，二曜薄蝕，其所關豈細故哉！虞舜著典，眚災肆赦；禹巡會稽，遇罪流泣；姬公作戒，勿誤庶獄；伯夷折民，惟刑惟敬；武丁明罰，不敢怠遑。之數君者，皆審慎遲留而不敢專决，乃其中固自有所好耳。當時之政，穆於春風，暄於冬日，五刑式序，萬品畢設，厥德顧不懋哉！若晚近世墨、劓、剕、宮之制，鑿頂、文額、拆脅之條，一切不係咎繇所設、呂侯所記，則皆所以殃君德而干天和者也，胡可好也！是故夏以刑顛，秦以慘裂，非殃及一身，則孽流數世，其理彰灼而不爽。而况人主撫齊萬方，一歲中擊斷無數，少逞雷霆之威，重以摧折之勢，則其隕越生人、取讎造物者，何可勝計！此削木畫地之議，所以諄復於綜核之朝也，戒之哉！雖然，刑之立也，所以生人。故郭璞氏謂重之以死者，正所以求其生，而罰輕則民易犯，
translation_en: …plunge them into pitfalls of certain death, so that even men of national distinction, unable to bear the cruelty, falsely confess against themselves. In such cases, harsh exactitude is like blowing aside hairs to seek a blemish, and urgent coercion is like tying up wet firewood; there is weeping at night in the round-door prisons, and wailing by day in the jujube-thorn courts. Perverse vapors steam upward without dispersing, gloomy haze gathers thick without clearing, the Three Luminaries are shaken, and the sun and moon suffer eclipses—how could what is at stake be a trifling matter! Shun of Yu set forth in his canon that inadvertent offenses and those caused by misfortune should be pardoned outright; Yu, on his tour of inspection to Kuaiji, wept upon encountering a criminal; the Duke of Zhou composed his admonition not to err in the multitude of judicial cases; Boyi, in restraining the people, relied on punishments with reverence alone; and Wuding, in making clear his penalties, dared not be indolent orremiss. All of these several rulers were circumspect and deliberate, not daring to decide arbitrarily, because within their hearts they naturally had that which they cherished. The governance of those times was gentler than the spring breeze and warmer than the winter sun; the Five Punishments were properly ordered, the myriad things were all duly arranged—was their virtue not grand indeed! As for more recent ages, the systems of tattooing, nose-cutting, foot-amputation, and castration, and the statutes for boring the crown of the head, branding the forehead, and breaking the ribs—none of which belong to what Gao Yao established or what the Marquis of Lü recorded—are all things that bring calamity upon the ruler's virtue and violate the harmony of Heaven; how could one delight in them! Therefore, the Xia dynasty toppled through its punishments, and the Qin dynasty was torn apart through its brutality; if calamity did not befall their own persons, the evil consequences flowed down for several generations—this principle is brilliantly clear and unfailing. How much more so when the sovereign governs and orders the myriad regions, and within a single year strikes down and decides countless cases! If he slightly indulges the majesty of thunderbolts and compounds it with the force of crushing and breaking, then the number of those who destroy living men and incur the enmity of the Creator will be beyond reckoning! This is why the plea regarding carved wood and lines drawn on the ground [representing jailers and prisons] was earnestly repeated during an administration devoted to strict verification. Let one beware of this! Even so, the establishment of punishments is meant to preserve human life. Thus Guo Pu said that making punishments heavy even unto death is precisely the way to seek that people live, whereas if penalties are light, the people easily transgress…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
在昔議之五服五流誰能去刑則彼所稱好生
云者無乃非齊法之大准哉蓋君人權斷主者
守文權斷則恩歸於主上守文則法立於有司
二者固自不偏廢也故削秋荼之令解凝脂之
網而後能爲君蔽淮南之獄執郭解之斷而後
能爲臣君養其德臣守其職而民稱平矣善乎
龜山氏之言曰天子以好生爲德有司以執法
爲公嗚呼盡之矣
表
===
擬輔臣應
制恭詠玄兔圖詩
進呈表
陳良心
同考試官教諭趙 批 對揚之辭類多勦襲此作事核
詞麗懇懇忠愛之心溢于言表得士如此可爲
國家慶矣
同考試官教諭顧 批 聲澡竝隆雅正不乏而遣詞使
事粹有體度可以式矣
punctuated:
在昔議之，五服五流，誰能去刑？則彼所稱好生云者，無乃非齊法之大准哉！蓋君人權斷，主者守文；權斷則恩歸於主上，守文則法立於有司，二者固自不偏廢也。故削秋荼之令，解凝脂之網，而後能爲君；蔽淮南之獄，執郭解之斷，而後能爲臣。君養其德，臣守其職，而民稱平矣。善乎龜山氏之言曰：「天子以好生爲德，有司以執法爲公。」嗚呼，盡之矣！

表
擬輔臣應制恭詠《玄兔圖》詩進呈表
陳良心
同考試官教諭趙批：對揚之辭，類多勦襲，此作事核詞麗，懇懇忠愛之心溢于言表。得士如此，可爲國家慶矣。
同考試官教諭顧批：聲澡竝隆，雅正不乏，而遣詞使事，粹有體度，可以式矣。
translation_en:
… has been discussed since antiquity. With the Five Punishments and the Five Banishments, who can dispense with penalties altogether? Does it not follow that what is called "loving life" is after all not the overarching standard for regulating the law? Indeed, the ruler of men exercises discretionary judgment, while the responsible officials uphold the letter of the law. Through discretionary judgment, grace is attributed to the sovereign above; by upholding the letter of the law, the law is established by the authorities below. Neither of the two can be neglected in favor of the other. Therefore, only by paring away ordinances as dense as autumn weeds and loosening nets as thick as congealed fat can one act as a true ruler; only by adjudicating the case of the King of Huainan and holding fast to the judgment against Guo Xie can one act as a true minister. When the ruler cultivates his virtue and the ministers guard their duties, the people will acclaim the fairness of the realm. How well put are the words of Master Guishan (Yang Shi 楊時): "The Son of Heaven takes loving life as his virtue; the authorities take enforcing the law as their impartiality." Alas, that sums it up completely!

Memorial
A Draft Memorial by Grand Secretaries Presenting Poems Respectfully Composed at Imperial Command on the "Painting of a Black Rabbit"
By Chen Liangxin 陳良心
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhao: Words composed in response to the sovereign mostly tend toward plagiarism and cliché, yet this piece employs accurate allusions and elegant diction, with a sincere heart of loyalty and affection overflowing between the lines. Obtaining a scholar such as this is a cause for celebration for the dynasty!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Gu: Its cadence and literary ornament [reading 藻 for 澡] are both lofty, without lacking in refined correctness; its choice of words and use of allusions are pure and possess proper decorum. It can serve as a model!

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭楊批荘重典則四六之佳者
考試官教諭湯批典雅駢儷宜錄以式
考試官教諭王批藻麗中有典則錄之
萬曆九年某月某日具官臣某等謹以所
撰應
制玄兔圖詩上
進者伏以
聖囿呈祥繪景爰留乎
宸鑒
===
天綃煥采摛辭共鬯乎
皇情蓋質秉玉衡歷千齡而始就而色分玄圃
應
萬壽以無疆覩茲舞獸之遺容披圖若見慚爾
雕蟲之末技表瑞難工臣等誠惶誠恐稽
首頓首竊惟治內治外國家以一統為弘
規來享來王夷夏以同文為盛世故寄象
鞮譯獻琛不却於湯廷鱗革羽毛圖貌兼
收於禹鼎獒來西旅雉進越裳旣顯異而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭楊批：「荘重典則，四六之佳者。」
考試官教諭湯批：「典雅駢儷，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭王批：「藻麗中有典則，錄之。」

萬曆九年某月某日，具官臣某等，謹以所撰應制《玄兔圖》詩上進者。伏以聖囿呈祥，繪景爰留乎宸鑒；天綃煥采，摛辭共鬯乎皇情。蓋質秉玉衡，歷千齡而始就；而色分玄圃，應萬壽以無疆。覩茲舞獸之遺容，披圖若見；慚爾雕蟲之末技，表瑞難工。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟治內治外，國家以一統為弘規；來享來王，夷夏以同文為盛世。故寄象鞮譯，獻琛不却於湯廷；鱗革羽毛，圖貌兼收於禹鼎。獒來西旅，雉進越裳，旣顯異而…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yang's comment: "Dignified and adhering to classical standards; a fine example of four-six parallel prose."
Examiner and Instructor Tang's comment: "Classically elegant and well-balanced in parallel couplets; it should be recorded as a model."
Examiner and Instructor Wang's comment: "Amidst its ornate beauty there is adherence to classical standards; record it."

On a certain day of a certain month in the ninth year of the Wanli reign (1581), your servants with full official titles, So-and-so and others, respectfully present the poems composed at Imperial command on the Painting of the Black Rabbit. We humbly reflect that as the Sacred Park manifests auspicious signs, the painted scene is accordingly retained for the Imperial gaze; as the heavenly silk glows with splendor, our spread-out phrases together give expression to the August sentiments. For its substance is endowed by the Jade Transverse of the Northern Dipper, taking a thousand years to come into being; and its color is shared from the Mystic Garden of Kunlun, responding to Your Boundless Longevity without end. Beholding the lingering likeness of this dancing beast, upon unrolling the painting it is as if seeing it before us; yet we are ashamed of our petty skill in "carving insects," finding it hard to skillfully set forth such an auspicious omen. Your servants, in utmost fear and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground again and again. We humbly consider that in governing the interior and governing the exterior, the state takes grand unification as its vast plan; in coming to present offerings and coming to acknowledge kingly sway, foreign peoples and Chinese alike take shared culture as the mark of a flourishing age. Therefore, through interpreters of the four quarters—the Ji, Xiang, Di, and Yi—proffered treasures were not rejected at the court of Tang; and creatures of scales, hides, feathers, and fur had their pictured forms comprehensively gathered onto the tripods of Yu. When the mastiff came from the Western Lü and the pheasant was presented by Yuechang, having both manifested extraordinary wonders and…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
效靈率登歌而獻奏覩赤驃以作頌岑參
之讚詠猶存感玄猿以吮豪吳筠之締飾
可翫乃若星精月彩益為地寶天符俯封
夘而毓形仰瑤華以孕質歷稽往牒罕覿
竒章白者僅著嘉名赤焉已為上應然未
有毳染緇林之色體分漆澤之光若此者
也惟
祖功
宗德柔懷誕格於遐夷而航海梯山賓貢充盈
===
於
禁苑蟾蜍玉魄無煩罝罘而自來霄漢玄絻
不待筌蹄而畢至在永樂甲申之歲受筐
篚於北陲暨宣德巳酉之年報
璽書於邊將付圉人愼加馴養宣畫史式繪英
標緇涅無加掃就若玄珠在掌鉛華弗著
瞻來如蒼璧盈眸兩勤侍從之歌章夙表
泰階之禎應聲詩巳光於往冊
繼述復慶於
punctuated: 效靈，率登歌而獻奏。覩赤驃以作頌，岑參之讚詠猶存；感玄猿以吮豪，吳筠之締飾可翫。乃若星精月彩，益為地寶天符，俯封夘而毓形，仰瑤華以孕質。歷稽往牒，罕覿竒章；白者僅著嘉名，赤焉已為上應。然未有毳染緇林之色，體分漆澤之光，若此者也。惟祖功宗德，柔懷誕格於遐夷；而航海梯山，賓貢充盈於禁苑。蟾蜍玉魄，無煩罝罘而自來；霄漢玄絻，不待筌蹄而畢至。在永樂甲申之歲，受筐篚於北陲；暨宣德巳酉之年，報璽書於邊將。付圉人愼加馴養，宣畫史式繪英標。緇涅無加，掃就若玄珠在掌；鉛華弗著，瞻來如蒼璧盈眸。兩勤侍從之歌章，夙表泰階之禎應。聲詩巳光於往冊，繼述復慶於
translation_en:
… display their numinous efficacy, all are celebrated in songs and presented in memorials. Upon beholding the red steed to compose a hymn, the encomium of Cen Shen 岑參 still survives; moved by the black gibbon to moisten the brush-tip, the ornate composition of Wu Yun 吳筠 can still be savored. As for that which embodies the essence of the stars and the luster of the moon, it is all the more an earthly treasure and a heavenly tally—bowing over the realm of Mao [the hare] to nurture its form, and looking up to the jade-flower stars to conceive its substance. Examining the records of the past, one rarely beholds such marvelous distinction: the white ones merely registered an auspicious name, while the red ones were already deemed a supreme response. Yet never has there been one whose down is dyed the hue of a dark forest and whose body shares the gleam of glossy lacquer such as this!

Only because the merits of the Grand Progenitor and the virtue of the Ancestors gently cherished and grandly reached the distant barbarians did guests bearing tribute cross the seas and scale the mountains, filling the Imperial Parks to overflowing. The jade-white spirit of the moon-toad came of its own accord without the trouble of rabbit-nets; the black-robed creature of the empyrean arrived in full without awaiting traps or snares. In the jiashen year of the Yongle 永樂 reign (1404), baskets of tribute were received from the northern frontier; and in the jiyou year of the Xuande 宣德 reign (1429), an imperial letter was dispatched in response to the frontier generals. They were entrusted to the grooms to be carefully tamed and reared, and court painters were summoned to depict their noble bearing. Without adding black dye, when brushed onto silk it was like a dark pearl held in the palm; with no lead powder applied, when gazed upon it was like a deep-hued jade disk filling the eye. Twice they inspired the poetic compositions of the imperial attendants, early on manifesting the auspicious response of the Grand Staircase stars. Those verses and poems have already shed luster upon past annals, and the continuation and transmission of this legacy is once again celebrated on…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
令辰恭惟
皇帝陛下
功叅五德
道際九玄
心含四始之奇葩
政列三驅之疎網
神營閱武近知沙漠來威
王會成編遠羨丹青馳譽求賢無類登庸取
駿於中林繩
===
祖有懷清燕探奇於
內府毛蟲獻狀清暉長護以玄雲冰縠傳神
黝質疑來於北極明視炯然而日映僊儀
颯矣其風旋擘春練以規摹爰爰故態織
秋煙而點綴趯趯馴姿霜杵澄鮮彷彿瑶
臺傳碧墨花摇動分明玉宇飛毫輕縑拂
而喜動
天顏華軸展而光昭
帝業卷藏惟舊宜卜世以卜年
punctuated: 令辰。恭惟皇帝陛下，功叅五德，道際九玄。心含四始之奇葩，政列三驅之疎網。神營閱武，近知沙漠來威；王會成編，遠羨丹青馳譽。求賢無類，登庸取駿於中林；繩祖有懷，清燕探奇於內府。毛蟲獻狀，清暉長護以玄雲；冰縠傳神，黝質疑來於北極。明視炯然而日映，僊儀颯矣其風旋。擘春練以規摹，爰爰故態；織秋煙而點綴，趯趯馴姿。霜杵澄鮮，彷彿瑶臺傳碧；墨花摇動，分明玉宇飛毫。輕縑拂而喜動天顏，華軸展而光昭帝業。卷藏惟舊，宜卜世以卜年；
translation_en: …this auspicious occasion. We reverently reflect that Your Imperial Majesty's merit participates in the Five Virtues, and Your Way reaches to the Nine Heavens. Your mind encompasses the wondrous blossoms of the Four Beginnings of the Odes, and Your governance arrays the wide-meshed nets of the three-sided royal hunt. Reviewing troops at the Sacred Camp, we recently see the desert regions submitting to Your awe; compiling the record of the Royal Audience, distant lands admire Your renown spreading through painted portraits. In seeking worthies without discrimination, You promote and employ fine steeds taken from the deep forest; mindful of carrying on the work of Your Imperial Ancestors, in moments of serene leisure You explore the rarities in the Inner Treasury. The furry creature presents its form, its pure radiance forever guarded by dark clouds; the icy crepe silk conveys its spirit, its glossy black substance seeming to have come from the North Pole. Its bright gaze gleams as if reflecting the sun, and its immortal bearing swirls briskly like the wind. Tearing spring silk to trace its likeness, there is its unhurried old manner; weaving autumn mist to embellish the scene, there is its leaping tamed posture. The frosty pestle is clear and fresh, as if transmitting azure jade from the Jasper Terrace; the ink-blossoms quiver with life, clearly showing flying brushwork from the Jade Empyrean. When the light silk is dusted off, joy moves the Heavenly Countenance; when the splendid scroll is unrolled, radiance illuminates the Imperial Enterprise. Though the stored scroll is old, it is fitting for divining generations and divining years; …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賞鑒重新可得名而得象豈留情於翫物將
適意於研詮宛文囿之游觀卑哉漢獵恍
鎬京之輸賫陋矣梁園方期侈詠以揚
休特奉
溫綸而應
制稽昔揄揚之作多歸鉛槧之流故庾信拜表
於周墀徒誇藻富而張浚颺言於宋室未
闡猷謨睠茲十館之詞林恭讚
累朝之瑞牒臣等業專班馬才愧左狐乏南山
===
隱豹之文負東郭驚盧之懼矢志敢營乎
三窟持身寧守乎一株目翫金精神怡月
德按圖而知上瑞均騰躍雀之歡搦管以
掞清辭殊切戴鰲之懼雕龍技殫徒云下
里裁歌繡虎心勞自謂上林借色蕪綴諸
臣之什繕塵
一夜之觀詞莫罄其鋪張意自關於對育瀟灑
煙霞之性難盡品題迷離毛穎之情粗能
punctuated: 賞鑒重新，可得名而得象。豈留情於翫物，將適意於研詮。宛文囿之游觀，卑哉漢獵；恍鎬京之輸賫，陋矣梁園。方期侈詠以揚休，特奉溫綸而應制。稽昔揄揚之作，多歸鉛槧之流。故庾信拜表於周墀，徒誇藻富；而張浚颺言於宋室，未闡猷謨。睠茲十館之詞林，恭讚累朝之瑞牒。臣等業專班馬，才愧左狐；乏南山隱豹之文，負東郭驚盧之懼。矢志敢營乎三窟，持身寧守乎一株。目翫金精，神怡月德。按圖而知上瑞，均騰躍雀之歡；搦管以掞清辭，殊切戴鰲之懼。雕龍技殫，徒云下里裁歌；繡虎心勞，自謂上林借色。蕪綴諸臣之什，繕塵一夜之觀。詞莫罄其鋪張，意自關於對育。瀟灑煙霞之性，難盡品題；迷離毛穎之情，粗能
translation_en: … as its appreciation and connoisseurship are renewed, one can grasp both its name and its image. How could this be lingering affection for mere playthings? Rather, it is taking pleasure in deep contemplation of the truth. It is just like roaming and viewing the Literary Park—how base were the hunts of the Han! It is as if tribute gifts were being delivered to the capital of Hao—how vulgar was the Garden of Liang! Just as we were hoping to compose grand verses to extol this blessing, we specially received Your warm decree to write in response to the imperial command. Examining the eulogistic works of the past, they mostly belonged to those engaged in writing and textual scholarship. Thus when Yu Xin 庾信 presented his memorial at the court of Northern Zhou, he merely boasted of florid abundance; and when Zhang Jun 張浚 spoke forth at the house of Song, he did not expound upon grand counsels. Looking upon this forest of literati in the ten historiographical halls, we reverently praise the auspicious records of successive reigns. We, Your servants, specialize in the craft of Ban Gu 班固 and Sima Qian 司馬遷, yet our talents put us to shame before Zuo Qiuming 左丘明 and Dong Hu 董狐; we lack the ornamental markings of the leopard hidden in the Southern Mountains, and bear the fear of the hare of Dongguo startled by the hound Hanlu. In swearing our resolve, how would we dare scheme for three burrows? In conducting ourselves, we would rather guard a single tree stump. Our eyes delight in the Essence of Metal, and our spirits rejoice in the Virtue of the Moon. Examining the painting and recognizing a supreme auspice, we all leap like sparrows in shared joy; grasping our brushes to spread forth pure phrases, we feel most keenly the dread of a giant turtle bearing a mountain on its head. Though our skill at carving dragons is exhausted, we can only say we are tailoring a rustic song of Xiali; though our minds labor like an embroidered tiger, we flatter ourselves that we are borrowing luster from the Shanglin Park. We have crudely stitched together the poems of the various officials, copying them out cleanly to sully Your Majesty's perusal during a night's vigil. Our words cannot exhaustively set forth its grandeur, yet our intent naturally pertains to responding to Heaven's nurturing of all things. Its aloof nature amid mist and rosy clouds is difficult to fully appraise in verse; the indistinct, elusive spirit captured by the rabbit-hair brush can barely be…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
緝煕懋學得心頓造於忘蹄
寤寐求才式燕頻歌乎斯首
斡旋元氣長收百鍊之眞精培養性靈不藉
千年之僊搗治以不治躋
上治俾漢賦絕筆於長楊玄之又玄格
重玄令虞舞再儀乎箭管臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹以所撰玄兔圖詩隨
表上
===
進以
聞
第參場
策
第一問
段蓋國
同考試官訓導趙批祝願
皇儲具見忠愛之至而條對內御祈祀莫不一秉于正庶幾乎藎臣用心哉
同考試官敎諭尹批守靜葆和乃根本之論
punctuated:
緝煕懋學，得心頓造於忘蹄；寤寐求才，式燕頻歌乎斯首。斡旋元氣，長收百鍊之眞精；培養性靈，不藉千年之僊搗。治以不治，躋上治，俾漢賦絕筆於《長楊》；玄之又玄，格重玄，令虞舞再儀乎箭管。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至。謹以所撰《玄兔圖詩》隨表上進以聞。

第參場
策
第一問
段蓋國
同考試官訓導趙批：祝願皇儲，具見忠愛之至；而條對內御、祈祀，莫不一秉于正，庶幾乎藎臣用心哉！
同考試官敎諭尹批：守靜葆和，乃根本之論。
translation_en:
…May Your Majesty pursue luminous and diligent learning, grasping the essence until the snare is forgotten; and seek out talent waking and sleeping, feasting guests while frequently singing “White-headed is the rabbit” [Pao you ku ye, Book of Odes]. Turning the primal vitality upon its axis, may You forever gather the true essence refined a hundredfold; nurturing the spirit and nature, You have no need of the immortal’s elixir pounded for a thousand years. Governing through non-governance, You ascend to supreme governance, causing the rhapsodies of Han to lay down their brushes after the Rhapsody on the Tall Poplars Palace [Changyang fu]; mystery beyond mystery, You reach the twofold mystery, making the dances of Yu bring the phoenixes once more to the bamboo flutes [or xiao pipes, reading 簫管 for 箭管?]. Your servants cannot contain our utmost reverence and trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look upon the Sage. We respectfully present the Poems on the Painting of the Dark Rabbit that we have composed, accompanying this memorial for Your Majesty’s attention.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Duan Gaiguo
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao: His prayers and wishes for an Imperial Heir fully reveal the utmost loyalty and affection; and his itemized responses regarding palace regulation and prayers and sacrifices cleave without exception to what is orthodox—how close this comes to the devoted mind of a loyal minister!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yin: Preserving tranquility and nurturing harmony is indeed a discourse that gets to the root of the matter.…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭湯批寓規於祝頌宜錄
考試官教諭王批條答甚悉而忠藎藹然
人主荷
天地
祖宗之託念承祧主器之重則稽典禮以迓
神休非本本原原至計哉夫
君猶天也頌天者以不息故日重光而乾道昌
祝
君者以無疆故明兩作而
===
皇圖鞏其克配均也欲隆無疆之業必先本原
之地故遐則監於成憲而法古之道備焉
邇則稽諸舊章而率
祖之心盡焉六職備脩三靈孚祐古之誼辟所
以式壼則而衍胤祥者事莫大於此矣執
事軫重
皇儲而以内御祈祀之典䇿諸生蓋爲
國本慮殷且亟也敢不稽古以復夫大君非
命於天者哉其冢嗣則天之宗子也其諸
punctuated:
考試官教諭湯批：寓規於祝頌，宜錄。
考試官教諭王批：條答甚悉，而忠藎藹然。

人主荷天地祖宗之託，念承祧主器之重，則稽典禮以迓神休，非本本原原至計哉？夫君猶天也。頌天者以不息，故日重光而乾道昌；祝君者以無疆，故明兩作而皇圖鞏。其克配均也。欲隆無疆之業，必先本原之地。故遐則監於成憲，而法古之道備焉；邇則稽諸舊章，而率祖之心盡焉。六職備脩，三靈孚祐，古之誼辟所以式壼則而衍胤祥者，事莫大於此矣。執事軫重皇儲，而以内御祈祀之典䇿諸生，蓋爲國本慮殷且亟也，敢不稽古以復？夫大君非命於天者哉？其冢嗣則天之宗子也，其諸
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: He embeds admonition within his prayers and eulogies; this ought to be recorded.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: His point-by-point responses are exceedingly thorough, and his loyal devotion shines forth warmly.

When the ruler bears the trust of Heaven, Earth, and the Ancestors, and reflects upon the weighty responsibility of succeeding to the ancestral temple and presiding over the sacrificial vessels, then is not examining the canonical rites in order to welcome divine blessings the ultimate plan rooted in first principles? Now, the sovereign is like Heaven. Those who eulogize Heaven do so for its ceaselessness, whereby the sun shines in doubled radiance and the Way of Heaven flourishes; those who offer prayers for the sovereign do so for his boundlessness, whereby brightness rises twice over and the imperial enterprise is consolidated. Their capacity to match one another is equal. If one wishes to exalt a boundless enterprise, one must put the fundamental ground first. Therefore, looking far back, one takes the established constitutions as a mirror, and the way of modeling oneself on antiquity is made complete; looking near at hand, one examines the old statutes, and the heart that follows the Ancestors is fully realized. When the six palace offices are fully cultivated and the three spiritual powers respond with assured blessing—whereby the righteous rulers of antiquity set the standard for the inner quarters and multiplied the auspiciousness of progeny—there is no matter greater than this. Your Excellency shows deep concern for the Imperial Heir and has posed a policy question to us students regarding the canons of inner governance and prayers and sacrifices; this is surely because your concern for the foundation of the dynasty is both earnest and urgent. How could I dare not examine antiquity in order to reply? Now, is not the great sovereign mandated by Heaven? His eldest son and heir is the lineal heir of Heaven, while his various…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
王以下則天所茂衍爲宗子支也而紫薇
垣象之矣太乙座其宸極乎第一星以象
冢嗣餘三星以象庶子森羅列置互爲維
亘夫使二星隱曜弗彰則光芒與紫宮不
相包絡而何以烜奕宸極乎故天必耦地
王必耦后其道相須而後成而天神効順
地軸發靈其機亦相感而類應繇斯以譚
所以樹茲
儲寳克昌來業者其道槩可覩已甞攷夐古
===
后稷之生寔自元妃下之則簡狄生契慶
都生堯娵訾生摯維時閫職未建掖位尚
乏烏睹所謂六宮哉自四妃始於帝嚳而
成周廣之爲王宮之令立之后以配天子
立之三夫人以象三公立之九嬪以象九
卿立之二十七世婦以象大夫立之八十
一御妻以象元士六宮之位與外班等而
翬珩褕組自是稍稍充椒塗也然而未濫
也載按禮文天地之祭主自天子次之則
punctuated:
王以下，則天所茂衍爲宗子支也，而紫薇垣象之矣。太乙座其宸極乎，第一星以象冢嗣，餘三星以象庶子，森羅列置，互爲維亘。夫使二星隱曜弗彰，則光芒與紫宮不相包絡，而何以烜奕宸極乎？故天必耦地，王必耦后，其道相須而後成；而天神効順，地軸發靈，其機亦相感而類應。繇斯以譚，所以樹茲儲寳、克昌來業者，其道槩可覩已。

甞攷夐古，后稷之生，寔自元妃；下之則簡狄生契，慶都生堯，娵訾生摯。維時閫職未建，掖位尚乏，烏睹所謂六宮哉？自四妃始於帝嚳，而成周廣之爲王宮之令：立之后以配天子，立之三夫人以象三公，立之九嬪以象九卿，立之二十七世婦以象大夫，立之八十一御妻以象元士。六宮之位與外班等，而翬珩褕組，自是稍稍充椒塗也，然而未濫也。

載按禮文，天地之祭，主自天子；次之則
translation_en:
… the princes and below are those whom Heaven abundantly multiplies as the collateral branches of the eldest son of the primary line, and the Purple Forbidden Enclosure (Ziwei yuan) represents this in the heavens. Is not the seat of the Supreme Unity (Taiyi) the imperial pole? The first star symbolizes the heir apparent, and the remaining three stars symbolize the sons of concubines; arrayed in dense order, they mutually support and connect with one another. Now, suppose two of the stars were to hide their brilliance and not shine forth; then their radiance would not envelop and interlink with the Purple Palace, and how could they illuminate the imperial pole in splendor? Therefore, Heaven must be paired with Earth, and the King must be paired with the Queen; their Way requires mutual dependence before it is complete. And when the spirits of Heaven render obedience and the axis of Earth manifests efficacy, their subtle mechanisms also mutually stimulate and respond in kind. Speaking from this perspective, the Way by which to establish this precious Heir Apparent and make prosperous the future patrimony can in general outline be seen.

I have examined remote antiquity: the birth of Hou Ji truly came from the primary consort; below her, Jiandi gave birth to Xie, Qingdu gave birth to Yao, and Juzi gave birth to Zhi. At that time, the offices of the inner quarters had not yet been established, and the ranks of the lateral courts were still lacking—where could one see what are called the Six Palaces? From the time the four consorts began with Emperor Ku, the flourishing Zhou expanded this into the regulations of the royal palace: establishing the Queen to match the Son of Heaven, establishing the Three Consorts to correspond to the Three Dukes, establishing the Nine Concubines to correspond to the Nine Ministers, establishing the Twenty-seven Hereditary Consorts to correspond to the Grand Masters, and establishing the Eighty-one Attendant Wives to correspond to the Servitors of the First Class. The ranks of the Six Palaces equaled those of the outer court, and pheasant-patterned robes, girdle gems, feathered garments, and silk cords from this time onward gradually filled the pepper-plastered halls—and yet there was no excess.

Examining further the ritual texts, the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were presided over by the Son of Heaven; next to these…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
秩於山川禋於六宗徧於羣神維時祝史
未繁祭義尚質烏覩所謂高禖哉自簡狄
見於商詩而秦官述之爲祈嗣之文期之
仲春以適生機候之玄鳥以符靈契主之
高禖以重始合從之嬙嬪以配陰陽授之
鞫矢以徵先兆禖祀之典與先蠶並而龍
旂鳳轝自是往往列春郊也然而未瀆也
後世闇帷房之戒廣事采擇而婦制莫釐
昧告虔之儀徒飾虛文而精意未協則去
===
古遠矣譚内御者毎藉口於周官以自遂
其狎昵之私有增級十四者焉漢之武元
是已而巫蠱燕啄内釁相尋不可長也有
爵視外朝者焉晉之武帝是已而下逮散
位盈溢至萬不可訓也有分列八品者焉
唐之襲隋是已而貽謀不善素舒失德不
可道也此惟端容麗服陪從宴閒内鮮求
賢審官之助外叢德纎猜長之譏吁可鑒
哉譚祀典者又藉口於秦官以自文其不
punctuated: 秩於山川，禋於六宗，徧於羣神。維時祝史未繁，祭義尚質，烏覩所謂高禖哉？自簡狄見於《商詩》，而秦官述之爲祈嗣之文：期之仲春，以適生機；候之玄鳥，以符靈契；主之高禖，以重始合；從之嬙嬪，以配陰陽；授之鞫矢，以徵先兆。禖祀之典與先蠶並，而龍旂鳳轝，自是往往列春郊也，然而未瀆也。後世闇帷房之戒，廣事采擇，而婦制莫釐；昧告虔之儀，徒飾虛文，而精意未協，則去古遠矣。譚内御者，毎藉口於《周官》，以自遂其狎昵之私。有增級十四者焉，漢之武、元是已，而巫蠱、燕啄，内釁相尋，不可長也；有爵視外朝者焉，晉之武帝是已，而下逮散位，盈溢至萬，不可訓也；有分列八品者焉，唐之襲隋是已，而貽謀不善，素舒失德，不可道也。此惟端容麗服，陪從宴閒，内鮮求賢審官之助，外叢德纎猜長之譏，吁，可鑒哉！譚祀典者，又藉口於秦官，以自文其不
translation_en: …offered in order to the mountains and rivers, sacrificed with pure intent to the Six Honored Ones, and extended them to all the spirits. At that time, the invocators and scribes were not yet numerous, and the principles of sacrifice still valued simplicity—where did one ever see the so-called Supreme Matchmaker (Gaomei 高禖)? It began with Jiandi 簡狄 appearing in the Odes of Shang (Shang shi), and the officials of Qin recounted it to create the ritual regulations for praying for an heir: scheduling it in mid-spring to accord with the vital impulse of life; awaiting the dark bird (swallow) to match the numinous tally; presiding over it through the Supreme Matchmaker to give weight to the initial union; having the palace ladies and concubines attend in order to pair yin and yang; and bestowing the bowcase and arrows tobetoken the auspicious omen beforehand. The canon of the Matchmaker sacrifice stood alongside that of the First Sericulturist (Xian Can 先蠶), and from this time onward, dragon banners and phoenix carriages were frequently arrayed in the spring suburbs—and yet it was not irreverent. In later ages, rulers grew blind to the warnings concerning the bedchamber, engaging broadly in the selection of women while failing to regulate the system of palace consorts; they grew ignorant of the rites of reverent supplication, merely adorning empty forms while failing to harmonize with the essential meaning. Thus they departed far from antiquity! Those who discuss the inner consorts always use the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) as a pretext to indulge their own selfish desires for intimate favor. There were those who increased the ranks to fourteen—such were Emperors Wu 武 and Yuan 元 of the Han; yet with witchcraft (wugu 巫蠱) and the "swallow pecking" (Yan zhuo 燕啄, i.e., Zhao Feiyan 趙飛燕), internal calamities followed one after another, which cannot be fostered! There were those who made their noble ranks correspond to the outer court—such was Emperor Wu 武帝 of the Jin; yet extending down to the unranked positions, they overflowed to ten thousand, which cannot be taken as a model! There were those who divided and arrayed them into eight ranks—such was the Tang following the Sui; yet the plans passed down were not good, and the loss of virtue by Su [?] and Shu [?] cannot bear speaking of! These women merely composed their countenances and wore gorgeous garments, attending the ruler in his banquets and leisure; internally they rarely offered the assistance of seeking the worthy and examining officials (as praised in the Ode "Juan'er"), while externally they gathered criticisms of petty virtue and growing suspicion. Alas, how worthy of serving as a warning! Those who discuss the sacrificial canons in turn use the officials of Qin as a pretext to gloss over their own uncanonical…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
經之說有設壇城南者焉則漢武以誕生
皇子之故而有報無祈何簡也有建立石
主者焉則晉采束晳高堂隆之議而瘞埋
破石何陋也有增置配帝者焉則北齊以
太昊爲配而義無所取何褻也此皆典禮
未稱明神不享徒事苟簡禷禨之儀罔識
前星少海之重吁可鄙哉
高皇帝詫業發神外自堦墀內逮房闥靡匪雝
雝肅肅以貽
神孫令則洪武初年卽
命禮官詳定女職設立六局尚宮則司記司言
司簿司闈也尚儀則司籍司樂司賓司賛
也尚服則司寶司衣司仗司飾也尚食則
司饌司醞司藥司供也尚寢則司設司輿
司苑司燈也尚功則司製司珍司綵司計
也戒正責罰則董之宮正而其秩無踰六
品法何具也或疑六尚之設雜就唐儀不
知唐沿隋者也隋沿宇文周者也宇文氏
punctuated:
經之說。有設壇城南者焉，則漢武以誕生皇子之故，而有報無祈，何簡也！有建立石主者焉，則晉采束晳、高堂隆之議，而瘞埋破石，何陋也！有增置配帝者焉，則北齊以太昊爲配，而義無所取，何褻也！此皆典禮未稱，明神不享，徒事苟簡禷禨之儀，罔識前星少海之重。吁，可鄙哉！
高皇帝詫業發神，外自堦墀，內逮房闥，靡匪雝雝肅肅，以貽神孫令則。洪武初年，卽命禮官詳定女職，設立六局：尚宮，則司記、司言、司簿、司闈也；尚儀，則司籍、司樂、司賓、司賛也；尚服，則司寶、司衣、司仗、司飾也；尚食，則司饌、司醞、司藥、司供也；尚寢，則司設、司輿、司苑、司燈也；尚功，則司製、司珍、司綵、司計也。戒正責罰，則董之宮正，而其秩無踰六品，法何具也！或疑六尚之設，雜就唐儀，不知唐沿隋者也，隋沿宇文周者也，宇文氏
translation_en:
…uncanonical theories. There were those who set up an altar south of the city: such was Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wu 漢武), who did so because of the birth of an imperial son, offering thanksgiving without prior prayer—how perfunctory! There were those who erected a stone spirit-tablet: such was the Jin dynasty, which adopted the proposals of Shu Xi 束晳 and Gaotang Long 高堂隆 and buried a broken stone—how vulgar! There were those who added a coadjutor deity: such was the Northern Qi, which made Taihao 太昊 the coadjutor without any basis in principle—how irreverent! In all these cases, the ritual canons were ill-suited and the bright spirits did not accept the offerings; they merely engaged in careless, makeshift, and superstitious ceremonies, failing to recognize the gravity of the Heir Apparent—symbolized by the Fore-star and the Lesser Sea. Alas, how despicable!

When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu) founded the imperial enterprise [?] and manifested his divine prowess, from the outer court steps to the inner palace chambers, all was harmonious and reverent, so as to bequeath a fine model to his divine descendants. In the early years of the Hongwu 洪武 reign, he immediately ordered the ritual officials to determine in detail the offices for palace women, establishing the Six Bureaus: the Palace Service Bureau (Shanggong 尚宮), comprising the Services of Records (Siji 司記), Messages (Siyan 司言), Accounts (Sibu 司簿), and Palace Gates (Siwei 司闈); the Ceremonial Service Bureau (Shangyi 尚儀), comprising the Services of Books (Siji 司籍), Music (Siyue 司樂), Guests (Sibin 司賓), and Ceremonial Guidance (Sizan 司賛); the Wardrobe Service Bureau (Shangfu 尚服), comprising the Services of Treasures (Sibao 司寶), Robes (Siyi 司衣), Regalia (Sizhang 司仗), and Ornaments (Sishi 司飾); the Food Service Bureau (Shangshi 尚食), comprising the Services of Delicacies (Sizhuan 司饌), Fermented Drinks (Siyun 司醞), Medicines (Siyao 司藥), and Provisions (Sigong 司供); the Bedchamber Service Bureau (Shangqin 尚寢), comprising the Services of Furnishings (Sishe 司設), Carriages (Siyu 司輿), Gardens (Siyuan 司苑), and Lamps (Sideng 司燈); and the Handicraft Service Bureau (Shanggong 尚功), comprising the Services of Tailoring (Sizhi 司製), Jewels (Sizhen 司珍), Silks (Sicai 司綵), and Reckoning (Siji 司計). Admonition, correction, and punishment were supervised by the Rectifier of the Palace (Gongzheng 宮正), and none of their ranks exceeded the sixth grade—how complete the regulations were! Some suspect that the establishment of the Six Bureaus was indiscriminately adapted from Tang ceremony, not realizing that the Tang followed the Sui, the Sui followed the Northern Zhou of the Yuwen 宇文 clan, and what the Yuwen clan…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所定又皆本周官者也洪武儒臣采而用
之奚甞不循周制耶
肅皇帝鑠勳恢烈大自
兩郊細及百祀靡匪皇皇奕奕以光
聖祖遐武嘉靖初年卽
命禮官議崇禖祀設壇震方南鄕則
皇天上帝也西鄕則
獻皇作配也牲則三品也禮則三獻也樂則九
奏也舞則八佾也
===
帝位則壇下北鄕也
后妃則以次稍南也弓矢弓韣則陳之壇下而
其數視乎
妃嬪制何詳也或疑禮文之縟半益周制不
知壇居東方震繼離也主以
上帝答元貺也配以
皇考本自出也
帝后異位坤承乾也嘉靖儒臣變而通之又奚
必泥古法耶夫攷之往古參以
punctuated:
所定，又皆本《周官》者也。洪武儒臣采而用之，奚甞不循周制耶？
肅皇帝鑠勳恢烈，大自兩郊，細及百祀，靡匪皇皇奕奕，以光聖祖遐武。嘉靖初年，卽命禮官議崇禖祀：設壇震方，南鄕則皇天上帝也，西鄕則獻皇作配也，牲則三品也，禮則三獻也，樂則九奏也，舞則八佾也，帝位則壇下北鄕也，后妃則以次稍南也，弓矢、弓韣則陳之壇下，而其數視乎妃嬪，制何詳也！或疑禮文之縟，半益周制，不知壇居東方，震繼離也；主以上帝，答元貺也；配以皇考，本自出也；帝后異位，坤承乾也。嘉靖儒臣變而通之，又奚必泥古法耶？
夫攷之往古，參以
translation_en:
… what [the Yuwen clan] established was in turn all based on the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). When the Confucian officials of the Hongwu era selected and adopted these, how did they ever fail to follow the institutions of the Zhou?

Emperor Su [the Jiajing Emperor] achievedsplendid merits and expanded heroic enterprises; from the Two Suburban Sacrifices on the grand scale down to the hundred lesser sacrifices in detail, there was nothing that was not august and resplendent, thereby glorifying the distant footsteps of the Sacred Ancestor [the Hongwu Emperor]. In the early years of the Jiajing era, he immediately ordered the ritual officials to deliberate on exalting the sacrifice to the Matchmaker Deity (Gaomei): an altar was erected in the eastern quarter [the direction of the trigram Zhen]; facing south was August Heaven the Supreme Emperor (Huangtian Shangdi); facing west as the correlate was the Xian Emperor [the Jiajing Emperor's biological father, Zhu Youyuan]; the sacrificial victims were of the three kinds; the ritual consisted of three offerings of wine; the music was performed in nine movements; the dance was in eight rows; the Emperor's place was below the altar facing north; the Empress and imperial consorts were arranged in order slightly to the south; and bows, arrows, and bow-cases were set out below the altar, their number corresponding to that of the consorts and concubines—how detailed the system was! Some may suspect that the elaborateness of the ritual forms added half again to the institutions of the Zhou. They do not understand that placing the altar in the east signifies the trigram Zhen succeeding Li; making the Supreme Emperor the principal deity is to respond to the primordial blessing; making the Imperial Deceased Father (Huangkao) the correlate is to honor the source from which one came; and giving the Emperor and Empress different positions signifies the trigram Kun [Earth/female] subordinately receiving Qian [Heaven/male]. When the Confucian officials of the Jiajing era adapted and flexibly applied these principles, why would they necessarily have had to cling rigidly to ancient methods?

Now, if we examine the distant past and compare it with…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
昭代時之升降可燭已禮之汙隆可鏡已方今
兩宮慈範齊軌姜嫄
中闈壼德方駕任姒且登九列而充六尚者非
良家之婉嫕則待年之淑女也簪珥成行
環珮振響肅
坤儀而脩四善體柔範以弘六義俔天之烈小
星之歌豈乏哉而
郊廟必親海岳必祀祈求胤嗣之典
兩宮尤惓惓焉然海內臣民之望又有出于廣
===
內御崇禋祀二者之外蓋亦有說矣夫禮
言時御易著貫魚非獨均恩嗇寵也將以
助
天資生也柰之何桂殿迎春則情與愛遷蘭房
侍夜則事為私奪或嬖而專席以妨廣胤
之理或溺而濫幸以虧生息之原此豈可
不為長慮哉詩紀玄鳥禮述高禖非尚禨
祥小數也將以翊
運承祧也柰之何內政未脩而專事徼福玄釐
punctuated: 昭代，時之升降可燭已，禮之汙隆可鏡已。方今兩宮慈範，齊軌姜嫄；中闈壼德，方駕任、姒。且登九列而充六尚者，非良家之婉嫕，則待年之淑女也。簪珥成行，環珮振響，肅坤儀而脩四善，體柔範以弘六義。「俔天」之烈、《小星》之歌，豈乏哉！而郊廟必親，海岳必祀，祈求胤嗣之典，兩宮尤惓惓焉。然海內臣民之望，又有出于廣內御、崇禋祀二者之外，蓋亦有說矣。夫《禮》言「時御」、《易》著「貫魚」，非獨均恩嗇寵也，將以助天資生也。柰之何桂殿迎春，則情與愛遷；蘭房侍夜，則事為私奪。或嬖而專席，以妨廣胤之理；或溺而濫幸，以虧生息之原。此豈可不為長慮哉！《詩》紀「玄鳥」、《禮》述「高禖」，非尚禨祥小數也，將以翊運承祧也。柰之何內政未脩，而專事徼福；玄釐
translation_en:
… our Illustrious Dynasty, the rise and fall of the times can be illuminated, and the decline and flourishing of ritual can be mirrored! At present, the compassionate example of the Two Palaces [the Empresses Dowager] matches the track of Jiang Yuan; the inner-palace virtue of the Central Apartments [the Empress] rides abreast of Tairen and Taisi. Moreover, those who ascend to the Nine Ranks of consorts and fill the Six Offices of palace women are either gentle and compliant daughters of good families or virtuous maidens awaiting their coming of age. With hairpins and ear-ornaments forming ranks and jade pendants resounding, they revere the Earthly Model [of the Empress] and cultivate the Four Virtues, embodying gentle norms to broaden the Six Principles. How could there be any lack of the illustrious merit of "a match for Heaven" [in the ode Daming] or the song of "Little Stars" (Xiaoxing)? Furthermore, the suburban altars and ancestral temples are invariably attended in person, and the seas and marchmounts are invariably sacrificed to; as for the rites of praying for imperial progeny, the Two Palaces are especially earnest about them. Yet the hopes of officials and commoners within the seas go beyond merely expanding the roster of inner-palace attendants and exalting pure sacrifices—and for this, indeed, there is an explanation.

Now, when the Book of Rites (Liji) speaks of "timely attendance" in the royal bedchamber and the Book of Changes (Yijing) sets forth the image of "a string of fish," this is not merely to equalize favor and economize on affection; it is meant to assist Heaven in bestowing life. Why is it, then, that when welcoming spring in the cassia halls, feelings shift along with infatuation, and when attending at night in the orchid chambers, duties are usurped by private partiality? Either a favorite monopolizes the mat, thereby obstructing the principle of multiplying descendants; or one indulges in excessive visitation, thereby impairing the very source of vitality and procreation. How can one not take long-term thought for this?

When the Book of Odes (Shijing) records the "Dark Bird" (Xuanniao) and the Book of Rites recounts the "Supreme Matchmaker" (Gaomei), this is not to prize the petty arts of omens and portents; it is meant to assist the dynastic destiny and continue the ancestral line. Why is it, then, that while the governance of the inner palace remains uncultivated, one devotes oneself exclusively to seeking blessings; while mysterious favors …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
濫乞而惑志媚神或假符緯以求赤虹白
魚之驗或弔詭幽以要吞鳥履跡之竒此
豈可為後訓哉
人主惟致虚守靜以儀刑於内嗇神葆和以考
祥於天則何福不應何瑞不臻故旣醉之
什曰釐爾女士從以孫子而假樂亦言子
孫千億干祿百福應感之機從可識矣乃
兹旣
明慎聘納虔脩祀事天下已望
===
明德於造舟為梁之時而愚生今日則又竊效
封人之祝而推廣之詩序不云天下和平
斯婦人樂有子焉藉令軒殿以内凝采髫
年賁章笄歲者風流行而雨窈窕而民間
多闕於伉儷后宫翡翠火齊膏脣耀首而
里巷士女不免葛屨杼軸之困則内外咨
怨終傷理道故夙夜幾康以薦天和而施
祉孫子者宜講也天道葆光於秋伏精於
冬而燠咻於春然後百昌殖萬彙作
punctuated: 濫乞而惑志媚神，或假符緯以求赤虹、白魚之驗，或弔詭幽以要吞鳥、履跡之竒，此豈可為後訓哉？人主惟致虚守靜以儀刑於内，嗇神葆和以考祥於天，則何福不應，何瑞不臻？故《旣醉》之什曰：「釐爾女士，從以孫子。」而《假樂》亦言：「子孫千億，干祿百福。」應感之機，從可識矣。乃兹旣明慎聘納，虔脩祀事，天下已望明德於「造舟為梁」之時，而愚生今日則又竊效封人之祝而推廣之：《詩序》不云「天下和平，斯婦人樂有子」焉？藉令軒殿以内，凝采髫年，賁章笄歲者，風流行而雨窈窕，而民間多闕於伉儷；后宫翡翠火齊，膏脣耀首，而里巷士女不免「葛屨」、「杼軸」之困，則内外咨怨，終傷理道。故夙夜幾康，以薦天和而施祉孫子者，宜講也。天道葆光於秋，伏精於冬，而燠咻於春，然後百昌殖，萬彙作。
translation_en: …extravagantly begged for, while minds are deluded into flattering the spirits. Some borrow from apocryphal prognostic texts to seek the signs of the red rainbow or the white fish, while others resort to bizarre and occult practices to court the marvels of swallowing a bird's egg or treading in a giant's footprint—how could such things serve as instruction for posterity? If only the sovereign attains emptiness and maintains tranquility so as to set a model within the palace, and husbands his spirit and preserves harmony so as to secure auspicious signs from Heaven, then what blessing will not respond, and what auspicious omen will not arrive? Thus the ode "Already Drunk" (Jizui) in the Book of Odes says: "You are granted a lady of virtue, followed by grandsons and sons." And the ode "Felicitous and Joyful" (Jiale) likewise says: "Sons and grandsons in thousands and hundreds of millions, seeking emoluments and a hundred blessings." From this, the subtle mechanism of stimulus and response can be understood. Now, since Your Majesty has already been enlightened and prudent in the selection of a consort and reverently conducted the sacrificial rites, the empire has already looked with hope upon your illustrious virtue from the moment "boats were lashed together to form a bridge" [to welcome the bride]. Yet today I, a foolish student, venture to imitate the border warden's blessing [of Yao] and expand upon it: Does not the Preface to the Odes (Shixu) say that "when the realm is at peace, women rejoice in having children"? Suppose that within the palace halls, young girls chosen in childhood or at the age of the hairpin enjoy overflowing grace and favor like spreading wind and rain, while among the common people many lack spouses; or suppose that in the rear palace, ladies adorn their lips with unguents and dazzle their heads with kingfisher feathers and fire-pearls, while the men and women of the lanes and alleys cannot escape the hardships depicted in the odes "Dolichos Shoes" (Geju) and "The Looms Are Empty" (Zhuzhu)—then resentment and sighing both within and without would ultimately harm the way of governance. Therefore, attending with vigilance and composure day and night in order to present harmony to Heaven and bestow blessings upon one's sons and grandsons is something that ought to be carefully considered. The Way of Heaven conceals its radiance in autumn, stores its vital essence in winter, and warms and nurtures in spring; only then do the hundred things flourish and the myriad creatures arise. …

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人主法陰陽之運養性命之精非堇堇焉習熊
經鳥伸以耽靜息也語曰天子不處全不
處極不處盈
皇皇上帝挈
太寶而屬之而以不貲之身靡曼於佚慾如子
孫黎民何如天意何故素封之家有材千
章而刳情約志無敢馳奢重弃糈也矧
至尊哉則上荅
蒼穹俯順人心往鑒流湎而來茂
===
鼎祚者宜講也樛木螽斯其小者也聖人刪詩
直取以美后妃則何以張之蓋樛木下垂
葛藟得附焉以豐其末螽斯不妬則天氣
全而種類繁滋后妃者法樛木之慈以逮
眾法螽斯之仁以馭下則蟄蟄振振之感
固可操左契而責之償則今之脩陰教以
章內則者可講也古者御幸之禮至嚴且
肅將侍君所無論后若夫人息燭以告行
易服以告虔奏雞鳴於太師以告時鳴珮
punctuated: 人主法陰陽之運，養性命之精，非堇堇焉習熊經鳥伸以耽靜息也。語曰：「天子不處全，不處極，不處盈。」皇皇上帝，挈太寶而屬之，而以不貲之身，靡曼於佚慾，如子孫黎民何？如天意何？故素封之家，有材千章，而刳情約志，無敢馳奢，重弃糈也，矧至尊哉！則上荅蒼穹，俯順人心，往鑒流湎，而來茂鼎祚者，宜講也。樛木、螽斯，其小者也，聖人刪《詩》，直取以美后妃，則何以張之？蓋樛木下垂，葛藟得附焉以豐其末；螽斯不妬，則天氣全而種類繁滋。后妃者，法樛木之慈以逮眾，法螽斯之仁以馭下，則蟄蟄振振之感，固可操左契而責之償。則今之脩陰教以章內則者，可講也。古者御幸之禮，至嚴且肅。將侍君所，無論后若夫人，息燭以告行，易服以告虔，奏《雞鳴》於太師以告時，鳴珮
translation_en:
When the ruler models himself on the revolutions of yin and yang and nurtures the vital essence of his nature and life, it is not merely a matter of practicing "bear-hangings and bird-stretchings" so as to indulge in quiet repose. The saying goes: "The Son of Heaven does not dwell in completeness, does not dwell in the extreme, and does not dwell in fullness." Glorious Supreme Heaven has taken the Great Treasure and entrusted it to him; if he then takes his priceless person and wastes it in voluptuousness and licentious desires, what will become of his descendants and the common people? What will become of the will of Heaven? Therefore, even a family of substantial private wealth that possesses a thousand great timbers will pare away its passions and restrain its ambitions, not daring to run wild in extravagance, because it attaches great weight to squandering its provisions—how much more so the Supreme Sovereign! Thus, how to answer the azure vault above, comply with the hearts of the people below, take warning from past dissipation, and bring flourishing to the dynastic fortune in the future—this ought to be discussed.

The curving trees ("Jiumu") and the locusts ("Zhongsi") are minor things; yet when the Sage edited the Classic of Odes (Shi), he directly selected them to praise the queen and consorts—why did he so magnify them? It is because when the curving trees droop downward, the creepers and vines are able to attach themselves to them and make their tips luxuriant; and because the locusts are free of jealousy, their heavenly vitality remains intact and their kind multiplies abundantly. If the Empress and imperial consorts model themselves on the kindness of the curving trees so as to extend grace to the multitude, and model themselves on the benevolence of the locusts so as to govern their subordinates, then the response of harmonious clustering and noble progeny can surely be claimed as reliably as holding the left tally of a contract to demand repayment. Thus, how at present to cultivate the teachings of the inner quarters (yinjiao) so as to make manifest the domestic regulations (neize)—this may be discussed.

In antiquity, the rites governing imperial favor and bedchamber attendance were most strict and solemn. When about to attend at the ruler's quarters, whether it was the queen or the consorts, torches were extinguished to announce her departure, garments were changed to announce her reverence, "The Cock Crows" ("Jiming") was performed by the Grand Musician to announce the hour, and jade pendants were sounded…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
王於房中以告去應門擊柝以告闉其禮
恭慎而不苟而又有女史簪彤管書其環
以進退之此非好瑣煩其令所以謹競榮
之防而杜色授之漸則今之昵策裯而越
矩矱者可講也大任之身文王目無邪視
耳無淫聽口無敖言文王生而褒然聖明
爲周宗太姒生十子自少至長恒以正道
押持之用成武王周公至德則古昔所稱
胎教内教者可講也審能是則陰陽順序
===
恩寵均齊慶澤綿遠本支千億以此格天
而上神歆以此格
廟而百靈契揚
太母徽音之烈成
中宮脫珥之賢刑家之化爰達寰宇重輪之
貺且延萬葉奚止
掖庭永巷之脩職哉宋魏鶴山氏言之矣
人君居内之日常少居外之日常多所以養壽
命之源雖子孫千億亦自此始此祈嗣之
punctuated: 王於房中以告去，應門擊柝以告闉，其禮恭慎而不苟。而又有女史簪彤管，書其環以進退之。此非好瑣煩其令，所以謹競榮之防，而杜色授之漸，則今之昵策裯而越矩矱者可講也。大任之身文王，目無邪視，耳無淫聽，口無敖言，文王生而褒然聖明，爲周宗。太姒生十子，自少至長，恒以正道押持之，用成武王、周公至德，則古昔所稱胎教、内教者可講也。審能是，則陰陽順序，恩寵均齊，慶澤綿遠，本支千億。以此格天而上神歆，以此格廟而百靈契；揚太母徽音之烈，成中宮脫珥之賢；刑家之化爰達寰宇，重輪之貺且延萬葉，奚止掖庭、永巷之脩職哉？宋魏鶴山氏言之矣：「人君居内之日常少，居外之日常多，所以養壽命之源。雖子孫千億，亦自此始。」此祈嗣之
translation_en: …jades [王 for 玉] inside the chamber to announce her departure, and striking the wooden clapper at the gate of response to announce the closing of the inner gates—the rites were reverent, cautious, and never careless. Moreover, there were Female Scribes who wore red-tube brushes in their hair and recorded the consort's silver rings to regulate who should advance or withdraw. This was not out of a fondness for making ordinances trivial and burdensome; rather, it was the means to guard the dike against vying for favor and to stop the gradual rise of conferring status on account of beauty. Thus, today's practice of showing intimate favor in bedsheets and coverlets [策 for 簀] and overstepping the proper rules and measures is something that ought to be examined! When Tai Ren was pregnant with King Wen, her eyes looked at nothing improper, her ears listened to nothing licentious, and her mouth spoke no arrogant words; when King Wen was born, he was preeminently sage and enlightened, becoming the ancestor of the Zhou. Tai Si gave birth to ten sons, and from their youth to maturity she constantly guided and upheld them [押 for 挾?] with the correct Way, thereby bringing to completion the supreme virtue of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou. Thus, what antiquity called fetal instruction and inner instruction is something that ought to be examined! If one can truly accomplish this, then yin and yang will follow their proper order, grace and favor will be evenly distributed, blessings and beneficence will stretch far into the future, and the main and collateral branches will number in the hundreds of millions. By this means one reaches Heaven and the High God delights in the offerings; by this means one reaches the Ancestral Temple and the hundred spirits are in harmony. It will exalt the illustrious achievements of the Empress Dowager's fine reputation, and fulfill the worthiness of the Empress in removing her earrings in remonstrance. The transforming influence of providing a model for the family will thereupon reach the entire realm, and the blessing of the "double wheel" [the heir apparent] will extend for ten thousand generations—how could it merely be a matter of the lateral courts and long lanes of the inner palace cultivating their duties? Wei Heshan (Wei Liaoweng 魏了翁) of the Song dynasty said it well: "The days a ruler spends in the inner palace are always few, while the days he spends in the outer court are always many; this is the means to nourish the source of longevity. Even having descendants in the hundreds of millions also begins from this." This is the… [of praying for heirs]…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
本也而非特宋臣有是說也
高皇帝初定女職亦甞言古者建設過多宜防
女寵垂法將來以故六局外無復剰員然
當時篤生二十四
王迄今稱親郡諸府及中尉將軍以下二萬
有奇天下比於鳯毛麟趾以爲上瑞然則
繼體守成之盛果在內御之繁與禋祀之勤耶
詩曰昭兹來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天
之祜以
===
高皇
世祖之功耀於日月長於天地神祇降康俾有
土者世世明章之矧
今上應昌期孚世德雲物告符鍾祥厥後一卜
於
瑤圖之曆再稽於大人之占多男之慶且旦
暮睹之矣
第二問
陳良心
punctuated:
本也。而非特宋臣有是說也，高皇帝初定女職，亦甞言：「古者建設過多，宜防女寵，垂法將來。」以故六局外無復剰員。然當時篤生二十四王，迄今稱親、郡諸府，及中尉、將軍以下，二萬有奇，天下比於鳯毛麟趾，以爲上瑞。然則繼體守成之盛，果在內御之繁與禋祀之勤耶？《詩》曰：「昭兹來許，繩其祖武。於萬斯年，受天之祜。」以高皇、世祖之功，耀於日月，長於天地，神祇降康，俾有土者世世明章之。矧今上應昌期，孚世德，雲物告符，鍾祥厥後。一卜於瑤圖之曆，再稽於大人之占，多男之慶，且旦暮睹之矣。

第二問
陳良心
translation_en:
…fundamental root [of praying for heirs]. And it was not only the Song minister who advanced this argument. When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu) first established the offices of the palace women, he also once remarked: "In antiquity, too many positions were created; one ought to guard against female favoritism and hand down a model for the future." For this reason, outside the Six Bureaus there were no superfluous personnel. Yet at that time he was blessed with the birth of twenty-four princes; down to the present day, those belonging to the princely establishments of the first and second ranks, along with the Commandants (zhongwei) and Generals (jiangjun) and below, number more than twenty thousand. The realm compares them to phoenix feathers and unicorn hoofs, regarding them as supreme auspices. Such being the case, does the flourishing of imperial succession and the preservation of dynastic accomplishments truly lie in a profusion of palace consorts or in the diligence of sacrificial rites? The Classic of Poetry (Shi 詩) says: "Brightly heave they come forth, continuing the footsteps of their ancestors. For ten thousand years, they shall receive the blessings of Heaven." Because the meritorious achievements of the Exalted Emperor and the Epochal Ancestor (Shizu 世祖, i.e., the Jiajing Emperor) shine brighter than the sun and moon and endure as long as Heaven and Earth, the spirits of Heaven and Earth send down peace and prosperity, enabling those who hold territories to make them illustrious from generation to generation. How much more so now that the Reigning Sovereign responds to a flourishing era and embodies the hereditary virtue of the dynasty, while auspicious clouds and portents announce favorable omens, concentrating blessings upon his posterity! Consulting first the calendar of the precious imperial chart, and verifying again by the divination of the great man, the celebration of numerous sons shall be witnessed morning or evening!

Second Question
Chen Liangxin 陳良心

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭趙批是能留心
國計者就所條畫次第施行殷富立致矣經濟材也錄之
同考試官教諭顧批以儉德立論是識時務者
同考試官教諭楊批會計始末闡揚殆盡
考試官教諭湯批是策有裨主計者宜錄
考試官教諭王批斟酌時事劈畫允當
財蓋難言哉聽而不爲之筴則大耗驟起
而持之則裒刻難行循故牘則盈縮無稽
而間爲陽驅陰脅之法則又近於籍外取
===
而讎民然則理財固無術乎財猶水也疏
則流泰疏則涸蓄則止泰蓄則滯故制其
出者毋若制其入而已數口之家日有膳
月有儲主者手屈心計握其奇贏而量用
焉終身可以無困朝得而夕散之廢其什
九而不知其存者什一卽計然猗頓立窘
耳況天下之廣其所仰給又千百億萬而
倍之乎夫天地之道至紘以大尚猶節其
章光愛其神明宇宙之財幾何而乃以填
punctuated:
同考試官教諭趙批：是能留心國計者，就所條畫次第施行，殷富立致矣。經濟材也，錄之。
同考試官教諭顧批：以儉德立論，是識時務者。
同考試官教諭楊批：會計始末，闡揚殆盡。
考試官教諭湯批：是策有裨主計者，宜錄。
考試官教諭王批：斟酌時事，劈畫允當。
財蓋難言哉！聽而不爲之筴，則大耗；驟起而持之，則裒刻難行；循故牘，則盈縮無稽；而間爲陽驅陰脅之法，則又近於籍外取而讎民。然則理財固無術乎？財猶水也，疏則流，泰疏則涸；蓄則止，泰蓄則滯。故制其出者，毋若制其入而已。數口之家，日有膳，月有儲，主者手屈心計，握其奇贏而量用焉，終身可以無困。朝得而夕散之，廢其什九而不知其存者什一，卽計然、猗頓立窘耳。況天下之廣，其所仰給又千百億萬而倍之乎！夫天地之道，至紘以大，尚猶節其章光，愛其神明。宇宙之財幾何，而乃以填…
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Instructor Zhao: This is someone capable of paying close attention to the fiscal administration of the state. If the measures outlined here are implemented step by step, abundance and wealth will be achieved immediately. He is a talent in statecraft; record this essay.
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Instructor Gu: Grounding the argument in the virtue of frugality, this is someone who understands the affairs of the times.
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Instructor Yang: The history and details of fiscal accounting are expounded almost exhaustively.
Comment by Examiner and County Instructor Tang: This policy essay will be beneficial to those in charge of fiscal administration; it ought to be recorded.
Comment by Examiner and County Instructor Wang: Weighing contemporary affairs, his analysis and planning are fitting and proper.
Finances are indeed difficult to speak of! If one leaves them alone and devises no plans for them, there is great depletion; if one abruptly steps in to take tight hold of them, harsh exactions prove difficult to enforce; if one merely follows old registers, surpluses and deficits go unverified; and if at times one resorts to methods of overt compulsion and covert coercion, that comes close to extracting revenue beyond the registers and making enemies of the people. That being so, is there truly no method for managing finances? Wealth is like water: if channeled, it flows, but if channeled excessively, it dries up; if stored, it stays still, but if stored excessively, it stagnates. Therefore, regulating expenditures is simply not as effective as regulating revenues. In a household of a few mouths, where there is daily fare and monthly savings, if the master counts on his fingers and calculates in his mind, grasping the surplus and measuring out expenses accordingly, he can go his whole life without hardship. If one acquires in the morning and scatters in the evening, squandering nine-tenths without knowing whether one-tenth remains, even Jiran 計然 or Yi Dun 猗頓 would immediately fall into distress. How much more so given the vastness of the empire, where those who depend on provisions are tens, hundreds, millions, and billions of times greater! Now, the Way of Heaven and Earth is supremely vast and great, yet it still moderates its shining light and cherishes its numinous vitality. How much wealth is there in the universe, that it should be used to fill…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
谿壑之欲塞江湖之漏哉古今言理財者
始於成周考之地官所隸若府史胥徒師
瞽眡瞭廩遺稍委之官以保養萬民者甚
設而大司空總土地所生料人民所出復
辨其山林川澤丘陵墳衍原隰之名物而
登之籍是會計之祖也間嘗按而求之兵
非不足也而比閭族黨遞相爲伍則犒食
不煩民官非不具也而卿大夫士等其功
緒以次而世之土爲祿入則廩餼不外索
===
其所爲上供者自祭祀宴饗匪頒好用公
旬之外不及焉固非如後世餒其家鬼而
淫於外神糜其祿食而疲民於枯魚之肆
也乃周公猶心憂之九賦以斂財賄自邦
中以至幣餘屬焉九式以節財用自祭祀
以至匪頒好用屬焉上自王后王世子下
至有司百執事經用具有等差無羨額此
雖不名爲會計而會計之防密於毫毛所
以約人主之侈德禁有司之苛征者無餘
punctuated: 谿壑之欲，塞江湖之漏哉！古今言理財者，始於成周。考之地官所隸，若府、史、胥、徒、師、瞽、眡瞭、廩、遺、稍、委之官，以保養萬民者甚設；而大司空總土地所生，料人民所出，復辨其山林、川澤、丘陵、墳衍、原隰之名物而登之籍，是會計之祖也。間嘗按而求之：兵非不足也，而比、閭、族、黨遞相爲伍，則犒食不煩民；官非不具也，而卿、大夫、士等其功緒，以次而世之土爲祿入，則廩餼不外索。其所爲上供者，自祭祀、宴饗、匪頒、好用、公旬之外，不及焉。固非如後世餒其家鬼而淫於外神，糜其祿食而疲民於枯魚之肆也。乃周公猶心憂之：九賦以斂財賄，自邦中以至幣餘屬焉；九式以節財用，自祭祀以至匪頒、好用屬焉。上自王后、王世子，下至有司、百執事，經用具有等差，無羨額。此雖不名爲會計，而會計之防密於毫毛，所以約人主之侈德，禁有司之苛征者，無餘
translation_en: …insatiable desires as deep as ravines and plug leaks as vast as rivers and lakes? In antiquity and modern times, discussions of financial management began with the flourishing Zhou dynasty. Examining those subordinate to the Minister of Education (diguan), such as the storehouse keepers, scribes, clerks, runners, musicians, blind musicians, sighted assistants, and officials in charge of granaries, relief, stipends, and provisions, the offices established to nurture the myriad people were thoroughly instituted; meanwhile, the Grand Minister of Works (da sikong) aggregated what the land produced, calculated what the populace yielded, and further distinguished the names and products of its mountains and forests, rivers and marshes, hills and mounds, riverbanks and lowlands, and plateaus and swamps, entering them into the registers—this was the ancestor of accounting. At times I have investigated and sought into this: troops were not insufficient, yet because the five-family neighborhoods (bi), twenty-five-family villages (lü), hundred-family clans (zu), and five-hundred-family districts (dang) successively formed military units among themselves, rewarding and feeding them did not trouble the people; officials were not lacking, yet because ministers, grand masters, and servicemen were graded by their achievements and successively received hereditary lands as their emoluments, their grain rations and stipends were not sought from outside. As for what constituted tributes to the sovereign, beyond sacrifices, banquets, discretionary distributions, favored uses, and public corvée labor, nothing else was reached. Surely it was not like in later ages, when they starved their ancestral spirits while indulging excessively in extraneous deities, or squandered their official emoluments while exhausting the people in the market of dried fish! Even so, the Duke of Zhou still worried about this in his heart: the Nine Revenues (jiufu) were used to collect wealth and goods, to which everything from the capital district down to surplus revenues belonged; the Nine Regulations (jiushi) were used to regulate expenditures, to which everything from sacrifices down to discretionary distributions and favored uses belonged. From the Queen and the Heir Apparent at the top, down to the various officials and hundred functionaries at the bottom, regular expenditures all had graded distinctions without any surplus quotas. Although this was not explicitly named "accounting," the safeguards of accounting were finer than a hair's breadth, and the means by which to restrain the extravagant inclinations of the ruler and prohibit harsh exactions by the authorities left nothing…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
內庫之類如
上供也賜給也奉養之類如
宗藩也戚里也武臣也歲餉之類如繕邊也
贍兵也市虜也
會典所載幾踰倍半自玆年愈久則費愈增
費愈增則賦愈急加以吏胥舞文豪强去
籍即欲考核往昔而且茫然矣況
會典統志非均輸專籍也不足以盡戶事項
故通計萬曆十年之例編為是錄勒成四
===
十三卷首之以舊額見額繼之以歲入歲
出大者若邊鎮漕屯小者若茶鹽鈔課靡
不畢舉冀
皇上一覽瞭然在目且
頒行中外所司以垂永據即所稱九賦九式奚
遜焉愚甞伏而思之今天下度田非加損
也山林川陂非減於昔也稅侯王之廬筭
筐販之緡差量非不纖悉也而其中消息
興革月異歲殊數年間領度支者旦暮案
punctuated: 內庫之類，如上供也、賜給也；奉養之類，如宗藩也、戚里也、武臣也；歲餉之類，如繕邊也、贍兵也、市虜也，《會典》所載，幾踰倍半。自玆年愈久則費愈增，費愈增則賦愈急，加以吏胥舞文，豪强去籍，即欲考核往昔，而且茫然矣！況《會典》、《統志》非均輸專籍也，不足以盡戶事項，故通計萬曆十年之例，編為是錄，勒成四十三卷。首之以舊額、見額，繼之以歲入、歲出，大者若邊鎮、漕屯，小者若茶鹽、鈔課，靡不畢舉。冀皇上一覽瞭然在目，且頒行中外所司，以垂永據，即所稱「九賦」、「九式」，奚遜焉？愚甞伏而思之：今天下度田非加損也，山林、川陂非減於昔也，稅侯王之廬，筭筐販之緡，差量非不纖悉也，而其中消息、興革，月異歲殊。數年間，領度支者旦暮案
translation_en: …In categories such as the Inner Treasuries—for instance, supplies for the imperial household and imperial bestowals; in categories such as stipends and maintenance—for instance, imperial clansmen and princely establishments, imperial relatives by marriage, and military officers; and in categories such as annual military provisions—for instance, repairing the frontiers, supporting the troops, and border markets with the northern tribes—what is recorded in the Collected Statutes (Huidian) has increased by more than two and a half times. From then on, the more years have passed, the more expenditures have grown; the more expenditures have grown, the more urgent taxation has become. Added to this, subofficial clerks manipulate the written rules and powerful families eliminate the registers, so that even if one wished to investigate the past, one would be completely at a loss. Moreover, the Collected Statutes and the Comprehensive Gazetteer (Tongzhi) are not specialized registers of equitable transport and fiscal administration; they are insufficient to exhaustively cover the detailed items of the Ministry of Revenue. Therefore, making a comprehensive calculation based on the precedents up to the tenth year of Wanli (1582), they compiled this record, organizing it into forty-three juan. It begins with the old quotas and current quotas, and continues with the annual revenues and annual expenditures. Major matters such as the frontier commands, grain transport, and military state farms, as well as minor matters such as tea, salt, and paper money levies, are all without exception fully listed. The hope is that when His Majesty takes a single look, everything will be clearly before his eyes, and furthermore that it will be promulgated to the relevant authorities at court and in the provinces to serve as a permanent standard. Even compared to what were anciently called the "Nine Tributary Revenues" and the "Nine Fiscal Formulas," how does it fall short? I have humbly reflected on this: today, the measured acreage of the empire has not diminished; the mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes have not decreased compared to the past; taxes are levied on the lodges of marquises and princes, and strings of cash are assessed on peddlers with baskets—the graded assessments are by no means lacking in minute detail. Yet the fluctuations, promotions, and abolitions within them differ from month to month and vary from year to year. Over the past several years, those in charge of revenue and expenditure morning and evening examine…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
計簿持金錢左盻操其贏右盻操其竒所
以佐縣官之緩急沃黎民之貨鏹備不冀
之虞遏無經之費者無不切至胡海内氓
庶富者日就朘削貧者不厭糟糠質子貸
穗以供租稅笞肉捶骨以急攀斂此其故
莫之能詰矣嗟夫財非天雨也賦非神輸
也陸輓川漕有時而息山冶海釜有時而
窮私求曲獻有時而禁而軍國有司經費
則旦暮歲月無已時度支惡能不告困哉
===
然當内空外乏之時而求足國裕民之道
則當論其所以耗財者而不當復論其所
以興利者非謾也耗財之路可塞而興利
之計已窮也
主上御寓以來十餘年間師旅未聞有所征發
禮樂未聞有所脩舉
諸侯王未聞與之剖符有所封建而纔一欲
謁
昭陵上
punctuated:
計簿、持金錢，左盻操其贏，右盻操其竒，所以佐縣官之緩急、沃黎民之貨鏹、備不冀之虞、遏無經之費者，無不切至。胡海内氓庶，富者日就朘削，貧者不厭糟糠，質子貸穗以供租稅，笞肉捶骨以急攀斂，此其故莫之能詰矣！嗟夫！財非天雨也，賦非神輸也；陸輓川漕有時而息，山冶海釜有時而窮，私求曲獻有時而禁，而軍國有司經費，則旦暮歲月無已時，度支惡能不告困哉！
然當内空外乏之時，而求足國裕民之道，則當論其所以耗財者，而不當復論其所以興利者。非謾也，耗財之路可塞，而興利之計已窮也。主上御寓以來十餘年間，師旅未聞有所征發，禮樂未聞有所脩舉，諸侯王未聞與之剖符有所封建，而纔一欲謁昭陵、上
translation_en:
…the accounting registers and grasp the cash, looking left to seize the surplus and looking right to seize the odd remainder; in their measures to aid the imperial government in its emergencies, enrich the common people's stores of coin, prepare for unexpected crises, and curb unregulated expenditures, nothing has been left undone. Why is it, then, that among the common folk within the four seas, the rich are daily further fleeced and pared down, while the poor cannot even get their fill of dregs and husks, pawning their children and borrowing grain-ears to pay their land taxes, having their flesh whipped and bones beaten to hasten the exactions [? 攀斂]? The reason for this is something no one can fathom! Alas! Wealth does not rain down from heaven, nor are taxes transported by spirits. Land cartage and river transport at times must cease; mountain smelting and sea-salt boiling at times are exhausted; private exactions and devious tribute-offerings at times are prohibited; yet the regular expenditures of the military, the state, and the authorities go on morning and evening, month and year, without end. How could the Ministry of Revenue not declare itself in distress!

Yet at a time of depletion within and scarcity without, if one seeks the way to make the state sufficient and the people prosperous, one ought to discuss what drains wealth, and ought not again discuss how to generate profit. This is no empty talk: the avenues that drain wealth can be blocked, whereas the schemes for generating profit have already been exhausted. During the more than ten years since our Sovereign ascended the throne, military forces have not been heard to be mobilized for campaigns, rites and music have not been heard to be newly instituted, and the imperial princes have not been heard to have tallies split with them for new enfeoffments; yet no sooner was there a single wish to pay a visit to the Zhaoling Mausoleum, to offer…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
太后壽及爲公主治裝卽三
詔稱乏至取司宰不足取冏寺又不足取太倉
借續之則連年進奉是果安在提空名自
炫而內自虛以畜百姓之怨失今不謹必
不支矣且司宰猶曰
皇上減膳之遺也冏寺所儲馬政所關已不可
輕秏而太倉則內贍百司外厭四夷
國家根本繫焉卽貫朽粟陳積空虛不用猶
日懇其匱今讀尚書洎臺省言事諸臣疏
===
則一歲所入未贍所出是何可以片語單
詞借也况頻歲河幸安瀾有如一日遷徙
胡以䇿之虜幸款塞今順義王且死有如
一日生心又胡以䇿之
親王封國諸公主第旦夕次第舉矣又胡以
䇿之故爲今計莫若矯之以儉矯之以儉
莫若倡之以
上奈之何
人君富有四海其尊無上其快意當前疇能狹
