punctuated: 太后壽，及爲公主治裝，卽三詔稱乏。至取司宰不足，取冏寺；又不足，取太倉借續之。則連年進奉，是果安在？提空名自炫，而內自虛，以畜百姓之怨。失今不謹，必不支矣。且司宰猶曰皇上減膳之遺也；冏寺所儲，馬政所關，已不可輕秏；而太倉則內贍百司，外厭四夷，國家根本繫焉。卽貫朽粟陳，積空虛不用，猶日懇其匱；今讀尚書洎臺省言事諸臣疏，則一歲所入未贍所出，是何可以片語單詞借也？况頻歲河幸安瀾，有如一日遷徙，胡以䇿之？虜幸款塞，今順義王且死，有如一日生心，又胡以䇿之？親王封國、諸公主第，旦夕次第舉矣，又胡以䇿之？故爲今計，莫若矯之以儉；矯之以儉，莫若倡之以上。奈之何人君富有四海，其尊無上，其快意當前，疇能狹
translation_en: … present birthday felicitations to the Empress Dowager, or prepare a trousseau for a princess, three imperial edicts in succession have already declared a shortage of funds! It has reached the point where, when drawing upon the Directorate for Imperial Accoutrements [司宰, i.e., Court of Imperial Entertainments] proves insufficient, funds are drawn from the Court of the Imperial Stud; and when that too is insufficient, funds are borrowed from the Grand Granary [Taicang] to make up the shortfall. Where, then, have all the tribute payments submitted year after year actually gone? Holding up an empty reputation for wealth to boast of oneself while being depleted within, and thereby accumulating the resentment of the common people—if we fail to exercise caution now, it will surely become unsustainable. Moreover, one might still say that the funds of the Directorate for Imperial Accoutrements are the savings from His Majesty's own reduced meals. Yet the reserves of the Court of the Imperial Stud pertain to horse administration and already must not be lightly squandered; as for the Grand Granary, internally it supports the hundred offices and externally it holds the four barbarian peoples in check—the very foundation of the state depends upon it. Even if the strings of cash were rotting and the grain moldering, piled up unused in idle spaces, one would still worry daily over their depletion. Now, reading the memorials of the Minister and the speaking officials of the Censorate and the Offices of Scrutiny, the revenue of a single year is not enough to cover its expenditures; how then can these reserves be borrowed away with a mere phrase or a single word? Furthermore, for several years running the Yellow River has fortunately remained calm; if one day it should shift its course, by what plan would we deal with it? The northern caitiffs have fortunately submitted at the frontier, yet the Shunyi King [Altan Khan] is now dead; if one day they should harbor treacherous intentions, by what plan would we deal with it? The enfeoffment of Imperial Princes into their fiefs and the construction of residences for the various princesses will soon be carried out one after another; by what plan would we deal with that? Therefore, in reckoning for the present, nothing is better than to rectify the situation through frugality; and to rectify it through frugality, nothing is better than for the initiative to come from the Sovereign above. Yet how can it be helped that a ruler possesses the wealth of all within the four seas, that his eminence is unsurpassed, and that with everything to gratify his wishes right before him, who is able to narrow…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
小制度而左右瞽御輩非從臾以侈無以
希寵售恩則儉之一言乃
人主之所慊而左右瞽御見以爲恡者故一二
大臣寓諷於會計庶幾量天地之數參
祖宗之規審
內府之盈虛察下里之疾苦節一朝之予而
存中人數十家之產節一事之費而留縣
官數十年之藏自是不侈於色則是編也
醉踞之屏女戎之戒也自是不侈於讒則
===
是編也蘇公之章巷伯之雅也自是不侈
於征討則是編也玉關之謝朱崖之罷也
自是不侈於馳射則是編也銜蹶之虞羌
夷之警也其益
主德裨
國計豈在周官下哉
聖天子旣躬行儉德於上賢公卿百執事孰不
奉清節以風四方而輶軒使者復明禁令
以導之約脩刑章以黜之浮丹青刻畫醲
punctuated:
小制度？而左右瞽御輩，非從臾以侈，無以希寵售恩。則「儉」之一言，乃人主之所慊，而左右瞽御見以爲恡者。故一二大臣寓諷於會計，庶幾量天地之數，參祖宗之規，審內府之盈虛，察下里之疾苦。節一朝之予，而存中人數十家之產；節一事之費，而留縣官數十年之藏。自是不侈於色，則是編也，醉踞之屏、女戎之戒也；自是不侈於讒，則是編也，蘇公之章、巷伯之雅也；自是不侈於征討，則是編也，玉關之謝、朱崖之罷也；自是不侈於馳射，則是編也，銜蹶之虞、羌夷之警也。其益主德、裨國計，豈在《周官》下哉？
聖天子旣躬行儉德於上，賢公卿、百執事孰不奉清節以風四方？而輶軒使者復明禁令以導之約，脩刑章以黜之浮。丹青刻畫、醲
translation_en:
…narrow the scale of his institutions? Moreover, the blind musicians and personal attendants around him have no way to curry favor and peddle his grace unless they egg him on to extravagance. Thus the single word "frugality" is something the ruler finds unsatisfying, and which his personal attendants regard as stinginess. Therefore, one or two grand ministers have lodged their remonstrance within the accounting records, hoping that he might measure the resources of Heaven and Earth, consult the regulations of the Imperial Ancestors, examine the surpluses and deficits of the Inner Treasury, and observe the hardships and sufferings of the humble villages. By curtailing the bestowals of a single morning, he preserves the patrimony of several dozen middle-income families; by curtailing the expenditure of a single affair, he retains several decades of reserves for the state treasury. If from this he avoids extravagance in sensual pleasures, then this compilation serves as the screen painted with drunken sprawling and a warning against female warfare. If from this he avoids extravagance in heeding slander, then this compilation serves as the stanza of the Duke of Su and the ode of the Eunuch Chamberlains (Xiangbo). If from this he avoids extravagance in military campaigns, then this compilation serves as the declining of requests at the Jade Gate and the abandonment of Zhuya. If from this he avoids extravagance in galloping and hunting, then this compilation serves as a precaution against bit-snapping stumbles and a warning against the Qiang and Yi tribes. In enhancing the sovereign's virtue and benefiting the state's finances, how could it rank below the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan)?

Once the Sacred Son of Heaven personally practices the virtue of frugality above, who among the worthy dukes, ministers, and hundred officials will not uphold pure restraint in order to influence the four quarters? And the envoys in light carriages will again clarify the prohibitions and ordinances to guide the people toward thrift, and maintain the penal statutes to suppress their frivolity. Those who indulge in painted and carved ornaments, rich…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
肥綺靡者必法而後財不耗於奢緇黄技
巧聲色邪歈者必法而後財不耗於蠹蛇
賦鼠斂虎噬鷹摶者必法而後財不耗於
墨如是則生之有道用之有度委遺山積
泉貨川流成周九府之贏可立致耳釋此
不講而區區於膚剥髓啄之術民就窮而
賦日急國與民竝困雖驅管晏以握筭走
桑孔以運籌末之能矣
第三問
孟養浩
同考試官訓導范批遣求書之官專校書之任此編
購要務也經生能一條對足覘博洽
同考試官訓導范批敘圖書興廢散合詞腴意博
考試官教諭湯批博古通今之士錄之以風後學
考試官教諭王批有裨右文之治者宜錄
天苞地符顯而圖書出焉蘭臺石室啓而
圖書聚焉夫圖書者豈世所稱纖眇長物
哉在人為國華而在天則為東壁宿東壁
punctuated:
肥綺靡者，必法，而後財不耗於奢；緇黄技巧、聲色邪歈者，必法，而後財不耗於蠹；蛇賦鼠斂、虎噬鷹摶者，必法，而後財不耗於墨。如是，則生之有道，用之有度，委遺山積，泉貨川流，成周九府之贏，可立致耳。釋此不講，而區區於膚剥髓啄之術，民就窮而賦日急，國與民竝困，雖驅管、晏以握筭，走桑、孔以運籌，末之能矣。
第三問
孟養浩
同考試官訓導范批：遣求書之官，專校書之任，此編購要務也。經生能一一条對，足覘博洽。
同考試官訓導范批：敘圖書興廢散合，詞腴意博。
考試官教諭湯批：博古通今之士，錄之以風後學。
考試官教諭王批：有裨右文之治者，宜錄。
天苞地符顯而圖書出焉，蘭臺石室啓而圖書聚焉。夫圖書者，豈世所稱纖眇長物哉？在人為國華，而在天則為東壁宿。東壁
translation_en:
…rich delicacies, and finery, then wealth will not be wasted on extravagance; if the laws are strictly enforced against Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, artisans of clever contrivances, and purveyors of sensual pleasures and licentious songs, then wealth will not be wasted on parasites; if the laws are strictly enforced against those who exact taxes like snakes and gather levies like rats, or devour like tigers and strike like falcons, then wealth will not be wasted on corrupt officials. If this is done, there will be a proper way of producing wealth and a measured standard for expending it; stores and surpluses will pile up like mountains, coins and goods will flow like rivers, and the abundance of the Nine Treasuries of the flourishing Zhou dynasty can be attained immediately. If one sets this aside without discussion and instead occupies oneself solely with the arts of flaying the skin and pecking the marrow, the people will fall into destitution while tax demands grow daily more urgent, and both the state and the people will be exhausted together; even if one were to drive Guan Zhong and Yan Ying to hold the counting rods, or send Sang Hongyang and Kong Jin to devise strategies, nothing could be achieved.

Third Question
Meng Yanghao 孟養浩
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Fan 范: Dispatching officials to seek out books and assigning dedicated responsibilities for collating them are the essential tasks of compilation and acquisition. That this student of the Classics can reply to each point in detail suffices to show his broad and thorough learning.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Fan 范: He recounts the rise and fall, dispersion and gathering of charts and books with rich diction and broad meaning.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang 湯: A scholar conversant with both antiquity and the present; we record his essay to inspire later students.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang 王: This contributes to governance that esteems civil culture; it ought to be recorded.

When Heaven's mysterious emblems and Earth's auspicious tallies were revealed, charts and books emerged; when the Orchid Terrace (Lantai) and the Stone Chamber (Shishi) were opened, charts and books were gathered together. Now, are charts and books merely what the world calls trivial and superfluous things? Among men, they are the splendor of the state, while in Heaven, they correspond to the Eastern Wall (Dongbi) constellation. The Eastern Wall…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
次奎室二星之中焉天下圖書秘府其星
明潤則圖書集道術行而世常泰其星失
色則圖書隱文士賤而世常否否泰汙隆
之運于圖書占之是惡可令一日廢哉然
是物也購之則蝟集匪購則散逸潛藏而
莫見編之則鱗次匪編則訛贗舛雜而無
章况未甞求之而謂缺軼焉未甞任之而
謂乏才焉謾也執事稱儒先語人有存歿
而學不息世有變故而書不亡誠然哉夫
===
典籍天下之神物也玉在山而草木潤珠
在淵而崖不枯典籍所聚不啻珠玉當有
卿雲輪囷金寶扶疎之氣時呵護焉是非
典籍之能爲神也古人往矣其精神在竹
素今雖去古遠甚而其神亦未甞不日與
人俱所以炳日月流江河而不息不亡者
以此乃孔壁酉巖之藏或廢或興或聚或
散代異而世殊何哉惟其爲天下之神物
也物神則變見幻化猶干將莫邪焉俄而
punctuated: 次奎、室二星之中焉，天下圖書秘府。其星明潤，則圖書集，道術行，而世常泰；其星失色，則圖書隱，文士賤，而世常否。否泰汙隆之運，于圖書占之，是惡可令一日廢哉？然是物也，購之則蝟集，匪購則散逸潛藏而莫見；編之則鱗次，匪編則訛贗舛雜而無章。况未甞求之而謂缺軼焉，未甞任之而謂乏才焉，謾也。執事稱儒先語：「人有存歿，而學不息；世有變故，而書不亡。」誠然哉！夫典籍，天下之神物也。玉在山而草木潤，珠在淵而崖不枯。典籍所聚，不啻珠玉，當有卿雲輪囷、金寶扶疎之氣，時呵護焉。是非典籍之能爲神也，古人往矣，其精神在竹素，今雖去古遠甚，而其神亦未甞不日與人俱。所以炳日月、流江河而不息不亡者，以此。乃孔壁、酉巖之藏，或廢或興，或聚或散，代異而世殊，何哉？惟其爲天下之神物也。物神則變見幻化，猶干將、莫邪焉，俄而
translation_en: …is positioned between the two constellations Kui and Shi, serving as the secret repository of all books in the realm. When this star is bright and lustrous, books are gathered, the Way and its arts flourish, and the world enjoys lasting peace; when the star loses its brilliance, books are hidden away, men of letters are despised, and the world falls into lasting stagnation. The cycles of stagnation and peace, of decline and prosperity, are divined from books—how then could they be allowed to fall into neglect for even a single day? Yet with such things, if they are sought and purchased, they gather as thick as hedgehog spines; if not sought and purchased, they scatter, lie hidden, and cannot be seen. If they are compiled, they are arranged in order like fish scales; if not compiled, they become corrupt, forged, confused, and devoid of order. Moreover, to claim that books are missing and lost when one has never sought them, or to claim that there is a lack of talent when one has never entrusted anyone with the task, is mere deception. Your Excellency cites the words of a former Confucian scholar: "Men live and die, yet learning does not cease; the world undergoes upheavals, yet books do not perish." Truly this is so! Canonical texts and records are the numinous objects of the world. When jade is in the mountain, the trees and plants are moistened; when pearls are in the deep pool, the banks do not wither. Where canonical texts and records are gathered, they are worth far more than pearls and jade; there is surely an aura of auspicious clouds curling upward and golden treasures branching out, constantly breathing protection over them. This is not because the books themselves have the capacity to be numinous. The ancients have passed away, yet their spirit abides in bamboo slips and silk scrolls. Although the present is very far removed from antiquity, their spirit has never ceased to be with men day by day. The reason they shine like the sun and moon, flow like the Yangtze and Yellow rivers, and neither cease nor perish, is because of this. Why is it, then, that the collections hidden in the walls of Confucius's house and in the caves of Mount You have at times fallen into ruin and at times flourished, at times been gathered together and at times been scattered abroad, varying from dynasty to dynasty and age to age? It is precisely because they are the numinous objects of the world. When an object is numinous, it manifests in wondrous transformations, just like the swords Ganjiang and Moye, which suddenly…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
圖書失記也夫書之類例若將兵然部伍
嚴雖多亦治部伍失雖寡亦紛禮一也凡
七種而以儀禮雜周官者非也春秋一也
凡五家而以啖趙雜公穀者非也推此而
它可知矣惟不明於類例其勢必至脫略
唐部有星書而無風雲氣候書宋庫有風
雲氣候書而無日月書推此而它可知矣
夾漈鄭氏謂七略苟簡六庫荒唐蓋有激
於此乎已自別爲一十二類散之爲四百
===
三十二種科條縷析覽者病焉則又不若
七略之疎而簡矣又謂書有名亡而實不
亡者如文言寓於周易鼓吹寄於樂府之
類是也有關於前而完於後者如淵明集
梁僅五卷隋增於梁而唐又倍於隋之類
是也有不出於當時而出於後代者如孔
安國舜典出晉連山易出唐之類是也鄭
氏之意以求書者未得其方校書者或失
其職故詳示凡例俾後代知倣而緝之其
punctuated: 圖書失記也。夫書之類例，若將兵然：部伍嚴，雖多亦治；部伍失，雖寡亦紛。《禮》一也，凡七種，而以《儀禮》雜《周官》者，非也；《春秋》一也，凡五家，而以啖、趙雜公、穀者，非也。推此而它可知矣。惟不明於類例，其勢必至脫略。唐部有星書，而無風雲氣候書；宋庫有風雲氣候書，而無日月書。推此而它可知矣。夾漈鄭氏謂「《七略》苟簡，六庫荒唐」，蓋有激於此乎？已自別爲一十二類，散之爲四百三十二種，科條縷析，覽者病焉，則又不若《七略》之疎而簡矣。又謂：書有名亡而實不亡者，如《文言》寓於《周易》、鼓吹寄於《樂府》之類是也；有關於前而完於後者，如《淵明集》梁僅五卷，隋增於梁，而唐又倍於隋之類是也；有不出於當時而出於後代者，如孔安國《舜典》出晉、《連山易》出唐之類是也。鄭氏之意，以求書者未得其方，校書者或失其職，故詳示凡例，俾後代知倣而緝之，其…
translation_en: …books and charts lose their record. Now the classification and principles of books are like commanding troops: when the ranks and units are strictly maintained, even a large host is orderly; when the ranks and units are lost, even a small force falls into confusion. Ritual (Li 禮) is a single subject, comprising seven subcategories in all, yet to mix the Ceremonials (Yili 儀禮) with the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官) is wrong. The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) is a single subject, comprising five schools in all, yet to mix Dan Zhu 啖助 and Zhao Kuang 趙匡 with the Gongyang 公羊 and Guliang 穀梁 traditions is wrong. Extending from this, the rest can be understood. Only because people are unclear about classification and principles does the situation inevitably lead to omissions and neglect. The Tang divisions included books on stars, yet lacked books on wind, clouds, and weather signs; the Song imperial repositories included books on wind, clouds, and weather signs, yet lacked books on the sun and moon. Extending from this, the rest can be understood. When Mr. Zheng of Jiazhai (Zheng Qiao 鄭樵) said that the Seven Epitomes (Qilüe 七略) was cursorily simplistic and the Six Repositories (Liuku 六庫) was absurd, was he not provoked by such things? He himself then divided books into twelve main classes and dispersed them into four hundred and thirty-two subcategories; the headings and items were so minutely analyzed that readers found them wearisome, which in turn was not as good as the broad simplicity of the Seven Epitomes. He also said: There are books whose titles are lost while their substance is not lost, such as the "Words of the Text" (Wenyan 文言) being lodged within the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi 周易), or the drum-and-fife songs (guchui 鼓吹) being preserved within the Music Bureau poems (Yuefu 樂府). There are books that were incomplete [or: defective, taking 關 for 闕] in earlier times yet became complete in later times, such as the Collected Works of Tao Yuanming (Yuanming ji 淵明集) having only five scrolls in the Liang dynasty, increasing over the Liang in the Sui dynasty, and doubling the Sui in the Tang dynasty. And there are books that did not appear in their own time but emerged in later ages, such as Kong Anguo's 孔安國 "Canon of Shun" (Shundian 舜典) appearing in the Jin dynasty, or the Lianshan Changes (Lianshan yi 連山易) appearing in the Tang dynasty. Mr. Zheng's intention was that because those who sought out books had not grasped the proper method, and those who collated books had sometimes failed in their duties, he therefore set forth the general principles in detail so that later generations would know how to follow his example and compile them. How…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
勤與嗟夫求書者能體鄭氏之志必無掛
漏之虞校書者能循鄭氏之法必無紕繆
之患奚至泯棼失傳也
高皇以馬上得天下不欲以馬上治改元未幾
命有司訪求古今書籍藏之
秘室又
遣使購遺書
頒行天下及脩治太學藏本
文皇奠鼎之初徵召名儒輯四書五經大全梓
===
布中外又開局纂著
永樂大典繕寫寳貯以備
昭代制作
二祖稽古右文之心皇皇若弗及而當時名山
石屋之遺牣充
天府較漢唐宋去萬矣然子史百家撰記諸書
行於世者攷之宋崇文總目十無一焉攷
之漢唐藝文志所載百無一焉誠有如執
事所云者此其故謂何大都天下之物不
punctuated:
勤與！嗟夫！求書者能體鄭氏之志，必無掛漏之虞；校書者能循鄭氏之法，必無紕繆之患，奚至泯棼失傳也？
高皇以馬上得天下，不欲以馬上治。改元未幾，命有司訪求古今書籍，藏之秘室。又遣使購遺書，頒行天下，及脩治太學藏本。文皇奠鼎之初，徵召名儒，輯《四書》《五經大全》，梓布中外。又開局纂著《永樂大典》，繕寫寳貯，以備昭代制作。二祖稽古右文之心，皇皇若弗及，而當時名山石屋之遺，牣充天府，較漢、唐、宋去萬矣。然子、史、百家撰記諸書行於世者，攷之宋《崇文總目》，十無一焉；攷之漢、唐《藝文志》所載，百無一焉。誠有如執事所云者，此其故謂何？大都天下之物，不
translation_en:
… diligence! Alas! If those who seek out books can embody Mr. Zheng's (Zheng Qiao 鄭樵) intent, there will surely be no worry of omissions; if those who collate books can follow Mr. Zheng's methods, there will surely be no trouble of errors and discrepancies. How then could books ever fall into oblivion and confusion or be lost to transmission?

When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huang 高皇, Emperor Taizu) won the empire on horseback, he did not wish to govern it from horseback. Not long after changing the reign era, he ordered the authorities to search for ancient and modern books and store them in the Palace Library. He also dispatched envoys to purchase lost books, promulgated them throughout the empire, and restored and put in order the editions housed in the Imperial University. At the beginning of the Cultured Emperor's (Wen Huang 文皇, Emperor Chengzu) establishment of the capital, he summoned renowned Confucian scholars to compile the Complete Collection of commentaries on the Four Books and Five Classics (Sishu Wujing daquan 四書五經大全), printing and distributing them inside the court and throughout the provinces. He also opened a bureau to compile the Great Canon of the Yongle Era (Yongle dadian 永樂大典), having it transcribed in fair copy and treasured in storage to provide for the institutions and literary productions of our illustrious dynasty. The minds of our Two Ancestors, in examining antiquity and esteeming culture, were anxiously earnest as if fearing they could not achieve enough; and at that time, the surviving texts from famous mountains and stone chambers filled the imperial storehouses to the brim, surpassing those of the Han, Tang, and Song by ten thousandfold. Yet among the various writings and records of the philosophers, histories, and hundred schools that circulate in the world today, if one checks them against the Song General Catalogue of the Chongwen Institute (Chongwen zongmu 崇文總目), not one in ten remains; if one checks them against what is recorded in the Han and Tang Treatises on Literature (Yiwen zhi 藝文志), not one in a hundred remains. It is truly just as Your Excellency has stated. What is the reason for this? Generally speaking, with all things in the world, if they do not…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有廢何以興不有散何以合昔奇章公謂
自周迄隋書籍已遭五厄况隋唐以後變
故滋多胡元以還散亡益甚書缺簡脫奚
惑哉
國初購募雖張搜訪未廣一旦欲遺編逸錄
林軸儷麗而與前代埒固難矣第至
今日文教大明而武庫所儲猶然絀焉則購
求之法未講而校讐之職未脩也夫求書
之官不可不遣校書之任不可不專乃自
===
古記矣盖綈緗未富貴在弋蒐故漢遣陳
農唐遣牛弘已而又遣苗發宋遣孫逢吉
李龜祥歷歷可指也今二百年來有奉
詔購募者乎則知求書猶未廣矣典籍旣彙貴
在讐勘故司馬遷世爲史官劉歆卒父前
業虞世南顏師古相繼爲秘書監令狐德
棻三朝脩史班班可觀也今二百年來有
世守專官者乎則知校書猶未精矣夫謂
求書之道有八曰卽類以求也旁類以求
punctuated: 有廢，何以興？不有散，何以合？昔奇章公謂自周迄隋，書籍已遭五厄；况隋、唐以後，變故滋多，胡元以還，散亡益甚，書缺簡脫，奚惑哉！國初購募雖張，搜訪未廣，一旦欲遺編逸錄林軸儷麗，而與前代埒，固難矣。第至今日，文教大明，而武庫所儲猶然絀焉，則購求之法未講，而校讐之職未脩也。夫求書之官不可不遣，校書之任不可不專，乃自古記矣。盖綈緗未富，貴在弋蒐，故漢遣陳農，唐遣牛弘，已而又遣苗發，宋遣孫逢吉、李龜祥，歷歷可指也。今二百年來，有奉詔購募者乎？則知求書猶未廣矣。典籍旣彙，貴在讐勘，故司馬遷世爲史官，劉歆卒父前業，虞世南、顏師古相繼爲秘書監，令狐德棻三朝脩史，班班可觀也。今二百年來，有世守專官者乎？則知校書猶未精矣。夫謂求書之道有八：曰卽類以求也，旁類以求
translation_en:
… suffer ruin, how can they flourish? If they do not suffer dispersal, how can they be gathered together? In the past, the Duke of Qizhang [Niu Hong 牛弘] said that from the Zhou down to the Sui, books had already suffered five catastrophes. How much more so since after the Sui and Tang, when upheavals multiplied still further, and from the Mongol Yuan dynasty onward, when scattering and loss grew even more severe! That books are defective and their bamboo slips missing—what wonder is it?

At the founding of our Dynasty, although efforts to purchase and solicit books were instituted, the search and inquiry were not yet wide-ranging. To wish all at once that surviving compilations and lost records should stand in splendid, serried ranks of scrolls and rival those of former dynasties was naturally difficult. Yet down to the present day, when literary and moral teaching is gloriously manifest, what is stored in the imperial repositories remains scant; this is because the methods of purchasing and seeking books have not been carefully studied, and the duties of collation have not been properly cultivated.

Now, that officials must be dispatched to seek out books, and that the responsibility for collating books must be made specialized, has been recorded since antiquity. For when silk-wrapped scrolls are not yet abundant, the priority lies in hunting and gathering them. Thus the Han dispatched Chen Nong 陳農, the Tang dispatched Niu Hong and afterward also dispatched Miao Fa 苗發, and the Song dispatched Sun Fengji 孫逢吉 and Li Guixiang 李龜祥—all of which can be pointed out one by one. Over the last two hundred years, has there been anyone who received an imperial edict to purchase and solicit books? From this we know that the search for books has still not been made broad enough.

Once canonical and historical texts have been assembled, the priority lies in collating and verifying them. Thus Sima Qian 司馬遷 held the post of Historiographer by hereditary succession, Liu Xin 劉歆 completed his father's prior undertaking, Yu Shinan 虞世南 and Yan Shigu 顏師古 succeeded one another as Director of the Palace Library, and Linghu Defen 令狐德棻 compiled histories across three reigns—all of which are clearly observable. Over the last two hundred years, has there been anyone holding a specialized office kept across generations? From this we know that the collation of books has still not been made thorough enough.

As for the statement that there are eight ways of seeking out books: first, to seek them according to their own category; second, to seek them through adjacent categories…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
華之縹乘者購之或著述家如司馬談之
藏名山者購之或學究家如伏生之匿壁
間者購之或勳臣家如侯君集之好書者
購之或隱逸家如惠施之五車者購之或
編氓家如越裴氏白下曹氏之聚書者購
之其檢括不稱者若蕭穎士即聽劾免而
又若唐之或以爵勸或以鏹購或以縑易
即有偽贋毋遽斥罰所謂與其過而廢之
也寧過而立之則異典畢出而燦然充棟
===
矣今學士舍人所居稱玉堂清秘而十館
列置纂脩不計歲月則唐宋校書之任也
第考其實果能紬金匱之藏乎果能秉太
乙之藜而訂金根之誤乎萬一殽駁謬戾
而令之部西崑之帙必不勝矣為今計者
宜分館列職計日受函業經術者專之如
梁丘賀夏侯勝董仲舒匡衡大小戴之於
五經業韜鈐者專之如任宏之於兵書業
博雜者專之如尹咸之於數術李柱國之
punctuated: 華之縹乘者購之，或著述家如司馬談之藏名山者購之，或學究家如伏生之匿壁間者購之，或勳臣家如侯君集之好書者購之，或隱逸家如惠施之五車者購之，或編氓家如越裴氏、白下曹氏之聚書者購之。其檢括不稱者，若蕭穎士，即聽劾免；而又若唐之或以爵勸、或以鏹購、或以縑易，即有偽贋，毋遽斥罰，所謂「與其過而廢之也，寧過而立之」，則異典畢出而燦然充棟矣。今學士、舍人所居稱玉堂清秘，而十館列置，纂脩不計歲月，則唐、宋校書之任也。第考其實，果能紬金匱之藏乎？果能秉太乙之藜而訂金根之誤乎？萬一殽駁謬戾，而令之部西崑之帙，必不勝矣。為今計者，宜分館列職，計日受函：業經術者專之，如梁丘賀、夏侯勝、董仲舒、匡衡、大小戴之於五經；業韜鈐者專之，如任宏之於兵書；業博雜者專之，如尹咸之於數術、李柱國之
translation_en:
…or families with cerulean-bound histories like [Zhang] Hua 張華, purchase them; or from families of authors who hid their works in famous mountains like Sima Tan 司馬談, purchase them; or from families of pedants who concealed texts inside walls like Scholar Fu 伏生, purchase them; or from families of meritorious statesmen who were fond of books like Hou Junji 侯君集, purchase them; or from families of recluses with five cartloads of books like Hui Shi 惠施, purchase them; or from families of commoners who amassed books like the Pei 裴 clan of Yue 越 and the Cao 曹 clan of Baixia 白下, purchase them. As for those who prove unequal to the task of searching out and gathering texts, like Xiao Yingshi 蕭穎士, allow them to be impeached and dismissed at once. And furthermore, following the practice of the Tang—sometimes encouraging contributions with noble ranks, sometimes purchasing them with strings of cash, sometimes trading silk for them—even if there are forgeries among them, do not hastily reject or penalize the contributors. As the saying goes, "Rather than err by abolishing it, it is better to err by establishing it." Thus, rare canons will all come forth and brilliantly fill the rafters.

Nowadays, the quarters where Academician (xueshi) and Drafters (sheren) reside are called the Jade Hall and Pure Secretariat, and the ten historiographical institutes are arrayed in place, compiling and editing without reckoning the months and years—this is the duty of collating books in the Tang and Song dynasties. Yet if we examine the reality, are they truly able to draw forth the treasures of the golden coffers? Are they truly able to hold the chenopodium torch of the Great Unity (Taiyi 太乙) and correct the "golden-root" (jingen 金根) scribal errors? If by chance they are confused,雜駁, and ridden with errors, to command them to classify the volumes of Xikun 西崑 will surely be beyond their capacity. To plan for the present, we ought to divide the institutes and array the posts, receiving book-cases on a daily schedule: let those who specialize in classical scholarship have exclusive charge of their field, as Liangqiu He 梁丘賀, Xiahou Sheng 夏侯勝, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, Kuang Heng 匡衡, and the Elder and Younger Dai 大小戴 did for the Five Classics; let those who specialize in military strategy have exclusive charge of their field, as Ren Hong 任宏 did for military books; let those who specialize in broad and miscellaneous learning have exclusive charge of their field, as Yin Xian 尹咸 did for calculations and arts (shushu) and Li Zhuguo 李柱國 did for…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
自解足稱雄辨
考試官敎諭湯批評隲人物表詳核
考試官敎諭王批掊擊精當不獨其詞雄古也
論一人而欲盡一人之槩也易論百代之
人而欲盡百代之人之槩也難何者以一
人獨觀則其呈德有象專才有形情貌可
以洞原顛末得以旋究如夷吾有釁浴之
耻許之以仁展禽有裸裎之褒闡之爲介
此謂以一言而蓋一人之生平不難也以
===
百代之人竝觀則歲歷綿曖稽覈難周派
别多端參伍寡决上斯人乎猶有上於斯
者下斯人乎猶有下於斯者是故辨二叔
非難也辨十六族難也然又安知五觀之
何如次乎辨四凶非難也辨十二牧難也
然又安知十亂之何如次乎使非稱博雅
之極精綜覈之方協總會之宜定銓次之
經其孰能進退古今悉當其則哉此班孟
堅古今人表所以不能無遺論也夫史之
punctuated:
自解，足稱雄辨。
考試官敎諭湯批：評隲《人物表》詳核。
考試官敎諭王批：掊擊精當，不獨其詞雄古也。
論一人而欲盡一人之槩也易，論百代之人而欲盡百代之人之槩也難。何者？以一人獨觀，則其呈德有象，專才有形，情貌可以洞原，顛末得以旋究。如夷吾有釁浴之耻，許之以仁；展禽有裸裎之褒，闡之爲介。此謂以一言而蓋一人之生平，不難也。以百代之人竝觀，則歲歷綿曖，稽覈難周，派别多端，參伍寡决。上斯人乎？猶有上於斯者；下斯人乎？猶有下於斯者。是故辨二叔非難也，辨十六族難也，然又安知五觀之何如次乎？辨四凶非難也，辨十二牧難也，然又安知十亂之何如次乎？使非稱博雅之極，精綜覈之方，協總會之宜，定銓次之經，其孰能進退古今，悉當其則哉？此班孟堅《古今人表》所以不能無遺論也。夫史之
translation_en:
…explain itself, which suffices to be called powerful argumentation.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Tang 湯: The evaluation of the "Table of Personages" (Renwu biao 人物表) is detailed and thoroughly verified.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Wang 王: The critique is precise and fitting, not merely vigorous and archaic in its phrasing.

To judge a single person and wish to exhaust the general character of that single person is easy; to judge the people of a hundred generations and wish to exhaust the general character of the people of a hundred generations is difficult. Why is this? When one observes a single person in isolation, the manifestation of their virtue has a clear image and their specialized talent has a distinct form; their disposition and demeanor can be penetrated to their source, and their beginning and end can be readily investigated. For instance, although Yiwu 夷吾 [Guan Zhong 管仲] bore the shame of being anointed and bathed [as a captive], he was granted recognition for his benevolence; although Zhan Qin 展禽 [Liuxia Hui 柳下惠] received praise even in the matter of someone stripping naked by his side, he was expounded upon as a man of firm principle. This means that to sum up a single person's entire life with a single word is not difficult. When one observes the people of a hundred generations side by side, however, the passage of years is long and obscure, making comprehensive verification difficult; their branches and categories are manifold, leaving cross-comparison with few settled conclusions. Should one place this person in a higher grade? Yet there are still those superior to this person. Should one place this person in a lower grade? Yet there are still those inferior to this person. Therefore, to distinguish the Two Younger Brothers (Er shu 二叔, i.e. Guanshu 管叔 and Caishu 蔡叔) is not difficult, whereas to distinguish the Sixteen Clans (Shiliu zu 十六族, the eight harmonies 八元 and eight accomplishments 八愷) is difficult; and yet how can one know how the Five Observers (Wu guan 五觀, the five rebellious sons of Qi 啟) ought to be ranked? To distinguish the Four Criminals (Si xiong 四凶) is not difficult, whereas to distinguish the Twelve Pastors (Shier mu 十二牧) is difficult; and yet how can one know how the Ten Able Ministers (Shi luan 十亂) ought to be ranked? Unless one attains the utmost breadth of learning and refinement, masters the method of comprehensive verification, harmonizes what is fitting in an overarching synthesis, and establishes a constant standard for grading and ranking, who could elevate and demote figures of antiquity and the present so that every single case matches its proper rule? This is why Ban Mengjian's 班孟堅 [Ban Gu 班固] "Table of Ancient and Modern Personages" (Gujin renbiao 古今人表) cannot be free from lingering criticism. Now, as for history…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
性靈之奧區啓耳目之茫昧其義例昭乎
若日月之光華其包括森乎若星辰之錯
落蔚宗氏稱其贍且詳也豈溢美哉第一
則聖之二則仁之三則智之九則愚之自
四以下自八以上卽孟堅亦不能揭而號
之矣不能揭而號之也豈非雄白之名可
詫而雌黃之義難施乎是以劉知幾史通
之作每每興慨於斯以爲其篇列之不類
於敘言也胡曾參之後伯牛也冉有之後
===
仲弓也抑鄧侯而又不果進聃雖諸甥也
晋文諸臣若舟之僑陽處父士會而其班
殊舛燕丹諸客若高漸離荆軻秦舞陽而
厥次不倫珍瓴甀而賤璠璵策駑駘而舍
騏驥以是爲監安所取衷哉至張晏氏又
以爲老子與文伯之母奈何四之而不知
老子已巍然聖列也田單魯仲連藺相如
奈何五之而不知魯藺二公原以二之而
單又未嘗五也大姬與寺人孟子奈何三
punctuated: 性靈之奧區，啓耳目之茫昧；其義例昭乎若日月之光華，其包括森乎若星辰之錯落。蔚宗氏稱其贍且詳也，豈溢美哉？第一則聖之，二則仁之，三則智之，九則愚之；自四以下，自八以上，卽孟堅亦不能揭而號之矣。不能揭而號之也，豈非雄白之名可詫，而雌黃之義難施乎？是以劉知幾《史通》之作，每每興慨於斯，以爲其篇列之不類於敘言也。胡曾參之後伯牛也？冉有之後仲弓也？抑鄧侯而又不果進聃、雖諸甥也？晋文諸臣，若舟之僑、陽處父、士會，而其班殊舛；燕丹諸客，若高漸離、荆軻、秦舞陽，而厥次不倫。珍瓴甀而賤璠璵，策駑駘而舍騏驥，以是爲監，安所取衷哉？至張晏氏又以爲老子與文伯之母奈何四之，而不知老子已巍然聖列也；田單、魯仲連、藺相如奈何五之，而不知魯、藺二公原以二之，而單又未嘗五也；大姬與寺人孟子奈何三
translation_en: … the profound realm of spiritual nature and enlighten the dimness of our eyes and ears. Its principles and precedents shine brightly like the radiance of the sun and moon; its comprehensive scope is arrayed like the scattered stars and constellations. When Weizong 蔚宗 (Fan Ye 范曄) praised it as rich and detailed, how could that be excessive praise? Yet it calls the first rank "sages," the second "benevolent," the third "wise," and the ninth "foolish"; from the fourth rank down and from the eighth rank up, even Mengjian 孟堅 (Ban Gu 班固) himself could not give them distinct designations. That he could not give them distinct designations—is it not because the titles of superiority and purity may be boasted of, yet the critical judgments of revision are hard to apply? Therefore, Liu Zhiji 劉知幾 in writing the Shitong 史通 (Comprehensive Perspectives on Historiography) time and again sighed over this, holding that the arrangement of the chapter did not match its prefatory remarks. Why is ZengCan 曾參 placed after Boniu 伯牛? Why is Ran You 冉有 placed after Zhonggong 仲弓? Why did he demote the Marquis of Deng 鄧侯 and yet fail to advance Dan 聃, Zhui 雖 [Chou 騅], and the other nephews? Among the ministers of Duke Wen of Jin 晋文, such as Zhou Zhiqiao 舟之僑, Yang Chufu 陽處父, and Shi Hui 士會, their rankings are utterly confused; among the retainers of Prince Dan of Yan 燕丹, such as Gao Jianli 高漸離, Jing Ke 荆軻, and Qin Wuyang 秦舞陽, their sequence is out of order. To prize clay tiles while despising fine fanyu 璠璵 jade, to whip on a worn-out nag while abandoning a thoroughbred steed—if one takes this as a mirror, where can one find a sound standard of judgment? As for Zhang Yan 張晏, he further asked why Laozi 老子 and the mother of Wenbo 文伯 were placed in the fourth rank, not realizing that Laozi was already loftily placed in the rank of sages; he asked why Tian Dan 田單, Lu Zhonglian 魯仲連, and Lin Xiangru 藺相如 were placed in the fifth rank, not realizing that the two worthies Lu and Lin were originally placed in the second rank, while Dan was never in the fifth; he asked why Taiji 大姬 and the eunuch Mengzi 寺人孟子 were placed in the third…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之而不知寺人固已四之嫪毐奈何七之
則表所不及吾又不知安所據而云然若
晏者可謂啽囈之語非旦晝之見也則又
何怪乎顏師古之議其後哉夫洪濛之世
昊古之初跡其人若有若無論其事若存
若亡繇斯以還上下千載文獻紛糅心術
幽秘夫孰能衡程而鏡照焉吾以爲姓氏
存而行事無所考見與行事可考而有之
不足爲勸無之不足爲戒者即不錄可也
===
顓頊之世不可必明孟堅猶且難之孟堅
固且以爲備乎何夏禹之時脫一庚辰老
君之時脫一尹喜鄹紇之時脫一徵在魯
莊公時會誅縣賁父而不書荆莊王時會
執珪佽飛而不書序西乞術而不及白乙
丙收江上丈人而不及激絮女又何也錄
倉頡謂其肇字也乃始皇時王次仲作隷
傳於世胡勿錄也錄奚仲謂其服駕也乃
黃帝時胡曹爲衣伯余爲裳荀始爲冠干
punctuated: 之，而不知寺人固已四之；「嫪毐奈何七之」，則表所不及，吾又不知安所據而云然。若晏者，可謂啽囈之語，非旦晝之見也，則又何怪乎顏師古之議其後哉！夫洪濛之世，昊古之初，跡其人若有若無，論其事若存若亡。繇斯以還，上下千載，文獻紛糅，心術幽秘，夫孰能衡程而鏡照焉？吾以爲姓氏存而行事無所考見，與行事可考而有之不足爲勸、無之不足爲戒者，即不錄可也。顓頊之世，不可必明，孟堅猶且難之，孟堅固且以爲備乎？何夏禹之時脫一庚辰，老君之時脫一尹喜，鄹紇之時脫一徵在？魯莊公時，會誅縣賁父而不書；荆莊王時，會執珪佽飛而不書。序西乞術而不及白乙丙，收江上丈人而不及激絮女，又何也？錄倉頡，謂其肇字也，乃始皇時王次仲作隷傳於世，胡勿錄也？錄奚仲，謂其服駕也，乃黃帝時胡曹爲衣、伯余爲裳、荀始爲冠、干
translation_en:
… the third grade?”—not knowing that the Eunuch [Mengzi] was already placed in the fourth grade. And when he asks, “Why place Lao Ai 嫪毐 in the seventh grade?”—that is someone the Table does not even reach, so I again do not know on what basis he makes such a claim! Someone like [Zhang] Yan 張晏 may be said to talk in his sleep rather than see by the light of day; what wonder, then, that Yan Shigu 顏師古 criticized him afterward!

Now, in the age of primordial chaos and the beginning of remote antiquity, if one traces the people, they seem at once to have existed and not existed; if one discusses their deeds, they seem at once preserved and lost. From that time onward, up and down across the millennia, documents and traditions are tangled and mixed, and the workings of the mind are hidden and secret—who could possibly weigh and measure them or reflect them as in a mirror? In my view, those whose surnames and clan names survive but whose deeds cannot be verified, as well as those whose deeds can be verified yet whose inclusion is insufficient to encourage virtue and whose omission is insufficient to serve as a warning, may simply be left unrecorded. Even for the era of Zhuanxu 顓頊, which cannot be known with certainty, Mengjian 孟堅 [Ban Gu 班固] himself found it difficult; yet did Mengjian really consider his Table complete? Why, in the time of Yu of Xia 夏禹, did he omit Gengchen 庚辰; in the time of Laozi 老君, omit Yin Xi 尹喜; and in the time of Zou He 鄹紇 [Shuliang He 叔梁紇], omit Zhengzai 徵在? In the time of Duke Zhuang of Lu 魯莊公, [the Table] notes the execution [?] of Xian Bofu 縣賁父, yet does not record him [in the Table]; in the time of King Zhuang of Jing 荆莊王 [Chu], it notes the holder of the jade tablet Cifei 佽飛, yet does not record him. Why does he rank Xiqishu 西乞術 while leaving out Baiyibing 白乙丙, and include the Old Man on the River 江上丈人 while leaving out the Silk-Washing Maiden 激絮女? He records Cangjie 倉頡 because he originated written characters; yet in the time of the First Emperor, Wang Cizhong 王次仲 created clerical script and transmitted it to the world—why was he not recorded? He records Xizhong 奚仲 because he yoked carriages; yet in the time of the Yellow Emperor, Hucao 胡曹 made upper garments, Boyu 伯余 made lower garments, Xunshi 荀始 made caps, and Gan…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
呂伋何遽不及鄧邠唐應而置之五徐偃
王宋襄公比於諸樊必有分矣而皆置之
六樂正子優於公孫丑辨在其師較若白
黑而置克丑下充程嬰杵臼之懿心也豈
不曰誠仁哉充輔果之蚤見也豈不曰誠
智哉然四之則恐泥也巢許卞務荷蕢接
輿之流豈不皆高蹈哉而巢許二之卞務
三之荷蕢接輿四之何也夫史名漢書乃
敘曠遠而脫本朝表載女士乃詳通顯而
略幽微則所謂體又安在乎故曰以山澤
量者不盡其珍也垢亦受之以鍾釜量者
不盡其粲也糲亦納之孟堅之史贍而不
免於穢詳而不免於體之紕也則此表之
謂也或者謂大家為其兄卒成之則以孟
堅既下請室而八表多出昭之手故遂意
之耳雖然吾無暇質此也所為孟堅計者
寄昂抑於一字如麟經之簡辭以立體上
也寓斷決於微言如遷史之即事以該情
punctuated: 呂伋何遽不及鄧邠、唐應，而置之五？徐偃王、宋襄公比於諸樊，必有分矣，而皆置之六。樂正子優於公孫丑，辨在其師，較若白黑，而置克丑下。充程嬰、杵臼之懿心也，豈不曰誠仁哉？充輔果之蚤見也，豈不曰誠智哉？然四之，則恐泥也。巢、許、卞、務、荷蕢、接輿之流，豈不皆高蹈哉？而巢、許二之，卞、務三之，荷蕢、接輿四之，何也？夫史名《漢書》，乃敘曠遠而脫本朝；表載女士，乃詳通顯而略幽微，則所謂體又安在乎？故曰：以山澤量者，不盡其珍也，垢亦受之；以鍾釜量者，不盡其粲也，糲亦納之。孟堅之史，贍而不免於穢，詳而不免於體之紕也，則此表之謂也。或者謂大家為其兄卒成之，則以孟堅既下請室，而八表多出昭之手，故遂意之耳。雖然，吾無暇質此也。所為孟堅計者，寄昂抑於一字，如《麟經》之簡辭以立體，上也；寓斷決於微言，如遷史之即事以該情，
translation_en: …How could Lü Ji 呂伋 be so far inferior to the Marquis of Deng 鄧 and the Marquis of Tang 唐—both descendants of the Duke of Zhou 周公 [reading 鄧邠唐應 as 凡、蔣、邢、茅、胙、祭 or similar] [?]—that he is placed in the fifth grade? When King Yan of Xu 徐偃王 and Duke Xiang of Song 宋襄公 are compared with Zhufan 諸樊, there must surely be a distinction between them, yet all are placed in the sixth grade. That Yuezhengzi 樂正子 was superior to Gongsun Chou 公孫丑 was judged by their master [Mencius] as clearly as black and white, yet Yuezheng Ke 樂正克 is placed below Gongsun Chou. If one extends to the fullest the admirable hearts of Cheng Ying 程嬰 and Gongsun Chujiu 公孫杵臼, could one not call them truly humane? If one extends to the fullest the foresight of Fu Guo 輔果, could one not call him truly wise? Yet to place them in the fourth grade is, I fear, overly rigid. Were not men of the ilk of Chao Fu 巢父, Xu You 許由, Bian Sui 卞隨, Wu Guang 務光, the Man Carrying a Straw Basket (Hekui 荷蕢), and Jie Yu 接輿 all lofty recluses? Yet Chao Fu and Xu You are placed in the second grade, Bian Sui and Wu Guang in the third, and the Man Carrying a Straw Basket and Jie Yu in the fourth—why is this? Now, the history is entitled History of the Former Han (Hanshu 漢書), yet it recounts remote antiquity while omitting the dynasty's own era; the table records men and women, yet it gives full details on the prominent and illustrious while neglecting the obscure and humble—where, then, is its so-called structural principle? Therefore it is said: he who measures by mountains and marshes does not get only treasures, for dirt is also received therein; he who measures by the zhong and fu vessels does not get only fine white grain, for coarse unhusked grain is also taken in. That Ban Mengjian's 班孟堅 [Ban Gu 班固] history is rich yet cannot avoid coarseness, and detailed yet cannot avoid flaws in its structural form—this refers precisely to this table [the "Table of Ancient and Modern Persons" 古今人表]. Some say that Ban Zhao 班昭 (Cao Dajia 曹大家) completed it for her brother, simply conjecturing so because after Mengjian was cast into prison (qingshi 請室), the Eight Tables mostly came from Ban Zhao's hand. Even so, I have no leisure to verify this. What I would reckon best for Mengjian is this: to lodge praise and blame in a single word, like the concise phrasing of the Classic of the Unicorn (Linjing 麟經, i.e., the Spring and Autumn Annals) in establishing its form, is the highest way; to embed decisive judgments in subtle words, like Sima Qian's 司馬遷 history in using actual events to encompass the full reality…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
識也智不出此而既立之傳復系之表表
而良也且不免於文之駢枝說之疣贅况
其舛駁脫漏若是是奚取焉夫聖固無二
品也如仁則夷齊是也微箕比干亦是也
雖然以方之孔甲伶倫則姱張貌象而失
其眞也如智則樗里鴟夷是也五羖大夫
亦是也雖然以方之方叔召虎則圖寫毫
毛而迷其似也夫表之言標也所以標世
系詔來許也而綜核名實評隲神理不與
===
焉乃其褒以單辭寵踰爵賞貶以隻字辱
過鞭箠則固檃括於紀載間而等列自具
矣故先儒謂列傳之中美惡備著足示鑒
誡表可無作信然哉遷史嘗作十表以傚
剛柔十日以定歷代系年而百世而下莫
之能易亦莫之能議者無它曰探研博而
考核精也曰總會周而銓配當也孟堅之
作是表果有得於此否耶嘗攷之孟堅在
漢以浮華剽獵稱故肅宗問禮樂而固對
punctuated: 識也。智不出此，而既立之傳，復系之表。表而良也，且不免於文之駢枝、說之疣贅；况其舛駁脫漏若是，是奚取焉？夫聖固無二品也。如仁，則夷、齊是也，微、箕、比干亦是也；雖然，以方之孔甲、伶倫，則姱張貌象而失其眞也。如智，則樗里、鴟夷是也，五羖大夫亦是也；雖然，以方之方叔、召虎，則圖寫毫毛而迷其似也。夫表之言標也，所以標世系、詔來許也，而綜核名實、評隲神理不與焉。乃其褒以單辭，寵踰爵賞；貶以隻字，辱過鞭箠，則固檃括於紀載間，而等列自具矣。故先儒謂「列傳之中，美惡備著，足示鑒誡，表可無作」，信然哉！遷史嘗作十表，以傚剛柔十日，以定歷代系年，而百世而下，莫之能易，亦莫之能議者，無它，曰探研博而考核精也，曰總會周而銓配當也。孟堅之作是表，果有得於此否耶？嘗攷之：孟堅在漢以浮華剽獵稱，故肅宗問禮樂，而固對
translation_en:
…is the second-best approach. If one's wisdom does not reach these levels, and having already established biographies for them, one further appends a table—even if the table were good, it still would not escape being a superfluous appendage in writing and an unnecessary excrescence in argument; how much less so when its errors, contradictions, and omissions are like this! What is there to commend in it?

Now, among sages there are inherently no two grades. Take benevolence (ren): Boyi 伯夷 and Shuqi 叔齊 are such, and Weizi 微子, Jizi 箕子, and Bigan 比干 are also such; even so, if one compares them alongside Kong Jia 孔甲 and Ling Lun 伶倫, it is exaggerating outward appearances and losing their true nature. Take wisdom (zhi): Chulizi 樗里子 and Chiyi Zipi 鴟夷子皮 [Fan Li 范蠡] are such, and the Grand Master of Five Ram Skins 五羖大夫 [Baili Xi 百里奚] is also such; even so, if one compares them alongside Fang Shu 方叔 and Shao Hu 召虎, it is sketching fine hairs while losing the true likeness.

Now, the word "table" (biao 表) means "marker" (biao 標); it is the means by which one marks genealogical lineages and instructs posterity, whereas comprehensively verifying names and realities and evaluating subtle moral principles have no part in it. As for praising with a single phrase so that the honor surpasses noble rank and reward, or censuring with a solitary word so that the disgrace exceeds the whip and rod—these are inherently framed within the historical narratives and records, and the gradations and ranks are naturally present therein. Therefore, when former Confucian scholars said, "Within the arrayed biographies, good and evil are fully manifest, sufficient to display warnings and lessons; the table could have gone unwritten," how true that is!

Sima Qian's 司馬遷 history [Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji)] once created ten tables, modeling them on the ten hard and soft celestial stems in order to fix the chronology of successive eras; that for a hundred generations thereafter none could alter them and none could criticize them is for no other reason than this: his inquiry and research were broad and his investigation and verification precise; his synthesis was comprehensive and his classification and matching appropriate. In Ban Gu's 班固 (Mengjian 孟堅) making of this table, did he truly grasp anything of this or not?

I have examined the matter: Ban Gu in the Han dynasty was known for superficiality,華 (flashiness), and plagiarism. Thus, when Emperor Suzong 肅宗 [Emperor Zhang] asked about rites and music, Ban Gu replied…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以在京諸儒必能知之及諸儒奏記固第
取叔孫通十二篇以上無乃探研之未博
與史稱孟堅掠人之美竊鍾揜耳自武帝
以上凡六世則皆彷彿遷書自昭帝以後
凡六世則皆憑藉賈劉無乃考核之未精
與旁行邪上固且未達漢紹堯運談更無
稽周秦旣不相因古今斯成間隔無乃統
會之未周與帝王儒老方駕並驅人物姓
名層出疊見聖賢之詳略不倫品格之低
===
昂失較無乃銓配之未當與夫是四者旣
皆不出遷右而徒欲以矯遷之失舉古今
人物彊立差等惡在其不穢與有體焉夫
漢孝肅固已窺其疎矣乃其語竇憲曰公
愛班固而忽崔駰此葉公之好龍耳而夾
漈氏至謂遷之與固猶龍之與豕則固不
逮遷遠甚諸史弃遷而用固劉知幾之徒
尊班而抑馬又不知其何說也愚因得而
評之遺親攘美徵賄鬻筆先儒之所以責
punctuated: 以在京諸儒必能知之；及諸儒奏記，固第取叔孫通十二篇以上，無乃探研之未博與？史稱孟堅掠人之美，竊鍾揜耳：自武帝以上凡六世，則皆彷彿遷書；自昭帝以後凡六世，則皆憑藉賈、劉，無乃考核之未精與？旁行邪上，固且未達；漢紹堯運，談更無稽；周、秦旣不相因，古今斯成間隔，無乃統會之未周與？帝王、儒、老，方駕並驅；人物姓名，層出疊見；聖賢之詳略不倫，品格之低昂失較，無乃銓配之未當與？夫是四者，旣皆不出遷右，而徒欲以矯遷之失，舉古今人物彊立差等，惡在其不穢與有體焉？夫漢孝肅固已窺其疎矣，乃其語竇憲曰：「公愛班固而忽崔駰，此葉公之好龍耳。」而夾漈氏至謂「遷之與固，猶龍之與豕」，則固不逮遷遠甚。諸史弃遷而用固，劉知幾之徒尊班而抑馬，又不知其何說也。愚因得而評之：遺親攘美，徵賄鬻筆，先儒之所以責
translation_en: …that the various Confucian scholars in the capital would surely know about them; yet when the scholars submitted their memoranda, Gu merely took the twelve chapters of Shusun Tong 叔孫通 and presented them to the throne—does this not show that his research was not broad enough? History says that Mengjian 孟堅 (Ban Gu 班固) appropriated the merits of others, stealing a bell while covering his own ears: for the six reigns up to Emperor Wu 武帝, he closely imitated Qian's 遷 (Sima Qian's 司馬遷) work; for the six reigns from Emperor Zhao 昭帝 onward, he relied entirely on Jia 賈 (JiaKui 賈逵 / Chu Shaosun 褚少孫 or Feng Shang 馮商/Liu Xin) and Liu 劉 (Liu Xiang 劉向 and Liu Xin 劉歆)—does this not show that his investigation and verification were not precise enough? As for the horizontal rows and diagonal upward lines of chronological tables, Gu did not even understand their principle; his talk of the Han succeeding the dynastic fortune of Yao 堯 is even more baseless; and since the Zhou and Qin are treated as having no continuity with one another, antiquity and the present are thus severed—does this not show that his synthesis was not comprehensive enough? Emperors and kings, Confucians and Daoists are driven side by side; the names of historical figures appear repeatedly in profusion; the degree of detail given to sages and worthies is out of proportion, and the elevation or abasement of their moral ranks loses all balance—does this not show that his grading and matching were not appropriate? Now, since in these four respects he never surpassed Qian, yet he vainly sought to correct Qian's failings by taking the figures of antiquity and the present and forcibly establishing graded ranks for them, how can his work be considered free of vulgarity and possessed of proper form? Indeed, Emperor Xiaosu 孝肅 (Emperor Zhang 章帝) of the Han had already perceived his superficiality, and thus said to Dou Xian 竇憲: "You love Ban Gu while neglecting Cui Yin 崔駰; this is just like Lord She's 葉公 fondness for dragons." And Master Jiaji 夾漈 (Zheng Qiao 鄭樵) even went so far as to say that "Qian compared to Gu is like a dragon compared to a pig," which means that Gu fell far short of Qian. That the various later histories abandoned Qian to follow Gu, and that men like Liu Zhiji 劉知幾 revered Ban while disparaging Ma 馬 (Sima Qian)—one truly does not know what their rationale could be! I may therefore offer an appraisal of him: neglecting his own father and appropriating the credit, soliciting bribes and selling his brush—the grounds on which former scholars criticized…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
班史者當矣然十志該富讚序弘麗宗經
以救遷之謬旨豐贍以掩遷之疎落如固
者是胡可盡訾哉乃或曰班彪有其業而
班固不能讀父書又不能保其身安在其
言爲天下法噫是又以固之冤古今人者
而冤固也
第五問
樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批書生譚田賦利弊犁然若指掌
===
而籌畫詳悉其經世之才耶録之
考試官教諭王批洞析弊源而條畫鑿鑿可用
今天下田賦之當均未有甚於楚者也田
賦均矣而爲之圖善後之筴亦未有急於
楚者也何也禹貢荊州之域厥土惟泥塗
厥田惟下中厥賦上下大都與揚州壤埒
而田有加焉則以淖濕同而人力異也楚
在春秋稱最彊大歲出兵車與秦晉爭雄
長非盡倚辦地利哉厥後揚州稱奧區而
punctuated:
班史者，當矣。然十志該富，讚序弘麗，宗經以救遷之謬旨，豐贍以掩遷之疎落，如固者，是胡可盡訾哉？乃或曰：「班彪有其業，而班固不能讀父書，又不能保其身，安在其言爲天下法？」噫！是又以固之冤古今人者而冤固也。

第五問
樊玉衡
考試官教諭湯批：書生譚田賦利弊，犁然若指掌，而籌畫詳悉，其經世之才耶？録之。
考試官教諭王批：洞析弊源，而條畫鑿鑿可用。

今天下田賦之當均，未有甚於楚者也；田賦均矣，而爲之圖善後之筴，亦未有急於楚者也。何也？《禹貢》荊州之域，厥土惟泥塗，厥田惟下中，厥賦上下，大都與揚州壤埒，而田有加焉，則以淖濕同而人力異也。楚在春秋稱最彊大，歲出兵車，與秦、晉爭雄長，非盡倚辦地利哉？厥後揚州稱奧區，而
translation_en:
… Ban Gu's History of the Former Han (Hanshu) are indeed justified. Yet his ten treatises are comprehensive and rich, and his appraisals and prefaces are grand and resplendent; he revered the Classics to remedy Sima Qian's erroneous purport, and used abundant fullness to cover Sima Qian's omissions. How can someone like Ban Gu be completely disparaged? Still, some say: "Ban Biao laid the foundation of the work, yet Ban Gu could not properly read his father's writings, nor could he preserve his own life—how can his words serve as a model for the world?" Alas! That is in turn wronging Ban Gu in the very way Ban Gu wronged the people of antiquity and the present!

Fifth Policy Question
Fan Yuheng 樊玉衡
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tang 湯: This scholar discusses the advantages and abuses of the land tax as clearly as pointing to his own palm, and his planning is detailed and thorough. Is he not a talent capable of ordering the world? Record it.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang 王: He penetrates to the root of the abuses, and his itemized plans are concrete and practicable.

In the empire today, nowhere is the need to equalize the land tax more acute than in Chu [Huguang]; and once the land tax is equalized, nowhere is the need to devise post-reform measures for its maintenance more urgent than in Chu. Why is this? In the territory of Jingzhou in the Tribute of Yu (Yugong), its soil was miry mud, its fields were of the middle-lower grade, and its tax revenue was of the lower-upper grade. On the whole its soil was comparable to that of Yangzhou, yet its fields were superior; this was because while both were equally marshy and damp, human effort differed. During the Spring and Autumn period, Chu was renowned as the most powerful and vast state, sending out war chariots year after year to contend for supremacy with Qin and Jin—did it not rely entirely on the productivity of its land to supply these? Thereafter, Yangzhou came to be acclaimed as a rich heartland, whereas…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
比於湯沐食邑不可勝數皆各爲私奉養
焉不領於天下之經費此大不均者二楚
故饒湖利而滄桑徙易靡常昔爲沮洳今
稱沃衍者不啻萬萬荆郢尤甚大姓與游
民彊有力者據之計畝歲入數鍾專其厚
積坐攫齊民食亡租稅而苦積逋者曾不
得以塗足而收半穗彼獨非王土哉而吏
不敢問如河南南陽此大不均者三屯非
獨楚有也而楚之屯非昔之屯矣按
===
制每軍給屯五十畝有奇今屯浮者什伯其額
此非獨依山濱水之地耕新墾遺也蓋亦
有占射焉夫屯軍不能世其業輒質之民
民利其賦薄無他役卽以已所有之民田
更籍爲軍歷十數傳不可窮竟所謂民竄
於屯屯竄於民者非邪此大不均者四先
是山澤之羡率弃不理今則臯濕原阪耕
者鱗集甚之叢箐幽蓽人力所不能通者
亦皆纍纍象耕鳥耘稱常稔焉乃聽其封
punctuated: 比於湯沐食邑，不可勝數，皆各爲私奉養焉，不領於天下之經費。此大不均者二。楚故饒湖利，而滄桑徙易靡常，昔爲沮洳，今稱沃衍者，不啻萬萬，荆、郢尤甚。大姓與游民彊有力者據之，計畝歲入數鍾，專其厚積，坐攫齊民食，亡租稅；而苦積逋者，曾不得以塗足而收半穗。彼獨非王土哉？而吏不敢問，如河南、南陽。此大不均者三。屯非獨楚有也，而楚之屯非昔之屯矣。按制，每軍給屯五十畝有奇，今屯浮者什伯其額。此非獨依山濱水之地，耕新墾遺也，蓋亦有占射焉。夫屯軍不能世其業，輒質之民；民利其賦薄無他役，卽以已所有之民田更籍爲軍，歷十數傳，不可窮竟。所謂「民竄於屯，屯竄於民」者，非邪？此大不均者四。先是，山澤之羡，率弃不理；今則臯濕原阪，耕者鱗集，甚之叢箐幽蓽，人力所不能通者，亦皆纍纍象耕鳥耘，稱常稔焉，乃聽其封…
translation_en:
…comparable to bath-towns and fiefs of maintenance, too numerous to count; all serve separately as private support and are not included in the regular revenues and expenditures of the empire. This is the second great inequality.

Chu [Huguang] has long been rich in the benefits of its lakes, and as waters and lands shift and change without constancy, places that were once marshes and swamps and are now called fertile expanses number in the tens of thousands—most notably in Jing [Jingzhou] and Ying [Chengtian]. Great clans and powerful vagrants seize them, taking in several zhong per mu each year; monopolizing these rich accumulations, they sit idle and snatch the food of the common people while paying no land tax. Meanwhile, those who suffer under accumulated tax arrears cannot so much as muddy their feet there to harvest half an ear of grain. Are those lands alone not the King's territory? Yet officials dare not inquire into them, as WAS done in Henan and Nanyang. This is the third great inequality.

Military colony lands (tun) are not unique to Chu, yet the colony lands of Chu are no longer those of the past. According to the dynastic regulations, each soldier was allotted fifty mu and odd of colony land; today the excess in colony lands is ten or a hundred times the quota. This is not merely because along the mountains and waters people plough newly opened land and reclaim abandoned fields; there is also fraudulent registration and tax-evasion by projection (zhanshe). For when colony soldiers cannot pass down their holdings from generation to generation, they readily mortgage them to civilians; and civilians, profiting from the light tax and absence of other corvée services on such land, even re-register their own civilian fields under military status. After ten or more generations of transmission, the matter cannot be thoroughly traced to the bottom. Is this not what is meant by the saying, "civilians slip into the military colonies, and the military colonies slip into the civilian registers"? This is the fourth great inequality.

Previously, the marginal lands of mountains and marshes were generally abandoned and left untended. Now, however, on low wet marshes and high slopes, cultivators gather as thick as fish scales; even in dense bamboo thickets and secluded brushwood where human strength could hardly penetrate, everywhere there is continuous cultivation—as if elephants ploughed and birds weeded—and they are spoken of as yielding regular harvests. Yet they are left to enclose and…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
殖自利幾世幾年不問所收此大不均者
五五者弊也而非所以弊也其失在庸有
司與舞文之吏不軌之民曰飛詭曰影射
曰虛懸曰那移曰隱沒曰兼并其姦狀若
蝟毛起務欺謾以逃其課以故富者連阡
陌而嫁稅於貧貧者或不厭糠粃而代富
人輸此大不均者六故曰今日田賦之當
均未有甚於楚者也議者不勝其憤輒曰
井田井田夫井田法黃虞氏以前尚矣靡
===
得而記云至周始備亦子輿氏所謂大略
也自李悝商鞅出而其法決裂廢滅不復
存二人誠萬世戎首然秦漢迄今英君誼
辟與奇謀石畫之臣莫之能變即有變者
或至紕戾無稽此豈商李之法有加於三
代聖人耶譚者謂戰國干戈之後丘陵城
郭墳壠廬舍鞠爲茂草即有平原亦半荆
棘漢去秦無幾已不能比次而經紀之顧
處千載之下而欲籠其業以授民踵新莽
punctuated: 殖自利，幾世幾年不問所收。此大不均者五。五者，弊也，而非所以弊也。其失在庸有司，與舞文之吏、不軌之民。曰飛詭，曰影射，曰虛懸，曰那移，曰隱沒，曰兼并，其姦狀若蝟毛起，務欺謾以逃其課。以故富者連阡陌而嫁稅於貧，貧者或不厭糠粃而代富人輸。此大不均者六。故曰：今日田賦之當均，未有甚於楚者也。議者不勝其憤，輒曰：「井田！井田！」夫井田法，黃、虞氏以前尚矣，靡得而記云。至周始備，亦子輿氏所謂「大略」也。自李悝、商鞅出，而其法決裂廢滅不復存。二人誠萬世戎首！然秦、漢迄今，英君誼辟與奇謀石畫之臣，莫之能變；即有變者，或至紕戾無稽。此豈商、李之法有加於三代聖人耶？譚者謂戰國干戈之後，丘陵、城郭、墳壠、廬舍鞠爲茂草，即有平原，亦半荆棘；漢去秦無幾，已不能比次而經紀之。顧處千載之下，而欲籠其業以授民，踵新莽
translation_en:
… amass wealth for their own profit, going for generations and years without anyone inquiring into their harvests. This is the fifth great inequity.

These five are abuses, yet they are not the root cause of the abuses. The fault lies with mediocre local officials, together with pettifogging clerks and lawless commoners. Through practices called "flying and fraudulent registration" (feigui), "sheltering under false names" (yingshe), "unassigned悬hung quotas" (xuxuan), "misappropriating and shifting" (nuoyi), "concealment" (yinmo), and "engrossment" (jianbing), their fraudulent schemes bristle like hedgehog quills, all aimed at deception and evasion of their tax quotas. Consequently, the wealthy own contiguous tracts of land across the paths and ridges yet shift their taxes onto the poor, while the poor, scarcely able to fill their bellies with chaff and husks, pay taxes in place of the rich. This is the sixth great inequity. Therefore it is said: nowhere today is the need to equalize land taxes more urgent than in Chu [Huguang].

Commentators, overcome with indignation, immediately cry out: "The well-field system! The well-field system!" Now, before the eras of the Yellow Emperor (Huang) and Shun (Yu), the well-field system was in the distant past, and no records of it can be found. Only in the Zhou dynasty did it become complete, yet even that was what Master Ziyu [Mencius] called merely an "outline." Once Li Kui and Shang Yang appeared, the system was torn apart, abolished, and obliterated, never to survive again. Those two men were truly the arch-criminals of ten thousand generations! Yet from the Qin and Han down to the present day, heroic and righteous sovereigns, along with ministers of extraordinary counsel and rock-solid plans, have been unable to alter this state of affairs; and even when someone did attempt to change it, the result was often perverse and impracticable. Could this mean that the laws of Shang Yang and Li Kui were superior to those of the sages of the Three Dynasties? Commentators say that after the warfare of the Warring States period, hills, city walls, burial mounds, and cottages were all overgrown with rank weeds, and even where level plains existed, they were half covered in thorns and brambles; the Han was not far removed in time from the Qin, yet it was already unable to arrange and regulate the land in orderly sequence. To live a thousand years later and yet wish to gather up all private holdings in order to distribute them to the people, following in the overturned tracks of Wang Mang of the Xin dynasty…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之覆轍吁亦迂矣是井田之不能復也勢
也議者無巳又有限田均田之說董仲舒
倡限田於元狩而武帝不果行師丹請限
田於鴻嘉而成帝不能用乾興初詔限公
卿以下與衙前將吏田而任事者以為不
便夫井地旣廢富民業巳肥殖長子孫傳
襲擬於封國而遽欲於歲月間盡褫其所
有此亦非人情矣是限田之不能行也亦
勢也由周而來七百年而魏孝文納李安
===
世之疏均授民田然不再傳而廢又百二
十年而唐太宗定口分世業之法然行未
乆而報罷又二百三十年而周世宗詔行
元稹均田圖法然世族羣起而撓之夫周
制旣遠生齒錯出民之遷徙靡定田之給
代亡常而履畝握筭官且不勝其鑿矣是
均田之不能乆也亦勢也夫田不能井又
不能限又不能均均亦不能乆第建步立
畝括田均賦此焉至策邇者八閩守臣議
punctuated: 之覆轍，吁，亦迂矣！是井田之不能復也，勢也。議者無巳，又有限田、均田之說。董仲舒倡限田於元狩，而武帝不果行；師丹請限田於鴻嘉，而成帝不能用；乾興初，詔限公卿以下與衙前將吏田，而任事者以為不便。夫井地旣廢，富民業巳肥殖，長子孫，傳襲擬於封國，而遽欲於歲月間盡褫其所有，此亦非人情矣。是限田之不能行也，亦勢也。由周而來七百年，而魏孝文納李安世之疏，均授民田，然不再傳而廢；又百二十年，而唐太宗定口分、世業之法，然行未乆而報罷；又二百三十年，而周世宗詔行元稹《均田圖》法，然世族羣起而撓之。夫周制旣遠，生齒錯出，民之遷徙靡定，田之給代亡常，而履畝握筭，官且不勝其鑿矣。是均田之不能乆也，亦勢也。夫田不能井，又不能限，又不能均，均亦不能乆，第建步立畝、括田均賦，此焉至策。邇者八閩守臣議
translation_en:
…in the overturned tracks of Wang Mang of the Xin dynasty—alas, how impractical that would be! Thus, that the well-field system (jingtian) cannot be restored is a matter of historical circumstance.

When commentators had no other recourse, they put forward proposals for limiting landholdings (xiantian) and equalizing landholdings (juntian). Dong Zhongshu董仲舒 advocated limiting landholdings during the Yuanshou era (122–117 BCE), yet Emperor Wu (Wudi) did not carry it out; Shi Dan 師丹 requested limiting landholdings during the Hongjia era (20–17 BCE), yet Emperor Cheng (Chengdi) could not put it to use; at the beginning of the Qianxing era (1022), an imperial decree limited the landholdings of officials from Ducal Ministers (gongqing) down as well as those of prefectural attendants and military officers (yaqian jiangli), yet those in charge of affairs considered it inconvenient. Now, once the well-field lands were abolished, wealthy commoners had already enriched and expanded their estates, raising sons and grandsons and passing them down by inheritance in a manner comparable to enfeoffed states; to suddenly wish within the space of a few months or years to strip them completely of all they possess—this too is contrary to human sentiment. Thus, that the limitation of landholdings cannot be put into practice is also a matter of circumstance.

Seven hundred years after the Zhou dynasty, Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei accepted the memorial of Li Anshi 李安世 and equally distributed land to the people, yet before two generations had passed it fell into abeyance. Another hundred and twenty years later, Emperor Taizong of Tang established the system of personal-share (koufen) and hereditary-estate (shiye) lands, yet not long after being put into practice it was declared abolished. Another two hundred and thirty years later, Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou decreed the implementation of the method of Yuan Zhen's 元稹 Chart for Equalizing Landholdings (Juntian tu), yet the hereditary great families rose up in droves to obstruct it. Now, since the institutions of the Zhou are already remote, the population has grown complex and uneven, the migrations of the people are unsettled, and the granting and succession of land lack constancy; if officials must pace out the acres (mu) and clutch counting rods, they will not be able to bear the contrived artifice of it all. Thus, that the equalization of landholdings cannot endure is also a matter of circumstance.

Now, since land cannot be arranged into well-fields, nor can holdings be limited, nor can they be equalized—and even if equalized, the arrangement cannot endure—simply establishing paces and setting out acres (mu) to survey the land and equalize taxes is the ultimate policy here. Recently, the provincial officials in charge of Eight Min (Fujian) deliberated on…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
括民田書奏
天子覽焉顧哀蒸庶失業天下罷匱乃下其議
於是太宰司農御史大夫言便宜者衆乃
下令撿括兩都十三部如閩部條章甚具
維時楚大小臣工罔不稟稟承
德意矢公矢毖分視督趣量山澤之入視莊屯
之額塞飛詭之竇責無籍之戶令所輸者
與所入相當取他羨補崩決償失額無嫁
稅匿逋者卽驗問嘉與更始弛其罰無論
===
世世偏累疲癃之民驩然若更生卽大姓
游民豪有力者亦喜過望謂千載始此一
睹則田不必井而井之之法存田不必均
而均之之法寓之役也楚壤數百年之積
蠹已去楚人數百年之沉痼已瘳當事諸
臣亦不遺餘力矣執事者猶以人窮吏弊
爲言而疑其難久復爲楚人規萬世長守
之策愚以爲法本無弊也其始也議之難
其旣也守之尤難人情狃於故常驟而語
punctuated: 括民田，書奏，天子覽焉。顧哀蒸庶失業，天下罷匱，乃下其議。於是太宰、司農、御史大夫言便宜者衆，乃下令撿括兩都十三部，如閩部，條章甚具。維時楚大小臣工罔不稟稟承德意，矢公矢毖，分視督趣。量山澤之入，視莊屯之額，塞飛詭之竇，責無籍之戶，令所輸者與所入相當。取他羨補崩決、償失額，無嫁稅。匿逋者卽驗問，嘉與更始，弛其罰。無論世世偏累疲癃之民驩然若更生，卽大姓、游民、豪有力者，亦喜過望，謂千載始此一睹。則田不必井而井之之法存，田不必均而均之之法寓。之役也，楚壤數百年之積蠹已去，楚人數百年之沉痼已瘳，當事諸臣亦不遺餘力矣。執事者猶以人窮吏弊爲言，而疑其難久，復爲楚人規萬世長守之策。愚以爲法本無弊也，其始也議之難，其旣也守之尤難。人情狃於故常，驟而語
translation_en: …to survey and register civilian lands. When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven reviewed it. Looking with compassion upon the common people who had lost their livelihoods and the exhaustion and impoverishment of the realm, he sent the proposal down for deliberation. Thereupon, the Minister of Personnel, the Minister of Revenue, the Censor-in-Chief, and many others spoke of its advantages, so an order was issued to inspect and survey the Two Capitals and Thirteen Provinces just as had been done in the Fujian region, with very complete regulations and statutes. At that time, the officials of Chu [Huguang], great and small, all reverently upheld His Majesty's benevolent intentions, swearing to be public-spirited and cautious as they divided the duties of inspection and supervision. They measured the yields of mountains and marshes, examined the quotas of estates and military farms, closed the loopholes of fraudulent transfers and false registrations, and held unregistered households accountable, ensuring that what was paid in tax matched what was taken in yield. They took surpluses from elsewhere to make up for land lost to collapses and floods and to compensate for shortfalls in quotas, eliminating shifted taxes. Those who had concealed land or evaded taxes, even when investigated and questioned, were graciously granted a fresh start and had their punishments remitted. Not only did the exhausted and infirm commoners who had suffered unfair burdens for generations rejoice as if given a new lease on life, even the great clans, vagrant people, and powerful magnates were delighted beyond their expectations, declaring that this was something seen for the first time in a thousand years. Thus, lands need not be divided into well-fields for the principle of the well-field system to be preserved, and lands need not be equalized for the principle of equalization to be embodied. Through this undertaking, the accumulated abuses of several hundred years in the lands of Chu have been removed, the chronic ailments of several hundred years among the people of Chu have been cured, and the officials in charge have spared no effort. Yet the Examiner still speaks of the poverty of the people and the malpractices of clerks, doubting whether this can last long, and again seeks to plan a policy for the people of Chu that can be maintained for ten thousand generations. In my humble opinion, the law itself has no flaws; at the beginning it is difficult to deliberate upon, and afterward it is even more difficult to maintain. Human nature is accustomed to old routines; if one suddenly speaks…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之以更革則必講張駭愕而不吾信故議
之難然利不十不苟興害不百不苟祛即
興且祛矣有一不當於衆心則條格未下
而訾者隨其後亟議亟罷鯈興鯈廢福端
未試而禍孽萌矣故守之尤難宋景祐中
命郭諮均田賦巳而重擾民遂罷怵於害
也皇祐中田京蔡挺均田而滄州民言不
便詔如舊摇於衆也嘉祐間遣包拯等分
按諸路行方田法而高本獨言不便甫均
===
數郡尋罷敗於私也三君子皆任事臣而
橫罹多口議亦垂寢法可易守哉顧守之
難者其弊不在下而在上其端不在未行
而在已行惟當事者弗爲害怵弗爲衆摇
弗爲私敗持獨斷之意操必然之畫法斯
久而無弊耳請即一二所目覩者商之兼
幷濫冒
詔旨嘗懲之而今偷玩繩約狃習故智者何衆
也楚
punctuated: 之以更革，則必講張駭愕而不吾信，故議之難。然利不十不苟興，害不百不苟祛。即興且祛矣，有一不當於衆心，則條格未下而訾者隨其後，亟議亟罷，鯈興鯈廢，福端未試而禍孽萌矣，故守之尤難。宋景祐中，命郭諮均田賦，巳而重擾民，遂罷，怵於害也；皇祐中，田京、蔡挺均田，而滄州民言不便，詔如舊，摇於衆也；嘉祐間，遣包拯等分按諸路行方田法，而高本獨言不便，甫均數郡尋罷，敗於私也。三君子皆任事臣，而橫罹多口，議亦垂寢，法可易守哉？顧守之難者，其弊不在下而在上，其端不在未行而在已行。惟當事者弗爲害怵，弗爲衆摇，弗爲私敗，持獨斷之意，操必然之畫，法斯久而無弊耳。請即一二所目覩者商之：兼幷濫冒，詔旨嘗懲之，而今偷玩繩約、狃習故智者何衆也！楚
translation_en: … to them of reform, they will inevitably exaggerate and be alarmed, refusing to believe us; therefore, deliberating upon it is difficult. Yet one does not lightly initiate a measure unless the benefit is tenfold, nor lightly eradicate an evil unless the harm is a hundredfold. Even after a measure is initiated and the evil eradicated, if there is a single point that does not suit the minds of the multitude, detractors will follow right behind before the regulations have even been handed down. Quickly deliberated upon and quickly abolished, suddenly initiated and suddenly abandoned [reading 鯈 as 倏], the seeds of disaster sprout before the beginnings of good fortune have even been tested; therefore, maintaining it is even more difficult. During the Jingyou era (1034–1038) of the Song dynasty, Guo Zi 郭諮 was ordered to equalize land taxes, but shortly thereafter, out of reluctance to trouble the people, the measure was abolished—this was being deterred by harm. During the Huangyou era (1049–1054), Tian Jing 田京 and Cai Ting 蔡挺 equalized the land, but when the people of Cangzhou 滄州 said it was inconvenient, an imperial edict ordered things restored as before—this was being swayed by the multitude. During the Jiayou era (1056–1063), Bao Zheng 包拯 and others were dispatched to inspect the various circuits separately and implement the Square-Field Method (fangtian fa), yet Gao Ben 高本 alone spoke of its inconvenience, so that after equalizing only a few commanderies it was soon abolished—this was being ruined by private interest. Those three gentlemen were all officials who shouldered responsibility for affairs, yet they perversely suffered from the clamor of many mouths, and their proposals were on the verge of being shelved; can a law be easily maintained? Yet as for the difficulty of maintaining it, the abuse lies not with those below, but with those above; its critical juncture lies not before its implementation, but after it has already been implemented. Only if the authorities in charge are not deterred by harm, not swayed by the multitude, and not ruined by private interest—upholding a resolve for independent judgment and wielding an unswerving plan—will the law endure long without abuse. Please allow me to discuss one or two things that I have witnessed with my own eyes. As for land engrossment and fraudulent evasion, imperial decrees have previously punished them, yet how numerous today are those who idly trifle with the regulations and restraints and remain habituated to their old tricks! In Chu 楚…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君相所常軫念爲之三令五申者直有司廢格
不用耳今之謀楚事者不求之上而求之
下舛也不求之已行而求之未行悖也卽
悖且舛而欲圖萬世之慮能乎記有曰地
廣大荒而不治士之辱也又曰虞芮之間
地有餘而人不足君子恥之假令郡縣長
吏人人懷恥辱之念而承奉
明詔若救火追亡子無敢後則弊無不祛利無
===
不興善後之圖宜無出此矣
punctuated: 君相所常軫念，爲之三令五申者，直有司廢格不用耳。今之謀楚事者，不求之上而求之下，舛也；不求之已行而求之未行，悖也。卽悖且舛，而欲圖萬世之慮，能乎？《記》有曰：「地廣大荒而不治，士之辱也。」又曰：「虞芮之間，地有餘而人不足，君子恥之。」假令郡縣長吏人人懷恥辱之念，而承奉明詔，若救火追亡子，無敢後，則弊無不祛，利無不興，善後之圖，宜無出此矣。
translation_en: …that about which the Sovereign and his ministers constantly show compassionate concern, and for which they have issued repeated orders and injunctions; it is simply that the authorities have shelved and neglected to implement them. Those today who plan for the affairs of Chu (Huguang) do not seek the solution from above, but seek it from below—this is erroneous; they do not seek it in what has already been enacted, but seek it in what has not yet been enacted—this is perverse. Being at once perverse and erroneous, if they wish to plan for the concerns of ten thousand generations, is it possible? The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "When the land is vast and left荒 [uncultivated] and untended, this is a disgrace to the scholar-officials." And another text says: "Between Yu and Rui, where the land is more than sufficient but the people are insufficient, the gentleman is ashamed of it." Suppose the chief officials of prefectures and counties everyone harbored a sense of shame and disgrace, and received and upheld the illustrious imperial edicts as urgently as fighting a fire or pursuing a runaway child, none daring to lag behind; then there would be no abuse that is not eliminated, and no benefit that is not promoted. Plans for sound future administration surely should not go beyond this.

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
御史旣大比楚士錄成將籍
奏之不佞有光以職事載牘宜
敘末端則思以
國家致士之意與
君臣大義明告多士迺後敢受成
也洪武初以弓矢平一海內
===
遭
明初定未遑庠序之事
高皇帝委心精意思爲天下作新
更始喟然歎興於學疾文言
之無實乃
詔中外博士弟子人各守受一經
三歲輒試非受業身通六藝
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
御史旣大比楚士，錄成，將籍奏之。不佞有光以職事載牘，宜敘末端，則思以國家致士之意，與君臣大義，明告多士，迺後敢受成也。洪武初，以弓矢平一海內，遭明初定，未遑庠序之事。高皇帝委心精意，思爲天下作新更始，喟然歎興於學，疾文言之無實，乃詔中外博士弟子，人各守受一經，三歲輒試。非受業身通六藝
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

Now that the Censor has conducted the triennial examination of the scholars of Chu [Huguang] and the examination record has been completed, it is about to be registered and presented to the throne. Because my official duties require my name to be inscribed in the documents, I, the unworthy [Feng] Youguang, ought to write a postface at the end of the volume. I therefore wish to clearly declare to the many scholars the Dynastic State's intention in recruiting scholars and the great righteous bond between ruler and minister, before I dare to accept the completed work.

At the beginning of the Hongwu era [1368–1398], when all within the seas had been pacified and unified by bow and arrow, the Ming had just been established and there was not yet leisure to attend to the affairs of schools. The High Emperor [Hongwu], devoting his heart and concentrating his thoughts, sought to bring about renewal and a fresh start for the realm. With a deep sigh, he turned his attention to promoting learning. Detesting empty rhetoric devoid of substance, he thereupon decreed that Erudites and Government Students inside and outside the capital should each study and hold fast to one Classic, and be examined every three years. Those who had not received instruction and personally mastered the Six Arts…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
者弗以名聞著爲
功令其它空語虛稱若詞賦諸
不在
令中者禁不得用卽漢所設孝
廉賢良明經茂才諸科皆一
切罷去若曰
國家所以致士非曉暢六經大
===
義莫可通今古分際備
任使耳
列聖承流道化熙洽二百年餘百
舉百全海內異能之士材懷
伊呂行若周孔靡不以此發
家焉誦義無窮蓋
高皇帝聖神文武於天下萬世皆
punctuated: 者，弗以名聞，著爲功令。其它空語虛稱，若詞賦諸不在令中者，禁不得用。卽漢所設孝廉、賢良、明經、茂才諸科，皆一切罷去。若曰：「國家所以致士，非曉暢六經大義，莫可通今古分際，備任使耳。」列聖承流，道化熙洽，二百年餘，百舉百全。海內異能之士，材懷伊、呂，行若周、孔，靡不以此發家焉，誦義無窮。蓋高皇帝聖神文武，於天下萬世皆
translation_en:
…were not to have their names reported to the court, and this was codified in the examination regulations. Other empty words and hollow expressions, such as rhapsodies and poetic expositions and anything else not included in the ordinances, were forbidden from being used. Even the various recruitment categories established in the Han dynasty—such as Filially Pious and Incorrupt (xiaolian), Worthy and Upright (xianliang), Understanding the Classics (mingjing), and Flourishing Talent (maocai)—were all completely abolished. It was as if to say: "In the state's recruitment of scholars, unless they thoroughly understand the great principles of the Six Classics, none can comprehend the distinctions and continuities between past and present or be prepared for official appointment and service."

Successive emperors carried on this tradition, and moral transformation flourished in harmony. For more than two hundred years, every measure undertaken has been wholly complete. Across the realm, men of extraordinary ability—harboring the talents of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, and conducting themselves like the Duke of Zhou and Confucius—have without exception risen to prominence through this system, praising its righteousness without end. Indeed, the High Emperor (Hongwu Emperor), sagely and divine, civil and martial, with respect to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有以灼睹其窾會而豫徵其
微眇旣已著爲
功令欲以制科網羅儁乂豈其
使在野猶有遺賢乎哉不佞
應御史聘而來也旣卒業多
士所爲文則見人人標本經
術根柢大義纚纚洋洋足聽
===
聞矣意者楚於
今日獨稱最盛山川靈爽默牖
其衷以保定
王國又其仰承
主上廣厲學官至意耳目歡感潛
潤臭味以是莫不雲蒸龍變
應
punctuated: 有以灼睹其窾會，而豫徵其微眇。旣已著爲功令，欲以制科網羅儁乂，豈其使在野猶有遺賢乎哉？不佞應御史聘而來也，旣卒業多士所爲文，則見人人標本經術，根柢大義，纚纚洋洋，足聽聞矣。意者楚於今日獨稱最盛，山川靈爽默牖其衷，以保定王國；又其仰承主上廣厲學官至意，耳目歡感，潛潤臭味，以是莫不雲蒸龍變，應
translation_en: …had the means to clearly perceive their crucial junctures and foresee their subtle intricacies. Now that these have been established as official examination regulations, intended to gather men of outstanding talent through the statutory examinations, how could it be that worthy men are still left neglected in the wilderness? When I, though unworthy, came in response to the Censor's invitation and finished reading all the essays composed by the many scholars, I saw that every one of them took canonical learning as both branch and root, and grounded themselves in the great principles—flowing and expansive, well worth hearing! Perhaps Chu [Huguang] today alone is acclaimed as the most flourishing because the numinous vitality of its mountains and rivers silently enlightens their inner hearts so as to safeguard the royal state; and furthermore, because they reverently receive His Majesty's earnest intention of broadly encouraging the schools, their ears and eyes are joyfully moved and they are quietly steeped in its spirit and flavor. For this reason, there is none who does not rise like gathering clouds and transform like dragons, responding to…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
明詔與雖然臣道至難言也事使
之義非細故矣名爲事君而
不造其極謂之不忠苞舉其
道告人而不語其至謂之不
盡請爲予多士畢陳之今夫
士伏處嵓巖究徧六經本指
不稱君臣之分無所逃於天
===
地乎事是君也雖以神州赤
縣之大至欲有所之而卒無
逃焉即終其身猶在日月照
臨之內其義可睹已人臣委
質事君道固多端總之不自
有其身者近是老生豎儒守
其師說白首不能窺見聖道
punctuated: 明詔與？雖然，臣道至難言也，事使之義，非細故矣。名爲事君而不造其極，謂之不忠；苞舉其道告人而不語其至，謂之不盡。請爲予多士畢陳之。今夫士伏處嵓巖，究徧六經本指，不稱君臣之分無所逃於天地乎？事是君也，雖以神州赤縣之大，至欲有所之，而卒無逃焉，即終其身猶在日月照臨之內，其義可睹已。人臣委質事君，道固多端，總之不自有其身者近是。老生豎儒守其師說，白首不能窺見聖道
translation_en: … the illustrious edict? Even so, the Way of the minister is exceedingly difficult to speak of, and the righteous principles of serving a ruler and employing a minister are no trivial matter. To serve one's ruler in name without reaching the utmost extreme of devotion is called disloyalty; to encompass this Way in speaking to others without telling of its highest perfection is called failing to do one's utmost. Allow me to set this forth in full for my many scholars. Now, when a scholar dwells in seclusion among crags and cliffs, thoroughly investigating the fundamental purport of the Six Classics, does he not declare that there is no escaping the duty between ruler and minister anywhere between heaven and earth? In serving this ruler, even across the vast expanse of the Divine Land and Red Precincts [China], should one wish to go elsewhere, in the end there is no escape; even to the end of one's life, one remains within the illumination of the sun and moon—the principle of this can readily be seen. When a minister pledges himself in service to his ruler, the ways of doing so are indeed manifold, but in sum, he who does not regard his person as his own comes closest to the mark. Aged pedants and petty Confucians cling to the doctrines of their teachers and, even until their heads turn white, are unable to catch a glimpse of the…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之大全一當利害輒掉臂不
顧以此爲稟於古昔夫聖人
之道具在六經可考鏡也平
生誦讀詩書豈眞未嘗決擇
異同探厥閫奧哉彼其心以
爲此可博名此可規利此可
遠嫌而避咎以故處其便於
===
===
厥躬而遺其難於
君父有所託而逃耳嗟乎
國家舉士之謂何廼重自愛惜
如此卽有緩急安所賴之爾
多士舉矣其務一乃心定乃
志毋持祿養交毋詭飾干譽
毋相眉睫與時浮沉毋矯矯
punctuated: 之大全，一當利害，輒掉臂不顧，以此爲稟於古昔。夫聖人之道，具在《六經》，可考鏡也。平生誦讀《詩》、《書》，豈眞未嘗決擇異同，探厥閫奧哉？彼其心以爲：此可博名，此可規利，此可遠嫌而避咎；以故處其便於厥躬，而遺其難於君父，有所託而逃耳。嗟乎！國家舉士之謂何？廼重自愛惜如此，卽有緩急，安所賴之？爾多士舉矣，其務一乃心，定乃志，毋持祿養交，毋詭飾干譽，毋相眉睫與時浮沉，毋矯矯
translation_en:
…the full completeness [of the Way of the Sages]; yet as soon as they encounter matters of personal advantage or harm, they swing their arms and walk away without looking back, claiming that this is what they have received from antiquity. Now, the Way of the Sages is fully contained in the Six Classics and can be examined as in a mirror. Spending their whole lives reciting the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), is it truly that they have never weighed the similarities and differences or probed their deepest mysteries? In their hearts they reckon: "This can win me fame, this can secure me profit, this can keep me far from suspicion and allow me to avoid blame." Thus they claim for themselves what is convenient for their own persons, while leaving what is difficult to their ruler and father—merely finding a pretext under which to flee! Alas! For what purpose does the state select scholars? If they cherish and spare themselves so heavily as this, then when an emergency arises, how can they be relied upon?

You many scholars have now been selected as provincial graduates. You must strive to unify your hearts and fix your resolve. Do not merely cling to your emoluments and cultivate personal connections; do not practice deceitful pretensions to seek fame; do not watch others' expressions to drift up and down with the times; do not affectedly…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以一節自好毋以利害付諸
身以成敗付諸
國事矢心殫誠事
上使凡所爲唯
天地鬼神實臨之其道詎不偉與
不佞道襄樊望隆中知諸葛
忠武侯楚產也彼當漢末造
===
國步多艱成敗利鈍非所逆
睹猶然鞠躬盡瘁今讀其言
忠貞之心千古如一日焉矧
皇上嚮意文學每飯側席天下賢
者百司庶府少有功能罔不
畢敘有
君如此其忍負之夫結縶蘊山懸
punctuated: 以一節自好，毋以利害付諸身、以成敗付諸國事。矢心殫誠事上，使凡所爲唯天地鬼神實臨之，其道詎不偉與？不佞道襄、樊，望隆中，知諸葛忠武侯，楚產也。彼當漢末造，國步多艱，成敗利鈍，非所逆睹，猶然鞠躬盡瘁。今讀其言，忠貞之心，千古如一日焉。矧皇上嚮意文學，每飯側席，天下賢者、百司庶府，少有功能，罔不畢敘。有君如此，其忍負之？夫結縶蘊山，懸…
translation_en: …indulge in self-satisfaction over a single point of integrity, and do not relegate gain and loss to your own person while leaving success and failure to the affairs of the state. Pledge your heart and exhaust your sincerity in serving the Emperor, so that in all you do, Heaven, Earth, and the spirits truly watch over you—how could such a Way not be great? When I, an unworthy person, traveled by way of Xiangyang and Fancheng and gazed toward Longzhong, I recognized that Zhuge, the Marquis of Loyal Martiality (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮), was a native of Chu. Facing the waning days of the Han, when the fortunes of the state were beset with difficulties and success or failure, advantage or setback could not be foreseen, he nonetheless bowed his body and exhausted his strength to the very end. When we read his words today, his loyal and steadfast heart remains across a thousand ages as if it were a single day. How much more so now, when His Majesty turns his mind toward letters and learning, leaving his mat vacant in anticipation of the worthy at every meal, so that among the worthies of the realm and the officials of all bureaus and offices, none who possess even a slight merit or capability fail to be fully recognized and advanced. Having a ruler such as this, how could you bear to fail him? Now, the Jielu jade lies hidden in the mountains, and the Xuan…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
黎匿頷良工嬰距爪披逆鱗
以求之亡所自愛重適用也
士人少負四方之志長試之
藝類能剌剌道天下計至今
受事則舉其生平而弁髦之
斯則燕石魚目末之若矣卽
工人者安所傅眊臊之誅焉
===
今多士挾筴登途方日夜裝
而見
天子趨
日月之末光非抱空質矣
上幸止輦而聽將試之庶官使得
自見有日也其尚誦說所聞
大義蘄自盡其經術以無負
punctuated: 黎匿頷，良工嬰距爪、披逆鱗以求之，亡所自愛，重適用也。士人少負四方之志，長試之藝，類能剌剌道天下計；至今受事，則舉其生平而弁髦之，斯則燕石、魚目末之若矣，卽工人者安所傅眊臊之誅焉！今多士挾筴登途，方日夜裝而見天子，趨日月之末光，非抱空質矣。上幸止輦而聽，將試之庶官，使得自見有日也。其尚誦說所聞大義，蘄自盡其經術，以無負
translation_en: …the Xuanli jade is hidden beneath the dragon’s chin, yet a skilled craftsman will brave claws and talons and stroke the inverted scales to seek them out, sparing no care for his own life, because he prizes what is fit for practical use. Scholars in their youth harbor ambitions for the four quarters of the world, and when grown and tested in the literary arts, they can all talk endlessly of plans for the empire. Yet when today they take up actual office, they cast aside all they have learned in their lives as if it were a useless cap; in so doing, they are not even the equal of fake stones from Yan or fish-eye pearls, and how then could the craftsman himself escape the blame for being dim-sighted and foul [?]! Now the many scholars, clasping their books and setting out on the road, are packing day and night to go for an audience with the Son of Heaven and hasten toward the far-reaching radiance of the sun and moon; they do not come holding mere empty pledges. Should His Majesty graciously halt his imperial carriage to listen, and soon test them in the various offices, the day when they can prove themselves is at hand. May they still recite and expound the great principles they have heard, striving to exhaust their mastery of the Classics so as not to betray…

title: 萬曆十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國家設科求材意不佞竝有榮
施哉
山東東昌府莘縣儒學敎諭
湯有光謹序
punctuated:
國家設科求材意，不佞竝有榮施哉！

山東東昌府莘縣儒學敎諭湯有光謹序。
translation_en:
… the dynasty's intent in establishing the examinations to seek out talent. Would not I, unworthy as I am, also share in this glorious bestowal!

Respectfully prefaced by Tang Youguang 湯有光, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shen County in Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
